to an even greater extent, however, the motivation that spurred the humanrights movement was revulsion worldwide, including in the us, against american aid to pinochets forces, a policy directed by president richard nixon and secretary of state henry kissinger.
在美國國內，國會議員將這次政變變成了推行人權運動的平臺。
in the us, members of congress turned the coup into a platform for efforts to promote human rights.
他們譴責智利的事態，舉行關於推行人權重要性的聽證，並克服了總統福特的否決，透過立法要求用人權標準作為美國對外政策的指導。
they condemned developments in chile, held hearings about the importance of promoting human rights, and adopted legislation over president gerald fords veto requiring that humanrights standards guide us foreign policy.
如今，這一立法仍然有效，只是略微做了一些修訂。
a slightly revised version of that legislation remains in force.
奧巴馬宣佈，敘利亞使用化學武器將跨越“紅線 ” — —並暗示如果越線將動用武力 — — 這反映了美國過去四十年來所形成的在世界範圍內推行人權的承諾。
obamas proclamation that the use of chemical weapons in syria would cross a red line and his implicit threat to use force if that line were crossed reflects the commitment that the us has made during the past four decades to promote human rights worldwide.
2001年9月11日發生的事件也對向敘利亞總統巴沙爾·阿薩德政權採取懲罰性打擊的問題起到了關鍵作用。
the events of september 11, 2001, are also playing a crucial role in deciding the question of a punitive strike against syrian president bashar alassads regime.
12年前的恐怖襲擊的一個後果是美國和其他西方國家認識到，中東的發展可能影響其自身安全和保障。
one consequence of the terrorist attacks 12 years ago is that americans and others in the west became aware that developments in the middle east could affect their own safety and security.
一開始，襲擊造成了極強的復仇慾望，隨後，由於後果不可預測，復仇慾望被謹慎干預取代。
initially, the attacks unleashed a strong desire to retaliate, which later gave way to caution about intervention, owing to unforeseen consequences.
在英國，人們對國家被騙參與伊拉克戰爭的騙局一直滿懷憎恨，這成為國會拒絕支援打擊敘利亞的主要原因。
in britain, continuing intense resentment over the deceptions that led to the countrys engagement in the iraq war seems to be the main reason for parliaments refusal to back a strike against syria.
擔心又一場中東戰爭也是奧巴馬只願意對敘利亞採取一次性懲罰性打擊的原因，一些國會議員甚至連這一點都反對。
wariness of another middle east war has also underpinned obamas unwillingness to go beyond a onetime punitive strike on syria with some in congress opposed to even that.
國會必須小心避免重蹈2003年支援伊拉克戰爭的災難性錯誤的覆轍，但美國在1973年9月11日後所秉承的推行人權承諾似乎才是評估奧巴馬的美國軍事幹預敘利亞方案的更合適的標準。
though congress must guard against repeating its disastrous mistake in 2003, when it supported the war in iraq, the commitment to promote human rights that the us made following september 11, 1973, seems a more appropriate standard for weighing obamas proposal for us military action in syria.
維護使用化學武器的國際禁令是迫切的問題。
maintaining the international prohibition on the use of chemical weapons is an urgent concern.
巴沙爾政權使用化學武器的罪行是毋庸置疑的。
the assad regimes culpability for using these weapons is not in doubt.
如果美國國會負責任地考慮奧巴馬的計劃，而不是屈服於次次讓他難堪的黨派私利，那麼就能增強其奪回憲法權力授權軍事衝突的立場 — — 在過去半個世紀中，這一權力往往遭受削弱而不是增強。
if the us congress deals with obamas proposal responsibly, and does not yield to those motivated by a partisan desire to embarrass him at every turn, it will enhance its own claim to recapture the constitutional power to authorize military conflict a power that has been disregarded more often than not in the past halfcentury.
這一角色的一個關鍵部分是謹慎考慮懲罰性打擊的界線。
a critical part of its role must be to consider with care the limits that should be placed on a punitive strike.
伊拉克戰爭從一開始就被誤解了，因為這是以侵略和佔領與事無干的國家報復2001年9月11日的恐怖襲擊。
the war in iraq was misconceived from the start, because it was an attempt to avenge the september 11, 2001, terrorist attacks by invading and occupying a country that had no part in them.
相反，奧巴馬打擊敘利亞的方案是為了強化重要的人權規範，其手段並不包括侵略和佔領，而是直接懲罰犯下重罪的物件。
obamas proposal to strike syria, by contrast, is an attempt to enforce an important humanrights norm by directly punishing through means that do not involve invasion and occupation those who committed a gross violation.
這讓人權重新回到了1973年9月11日後設定的美國對外政策核心位置上。
it restores human rights to the central place in american foreign policy set forth after september 11, 1973.
約束重重的美國選擇
americas constrained choice
紐波特海灘—關於11月的美國總統大選，傳統智慧只能說是部分正確。
newport beach the conventional wisdom about the november presidential election in the united states is only partly correct.
是的，經濟問題將在結果決定中起到很大作用。
yes, economic issues will play a large role in determining the outcome.
但下一個階段 — — 在日趨醜陋的競賽中獲勝的那一方是否擁有采取與其對手截然不同的政策的奢侈 — — 的不確定性要大得多。
but the next step in the argument that the winner of an increasingly ugly contest will have the luxury of pursuing significantly different policies from his opponent is much more uncertain.
新總統的任期將從2013年1月開始，與目前奧巴馬和羅姆尼競爭口號中所描述的情形相反，上臺者將會發現沒有多少空間可以用於調整經濟政策。
by the time the next presidential term starts in january 2013, and contrary to the current narratives advanced by the obama and romney campaigns, the incumbent will find himself with limited room for maneuver on economic policy.
事實上，美國的潛在分歧隨處可見，選民們對此並沒有充分的認識。
indeed, the potential differences for america are elsewhere, and have yet to be adequately understood by voters.
他們將注意力集中在伴隨著範圍甚廣的類似經濟政策的社會政策上；而在這方面，候選人之間的分歧將產生重大後果。
they center on the social policies that would accompany a broadly similar set of economic measures and, here, the differences between the candidates are consequential.
不管誰當選，都將在明年面臨經濟增長只有2%的局面，並伴隨著完全停滯的風險。
whoever wins will face an economy growing at a sluggish 2 or less next year, with a nagging risk of stalling completely.
失業率仍處於過高的水平，大約有一半的失業者是難以找到工作的長期失業者 — — 要是我們把退出勞動力市場的美國人也算上的話（理應如此）這個比例還會更高。
unemployment will still be far too high, and almost half of it will be hardtosolve, longterm joblessness and even more if we count as we should the millions of americans who have dropped out of the labor force.
經濟的財政面也值得擔憂。
the financial side of the economy will also be a source of concern.
財政赤字將繼續在10%GDP的水平上徘徊，令人對美國中期債務動態愈加擔心了。
the fiscal deficit will continue to flirt with the 10ofgdp level, adding to worries about the countrys mediumterm debt dynamics.
銀行部門仍在“去風險 ” ， 因此限制了流向中小企業、提振招聘和產房裝置投資所必須的信貸流。
the banking sector will still be derisking, limiting the flow of credit to small and mediumsize companies and undermining hiring and investment in plant and equipment.
而家庭部門痛苦的去槓桿化階段也只進行了一半。
and the household sector will be only partly through its painful deleveraging phase.
政策面也同樣令人不安。
the policy front will be equally unsettling.
在猶豫和扯皮了太久之後，美國國會將發現，不能在拖延應對這些挑戰的措施了。
having dithered and bickered for too long, the us congress will find it increasingly difficult to postpone action on these challenges.
與此同時，美聯儲翻唱的激進主義 — — 包括不斷延長的“摸石頭過河”措施清單 — — 收效將越來越少，而成本與風險將越來越大。
meanwhile, the federal reserves unusual activism, including an everexpanding list of experimental measures, will yield fewer benefits and entail growing costs and risks.
美國經濟執行的全球環境也越來越困難。
the us economy will also be operating in a more difficult global environment.
在未來幾個月中，歐洲債務危機極有可能會繼續惡化。
in the next few months, europes debt crisis will most likely worsen.
由於新興市場（包括中國）的減速，同時有意義的多邊政策協調始終不夠充分，主要貿易大國將競爭一塊不再變大的餅，因此保護主義壓力將會大增。
with emerging economies including china slowing, and with meaningful multilateral policy coordination remaining inadequate, protectionist pressures will mount as major trading powers compete for a stagnant pie.
因此，不管現任總統奧巴馬還是羅姆尼在11月勝出，新總統都將受到雙重壓力的約束 — — 一邊是急需穩定經濟，一邊是長期改革。
so, whether president barack obama or mitt romney prevails in november, the next president will be constrained by the twin need for urgent economic stabilization and longerterm reforms.
而在歐洲危機和世界各國同時放緩的壓力下，兩位候選人別無選擇，只能採取相似的經濟政策重建就業創造活力和金融穩定，至少在任期開始時是如此。
and, with headwinds from europe and a synchronized global slowdown, the candidates will have no choice but to pursue, at least initially, similar economic policies to restore dynamic job creation and financial stability.
在尋求短期經濟刺激和中期財政可持續性之間的平衡的過程中，最要緊的步驟是合理處置因暫時性減稅政策到期結束以及深度跨部門削減支出自動開始所導致的財政懸崖。
in striking the right balance between immediate economic stimulus and mediumterm fiscal sustainability, the most urgent step will be to counter properly the looming fiscal cliff, as temporary tax cuts expire and deep, acrosstheboard spending reductions kick in automatically.
在這方面失敗將大大增加美國陷入全面衰退的風險。
failure to do so would significantly increase the risk of an outright american recession.
深度中期預算改革是應對國會一再不作為所造成的問題之所必須。
serious mediumterm budget reforms are needed to deal with the legacy of repeated congressional failures.
此外，如能瞭解到真實的數字，下任總統很快就會認識到，正確的稅收和支出改革之路已經非常狹窄，遠非今天競爭性政治口號所描繪得那樣寬闊。
and, if provided with realistic numbers, the next president will soon recognize that the right mix of tax and spending reforms falls into a much narrower range than todays competing political narratives suggest.
這絕對不是一個要麼/要麼命題。
it is certainly not an eitheror proposition.
財政改革在充滿活力的經濟中才能取得最佳效果。
fiscal reforms work best in a dynamic economy.
在這方面，奧巴馬和羅姆尼必須排除萬難，實現增長和就業創造。
to this end, obama and romney will need to lift the impediments to growth and job creation.
與房地產、勞動力市場、信用中介和基礎設施等領域一樣，在這一領域，辦法並不像政客們希望我們所認為的那樣多。
here again in areas like housing, the labor market, credit intermediation, and infrastructure there is less room for maneuver than most politicians would like us to believe.
但這並不意味著一點改變都無法做出。
but this does not mean that there is no scope for differences.
改變的空間是有的，這反映出一個事實：總體經濟趨勢將伴隨多重水平不同速度的動態。
there is, and they reflect the fact that general economic tendencies will be accompanied by multispeed dynamics at many levels.
根據技能和教育程度的不同，失業率存在持久差異；收入和財富不平等性正在創出歷史記錄 — — 從分配效應看，任何經濟決策都將伴隨著社會調整的需要，這種需要可能是直接的，但更多情況下將是隱含的。
from persistent differences in unemployment rates depending on skills and education to recordhigh income and wealth inequalities, each economic decision will be accompanied by the need for social judgment whether explicit or, more likely, implicit regarding its distributional impact.
在經歷了過度槓桿化、債務創造和信貸氾濫、並在2008年全球金融危機爆發前達到頂峰的“時代”後，美國仍然面臨著一項艱鉅的挑戰 — — 如何分配持久抑制投資、就業和競爭力的累積損失。
after an age of excessive leverage, debt creation, and credit entitlement that culminated in the 2008 global financial crisis, america still faces the tricky challenge of allocating cumulative losses that continuously inhibit investment, jobs, and competitiveness.
到目前為止，國會的過度政治極端化已經產生了讓承受能力較弱者經受更多調整負擔的效果。
until now, congresss excessive political polarization has translated into an approach that has pushed more of the burden of adjustment onto those who are less able to bear it.
在理想世界中，美國新總統應快速實施兩步走計劃以重塑就業活力、重振金融穩定性。
in an ideal world, americas next president would rapidly embark on a twostep approach to restoring job dynamism and financial soundness.
首先，他應該設計可行而令人滿意的全面經濟政策計劃組合 — — 在這方面，做出重大不同的空間是有限的。
first, he would devise a comprehensive set of economicpolicy initiatives that are both feasible and desirable and, again, the scope for major differences here is limited.
其次，對於這些經濟政策，應輔之以明確的社會政策組合 — — 在這方面，潛在改變空間極大 — — 以滿足公平負擔共擔的需要。
second, he would accompany this with an explicit set of social policies and here the potential differences are profound that addresses the need for equitable burdensharing.
其實，此次選舉絕非選擇外包和增稅還是福利改革；選擇政府控制生產還是自由放任私人部門活動；選擇就業創造還是免費搭車等熱門���題。
this is not really an election about such hotlydebated issues as outsourcing, tax increases versus entitlement reforms, government control of production versus unfettered private sector activity, or job creators versus free riders.
此次選舉中茲事體大者在於它所伴隨的社會公平、福利、平等呢個性以及富庶文明社會行為準則等概念。
it is much more about the accompanying concepts of social fairness, entitlement, equality and, yes, standards of behavior for a rich and civilized society.
這是一場事關社會責任的選舉。 所謂社會責任，即社會支援因並非由其自身造成的錯誤而承受尋找工作、實現收支平衡壓力的群體的義務。
this is an election about social responsibility a societys obligation to support those who are struggling, through no fault of their own, to find jobs and make ends meet.
這場選舉事關透過讓他們獲得健康保險保護社會最脆弱群體。
it is about protecting the most vulnerable segments of society, including by providing them access to proper health coverage.
這場選舉事關改革讓美國年輕人落於人後的教育制度（以及向需要者提供合適的再培訓 ） 。
it is about reforming an education system that fails americas young people and about providing appropriate retraining to those who need it.
在諸多公平和公正問題中，讓富人回饋給他們帶來不可想象的財富的制度才是此次選舉的重點。
among the numerous issues of fairness and equality, it is about the rich giving back to a system that has brought them unimaginable wealth.
奧巴馬和羅姆尼的分歧之所以重要，原因就在這裡。
it is here where the differences between obama and romney are important.
競選活動越早以此為重心，美國人民就越有可能做出資訊更充分的選擇，從而採取必須的集體行動讓美國免蹈傾覆之轍。
the sooner the campaign debate pivots to this, the greater the probability that americans will make a more informed choice and, thus, buy into the collective effort needed to escape national malaise.
美國的裙帶資本主義
americas crony capitalism
布宜諾斯艾利斯－20年來，美國一直在公開抨擊第三世界國家，特別是亞洲國家的“裙帶資本主義 ” 。
buenos aires for 20 years, americans have denounced the crony capitalism of third world countries, especially in asia.
然而，就在這些受到美國抨擊的地區一直在改善其政府和公司治理的時候 — — 香港法院剛剛作出了一個對當地電信巨頭不利的具有突破性的判決，該電信巨頭是香港地區最富有和最有權勢的人的兒子 — — 裙帶資本主義卻在美國這樣一個長期以來被世界看作是公平商業競爭環境卓越典範的國家，生根發芽了。
but, just as those regions have been improving their public and corporate governance hong kong just witnessed a breakthrough court decision against a telecom tycoon who is the son of the provinces richest and most powerful man crony capitalism is taking root in the united states, a country that the world long considered the gold standard of a level playing field in business.
美國財政部最近完成的銀行 “壓力測試 ” ， 只是裙帶資本主義佔領華盛頓特區的一個最新標誌而已。
the recently completed stress tests of us banks are but the latest indication that crony capitalists have now captured washington, dc.
美國財政部長蒂莫西·蓋特納（Timothy Geithner）對美國大銀行進行了壓力測試，而在測試結果正式公佈的幾個星期之前，其大致結果就被洩露了，這就難怪股票市場會歡迎壓力測試的結果了。
it is no surprise that stock markets liked the results of the stress tests that us treasury secretary timothy geithner administered to americas big banks, for the general outcome had been leaked weeks before.
事實上，許多專業投資者即使因為持有股票而從股市的上漲中獲益，也仍然認為壓力測試是不誠實的。
indeed, most professional investors trashed the tests as dishonest even as their holdings benefited from a rising market.
就連通常是金融市場聲音最響亮的拉拉隊長的《華爾街日報 》 ， 也公開懷疑測試的誠實性，因為美國政府允許銀行家就壓力測試的結果進行“談判 ” ， 這就像是一個學生參加期末考試後和老師談判其成績一樣。
even the wall street journal, usually financial markets loudest cheerleader, openly disparaged the tests integrity. the government had allowed bankers to negotiate the results, like a student taking a final examination and then negotiating her grade.
壓力測試是用來反映大量持有房屋貸款和金融衍生產品的銀行未經審計的有害資產的真實情況的，因而，進行壓力測試背後的理由似乎是無懈可擊的。
the tests were supposed to reveal the true conditions of banks saddled with unaudited toxic assets in housing loans and financial derivatives. the reasoning behind the tests seemed unimpeachable.
但是，事實果真如此嗎？
but was it?
任何經驗豐富的銀行家都知道，管理良好的銀行應該將定期進行內部“壓力測試”作為良好的企業管理的一部分。
as any seasoned banker knows, a wellmanaged bank should undertake internal stress tests regularly as a matter of good housekeeping.
金融危機本來應該已經迫使銀行自己進行持續的壓力測試，以便銀行高層知道銀行的最新情況，然而事實卻並非如此。 那麼，為什麼美國需要政府來進行銀行家自己能夠進行並且應該做得更快更好的金融行為呢？
the financial crisis should have mandated a running stress test to keep senior management up to date daily. why, then, did the us need the government to conduct a financial exercise that bankers themselves could and should have done far better and faster?
這背後的真相是，美國進行壓力測試的目的不是為了找到問題的答案。
the truth is that the tests were not designed to find answers.
華爾街的巨頭們和奧巴馬政府都已經知道了問題的真相。
both wall streets chieftains and the obama administration already knew the truth.
他們知道，如果公開披露美國大銀行的真實情況，許多銀行就會立即被宣佈破產，而這會迫使政府的破產管理機構來阻止由此而引發的銀行擠兌浪潮。
they knew that if the true conditions at many big banks were publicly revealed, many would have been immediately declared bankrupt, necessitating government receivership to stop a tsunami of bank runs.
雖然像美聯儲前主席保羅·沃爾克（Paul Volcker）這樣的專家都推薦美國進行銀行國有化，但是，奧巴馬政府卻連非常短暫的國有化也不願意進行，因為它不想因為國有化銀行而被貼上“社會主義者”的標籤。
but the obama administration did not want to be tagged as socialist for nationalizing banks, however temporarily, even though experts such as former us federal reserve chairman paul volcker had recommended just that.
而且，如果美國進行銀行國有化，就一定會有一些華爾街巨頭及其同僚因為嚴重經營不善而遭到解僱。
moreover, nationalizing banks would have required dismissing wall street captains and their boards for grossly mismanaging their firms.
然而，華爾街的巨頭們已經讓奧巴馬及其政府成員相信，他們持續工作對世界經濟擺脫當前的危機至關重要。
wall streets titans, however, had convinced obama and his team that their continued stewardship was essential to getting the world out of its crisis.
而且，他們還成功地將自己描繪成經濟危機的受害者，而不是引發經濟危機的幫兇。
they successfully portrayed themselves as victims of a firestorm, rather than as accessories to arson.
蓋特納和奧巴馬的首席經濟顧問拉里·薩默斯（Larry Summers ） ， 是曾任美國財政部長、後來擔任花旗集團董事會主席和高階顧問的羅伯特·魯賓（Robert Rubin）的門徒，他們認同華爾街的文化，因而都不覺得接受華爾街銀行家荒謬的邏輯是很困難的。
geithner and larry summers, obamas chief economic advisor, share wall streets culture as protgs of robert rubin, the former treasury secretary who went on to serve as a director and senior counselor at citigroup. neither man found it difficult to accept the bankers absurd logic.
壓力測試本來是要告訴公眾，銀行沒有迫在眉睫的破產威脅。
the stress tests were meant to signal to the public that there was no immediate threat of bank failures.
政府希望，這樣的資訊可以穩定市場，以便“有毒”資產的價格可以上漲到銀行家在賣掉它們時可以感覺不太為難的水平。
this message, it was hoped, would stabilize the market so that prices for toxic assets could rise to a level at which bankers might feel comfortable selling them.
畢竟，高階銀行家曾經聲稱這些銀行資產的“價格定錯了 ” ， 將它們按市場水平定價會使銀行遭受了不必要地懲罰。
after all, senior bankers had been claiming that these assets were mispriced, and that pricing them at market levels would penalize the banks unnecessarily.
目前看來，蓋特納的“壓力測試”似乎成功了，因為事實上，股票市場不只是穩定下來而已，像花旗集團和美國銀行這樣的銀行股票的價格，還從最低點上漲了四倍。
so far, geithner seems to have succeeded in his tests, as the stock market has indeed more than stabilized, with prices of bank shares such as citigroup and bank of america quadrupling from their lows.
以前人們所擔憂的華爾街的破產，現��似乎已經避免了。
the feared implosion of wall street seems to have been avoided.
但是，從來沒有人真正地認為美國會讓花旗集團和美國銀行 — — 在此，我僅列舉兩家銀行 — — 破產。
but no one ever seriously thought that the us would allow citigroup and bank of america, to name just two, to fail.
事實上，股票市場在去年冬天就已經見底了。
in fact, the stock market bottomed out last winter.
市場已經將人們對美國政府不會讓更多的銀行破產的看法，反應到股票的價格中去了。
markets had factored into share prices the belief that the us government would not allow any more banks to collapse.
世界想要的東西，是有關銀行價值的準確資料和根據銀行還需要多少注資所確定的引導投資者的“市價”估值。
what the world wanted was an accurate picture of what the banks were worth and marktomarket valuations to guide investors as to how much new capital they needed.
世界也希望看到，美國能夠重新回到增強商業道德和誠實信用的道路上來 — — 上一屆的美國政府非常缺乏這兩樣東西。
the world also wanted to see the us retaking the high road in reinforcing business ethics and integrity so lacking under the last administration.
因為納稅人已經為挽救瀕臨破產的銀行投入了鉅額資金，並且可能還要投入更多的資金，所以，有一個表明這些錢是怎樣使用的透明的程式，勢在必行。
as taxpayers had already put huge sums into rescuing failing banks, with the prospect of more to come, a transparent process to reveal how the money was being used was imperative.
據報道，美國有大量的公共援救資金，不是為了保護公共利益的目的而被轉移到了外國銀行、高盛手中或者被當作金融機構員工的獎金。
substantial public rescue funds have reportedly been siphoned off to foreign banks, goldman sachs, and staff bonuses for purposes unrelated to protecting public interests.
蓋特納的壓力測試沒有披露或拆穿這些情況。
none of this was either revealed or debunked by geithners tests.
相反，美國政府的工作人員現在卻似乎在和華爾街沆瀣一氣，營造出一個虛假的盈利氛圍。
instead, public servants now appear to be in cahoots with wall street to engineer an artificial aura of profitability.
而且，美國對有毒資產的價值和以前一樣諱莫如深。
moreover, the value of toxic assets remains as murky as ever.
為了讓銀行基本上能夠隨心所欲的進行報告，在華爾街的要求下，美國政府將神聖的會計準則都進行了修改。
once sacrosanct accounting principles have been amended at wall streets behest in order to allow banks to report essentially whatever they want.
現在，美國公佈了由美國政府和銀行進行談判形成的壓力測試結果，想以此 “證明”美國的銀行比人們想象的要健康得多。
and now negotiated stress test results have been released to prove that the banks are a lot healthier.
雖然將這種行為稱為旁氏騙局可能太尖刻了，但是它們卻有相似的地方。
calling this a ponzi scheme might be too harsh.
這種騙局愚弄不了大多數的金融專業人士。
but few financial professionals have been fooled.
同時，華爾街巨頭及其董事們對美國政府已經沒什麼好擔心的了，相反，他們現在在完成這個不誠實的計劃的共同冒險中，成為了美國政府的合作伙伴。
meanwhile, wall street chieftains and their boards of directors have nothing to fear from government. on the contrary, they are now the governments partners in a joint venture to manage this dishonest scheme.
像豬流感那樣，裙帶資本主義已經從腐敗的第三世界國家轉移到了曾經是可靠的政府和公司治理根據地的美國。
like swine flu, crony capitalism has migrated from corrupt third world countries to america, once the citadel of sound public and private governance.
所以，對中國被認為是發展中國家越來越可靠的典範，而美國現在被認為是偽善和雙重標誌的象徵，我們有什麼好奇怪的呢?
is it any wonder that china is perceived as an increasingly credible model for much of the developing world, while the us is now viewed as a symbol of hypocrisy and double standards?
引火燒身的美國債務限額之辯
americas dangerous debt ceiling debate
發自紐波特灘 — — 美國政府的債務限額在過去50年內已經上調了超過70次，一般都沒有什麼異議。
newport beach it has been raised more than 70 times in the last 50 years, mostly without commotion.
而當今美國政府如果還想繼續按時還債的話，就必須在今年夏天再次上調這一限額。
it must be raised again this summer if the united states government is to continue paying its bills on time.
於是該額度就成為了政治家們私下頻繁政治表態和緊急談判的議題，而其最終結果顯然也將對美國以外的世界各地造成廣泛影響。
but now americas debt ceiling has become the subject of intense political posturing and touchandgo negotiations behind closed doors. and, obviously, the outcome has implications that go well beyond the us.
作為美國製衡政治體制的組成部分，國會不僅扮演著審批聯邦預算的角色，還負責制定美國財政部的債務限額。
as part of americas system of checks and balances, congress gets to do more than just approve the annual federal budget. it also sets a limit on how much debt the us treasury is allowed to issue.
一旦超出該限額，政府就只好從當年財政收入中掏錢支出了。
beyond this ceiling, the government can spend only from current revenues.
美國財政部長蓋特納最近就政府將在8月2日左右觸及債務限額一事向國會作了彙報。
us treasury secretary timothy geithner recently informed members of congress that the government will be in this situation on or around august 2.
在借債總額已經到達上限的情況下，財政部當前正在東挪西湊地動用各種閒置資金還債。
having already officially hit the ceiling, the treasury is moving money around and tapping various pots of unused funds to pay its bills.
而再過幾個星期，這些“流動性”也將告罄。
in a few weeks, this flexibility will be used up.
考慮到美國政府當前每1美元的支出中就有40美分債務的處境，一個真正具有約束力的債務限額將迫使其不顧一切地大幅削減支出。
with the us government now borrowing around 40 of every dollar it spends, a truly binding debt ceiling would immediately force the government to reduce spending radically and in a disorderly fashion.
各黨政治家們都知道這一狀況將動搖早已脆弱不堪的美國經濟，嚴重削弱美元，並引發包括美國未來仍需仰仗的國外債權人在內的市場各方對美國還債能力的高度懷疑。
politicians across the political spectrum know that such a situation would unsettle an already fragile us economy, severely weaken the dollar, and raise serious concerns about the country's ability to meet its debtservice obligations, including to the many foreign creditors that the us will need in the future.
但在華盛頓當前極端對立的政治環境下，共和黨和民主黨彼此都不願妥協 — — 或者認為現在妥協還為時尚早。
yet, in todays polarized environment in washington, republicans and democrats are unwilling to compromise or at least to compromise too early.
共和黨人想利用僵持來迫使奧巴馬當局大規模消減開支。
by holding out, republicans wish to force president barack obamas administration into massive spending cuts.
民主黨則辯稱這個不考慮其他因素的單一手段不但會損害經濟，還會造成社會不公。
democrats respond that such a onesided approach would be economically harmful and socially unjust.
與此同時，雙方都冒著擾亂轉移支付（包括老人補助）和公共服務供給的風險，甚至進一步威脅到美國的全球信用。
in the meantime, both sides risk disrupting transfer payments including to the elderly and the provision of public services, as well as eroding further americas global credit standing.
目前主流（也合理）的期望是，兩黨能在國內經濟和金融嚴重扭曲前不計前嫌，調高債務限額。
the overwhelming and sensible expectation is that the two parties will compromise and raise the debt ceiling before inflicting serious economic and financial dislocations.
而最近的範例就是在今年早些時候的本年度財政預算案，當時這一預算案一直未能得到國會批准，進而威脅到政府的正常執行，最後終於在妥協中過關。
the most recent precedent was the bipartisan agreement reached earlier this year on another fiscal issue that threatened to disrupt the normal functioning of government the absence of a formally approved budget for this year.
彼此妥協則雙方都能各得其所，既能讓政府承諾減少支出，又能採取一系列步驟來使稅收具有更多的社會正義性。
a compromise would allow both parties to declare partial victory, for it would likely entail commitments to cut spending and some steps to make taxation more socially just.
但正如眾多最後一刻達成的協議一樣，這個協議也缺乏長期效力。
but, like many lastminute agreements, it would have little durable impact.
事實上，美國的政治系統很快又會故伎重演，對協議敷衍塞責，而人們所期望的財政改革只有在2012年總統大選之後才能取得實質性進展。
in effect, the political system would again be kicking the can down the road, with real progress on necessary fiscal reforms expected only after the november 2012 presidential election.
兩黨暫時取得妥協的時間點將取決於是一步到位還是分兩步走，因此可能出現兩種情況：大多數人認為在8月2日之前兩黨會選擇直接達成妥協協議。
two scenarios for the timing of an interim compromise are possible, depending on whether it is a one or twostep process. most observers expect a onestep process for bipartisan agreement before august 2.
此外就是政治家們需要分兩步走：首先是協議失敗，��後在引發金融市場動盪後迅速妥協。
but politicians may need two steps an initial failure to agree, and then a quick deal in response to the resulting financialmarket convulsions.
同時財政部會暫時重新安排還款優先次序並延緩付款。
in the meantime, the treasury would temporarily reprioritize and slow outgoing payments.
這個兩步走的過程與2008年的情況有點相似，當時國會面對的是另一種危險狀況：布什政府要求動用700億美元來防止金融市場崩潰和經濟衰退。
this twostep process would be similar to what happened in 2008, when congress was confronted with another cliffhanger the bush administrations request for 700 billion to prevent a financialmarket collapse and an economic depression.
國會一開始拒絕了這一要求，但股市急挫770點使得政治家無暇旁顧，隨後將這一提案重新提上議程並最終透過。
congress initially rejected the measure, but a dramatic 770point drop in the stock market focused politicians minds, bringing them back to the table and to agreement.
但這個方案會為美國經濟及其全球地位埋下眾多慢性風險，而美國政治家解決債務限額問題所耗費的時間越長，則發生意外事故的風險越大。
but the twostep scenario involves incremental risks to the us economy, and to its standing in the global system. and the longer americas politicians take to resolve the debtceiling issue, the greater the risk of an inadvertent accident.
這樣一來就可能引發更為令人擔憂的第三種情況：談判曠日持久，遙遙無期，給政府的財政支付，履行其他合同義務以及公共服務造成更大的紊亂。
this brings us to a third, and even more unsettling possibility a longer and more protracted negotiation, resulting in greater disruptions to government entitlement payments, other contractual obligations, and public services.
而那些已經大量持有美國債券的債權人則會在繼續購買時表達更嚴重的憂慮，從而使已經面臨失業危機和不穩定增長的美國經濟遭遇更多阻力。
creditors would then ask many more questions before adding to their alreadyconsiderable holdings of us government debt, generating still more headwinds in a us economy that already faces an unemployment crisis and uneven growth.
未來5個星期的政治舞臺必有眾多好戲上演。
the next few weeks will provide plenty of political drama.
而我們的最基本期望是民主黨和共和黨能在風險之下想辦法避免給脆弱的美國經濟製造紊亂，只是這一妥協並不能帶來有實質意義的中期財政改革。
the baseline expectation, albeit subject to risk, is that democrats and republicans will find a way to avoid disruptions that would damage the fragile us economy, but that the compromise will not meaningfully address the need for sensible mediumterm fiscal reforms.
對美國的私人企業以及依賴美國在全球經濟中扮演核心角色的國家來說，美國政治體制在面臨如此關鍵的經濟問題時所發生的癱瘓更加令他們感到不安。
such political paralysis on key economic issues is increasingly unsettling for the us private sector, and for other countries that rely on a strong us at the core of the global economy.
這就解釋了為什麼這麼多企業願意繼續持有現金而不進行國內投資，也解釋了為什麼越來越多的國家想方設法逐步實施多元化策略，不再將美元作為單一儲備貨幣，也不願藉助美國金融市場來管理他們辛苦積蓄的血汗錢。
this helps to explain why so many companies continue to hoard cash, rather than investing domestically, and why a growing number of countries want to diversify gradually away from dependence on the dollar as the reserve currency and on us financial markets for intermediation of their hardearned savings.
全球經濟與一個強勢美國的假設緊密相連，而美國人也從中大獲其利。
the world economy is hardwired to the assumption of a strong america, and americans benefit from this.
但美國政治家在債務限額問題上的爭論越激烈，這一關聯就越有可能發生無法挽回的斷裂。
but the more their politicians argue over the debt ceiling, the greater the risk that the wiring will become irreparably frayed.
不斷惡化的美國道德危機
americas deepening moral crisis
發自紐約 — — 美國的政治和經濟危機必將在11月國會中期選舉之後進一步惡化。
new york americas political and economic crisis is set to worsen following the upcoming november elections.
而一直致力於推動扶助貧困階層和環保立法的奧巴馬也將失去最後一絲希望。
president barack obama will lose any hope for passing progressive legislation aimed at helping the poor or the environment.
事實上，所有重要的立法和改革都將停滯不前，直到2013年的新一輪總統大選之後才有轉機。
indeed, all major legislation and reforms are likely to be stalemated until 2013, following a new presidential election.
而這個充斥著僵局和刻薄攻擊的可悲狀況很可能會愈演愈烈，因此世界也不必指望這個內部急劇分化的美國能表現出多少全球領導力。
an already bad situation marked by deadlock and vitriol is likely to worsen, and the world should not expect much leadership from a bitterly divided united states.
大部分美國人如今都懷著一種醜陋的心態，而同情和憐憫之心則被拋到了九霄雲外。
much of america is in a nasty mood, and the language of compassion has more or less been abandoned.
兩大黨雖然都自稱捍衛中產階級利益，但其實只為那些富有的選舉捐款人服務。
both political parties serve their rich campaign contributors, while proclaiming that they defend the middle class.
官方統計說美國有15%的貧困人口，但如果我們把那些在醫療，住房，就業等方面苦苦掙扎的家庭計算在內的話，實際的數目會更加龐大，但民主共和兩黨卻對此絕口不提。
neither party even mentions the poor, who now officially make up 15 of the population but in fact are even more numerous, when we count all those households struggling with health care, housing, jobs, and other needs.
共和黨最近釋出了一份名為《向美國宣誓：新共和黨議程》的宣言來闡述自己的信念和選舉承諾。
the republican party recently issued a pledge to america to explain its beliefs and campaign promises.
但宣言中卻充斥著類似“高稅率和過度監管導致了美國高失業率”這樣的荒唐言論，堪稱一派胡言。
the document is filled with nonsense, such as the fatuous claim that high taxes and overregulation explain americas high unemployment.
此外宣言還蓄意誤導公眾，比如引用美國前總統約翰·F·肯尼迪關於“高稅率會令經濟窒息”的語錄，卻不知道這番話發表於半個世紀之前，而當時的最高邊際稅率是如今的兩倍。
it is also filled with propaganda. a quotation by president john f. kennedy states that high tax rates can strangle the economy, but kennedys was speaking a halfcentury ago, when the top marginal tax rates were twice what they are today.
最糟糕的是，共和黨陣營根本就毫無同情心可言。
most of all, the republican platform is devoid of compassion.
而美國之所以發生這種富裕國家內部解體現象，就是因為其核心價值已經崩潰。
america today presents the paradox of a rich country falling apart because of the collapse of its core values.
美國的生產力居世界前列。
american productivity is among the highest in the world.
人均國民收入高達4.6萬美元 — — 不僅能保證溫飽，還足以令民眾過上富足的生活。
average national income per person is about 46,000 enough not only to live on, but to prosper.
但整個國家卻被一場嚴重的道德危機所荼毒。
yet the country is in the throes of an ugly moral crisis.
收入不均程度已經達到了歷史最高點，但富人們卻宣稱自己不需要對其他國民負責。
income inequality is at historic highs, but the rich claim that they have no responsibility to the rest of society.
他們不願扶助貧困階層，而且儘可能地為減稅政策辯護。
they refuse to come to the aid of the destitute, and defend tax cuts at every opportunity.
所有人都在抱怨，所有人在維護自己那些狹隘的短期利益，所有人都將社會長遠利益和推己及人的理念拋諸腦後。
almost everybody complains, almost everybody aggressively defends their own narrow and shortterm interests, and almost everybody abandons any pretense of looking ahead or addressing the needs of others.
在美國當前的政治辯論中，最流行的做法莫過於兩黨爭相向中產階級做出更大的政治承諾，而且主要集中在削減政府預算和減稅上，但與此同時美國的財政赤字卻已經超過了GDP的10 % 。
what passes for american political debate is a contest between the parties to give bigger promises to the middle class, mainly in the form of budgetbusting tax cuts at a time when the fiscal deficit is already more than 10 of gdp.
美國人似乎相信他們本來就該免費享用政府服務而無需繳稅。
americans seem to believe that they have a natural right to government services without paying taxes.
在美國的政治詞彙中 ， “ 稅”就意味著“限制自由 ” 。
in the american political lexicon, taxes are defined as a denial of liberty.
但就在不久之前的一個時期，美國人其實非常熱衷於在國內外談論消除貧困問題。
there was a time, not long ago, when americans talked of ending poverty at home and abroad.
1960年代中期林登·約翰遜的“向貧困宣戰”運動就反映了當時的風貌，全國上下都瀰漫著樂觀情緒，相信整個社會必須聯合行動來解決貧困，汙染和醫療衛生這類宏觀問題，還執行了一系列貧民區重建，改善空氣和水汙染以及老年人醫療保障的專案。
lyndon johnsons war on poverty in the mid1960s reflected an era of national optimism and the belief that society should make collective efforts to solve common problems, such as poverty, pollution, and health care. america in the 1960s enacted programs to rebuild poor communities, to fight air and water pollution, and to ensure health care for the elderly.
但隨後全社會在越戰和民權議題上爆發分歧，加上消費主義和廣告的入侵，似乎最終令這個為公共福利共同付出的時代走向了終結。
then the deep divisions over vietnam and civil rights, combined with a surge of consumerism and advertising, seemed to end an era of shared sacrifice for the common good.
其後40年間，我們的政治同情心不斷消退。
for 40 years, compassion in politics receded.
羅納德·里根透過減少貧困階層的社會福利（他宣稱窮人經常用欺騙的手段獲取額外福利）並贏得了支援。
ronald reagan gained popularity by cutting social benefits for the poor claiming that the poor cheated to receive extra payments.
而比爾·克林頓則在1990年代故伎重施。
bill clinton continued those cuts in the 1990s.
時至今日，甚至沒有政治家敢於提起任何扶貧政策了。
today, no politician even dares to mention help for poor people.
那些財大氣粗的選舉捐款人花錢的目的就是為了確保他們的既得利益能主導整個政治辯論的方向。
the big campaign contributors to both parties pay to ensure that their vested interests dominate political debates.
這意味著兩大黨都不斷為富人的利益辯護，只不過共和黨的作為比民主黨稍稍多一點而已。
that means that both parties increasingly defend the interests of the rich, though republicans do so slightly more than democrats.
即便是某個針對富人的溫和加稅政策在美國也是無人問津的。
even a modest tax increase on the rich is unlikely to find support in american politics.
所有這一切的最終結果就是美國實力和繁榮的長期衰退，因為美國人再也不集體投資於他們的共同未來了。
the result of all of this is likely to be a longterm decline of us power and prosperity, because americans no longer invest collectively in their common future.
美國在一段長時期內依然會是一個富裕的國家，但同時也會逐漸走向分化和動盪。
america will remain a rich society for a long time to come, but one that is increasingly divided and unstable.
恐懼和誤導性宣傳將導致美國發起更多國際戰爭，正如過去十年那樣。
fear and propaganda may lead to more usled international wars, as in the past decade.
而發生在美國的一切也會在世界其他地方重演。
and what is happening in america is likely to be repeated elsewhere.
社會的高度分化導致美國極其容易發生社會崩潰。
america is vulnerable to social breakdown because it is a highly diverse society.
而種族主義和反移民思潮其實就是對貧困人口的攻擊的重要部分，或者至少是人們願意聽信那些反對扶助貧困階層的政治宣傳的原因。
racism and antiimmigrant sentiments are an important part of the attack on the poor, or at least the reason why so many are willing to heed the propaganda against helping the poor.
隨著其他各國社會內部分化的惡化，他們最終也會步美國後塵。
as other societies grapple with their own increasing diversity, they may follow the us into crisis.
瑞典選民最近給一個右翼反移民政黨投下了足夠多的選票，足以讓其在議會擁有一席之地，這反映出瑞典人對外國移民越來越強烈的抵制心理。
swedes recently gave enough votes to a rightwing, antiimmigrant party to give it representation in parliament, reflecting a growing backlash against the rising number of immigrants in swedish society.
在法國，薩科齊政府嘗試透過將吉普賽移民驅逐出境的方式來贏得工薪階層支援，而這些人在法國早已成為種族仇恨和攻擊的眾矢之的。
in france, nicolas sarkozys government has tried to regain popularity with the working class by deporting roma migrants, a target of widespread hatred and ethnic attacks.
這兩個例子都顯示出隨著我們的社會在種族上越來越多元化，歐洲也無法克服隨之誘發的政治分裂現象，正如美國一樣。
both examples show that europe, like the us, is vulnerable to the politics of division, as our societies become more ethnically diverse.
美國的教訓就是經濟發展並不能確保人民幸福和政治穩定。
the lesson from america is that economic growth is no guarantee of wellbeing or political stability.
美國的社會形勢正不斷惡化，富人們用錢來換取政治權力，而窮人則自生自滅。
american society has become increasingly harsh, where the richest americans buy their way to political power, and the poor are abandoned to their fate.
在私人生活中，美國人已經深陷於消費主義無法自拔，而消費主義則反過來吞噬了美國人的時間、金錢、精力，以及致力於集體福祉的傾向。
in their private lives, americans have become addicted to consumerism, which drains their time, savings, attention, and inclination to engage in acts of collective compassion.
全世界都必須引以為戒。
the world should beware.
除非我們能擺脫這種權錢交易和病態消費主義的怪圈，否則的話，每增加一點生產力，我們就會多丟失一點人性。
unless we break the ugly trends of big money in politics and rampant consumerism, we risk winning economic productivity at the price of our humanity.
美國的經濟僵局
americas economic stalemate
坎布里奇 — — 美國似乎陷入了危險的經濟停滯陷阱。 共和黨和民主黨均拒絕在預算問題上讓步，這讓美國政府無法處理大規模財政赤字和快速上升的國民債務問題。
cambridge the united states appears trapped in a dangerous economic stalemate. the refusal by both republicans and democrats to give ground on the budget is preventing the government from dealing with its massive fiscal deficit and rapidly rising national debt.
事實上，國會預算辦公室估計，國民債務將在未來十年內上升至GDP的82 % ， 即2008年水平的兩倍。
indeed, the congressional budget office projects that the national debt could increase to 82 of gdp over the next ten years more than double the debt ratio as recently as 2008.
此外，這一估計是建立在十分樂觀的經濟增長和低利率假設上的。
that forecast, moreover, is based on quite optimistic assumptions of strong economic growth and low interest rates.
如果增長率沒有那麼高，名義利率沒有那麼低，則債務比率將在2021年突破100 % ， 在2030年超過150 % 。
with slower growth and more normal interest rates, the debt ratio could easily rise to more than 100 in 2021, and exceed 150 by 2030.
政府債務上升越來越快的一個主要原因是美國人口在迅速老齡化，這導致全民退休金和醫保專案 — — 社會福利和醫療保險（Social Security and Medicare ） — —成本節節攀升。
a major reason for the accelerating growth in government debt is americas rapidly aging population and the resulting increase in the cost of the universal pension and healthcare programs social security and medicare.
大多數專家認為，欲限制債務增長，就必須降低這些“福利”專案佔GDP的比重，同時提高稅收佔GDP的比重。
most experts believe that limiting the rise in debt will require slowing the growth of these entitlement programs and increasing taxes as a share of gdp.
但奧巴馬總統和國會中的民主黨反對任何福利專案削減計劃，而共和黨總統候選人及其國會代表反對任何稅收增加計劃。
but president barack obama and the congressional democrats oppose any reduction in future entitlement programs, while the republican presidential candidates and their partys congressional delegation oppose any increase in tax revenues.
結果就是當前的僵局 — — 無法削減財政赤字，也無法扭轉國民債務的上升趨勢。
the result is the current stalemate in reducing the fiscal deficit and reversing the growth of the national debt.
共和黨指出，國民債務增長只能透過削減政府支出來限制。
republicans argue that the national debts growth should be limited only by cutting government spending.
儘管一些傳統開支的削減原本就是支出控制的一部分，但這一辦法需要輔之以削減“稅收支出 ” — —即稅法中補貼醫保、按揭貸款和地方政府稅收之類的部分。
although some cuts in traditional outlays should be part of efforts to rein in spending, this approach should be supplemented by reducing tax expenditures the special features of the tax code that subsidize health care, mortgage borrowing, localgovernment taxes, etc..
限制稅收支出可以削減相當於2%GDP的年度赤字，從而在2021年將債務-GDP比率拉低25個百分點以上。
limiting tax expenditures could reduce the annual deficit by as much as 2 of gdp, thereby reducing the debttogdp ratio in 2021 by more than 25 percentage points.
共和黨普遍拒絕這種形式的支出削減，因為這會導致稅收增加。
republicans generally reject this form of spending reduction, because it results in additional tax revenue.
該方法確實會讓總稅收收入增加，但限制稅收支出的經濟效應與透過其他方法減少這些專案的支出是完全一樣的。
while this method does indeed increase total revenue, the economic effect of limiting tax expenditures is the same as it is under any other method of cutting spending on those programs.
但共和黨反對任何令稅收收入增加的辦法，這意味著這一打破預算僵局的關鍵永遠不會得到實施。
but the republicans opposition to anything that raises revenue means that this key to breaking the budget stalemate wont be implemented.
社會福利的預算成本可以透過用基於投資的個人退休金賬戶所產生的年金替代部分目前靠稅收支付的福利專案來實現逐步削減。
the budget cost of social security pensions could be gradually reduced by substituting annuities generated by investmentbased personal retirement accounts for part of the current taxfinanced benefits.
但即使這樣的改革可以維持退休者的收入水平，民主黨也會反對，因為這會讓傳統政府福利減少。
but even though such a reform could maintain income levels for retirees, democrats oppose it, because it lowers traditional government benefits.
於是，僵局會因此加深。
this reinforces the stalemate.
兩黨立場均十分強硬，這將影響到2012年的國會和總統選舉。
the two parties hardline stances anticipate the upcoming congressional and presidential elections in november 2012.
事實上，共和黨向選民打出的口號將是“我們不會對你們增稅，但民主黨會。
the republicans, in effect, face the voters with a sign that says, we wont raise your taxes, but the democrats will.
”而民主黨將針鋒相對，樹立“我們不會削減退休金和醫保福利，但共和黨會”的大旗。
the democrats sign, by contrast, says, we wont reduce your pension or health benefits, but the republicans will.
雙方在大選前都將保持鮮明的立場，因此，馬上實現稅收支出和未來社保退休金變化是不可能的。
neither side wants any ambiguity in their message before the election, thus ruling out the possibility of any immediate changes in tax expenditures or future social security pensions.
但是，出於同樣的理由，我對僵局將在大選後不復存在十分樂觀。
but, for the same reason, i am optimistic that the stalemate will end after the election.
那時候，不論是共和黨還是民主黨，都可以接受當前必須拒絕的改革。
at that point, both republicans and democrats will be able to accept reforms that they must reject now.
另一條在選舉後赤字削減的辦法是降低邊際稅率，同時用削減稅收支出來彌補收入的減少。
another postelection route to deficit reduction would be to lower marginal tax rates and balance that revenue loss with cuts in tax expenditures.
官方分析低估了降低邊際稅率對可徵稅收入的影響，但經驗表明，邊際稅率降低會讓納稅人工作更賣命、更多地以可徵稅現金而不是以額外津貼的形式獲得報酬，並減少退稅消費，從而使可徵稅收入水平大幅提高。
official analyses downplay the effect of lower marginal tax rates on taxable income, but experience shows that taxable income rises substantially as taxpayers respond to lower marginal rates by working more, taking more of their compensation in taxable cash than in fringe benefits, and reducing their taxdeductible consumption.
削減稅收支出和降低邊際稅率雙管齊下可以透過增加可納稅收入水平大大增加稅收收入。
reducing tax expenditures while lowering marginal tax rates can produce substantial revenue by increasing the level of taxable income.
當前的經濟僵局十分危險，因為金融市場可能對此產生負面反應，且推遲解決財政赤字問題意味著國民債務會繼續攀升。
the current economic stalemate is troubling, because financial markets could react adversely, and because delays in addressing the fiscal deficit means a higher national debt.
我也許有些過於樂觀了，但我認為有很好的理由相信當前的預算僵局���粹是為了給選舉造勢，一旦選舉結果塵埃落定，美國政治體系將在財政整合問題上顯示出高效率。
i may be too optimistic, but i think there is good reason to believe that the current budget stalemate reflects election posturing, and that the us political system will prove more effective at making progress on fiscal consolidation once the election is past.
美國大選和全球經濟
americas election and the global economy
斯坦福—美國大選臨近，總統奧巴馬以微弱優勢領先於共和黨挑戰者、馬薩諸塞州州長羅姆尼，民意專家則仍然認為美國總統和參議員選舉還遠未分出勝負，眾議院則極有可能仍保持在共和黨手裡。
stanford as americas elections approach, with president barack obama slightly in front of his republican challenger, former massachusetts governor mitt romney, pollsters still rate the races for control of the presidency and the united states senate too close to call, with the house of representatives likely to remain in republican hands.
候選人之間的差異是顯而易見的，對美國經濟政策和全球經濟的影響是重大的，儘管總統經濟政策的實施還要看眾議院的臉色。
the differences between the candidates are considerable, and highly consequential for american economic policy and the global economy, although enactment of their programs will depend on the makeup of congress.
兩大總統候選人的主要差別可以總結如下：
the most important differences between the two candidates can be summarized as follows
指出。
spending.
奧巴馬大舉增加了支出。
obama has dramatically increased spending.
他可能會繼續實施臨時性措施（正如米爾頓·弗裡德曼曾經觀察到的 ， “ 沒有什麼比政府臨時政策更持久的了。 ” ） ；增加一倍投入讓政府來決定綠色能源領域的贏家和輸家；擴大教育和基礎設施支出；以及大規模削減防務支出。
he would likely continue many of his temporary programs as milton friedman once observed, there is nothing so permanent as a temporary government program. double down on having government pick winners and losers in green energy expand spending on education and infrastructure and substantially reduce defense expenditures.
相反，羅姆尼支援限制聯邦總支出，將其規模從目前佔GDP的24%縮減至20 % ， 並將赤字維持在GDP的4%的水平。
romney, by contrast, favors limiting overall federal spending, currently 24 of gdp, to 20, and keeping defense at 4.
他希望讓私人市場而不是政府來選擇企業和技術贏家。
he wants private markets, not government, to choose winning firms and technologies.
民主黨反對大多數非防務支出削減，他們指出，削減支出將導致經濟衰退。
democrats oppose most nondefense spending cuts, arguing that reductions would cause the economy to contract.
當支出削減突然性地發生在疲軟經濟時，這種效應最為強烈。
that case is strongest if the spending reductions are large and abrupt in a weak economy.
如果在多年的經濟復甦過程中實現（如羅姆尼所規劃的 ） ， 那麼節流可能會收到擴張性的效果。
if phased in over a multiyear period as the economy recovers, as romney proposes, thrift would likely be expansionary.
比如，美國聯邦支出佔GDP的比重在20世紀80年代中期至90年代末之間下降了5個百分點，在最近幾十年的加拿大，支出-GDP比下降得更多 — — 都是在經濟強勁增長期間發生的。
for example, federal spending relative to gdp fell by five percentage points from the mid1980s to the late 1990s in the us, and by an even larger margin in recent decades in canada that is, through periods of strong economic growth.
稅收。
taxes.
奧巴馬將提高工資、資本利得、分紅、利息和房地產的最高邊際稅率，特別是對高收入個人和小企業。
obama would raise the top marginal tax rates on wages, capital gains, dividends, interest, and estates, especially on higherincome individuals and small businesses.
但不論是在個人還是在公司所得稅方面，他都沒有提出全面的改革計劃。
yet he has never proposed comprehensive reform of either the personal or corporate income tax.
相反，羅姆尼將把美國公司稅率（為經合組織國家的最高水平）降至25 % ， 並將對美國跨國公司的稅基從全世界改為地方，以增加稅收競爭力。
by contrast, romney would reduce americas corporate tax rate the highest in the oecd to 25 and tax american multinationals on a territorial, rather than a worldwide, basis in order to increase their tax competitiveness. he would also lower personal tax rates by 20, and make up lost revenue by limiting tax deductions and credits, particularly at the upper end, thereby raising about 18.5 of gdp, just above the historical average, at full employment.
他還將把個人稅率降低20 % ， 並透過限制稅收減免（特別是高階人群的稅收減免，該措施可以籌集相當於充分就業水平GDP的18.5%的稅收，略高於歷史平均水平）衝抵收入的下降。
romneys fiscal plan thus reduces deficits sufficiently to decrease the debttogdp ratio. he favors a balancedbudget amendment to the constitution, and hopes to balance the budget over eight years.
相反，奧巴馬將擴大赤字 — — 他的增支計劃遠比增稅計劃龐大 — — 這意味著未來會發生大規模增稅。
obama, by contrast, would run larger deficits his spending increase is much larger than his tax increase which imply large tax hikes in the future.
此外，奧巴馬的稅收比率將遠高於羅姆尼，因為債務的最大原因的福利支出。
moreover, he would run far larger debt ratios than romney, because the main driver of the debt is entitlement spending.
福利。
entitlements.
奧巴馬在醫療保險和社會保障方面的改革一直緘口不言，這些計劃的長期赤字是國民債務的數倍。
obama has remained silent about reform of medicare and social security, whose longrun deficits are several times the national debt.
副總統拜登甚至說社會保障計劃“不會有變化 ” 。
vice president joe biden has even said that no changes to social security are to be made.
羅姆尼支援逐漸提高退休年林、以保險金支援的醫療保險模式、以及將醫療補助（面向窮人的醫保）透過取消補助移交給各州。
romney supports gradually increasing retirement ages, a premiumsupport model for medicare, and shifting medicaid health insurance for the poor to the states via block grants.
奧巴馬的競選方針是攻擊羅姆尼的醫療保險計劃，而羅姆尼的策略是攻擊奧巴馬拒絕討論該問題甚至拿不出解決方案草案。
the obama campaign is pummeling romney on medicare, and the romney campaign is hammering obama for his refusal to negotiate or even propose a solution.
因此，奧巴馬的政策將導致更高的赤字水平，債務比率將遠高於GDP的100 % ， 大量研究表明，如此水平將導致美國經濟增長率萎縮三分之一以上，並引發主權債務危機。
the obama policy would thus lead to everhigher deficits and debt ratios well over 100 of gdp, a level that numerous studies imply would reduce us economic growth by onethird or more and might induce a sovereigndebt crisis.
一些觀察者認為奧巴馬未明言的計劃是用歐洲式的增值稅來為不斷增加的福利支出買單。
some observers suggest that obamas unspoken plan is evergrowing entitlements eventually paid for by a europeanstyle valueadded tax.
貿易。
trade.
奧巴馬是相當長的一段時間以來第一位沒有在全球貿易自由化方面起到領導作用的美國總統。
obama is the first us president in a long time who has not played a leading role on global trade liberalization.
世貿談判多哈回合依然停滯不前，並推遲了三項自他入主白宮以來一直等在簽署的雙邊自由貿易協定。
the doha round of global trade talks remains stalled, and obama delayed the three bilateral freetrade agreements that awaited approval when he came into office.
羅姆尼是自由貿易的支持者，但也表示將對中國貿易行為和貨幣政策採取更強硬的立場。
romney is a proponent of free trade, but has said that he would be tougher on chinas trade practices and currency policies.
監管。
regulation.
奧巴馬希望進一步擴大聯邦指令-控制（command-and-control）監管（儘管法院已經叫停了他的某些監管權力的擴張 ） 。
obama wants to expand federal commandandcontrol regulation further though the courts have stopped his extension of some regulatory powers.
羅姆尼的方案採取經濟平衡的立場，將改革奧巴馬的主要衛生、環境和金融服務監管。
romney vows an economically balanced approach that would reform obamas major healthcare, environmental, and financialservices regulations.
任命。
appointments.
每位美國總統都會任命幾千官員，其中許多人將掌握重權。
every us president appoints thousands of officials, many with considerable power.
羅姆尼聲稱他將不會任命伯南克為美聯儲主席（可能的候選人選包括胡巴德（Glenn Hubbard ） 、 曼昆（Greg Mankiw ） 、 泰勒（John Taylor ） 、 費爾德斯坦（Martin Feldstein）等經濟學家 ） 。
romney has said that he would not reappoint ben bernanke as fed chairman likely candidates economists glenn hubbard, greg mankiw, john taylor, and martin feldstein.
其他總統任命職位將對企業、產業甚至整個經濟產生重大影響。
other presidential appointees exert considerable influence on firms, industries, or the entire economy.
比如，奧巴馬授命成立的神秘的美國勞工關係委員會（National Labor Relations Board）試圖阻止波音公司在南卡羅來納州的擴張，儘管該州透過了反工會的“工作權利”立法。
for example, obamas appointees to the obscure national labor relations board tried to prevent boeing from expanding in south carolina, despite the states antiunion right to work legislation.
這些政策將影響到美國的經濟增長、預算赤字、國民儲蓄，從而影響全球貿易和資本流。
these policies would affect us economic growth, the budget deficit, national saving, and hence global trade and capital flows.
奧巴馬的赤字將高於羅姆尼，因此美國也將更需要來自歐洲、拉美和亞洲的資本，與此同時，稅收和債務的增加將阻礙美國的經濟增長，從而破壞這些地區的出口。
with larger deficits under obama than under romney, america would need more capital from europe, latin america, and asia, while higher taxes and debt would impede us growth and thus undermine these regions exports.
奧巴馬將把美國駛上歐洲式社會福利國家的道路；而羅姆尼的方案是阻止這一幕的發生。
obama would steer america in the direction of european socialwelfare states romneys agenda is designed to prevent that.
不論誰獲勝，財政懸崖都將是2012年底的一打陰影。
whoever wins, a fiscal cliff looms at the end of 2012.
此前的立法如果不能扭轉，將導致突發性的大規模增稅和減支，據聯邦預算委員會的預計，這極有可能在2013年導致衰退。
previous legislation, if not reversed, will lead to large abrupt tax hikes and spending cuts, which the congressional budget office forecasts would likely cause a recession in 2013.
選舉之後的國會免不了像只跛腳鴨，儘管它會解決財政懸崖，但共和黨和民主黨之間在稅收和支出問題上的重大差異依然難以彌合。
while a postelection, lameduck session of congress will address the fiscal cliff, the deep differences between republicans and democrats on taxes and spending remain wide and difficult to bridge.
不確定性正在折磨歐洲財政，中國正在經歷減速，如果美國經濟再停滯不前甚至衰退，那世界經濟就完了。
with uncertainty plaguing europes finances and china slowing, the last thing the global economy needs is a stagnant or shrinking us economy.
但要阻止這一幕，就需要總統大選選出強大的領袖。
but it will take strong leadership by the presidentelect to avoid it.
美國的另類財政保守主義
americas exceptional fiscal conservatism
華盛頓—在大多數國家，身為“財政保守派”意味著你非常擔心預算赤字和債務水平，並將這類問題置於政策日程的最優先位置。
washington, dc in most countries, to be fiscally conservative means to worry a great deal about the budget deficit and debt levels and to push these issues to the top of the policy agenda.
如今，在許多歐元區國家 ， “ 財政保守派”是一個很有力量的集團，他們堅持政府需要增加收入，同時控制支出。
in many eurozone countries today, fiscal conservatives are a powerful group, insisting on the need to boost government revenue while bringing spending under control.
在英國，執政的保守黨最近也顯示出徵稅和限制未來支出的意願。
in great britain, too, leading conservatives have recently proved willing to raise taxes and attempted to limit future spending.
在這方面，美國顯得極為不同。
the united states is very different in this respect.
在美國，自稱“財政保守派”的政治領袖 — — 比如共和黨確定的與總統候選人羅姆尼共同挑戰11月大選的副總統人選保羅·萊恩 — — 更關注減稅，而不管這會對聯邦赤字和總未償還債務水平的影響。
there, leading politicians who choose to call themselves fiscal conservatives such as paul ryan, now the republican partys presumptive vicepresidential nominee to run alongside presidential candidate mitt romney in novembers election care more about cutting taxes, regardless of the effect on the federal deficit and total outstanding debt.
為什麼與其他國家的同道相比，美國的財政保守派基本不關注政府債務呢？
why do us fiscal conservatives care so little about government debt, relative to their counterparts in other countries?
並非總是如此。
it has not always been this way.
比如，1960年，艾森豪威爾總統的顧問就建議他減稅從而為其副總統尼克松問鼎總統寶座創造條件。
for example, in 1960, president dwight d. eisenhowers advisers suggested that he should cut taxes in order to pave the way for his vice president, richard nixon, to be elected to the presidency.
艾森豪威爾拒絕了這一建議，部分是因為他並不是很喜歡和信任尼克松，但主要原因是他認為給繼任者留下更接近收支平衡的預算非常重要。
eisenhower declined, partly because he did not particularly like or trust nixon, but mostly because he thought it was important to hand over a more nearly balanced budget to his successor.
1971年國際貨幣體系崩潰後，美國宏觀政策框架有了極大的改變。
the framework for us macroeconomic policy changed dramatically when the international monetary system broke down in 1971.
美國不再能夠維持美元和黃金之間的固定兌換率，而這正是戰後佈雷頓森林體系的基石。
the us could no longer maintain a fixed exchange rate between the dollar and gold the cornerstone of the postwar bretton woods system.
該安排之所以崩潰，是因為美國不再願意緊縮貨幣政策以及採取更嚴格的財政政策：不難理解，對尼克松總統來說，取悅美國選民要比維持全球固定匯率體系更加重要。
the arrangement collapsed because the us did not want to tighten monetary policy and run more restrictive fiscal policy keeping us voters happy was understandably more important to president nixon than maintaining a global system of fixed exchange rates.
不過，諷刺的是，佈雷頓森林體系的終結並沒有動搖美元在國際上的主導地位，實際上反而增加了美元在世界範圍的使用。
ironically, however, rather than undermining the predominant international role of the us dollar, the end of bretton woods actually boosted its use around the world.
過去四十年來，關於美元將要衰落的言論和行為層出不窮，但事實卻是如今由外國人持有的美元資產比1971年規模大多了。
much has been written, and many hands wrung, about the dollars decline over the last four decades, but the fact remains that holdings of us dollar assets by foreigners today are vastly greater than they were in 1971.
這是一柄雙刃劍，因為這導致美國不再關注財政賬戶。
this turns out to be a mixed blessing, because it has allowed the us to become less careful about its fiscal accounts.
如今，外國人大約持有了美國聯邦政府債務的一半，而即使在這筆債務的美元回報率極低（以及美元出現貶值）的情況下，他們也願意持有
foreigners now hold roughly half of all us federal government debt, and they are willing to hold it when it yields a very low return in dollars and even when the dollar depreciates.
事實上，每當世界不太穩定的時候，投資者就會願意持有更多的美元 — — 即使不穩定的根源正是來自美國。
in fact, whenever the world looks unstable, investors want to hold more dollar assets even when the us is the cause of the instability.
當美國大銀行陷入麻煩或美國陷入危害甚深的公共財政政治鬥爭時，全球投資者忙不迭地買入美國國債。
when big us banks are in trouble or americans are having another debilitating political fight over their public finances, global investors scramble into us treasuries.
去年國會關於聯邦債務上限的大斗爭導致美國失去了標註普爾AAA級主權評級，但如今聯邦政府的借貸成本卻比那時候更低了。
last years congressional showdown over the federal debt ceiling may have cost the us its aaa sovereign rating with standard poors, but the federal governments borrowing costs are actually lower now than they were then.
美國利用這一機會做了些什麼呢 — — 這也許是人類歷史上最低廉的融資成本了？
what has america done with this opportunity arguably the lowestcost funding in the history of humankind?
沒做什麼，如果你從生產性投資、加強教育或維持基本基礎設施角度來看的話。
not much, in terms of productive investment, strengthening education, or maintaining essential infrastructure.
但若從採取減稅措施以增加消費相對收入的比例以及降低政府收入相對支出的比例來說，美國又做了很多。
but the us has done a great deal in terms of adopting tax cuts that boost consumption relative to income and lower government revenue relative to expenditure.
這是小布什政府在21世紀初所採取的“臨時”減稅措施的最後遺留效應。
this is the lasting legacy of the temporary tax cuts adopted by george w. bushs administration in the early 2000s.
而美國人的政治觀念有了很大改變，不管是左派還是右派，都把公債問題視為僅僅是個干擾因素��或者用前副總統切尼的話說 ， “ 里根教導我們，赤字不是問題 ” — —他指的是羅納德·里根減了稅、增加了赤字，卻沒有因此承受任何不利的整治後果。
and americans have shifted greatly toward political philosophies on the right and on the left that regard public debt merely as a distraction. or, as former vice president dick cheney put it, reagan taught us that deficits do not matter meaning that ronald reagan cut taxes, ran bigger deficits, and did not suffer any adverse political consequences.
萊恩和共和黨中的茶黨成員毫無疑問希望削減聯邦政府的規模，他們交流這方面的計劃已經幾十年了。
ryan and members of the tea party wing of the republican party undoubtedly want to cut the size of the federal government, and they have articulated plans to do this over several decades.
但是，在短期，他們的承諾主要是減稅：他們的整個實用性規劃是一個朝著這個方向前進的前瞻性計劃。
but, in the near term, what they promise is primarily tax cuts their entire practical program is frontloaded in that direction.
他們的算盤是，政治上，這會得到民眾支援（也許是對的 ） ， 與此同時，這會讓後續的減支計劃更容易實施（正確性不那麼明顯 ） 。
the calculation is that this will prove politically popular probably true while making it easier to implement spending cuts down the road less obvious.
而未來數十年公債增加所引起的脆弱性完全不在他們的考慮範圍內。
the vulnerability caused by higher public debt over the next few decades is simply ignored.
比如，萊恩支援小布什的無節制支出。
for example, ryan supported george w. bushs spending spree.
他還支援將防務開支維持在（接近）現有水平，拒絕接受根據2011年預算控制法實施的防務開支縮減。
he also supports maintaining defense spending at or near its current level resisting the cuts that were put in place under the budget control act of 2011.
他們的假設 — — 並沒有明說，也很可疑 — — 是在可預見的未來，美國仍能以極低的利率出售任意數量的國債。
the assumption here unstated and highly questionable is that the us will be able to sell an unlimited amount of government debt at low interest rates for the foreseeable future.
在其他國家，沒有哪個財政保守派願意進行如此高賭注的豪賭。
there is no other country in the world where fiscal conservatives would want to be associated with such a highstakes gamble.
美國失敗的軍事化外交政策
americas failed militarized foreign policy
當今許多戰火不斷的地區—包括阿富汗、衣索比亞、伊朗、伊拉克、巴基斯坦、索馬利亞和蘇丹—都有著植根於它們衝突之中的基本問題。
many of todays war zones including afghanistan, ethiopia, iran, iraq, pakistan, somalia, and sudan share basic problems that lie at the root of their conflicts.
它們都很貧窮，飽受自然災害之苦—特別是洪水、乾旱和地震—並且都有著急速增長的人口，給土地的承載力帶來巨大的壓力。
they are all poor, buffeted by natural disasters especially floods, droughts, and earthquakes and have rapidly growing populations that are pressing on the capacity of the land to feed them.
年輕人口的比例很高，達到入伍年齡(15-24 歲)的年輕人數量也在不斷增加。
and the proportion of youth is very high, with a bulging population of young men of military age 1524 years.
所有的這些問題透過長期可持續的經濟發展都可以解決。
all of these problems can be solved only through longterm sustainable economic development.
然而，美國的反應卻是治標不治本，試圖透過軍事手段應對每一場衝突。
yet the united states persists in responding to symptoms rather than to underlying conditions by trying to address every conflict by military means.
它在索馬利亞支援衣索比亞軍隊。
it backs the ethiopian army in somalia.
它佔領了伊拉克和阿富汗。
it occupies iraq and afghanistan.
它威脅轟炸伊朗。
it threatens to bomb iran.
它支援巴基斯坦的軍事獨裁政權。
it supports the military dictatorship in pakistan.
沒有一項這樣的軍事行動是旨在解決引發衝突的問題。
none of these military actions addresses the problems that led to conflict in the first place.
相反，美國的政策通常是給當前的局勢火上澆油。
on the contrary, american policies typically inflame the situation rather than solve it.
這種軍事手段使得美國屢屢自釀苦酒。
time and again, this military approach comes back to haunt the us.
它曾以提供大量武器裝備的形式支援伊朗國王，但這些裝備在1979年以後卻落入了伊朗“革命政府”手中。
the us embraced the shah of iran by sending massive armaments, which fell into the hands of irans revolutionary government after 1979.
美國在那時支援薩達姆攻打伊朗，直到調轉槍頭對準薩達姆本人。
the us then backed saddam hussein in his attack on iran, until the us ended up attacking saddam himself.
美國曾在阿富汗支援本•拉登抵抗蘇聯，直到他最終成為美國的頭號敵人。
the us backed osama bin laden in afghanistan against the soviets, until the us ended up fighting bin laden.
自2001年起，美國給巴基斯坦的穆沙拉夫提供了超過100億美金的援助支援，而現在所面對的卻是一個搖搖欲墜的政權。
since 2001 the us has supported pervez musharraf in pakistan with more than 10 billion in aid, and now faces an unstable regime that just barely survives.
美國的外交政策如此低效的原因是它被軍方控制了。
us foreign policy is so ineffective because it has been taken over by the military.
就連美國佔領下的伊拉克戰後重建也是由五角大樓而不是民間機構主導的。
even postwar reconstruction in iraq under the usled occupation was run by the pentagon rather than by civilian agencies.
美國的軍事預算主導著外交政策的方方面面。
the us military budget dominates everything about foreign policy.
將五角大樓、伊拉克及阿富汗戰爭、國土安全部、核武計劃和國務院的軍事協助專案的預算加在一起，美國今年將在安全方面花費約8000億美元，而用於經濟發展的預算卻只有200億美元。
adding up the budgets of the pentagon, the iraq and afghanistan wars, the department of homeland security, nuclear weapons programs, and the state departments military assistance operations, the us will spend around 800 billion this year on security, compared with less than 20 billion for economic development.
在一篇關於布什政府對巴基斯坦的援助的文章中，Craig Cohen 和 Derek Chollet赫然揭示了這種軍事化手段的災難性特質—甚至在岌岌可危的穆沙拉夫政權最近的鎮壓行動之前。
in a stunning article on aid to pakistan during the bush administration, craig cohen and derek chollet demonstrated the disastrous nature of this militarized approach even before the tottering musharraf regimes latest crackdown.
文章透露儘管巴基斯坦面臨貧困、人口和環境的巨大難題，100億美援中仍有75%流向了巴勒斯坦軍方，公然對巴基斯坦在“反恐戰爭”中所做的貢獻進行償付，並幫助其購買F16戰鬥機和其他武器系統。
they show that even though pakistan faces huge problems of poverty, population, and environment, 75 of the 10 billion in us aid has gone to the pakistani military, ostensibly to reimburse pakistan for its contribution to the war on terror, and to help it buy f16s and other weapons systems.
另有16%直接流入巴基斯坦的預算，具體去向不明。
another 16 went straight to the pakistani budget, no questions asked.
所剩給發展與人道主義援助的部分不足10 % 。
that left less than 10 for development and humanitarian assistance.
用於巴基斯坦教育方面的年度美國援助總額僅有6400萬美元，平均到每個學齡兒童身上只有1.16美元。
annual us aid for education in pakistan has amounted to just 64 million, or 1.16 per schoolaged child.
該文的兩位作者還指出“巴基斯坦的戰略方向早先是由布什政府高層的一個小圈子設定的，其中心是戰爭而不是巴基斯坦的國內狀況。
the authors note that the strategic direction for pakistan was set early by a narrow circle at the top of the bush administration and has been largely focused on the war effort rather than on pakistans internal situation.
”他們還強調“美國與巴基斯坦的接觸是高度軍事化和集中化的，與廣大巴基斯坦民眾幾乎不相干。
they also emphasize that us engagement with pakistan is highly militarized and centralized, with very little reaching the vast majority of pakistanis.
”他們援引布什的話 ： “ 當（穆沙拉夫）直視著我的眼睛說 … … 將不會有塔利班也不會有基地組織時，我相信他，你���白麼？ ”
they quote george bush as saying, when musharraf looks me in the eye and saysthere wont be a taliban and wont be alqaeda, i believe him, you know?
這種軍事化的手段正將世界引入無止境的暴力與衝突之中。
this militarized approach is leading the world into a downward spiral of violence and conflict.
“出售”或給予該地區的每一件新的美國武器系統都會增加戰爭擴大和進一步軍事政變的機率，也會增加將這些武器用來對付美國自身的機率。
each new us weapons system sold or given to the region increases the chances of expanded war and further military coups, and to the chance that the arms will be turned on the us itself.
它們對解決那些重要的問題毫無幫助：如在巴基斯坦西北的邊疆省、蘇丹的達爾富爾地區或索馬利亞的貧困、兒童死亡、水源缺乏及缺少謀生手段。
none of it helps to address the underlying problems of poverty, child mortality, water scarcity, and lack of livelihoods in places like pakistans northwest frontier province, sudans darfur region, or somalia.
這些地區的眾多人口都面臨著降雨不足和草場退化的嚴重威脅。
these places are bulging with people facing a tightening squeeze of insufficient rainfall and degraded pasturelands.
很自然，在這樣的情況下很多人加入了激進組織。
naturally, many join radical causes.
布什政府沒有意識到這些人口和環境方面的挑戰，8000億的安全支出不會給阿富汗、巴基斯坦、蘇丹和索馬利亞帶來灌溉，因此也無法帶來和平。
the bush administration fails to recognize these fundamental demographic and environmental challenges, that 800 billion of security spending wont bring irrigation to afghanistan, pakistan, sudan, and somalia, and therefore wont bring peace.
他們看不到危機中的真實民眾，而只看得到漫畫般的，藏匿在每個角落的恐怖分子。
instead of seeing real people in crisis, they see caricatures, a terrorist around every corner.
只有當美國人及其盟友開始從他們假想敵的視角看問題，並意識到當今源自於絕望的衝突只能透過經濟發展而不是戰爭來解決時，我們才可能擁有一個更為和平的世界。
a more peaceful world will be possible only when americans and others begin to see things through the eyes of their supposed enemies, and realize that todays conflicts, having resulted from desperation and despair, can be solved through economic development rather than war.
如果我們注意聆聽肯尼迪總統在遇刺前的幾個月所說的話，就能得到和平—他說 ： “ 因為，終究我們最基本的共同聯絡是我們都生活在這個小小的星球；我們都呼吸著同樣的空氣；我們都珍惜孩子們的未來，而且我們都是凡人。
we will have peace when we heed the words of president john f. kennedy, who said, a few months before his death, for, in the final analysis, our most basic common link is that we all inhabit this small planet. we all breathe the same air.
”
we all cherish our childrens future. and we are all mortal.
美國的金融利維坦
americas financial leviathan
伯克利 — — 根據美國商業部的統計數字，1950年，美國金融和保險業佔GDP的比重為2.8 % 。
berkeley in 1950, finance and insurance in the united states accounted for 2.8 of gdp, according to us department of commerce estimates.
1960年，這一比重已上升為3.8 % ， 1990年則達到了6 % 。
by 1960, that share had grown to 3.8 of gdp, and reached 6 of gdp in 1990.
今天，這一數字是8.4 % ， 而且並沒有出現下滑。
today, it is 8.4 of gdp, and it is not shrinking.
《華爾街日報》的賈斯丁·萊哈特（Justin Lahart）報道說，2010年，該比重超過了2006年前一次高峰值。
the wall street journals justin lahart reports that the 2010 share was higher than the previous peak share in 2006.
萊哈特繼續指出，金融和保險佔經濟比重的增加“大體而言並非壞事 … … 讓資本流到用場最大的地方有助於經濟的增長 … … ”
lahart goes on to say that growth in the financeandinsurance share of the economy has not, by and large, been a bad thing....deploying capital to the places where it can be best used helps the economy grow...
但如果美國從這如今付給金融和保險業的額外資金 — — 佔GDP的5.6 % ， 相當於從付給直接生產有用商品和直接提供有用服務的人的錢中每年抽出7 500億美元 — — 中得到好處的話，那麼統計數字應該有所體現。
but if the us were getting good value from the extra 5.6 of gdp that it is now spending on finance and insurance the extra 750 billion diverted annually from paying people who make directly useful goods and provide directly useful services it would be obvious in the statistics.
按風險現金流實際利率的通常水平5%計算，在今年將如此大比重的資源從直接可用的商品和服務中抽出，如果要讓其不至於得不償失，就意味著這筆資源能夠提振0.3%的年經濟增長 — — 或在25年的一代人的時間裡提振6 % 。
at a typical 5 annual real interest rate for risky cash flows, diverting that large a share of resources away from goods and services directly useful this year is a good bargain only if it boosts overall annual economic growth by 0.3 or 6 per 25year generation.
過去幾代人經歷了多次對美國經濟的衝擊，諸多因素都領經濟增長雪上加霜。
there have been many shocks to the us economy over the past couple of generations, and many factors have added to or subtracted from economic growth.
但沒有明顯的證據表明，如果金融-保險系統維持1950年的水平，而沒有像過去20年那樣出現爆發式增長，那麼今天美國經濟的生產率會比現在低6 % 。
but it is not obvious that the us economy today would be 6 less productive if it had had the financeinsurance system of 1950 rather than the one that prevailed during the past 20 years.
經濟從運轉良好的金融-保險系統中獲益，存在五種途徑。
there are five ways that an economy gains from a wellfunctioning financeinsurance system.
其一，人們不再會因火災、水災、疾病、失業、企業倒閉、部門興衰等因素而遭受打擊，因為運轉良好的金融-保險系統會分散從而消解一部分風險，並能將懼怕某種風險的人與能夠安然承受這種風險等人之間匹配交易。
first, people are no longer as vulnerable to the effects of fires, floods, medical disasters, unemployment, business collapses, sectoral shifts, and so forth, because a wellworking financeinsurance system diversifies and thus dissipates some risks, and deals with others by matching those who fear risk with those who can comfortably bear it.
誠然，美國當前的金融-保險系統在某種程度上說也許更好地分散了風險，但從過去二十年的股票和房地產投資者的經歷看，很難判定這一點是否真的成立。
while it might be true that americas current financeinsurance system better distributes risk in some sense, it is hard to see how that could be the case, given the experience of investors in equities and housing over the past two decades.
其二，運轉良好的金融-保險系統將大規模、低流動性的投資專案與相對較小、由看重流動性的個人儲蓄者提供的資金組成的資金池匹配了起來。
second, wellfunctioning financial systems match large, illiquid investment projects with the relatively small pools of money contributed by individual savers who value liquidity highly.
在過去兩代人的時間裡，有一項重要創新：現在，企業可以發行高收益債券。
there has been one important innovation over the past two generations businesses can now issue highyield bonds.
但是，處於破產過程成本的考慮，企業為什麼喜歡發行高收益債券（除了與稅收系統周旋的原因之外 ） 、 投資者為什麼喜歡購買高收益債券，而不採用股票發行和購買的方式還並沒有水落石出。
but, given the costs of the bankruptcy process, it has never been clear why a business would rather issue highyield bonds besides gaming the tax system, or why investors would rather buy them than take an equity stake.
其三，借貸機會的改善使得人們可以在今天（較窮時）支出得更多，在未來（較富時）儲蓄得更多。
third, improved opportunities to borrow allow one to spend more now, when one is poor, and save more later, when one is rich.
家庭的借貸機會有了明顯的提高，這得歸功於住房所有權貸款、信用卡賬戶和發薪日貸款。
households are certainly much more able to borrow, thanks to homeequity loans, creditcard balances, and payday loans.
但實際上他們買了些什麼呢？
but what are they really buying?
許多人並沒有買到較窮時支出、較富時儲蓄的能力，而是買到了暫時不必與其他家庭成員討論“不愉快的財務緊縮”的機會。
many are not buying the ability to spend when they are poor and save when they are rich, but instead appear to be buying postponement of the unpleasant financial retrenchment talk with the other members of their household.
而這正是你所想買到的。
and that is not something you want to buy.
其四，我們看到，交易的便利性有了極大的改善。
fourth, we have seen major improvements in the ease of transactions.
但是，儘管電子交易讓金融生活有了極大的便利，但這應該伴隨著GDP的金融比重的下降而不是上升，正如通訊裝置的自動開關應該使手機上的電話按鍵操作減少一樣。
but, while electronic transactions have made a great deal of financial life much easier, this should have been accompanied by a decrease, not an increase, in the finance share of gdp, just as automated switching in telecommunications led to a decrease in the number of telephone switchboard operators per phone call.
事實上，與���術進步關係最密切的那部分金融系統的操作有了顯著的簡化，地區聯邦儲備銀行的核對操作就是明證。
indeed, the operations of those parts of the financial system most closely related to technological improvements have slimmed down markedly consider what has happened to the checking operations of the regional federal reserve banks.
最後，更棒的金融意味著更棒的公司治理。
finally, better finance should mean better corporate governance.
由於股東民主沒能有效控制管理層的放任恣睢，金融扮演著保證公司管理者按股東利益行事的重要角色。
since shareholder democracy does not provide effective control over entrenched, runaway, selfindulgent management, finance has a potentially powerful role to play in ensuring that corporate managers work in the interest of shareholders.
而在過去兩代人的時間裡，的確發生了深遠的變化：CEO們比以前更關注股市表現了，這或許是件好事。
and a substantial change has indeed occurred over the past two generations ceos focus much more attention than they used to on pleasing the stock market, and this is likely to be a good thing.
不過，總的來說，不管是在圍觀還是宏觀層面，我們並沒有看見顯而易見的大好處，這一點始終令人不安。 美國經濟的效率並沒有提高到能證明將這筆相當於GDP的5.6%的額外資金花在金融和保險上物有所值的程度。
overall, however, it remains disturbing that we do not see the obvious large benefits, at either the micro or macro level, in the us economys efficiency that would justify spending an extra 5.6 of gdp every year on finance and insurance.
萊哈特引用了紐約大學的托馬斯·菲力彭（Thomas Philippon）的結論：今日美國的金融部門顯得太大了，佔GDP的比重至少比合理水平高2個百分點。
lahart cites the conclusion of new york universitys thomas philippon that todays us financial sector is outsized by two percentage points of gdp.
而且菲力彭對美國金融部門規模的估計很有可能是低估的。
and it is very possible that philippons estimate of the size of the us financial sectors hypertrophy is too small.
為什麼投入金融和保險部門的技能和創業精神沒有產生顯而易見的經濟紅利？
why has the devotion of a great deal of skill and enterprise to finance and insurance sector not paid obvious economic dividends?
在金融業中賺錢的可持續之道有二：找到有風險可轉的人，並將他們與有風險承擔能力的人相匹配；或找到有風險的人，並將他們與身份不明但手握重金的人相匹配。
there are two sustainable ways to make money in finance find people with risks that need to be carried and match them with people with unused riskbearing capacity, or find people with such risks and match them with people who are clueless but who have money.
金融業的增長主要來自從事前一種業務還是後一種業務的專業人士，這個問題的答案有誰能確切知道嗎？
are we sure that most of the growth in finance stems from a rising share of financial professionals who undertake the former rather than the latter?
美國的財政孤立主義
americas fiscal isolationism
丹佛 — — 耐心是一種美德，但在美國外交政策上絕非如此。
denver patience might be a virtue, but not necessarily when it comes to american foreign policy.
想想“漫長的戰爭”吧，這一醒目的概念是幾年前用來描述與恐怖主義曠日持久的戰爭的，獲勝可以做到，但其巨大的財政負擔將在多年內都無法消除。
consider the long war, a bold concept embraced a few years ago to describe the continuing struggle against terrorism, the grudging progress that could realistically be achieved, and the enormous financial burden that it would impose for years to come.
這一概念也是對預期中的挫折的強權政治式的承認（用當時國防部長拉姆斯菲爾德的話說，就是“決勝 ” ） 。
it was also a realpolitik acknowledgement of the setbacks to be expected along the way the slog, as then defense secretary donald rumsfeld put it.
無論如何，這個詞是說給美國人聽的，美國人習慣於發動決定性速決戰（自越戰以來這就是美軍所堅持的方針 ） ， 為事關存亡的戰爭作出長期犧牲和奮鬥。
above all, the term was an effort to communicate to americans, accustomed to waging war with speed and decisiveness and insistent on it since vietnam, the longterm sacrifice and commitment needed to win a war of survival.
其擁護者也明白，戰爭並非只是武器的比拼，而是連續不斷的付出，用他們的話說，要摧毀“政府全力投入”不僅是軍事或準軍事實體，還有其背後的民事機構。
its proponents also understood that the war would not be limited to weapons, but would need to be a sustained effort, involving, as they put it, the whole of government, with civilian agencies marshaled behind military or paramilitary objectives.
這樣的付出令人生畏，因此其鼓吹者需要可持續的政治一致來支援它。
daunting as the effort would be, its advocates assumed a sustainable political consensus to support it.
畢竟，美國也曾被攻擊過。
after all, the united states had been attacked.
如今，隨著美國政客在曠日持久的聯邦預算論戰中鬥得不可開交，這個一致條件已不再成立。
today, that consensus is unraveling as americas politicians wrestle with a federal budget that is itself turning into a long war one with its own casualties.
這場論戰表明，政治精英在所有支出方案上都存在分歧，更不用說勞師遠征事宜了。
the battle lines in this struggle suggest that there is little accord among political elites for any spending, let alone for a long war with farflung commitments.
結果，每走一步，基本條件就會受到質疑。
as a result, basic assumptions are being questioned at every turn.
事實上，當前預算論戰似乎重新撕開了美國對其自身以及世界看法的舊有分歧。
indeed, the current budget war seems to be reopening old divisions about americas view of itself and the world.
論戰結果遠未明瞭，甚至有孤立主義（在美國由來已久的弊端）捲土重來的可能。
the outcome is far from certain, but even isolationism, a perennial american malady, seems to be making a comeback.
美國外交政策經常陷入孤立主義的囹圄，孤立主義者既包括總是認為美國在全世界鶴立雞群的美國右派，也包括認為美國是全球不穩定因素的左派。
isolationism is a familiar refrain in us foreign policy among those elements of the right that consider the us too good for the world, as well as among those on the left who consider america a destructive global force.
但這一回可能與前幾次都不一樣，預算問題正在催生跨黨派孤立主義。
but this time, as perhaps never before, a bipartisan isolationist impulse is being driven by the budget.
美國的財政危機影響深遠，絕對不是幾個數字那麼簡單。
americas fiscal crisis is profound, and it is not just about numbers.
華盛頓的情緒表明，對加稅的厭惡要遠勝於當前經濟和就業表現。
as the emotions in washington today suggest, the aversion to tax increases runs far deeper than concern about their effect on current economic performance and job growth.
從某種程度上說，這代表著一種正統 — — 一些人稱之為正統派 — — 觀點，即稅收之於政府，就像威士忌之於酒鬼。
in part, it represents a fundamental some would say fundamentalist view that taxes are to government what a bottle of whisky is to an alcoholic.
羅納德·里根告訴我們，政府不是解決方案，政府本身就是問題。
government, as ronald reagan told us, is the problem, not the solution.
這對美國外交來說可是個壞訊息。
that message is bad news for american diplomacy.
政客一方面不願為國內計劃提供資金，一方面又在大打“漫長的戰爭 ” ， 美國外交圈可能會忽視兩者之間的聯絡，但其他美國人可不會。
the linkage between politicians unwillingness to fund domestic programs and the imperiled commitment to the long war might elude those in us foreignpolicy circles, but it is not lost on the rest of the country.
民意調查顯示，美國人願意維持許多“自由裁量”國內計劃 — — 學校、醫院、交通基礎設施，休閒公園等 — — 而這些計劃如今成了預算談判樽俎上的魚肉。
opinion surveys suggest that americans want to maintain many of the discretionary domestic programs schools, hospitals, transportation infrastructure, recreational parks, etc. that are now on the chopping block in budget negotiations.
在艾爾帕索縣（El Paso County）農村等地區，在科羅拉多州東部平原，在那些遠離聯邦預算論戰中心的地區，支出削減已經提上了議程。
in places like rural el paso county, on the eastern plains of colorado, far from the federal budget debates epicenter, spending cuts are the order of the day.
隨著教師裁員，各學區紛紛提高了班級規模，校舍修繕計劃被推遲，校車服務也收到了影響。
school districts are increasing class sizes as they shed teachers, as well as deferring maintenance projects and curtailing the schoolbus service.
支出削減正在對艾爾帕索縣居民造成直接影響。
these cuts are having a very real and immediate impact on el paso countys residents.
他們（以及其他正在失去生活必須服務的美國人）真的會期待付出更多的稅收來為阿富汗建設新學校提供資金？
can they, and other americans who are losing vital services, really be expected to rise above it all and support funding to build new schools in afghanistan?
不但美國公立學校正在淪為二等，美國基礎設施亦然，而這長期以來一直是美國人民的驕傲。
not only are americas public schools starting to look secondrate, but so is its infrastructure, which had long been a source of national pride.
現在，有多少旅行者會分不清亞洲的新建高效機場和美國各主要城市那老邁低效的古董機場？
how many travelers nowadays can fail to note the difference between asias new, efficient airports and the aging, clogged antiques in some major us cities?
預算論戰並沒有就修補美國基礎設施���成任何一致，倒是在造成這樣的印象：阿富汗和巴基斯坦才是美國的核心國家利益。
the budget war is not producing any consensus on fixing americas infrastructure, but it is beginning to produce a view that afghanistan and pakistan are far from being core us national interests.
人們不禁要問，為什麼阿富汗和伊拉克的學校和道路比科羅拉多和加利福尼亞更重要？
why, people ask, are schools and roads in afghanistan and iraq more important than those in colorado or california?
在2008年，美國軍隊承擔了向巴格達動物園運送一隻老虎的費用。
at one point in 2008, the us military picked up the cost of transporting a tiger for the baghdad zoo.
美國政府上一次為美國動物園做同樣的事情要追溯到何年何月了（當然，華盛頓除外 ） ？
when was the last time the us government did that for a us zoo outside of washington, of course?
這場論戰如何收場將對美國如何在世界上給自己定位造成深遠影響。
how this debate sorts itself out will have profound consequences for how america conducts itself in the world.
但這也將有損於世界對美國增長最快的出口專案 — — 主動提供意見 — — 的反應。
but it might also take a toll on how the world reacts to americas fastestgrowing export unsolicited advice.
一國接受他人意見的原因很多。
countries take others advice for many reasons.
有時他們尊重意見提供者的智慧和洞見（這在外交中非常罕見 ） 。
sometimes they respect the advisers wisdom and insights fairly rare in diplomacy.
有時他們害怕拒絕建議的後果（及不得不接受的意見 ） 。
or they might fear the consequences of not taking the advice an offer one cannot refuse, so to speak.
有時（正如大量美國外交交易所顯示的）接受建議開啟改善關係之門，從而帶來進一步的援助。
or, as is true of many of americas diplomatic transactions, accepting advice could open the way to a better relationship and to additional assistance.
簡言之，外交 — — 特別是美國外交 — — 通常與金錢有關。
in short, diplomacy and us diplomacy, in particular often involves money.
但沒錢進行外交會怎麼樣呢？
but what if there is no money to offer?
如果美國人厭惡了對自己所住社群預算的削減，從而拒絕為“漫長的戰爭”掏腰包，情況又會如何？
what if americans, tired of the budget cuts in their neighborhoods, refuse to support funds even for the long war?
真到了這一步，可能會是這樣：美國高官抵達某個國家，給出一些建議，結果發現根本沒人理他。
at that point, senior us officials might well arrive in a country, offer advice, and find that nobody is bothering to listen.
汲取被遺忘的美國違約的教訓
learning from americas forgotten default
洛杉磯—關於美國的一則流傳甚廣的傳說是聯邦政府從未對其債務違過約。
los angeles one of the most pervasive myths about the united states is that the federal government has never defaulted on its debts.
每一次國會爭論債務上限，政客和記者都會站出來說，美國不會失信於債權人。
every time the debt ceiling is debated in congress, politicians and journalists dust off a common trope the us doesnt stiff its creditors.
只有一個問題：這不是真的。
theres just one problem its not true.
幾十年前，美國曾經一度更像是一個“香蕉共和國”而不是發達經濟體，單方面和追溯性地重組債務。
there was a time, decades ago, when the us behaved more like a banana republic than an advanced economy, restructuring debts unilaterally and retroactively.
儘管很少有人記得這段經濟史上的重要時期，但它對於今天的領導人來說是非常寶貴的教訓。
and, while few people remember this critical period in economic history, it holds valuable lessons for leaders today.
1933年4月，為了幫助美國擺脫大蕭條，羅斯福總統宣佈準備讓美國脫離金本位並讓美元貶值。
in april 1933, in an effort to help the us escape the great depression, president franklin roosevelt announced plans to take the us off the gold standard and devalue the dollar.
但這不像羅斯福想象的那麼簡單。
but this would not be as easy as fdr calculated.
當時的大部分債務合同都含有“黃金條款 ” ， 規定債務人必須用“金幣”或“黃金等價物”償付。
most debt contracts at the time included a gold clause, which stated that the debtor must pay in gold coin or gold equivalent.
這些條款產生於內戰時期，初衷是為了保護投資者免收可能的通貨膨脹飆升的影響。
these clauses were introduced during the civil war as a way to protect investors against a possible inflationary surge.
但對羅斯福來說，黃金條款成為美元貶值的障礙。
for fdr, however, the gold clause was an obstacle to devaluation.
如果在不解決合同問題的情況下就讓美元貶值，那麼債務的美元價值就會自動上升以抵消下跌的匯率，導致大規模破產和公共債務水平飆升。
if the currency were devalued without addressing the contractual issue, the dollar value of debts would automatically increase to offset the weaker exchange rate, resulting in massive bankruptcies and huge increases in public debt.
為了解決這個問題，國會在1933年6月5日透過了聯合決議，廢除過去和未來的一切黃金條款。
to solve this problem, congress passed a joint resolution on june 5, 1933, annulling all gold clauses in past and future contracts.
貶值的大門開啟了 — — 政治鬥爭的大門也隨之開啟。
the door was opened for devaluation and for a political fight.
共和黨感到沮喪，因為美國的聲譽岌岌可危，而羅斯福政府認為決議並不構成“否認合同 ” 。
republicans were dismayed that the countrys reputation was being put at risk, while the roosevelt administration argued that the resolution didnt amount to a repudiation of contracts.
1934年1月30日，美元正式貶值。
on january 30, 1934, the dollar was officially devalued.
黃金價格從每盎司20.67美元 — — 自1834年生效的價格 — — 上漲到每盎司35美元。
the price of gold went from 20.67 an ounce a price in effect since 1834 to 35 an ounce.
毫不奇怪，受黃金條款保護的證券持有者宣稱此舉違憲。
not surprisingly, those holding securities protected by the gold clause claimed that the abrogation was unconstitutional.
