since the descendants of todays living species will go on to comprise all future ecosystems formed when humans or planetary processes generate novel conditions there is a clear advantage to having more kinds of them.
事實上，更多物種形成了環境的“備用件 ” ， 保護算得上是一種長期環境保險。
indeed, more species function as spare parts for the environment, and conservation amounts to a kind of longterm environmental insurance policy.
爭議較大的是將物種轉移到新生態系統中。
more contentious is the transportation of species to new ecosystems.
園丁喜歡在後院種植外來物種，但本地種常常將開始在後院中生長的“外來”植物視為入侵者 — — 對過去的危險的偏離。
gardeners may love to plant exotic species in their backyards, but communities often treat the foreign plants that begin to grow in the countryside as invasive a dangerous departure from the past.
有時候，這些植物連除草劑都無從除去。
sometimes, those plants are doused in herbicides, usually to no avail.
對這種變化的抵制是如此強烈，以至於英國要等待1,000年左右才會將一個物種，比如兔子，視為本地種。
so strong is the resistance to such changes that the united kingdom waits about 1,000 years before it regards a species, like the rabbit, as native.
在澳大利亞，澳洲野狗 — — 幾百年前引入 — — 是否應該被認為是本地種仍在爭論當中。
in australia, there is a debate over whether the dingo introduced thousands of years ago should be counted as indigenous.
但到目前為止，大約2,000中非本地動植物並未直接導致本地種滅絕，大部分只是引起了很微小的傷害或毫無傷害。
yet, so far, the roughly 2,000 nonnative plant and animal species in the uk have not directly caused any native species to become extinct, with most causing little or no harm at all.
事實上，在過去幾個世紀中，外來物種的輸入和傳播增加了世界大部分地區的生物多樣性。
in fact, the importation and spread of immigrant species has increased biological diversity in most regions of the world in the last few centuries.
這些地區性的生物多樣性增加 — — 歐洲國家和美國野生植物種類數量增加了20 % ， 夏威夷群島和其他太平洋島嶼植物物種數量增加了一倍 — — 應該被視為是積極的發展趨勢。
these regional increases including a 20 rise in the number of plant species growing wild in european countries and the united states, and a doubling of plant species in the hawaiian archipelago and other pacific islands could be interpreted as a positive development.
考慮到這一點 — — 並且將大部分外來物種遣返也不現實 — — 新來物種或多或少應該被立即接受。
given this and the impracticality of trying to repatriate most foreign species newcomers should be accepted more or less immediately.
這顯然要比打著某種理想化的舊自然世界旗號曠日持久地爭論它們更有意義。
that certainly makes more sense than engaging in millennialong debates about them, in the name of some idealized past version of the natural world.
這不是倒退，因為全新物種一直在產生，特別是透過遷移物種的雜交。
there is no going back, because entirely new species continually come into existence, particularly through the hybridization of transported species.
在過去三個世紀中，在英國演化的雜種作物 — — 如大米草和猴面花 — — 要比整個歐洲滅絕的作物（以滅絕記錄為準）更多。
more new hybrid plants such as cord grass and monkey flowers have evolved in the uk in the last three centuries than have gone extinct throughout europe over the same period according to existing records.
北美也有類似情況。
the situation is similar in north america.
這一在人類幫助下發生的新演化意味著在人類世，我們其實既是舊生物多樣性的毀滅者，也是新生物多樣性的創造者。
this evolution of new humanassociated species means that, in the anthropocene, we are effectively creators of new biological diversity as well as destroyers of the old.
我們不再僅僅依靠地球；現在我們也在改變地球。
we no longer merely depend on the planet we are now also shaping it.
認識到這一點，我們絕對應該明確絕非所有改變都是“壞的 ” 。
recognizing that, we should certainly resist changes that are unequivocally bad.
但對於讓物種適應環境變化的生物學改變 — — 物種一直是透過這一過程實現生存 — — 我們應該採取更多的接受乃至積極的態度。
but when it comes to biological changes that will enable species to adjust to environmental changes the process by which species have always survived we should take a more accepting and even proactive approach.
我在我的新書《地球的繼承者：滅絕時代自然如何繁榮 》 （ Inheritors of the Earth: How Nature is Thriving in an Age of Extinction）中指出，我們生活在一個“新的自然界”中。
as i argue in my recent book inheritors of the earth how nature is thriving in an age of extinction, we are living in a new natural world.
它仍然和過去一樣被生態和演化動態所推動。
it is still driven by the same ecological and evolutionary dynamism as always.
區別在於這一動態如今主要來自76億（並在不斷增加）的人類的活動。
the difference is that that dynamism is now fueled largely by the activities of a human population of 7.6 billion and rising.
物種將進入新的人類創造的環境，並與我們一同演化。
species will move into new humancreated environments and evolve alongside us.
我們應該讓它們這樣演化。
we should let them.
也許我們甚至應該幫助它們。
maybe we should even help them.
農業的壞藥方
agricultures bad medicine
聖迭戈—我們大部分人，當由我們的行為所造成的威脅還沒有進入視線之前，不會想到這些威脅的存在。
san diego most of us are oblivious to the threats caused by our actions when those threats are invisible.
對抗生素的使用就是如此。
our use of antibiotics is a case in point.
明智而審慎地使用的話，抗生素能夠拯救生命、阻止致命疾病的傳播。
when used judiciously, antibiotics save lives and prevent the transmission of deadly diseases.
但抗生素的效力正在因為它們在農業中的不審慎使用而被浪費。
but the therapeutic power of antibiotics is being squandered by their imprudent use in agriculture.
如今，全世界一大半抗生素用量被用在了食品生產中。
today, more than half of the antibiotics administered around the world are used in the production of food.
農民用抗生素治療牲口感染。
farmers use antimicrobials to treat infections in their livestock.
問題在於他們常常用錯了抗生素，要麼把它們用於補救不合理的農業做法 — — 如過度擁擠的工廠化農場讓疾病更加容易傳播 — — 要麼把它們用於加快生長和降低生產成本。
the problem is that they commonly misuse antibiotics either to compensate for poor agricultural practices such as overcrowding on factory farms, which encourages the spread of disease or to accelerate growth and reduce production costs.
這些做法獨立看來也許無甚傷害，但它們的總效應相當危險。
these practices may appear harmless in isolation, but their aggregate effect is dangerous.
抗生素透過人們所吃的食物或動物產生的廢物而進入環境中，導致抗生素耐藥性加劇。
as antibiotics enter the environment through the food people eat or the waste animals produce, antimicrobial resistance intensifies.
而這給人類健康帶來了非常不利的影響。
and this affects human health in troubling ways.
每一天，在全世界的醫院和診所中，患者都會因為結核病、淋病或肺炎能夠傳染病而是用抗生素治療細菌感染。
every day, at hospitals and clinics around the world, patients are given antibiotics for bacterial infections like tuberculosis, gonorrhea, or pneumonia.
也有人因為預防目的而是用抗生素，以避免手術過程或有損免疫力的基本情況或治療（如化療）過程中的細菌感染。
others receive antibiotics prophylactically, to prevent bacterial infections during surgery, or when underlying conditions or treatments such as chemotherapy compromise their immunity.
不幸的是，許多被廣泛使用的抗生素正在失去它們保護患者、治療疾病的能力；一個關鍵原因是農業作業對抗生素的日常濫用。
unfortunately, many widely used antibiotics are losing their ability to protect patients and treat disease routine misuse of antibiotics in farming is a key reason why.
蘇格蘭微生物學家亞歷山大·弗萊明（Alexander Fleming）發現能夠殺死細菌的菌類後不久就認識到，過度使用抗生素會引起耐藥性。
not long after the scottish microbiologist alexander fleming discovered a fungus that could kill bacteria, he recognized that overuse of antibiotics would encourage resistance.
他在1945年警告說 ， “ 輕率使用青黴素的人要為因為感染了具有青黴素耐藥性的微生物而死去的人負有道德責任。 ”
as he warned in 1945, the thoughtless person playing with penicillin is morally responsible for the death of the man who finally succumbs to infection with the penicillinresistant organism.
抗生素在農業中的大規模濫用是“輕率使用青黴素”的最臭名昭著的形式之一。
widespread misuse of antibiotics in agriculture is one of the most egregious forms of playing with penicillin.
2015年，中國家豬身上發現了一種新的抗生素耐藥菌，隨後中國病人身上也出現了這種細菌。
in 2015, a new antibioticresistant bacterium was discovered in chinese pigs, and then in chinese patients.
此後又發現了兩個變種，而令這些細菌擁有抗生素耐藥性的基因可以在物種間躍遷 — — 即所謂的“流動性遺傳要素 ” — —目前已經在全世界的農場和醫院中發現。
since then, two more variants of the bacterium have been discovered, and the genes that enable these bacteria to resist antibiotics and jump between species socalled mobile genetic elements have been found on farms and in hospitals around the world.
如果抗生素在農業中的魯莽使用情況繼續下去，對人的影響將十分嚴重。
if the reckless use of antibiotics in agriculture continues, the impact on people will be severe.
幸運的是，我們有解決辦法。
fortunately, there is a solution.
十多年前，歐盟禁止除了治療感染之外的一切原因的抗生素農業用途。
more than a decade ago, the european union banned antibiotics in agriculture for any purpose other than treating infections.
此外，儘管這個規則並不完美，但它有助於降低抗生素的使用。
and, although the rule is not perfect, it has helped lower antibiotic use.
比如，在丹麥，豬農抗生素用量出現了下降，儘管用於治療豬瘟的抗生素用量略有增加。
in denmark, for example, total antibiotic use by pig farmers has decreased, despite a slight increase in antibiotics administered for treating porcine diseases.
這些收益不管多麼微小，對協調行動起著鼓勵作用 — — 並應該進一步鼓勵。
these gains, however modest, are encouraging and should encourage further coordinated action.
抗生素耐藥性問題是一個全球性威脅，因此，唯有多邊合作 — — 以新條約或貿易協定的形式 — — 才能保證各國農民都受到最低標準的約束 — — 在牲畜養殖中不再非必要的情況下使用抗生素。
because of the global nature of the threat, only multilateral cooperation in the form of a new treaty or trade agreements can ensure that farmers everywhere abide by minimal standards for raising livestock without the unnecessary use of antibiotics.
2015年12月，英國政府組織、經濟學家吉姆·奧尼爾（Jim O’Neill）領銜的一項研究發現，改變行為的最有效的手段是限制使用抗生素，但允許個體國家嘗試用稅收或者管制來實現這一限制。
in december 2015, a study commissioned by the british government and chaired by the economist jim oneill found that the most effective means of changing behaviors would be to cap the use of antibiotics, but allow individual countries to experiment with taxes or restrictions to meet the cap.
此外，我在其他文章中指出，應該要求農民在對牲畜使用抗生素前獲得處方。
moreover, as i have argued elsewhere, farmers should be required to obtain a prescription before administering medicine to livestock.
儘管歐盟的禁令包含了這一條款，但規避和豁免導致這條規則形同虛設。
although the eus ban includes such a provision, waivers and exemptions have watered down the rule.
如果達成全球共識 — — 比如透過G20或聯合國大會達成 — — 選擇對農業抗生素徵稅的國家可以用所得稅收收入推動替代農業作業的轉型。
if a global consensus were reached for example, through the g20 or the united nations general assembly countries choosing to tax agricultural antibiotics could use the revenue to help ease the transition to alternative farming practices.
錢還可以用於資助試管肉的研究，試管肉能大大降低動物的痛苦和傳染病負擔。
money could also go to fund research on in vitro meat, which would dramatically reduce animal suffering and lower the burden of infectious diseases.
最重要的是，新條約必須允許簽署國靈活地滿足農民的多樣化需要。
most important, any new treaty must provide signatories with flexibility to meet the diverse needs of their farmers.
全球行動的目標應該是激勵農民減少抗生素使用，而不是進行懲罰。
the goal of global action should be to incentivize farmers to reduce their antibiotic use, not to mete out punishment.
有希望形成一些條件，讓抗生素只用於治療病患，而不會用在健康的動物身上。
it is possible to create conditions under which antibiotics are used only to treat sick patients, not healthy animals.
儘管世界距離這一目標還有很長的路要走，但和消費者驅動的美國的做法歐洲的監管已經證明，如果被鼓勵或被要求這樣做，農民會改變方針。
although the world is a long way from that goal, consumerdriven practices in the united states and regulations in europe have demonstrated that farmers will change their approach if encouraged or required to do so.
儘管如此，我們中大部分人依舊對我們的決定所造成的意外後果視而不見。
still, most of us remain blind to the unintended consequences of our decisions.
除非人民自願不再消費工廠化農場生產的肉製品，否則我們必須依靠政府和多邊組織讓我們保持正確的道路。
unless people voluntarily refrain from consuming factoryfarmed meat, we will need governments and multilateral organizations to keep us on the right path.
有效的抗生素
antibiotics that work
墨西哥城 — — 從1928年發現青黴素到二十世紀六十年代最後一批主要抗生素進入市場，人類抵禦病原菌的能力發生了極大的變革。
mexico city from the discovery of penicillin in 1928 to the introduction of the last of the main groups of antibiotics in the 1960s, humanitys capacity to fight pathogenic bacteria has been transformative.
但是，隨著時間的推移，細菌易感的抗生素數量正在逐漸減少，並且某些病原體已經對多數或所有現有藥物產生了耐藥反應。
but, over time, the number of antibiotics to which bacteria are susceptible has been dwindling, and some pathogens have become resistant to most or all existing drugs.
結果導致曾經可以治療的感染正在重新變得致命。
as a result, oncetreatable infections are becoming deadly again.
目前，抗生素耐藥性每年導致約70，000人死亡，由此造成高達成百上千億美元的財務損失。
already, antibiotic resistance is leading to an estimated 700,000 deaths per year, with financial costs reaching tens of billions of dollars.
由於抗生素耐藥性繼續影響我們治療癌症、移植器官和植入假體，抗生素耐藥性造成的損失將會更加嚴重。
as antibiotic resistance continues to undermine our ability to treat cancers, transplant organs, and implant prosthesis, these figures will only rise.
抗生素耐藥性上升是由諸多因素共同導致的。
many factors have contributed to rising antibiotic resistance.
細菌可以快速繁殖和突變，並能建立某種類似“基因網際網路”的網路，允許某些病原菌“下載”抗生素耐藥基因。
bacteria can reproduce and mutate rapidly, and they can establish something of a genetic internet that enables certain pathogenic bacteria to download antibioticresistant genes.
此外，多數抗生素是土壤細菌的天然產物，而抗生素耐藥性可以在土壤菌群中自然產生。
moreover, most antibiotics are natural products of soil bacteria, in which antibiotic resistance can occur naturally.
當大規模引入人造抗生素時，具有耐藥性的細菌就會越來越盛行。
when humanmade antibiotics were introduced on a massive scale, the bacteria with resistance became the most prevalent.
今天，人類每年釋放約100,000噸抗生素。
today, humans release about 100,000 tons of antibiotics per year.
如果這些抗生素運用恰當並能挽救生命，合理的成本效益分析或許會成為可能。
if those antibiotics were being used properly and saving lives, a reasonable costbenefit analysis might be possible.
但約70%的抗生素卻被用於加快農場動物的生長速度。
but about 70 of them are used to make farm animals to grow a bit faster.
其餘30%雖然用於治療病人，但處方卻往往不正確或不必要。
the other 30, while used to treat people, are often prescribed incorrectly or needlessly.
而且，由於大部分用過的藥物隨廢水和糞便排入環境，從而導致土壤、水體和野生動物當中的菌群也能接觸到。
and, because a substantial share of the used drugs are released into the environment with wastewater and manure, bacterial communities in soils, waters, and wildlife are also exposed.
如果這種濫用抗生素的局面不盡快結束，我們很快就會發現自己沒有有效治療細菌感染的藥物可用。
if this abuse of antibiotics does not end, we will soon find ourselves without drugs to treat bacterial infections effectively.
但儘管正在採取某些措施 — — 去年9月召開的一次聯合國高階別會議提出了某些國際政策建議 — — 但採取的措施還遠遠不夠。
but while some steps are being taken a highlevel united nations meeting last september produced proposals for some international measures they are far from adequate.
人類真正需要的是立即在全球範圍內禁止抗生素的農業應用。
what is really needed is an immediate worldwide ban on the agricultural use of antibiotics.
此外，現在在醫療界執行力度堪比如何選擇領帶指南的抗生素臨床使用指南必須得到嚴格的稽核和執行。
moreover, guidelines for the clinical use of antibiotics, which the medical community now follows as closely as those concerning how to pick a necktie, must be reviewed and strongly enforced.
僅靠這兩項措施 — — 兩者都可以由政府監管機構頒佈 — — 就可以減少近80%的抗生素用量，從而大大延緩抗生素耐藥性的產生。
these two measures alone both of which could be enacted by governmental regulatory agencies would reduce the use of antibiotics by nearly 80, slowing the rise of antibiotic resistance substantially.
當然，讓政府實施這些政策並不容易，因為它們與強大的經濟利益背道而馳，其中最明顯的莫過於製藥行業，該行業每年出售價值400億美元的抗生素。
of course, getting governments to implement such measures will not be easy, because they run counter to powerful economic interests, the most obvious being the pharmaceutical industry, which sells 40 billion worth of antibiotics each year.
儘管大型藥企對繼續濫用抗生素興趣強烈，但卻對研發新抗生素應對耐藥菌缺乏興趣。
while big pharma has a strong interest in continued antibiotic abuse, it has little interest in developing new antibiotics to tackle drugresistant bacteria.
他們的底線是抗生素能夠治療癌症和慢性病。
drugs for chronic illnesses and cancer are better for their bottom line.
因此大型藥企要求“激勵措施”才願開展新抗生素的研發，比方說延長專利期限或減稅；另外一種辦法是為新藥開出天文數字的價格。
so big pharma is seeking incentives to pursue research and development of new antibiotics, such as extended patents or tax breaks the alternative would be to charge astronomical prices for new drugs.
但這些激勵措施為製藥企業帶來的收益遠遠超過了實際研發成本；於是成為讓公共資金流入私人腰包的工具 — — 而恰恰是這些人最初造成了問題。
but the benefits of such incentives for pharmaceutical companies would far exceed the cost of the actual rd pursued they would be instruments to funnel public funds into private hands the very hands that caused the problem.
但除了這些胡蘿蔔，社會還應該考慮使用大棒。
beyond all of these carrots, however, societies should consider using some sticks.
我建議實行一項計劃，根據藥企在解決抗生素耐藥性問題方面的貢獻對其進行評級；應當懲罰那些不做貢獻的企業減少其銷售額。
i propose an initiative that rates pharmaceutical companies according to their contribution to solving the antibioticresistance problem those that do not contribute should be punished with fewer sales.
我稱之為NANBU計劃（即沒有抗生素、就沒有業務 ） 。
i call it nanbu no antibiotics, no business.
NANBU計劃會給積極研究新抗生素的企業新增分數。
nanbu would grant points to companies with vigorous research programs or with new antibiotics in the development pipeline.
不為農業目的製造或出售抗生素、抑或拒絕在不需要此類藥物的疾病領域推廣抗生素應用的企業也能夠獲得分數。
companies that do not manufacture or sell antibiotics for agricultural purposes, or that refuse to promote the use of antibiotics for diseases that do not require such drugs, would gain points as well.
而那些從事相反行為的企業 — — 將抗生素作為牲畜“生長促進劑”出售或積極鼓勵醫生開藥的企業 — — 將會丟掉分數。
those that engaged in the opposite behaviors selling antibiotics as livestock growth promoters or actively encouraging physicians to prescribe the drugs would lose points.
起初，幾乎所有製藥企業都會丟掉分數。
at first, virtually all drug companies would have negative scores.
但隨著時間的推移可以對評級進行調整，而調整評級一定要以獨立專家組的合理建議為依據。
but, over time, the ratings could be adjusted, always according to scientifically sound advice from an independent group of experts.
然後可以使用評級來指導購藥決策。
the ratings could then be used to guide drugpurchasing decisions.
對諸多相關藥物種類來講，往往有不同製藥企業生產的若干種藥物具有相似的功效和安全性。
for many kinds of relevant drugs, there are several options with similar efficacy and safety, produced by different companies.
於是臨床醫生可以大量使用來自高評級企業的藥物，避免讓低評級企業的藥物流入市場。
so clinicians could prescribe drugs mostly from highly rated companies, and avoid drugs from companies with low ratings.
患者則應當鼓勵這樣的決策，並遵循同樣的原則購買非處方藥。
patients could encourage such decisionmaking, and follow suit when purchasing overthecounter drugs.
隨著時間的推移，抗生素可以再次獲得更強的盈利能力，因為相關公司可以銷售更多其他藥物，因此逐漸降低對昂貴激勵政策的需求。
over time, antibiotics could become more profitable again, as engaged companies sell more of their other drugs and the need for costly incentives diminishes.
NANBU計劃成功的關鍵是確保人們廣泛瞭解抗生素耐藥性造成的威脅及其相關應對舉措。
the key to nanbus success will be to ensure widespread understanding of the antibioticresistance threat and what is needed to combat it.
這將推動患者和醫生在決定使用何種藥物時考慮NANBU 評級，並迫使它們的政府採取更加有力的行動。
this would give patients and doctors the impetus to regard nanbu ratings in making drug decisions, as well as to pressure their governments to take even stronger action.
利用公眾宣傳加強政府落實必要但困難政策的壓力曾經獲得過成功 — — 這方面的例子包括推進林業和漁業的可持續性。
the use of a public awareness campaign to intensify pressure on governments to pursue necessary but difficult measures has worked before for example, in advancing forest and fishery sustainability.
公眾宣傳是聯合國會議強調的重點事項。
public awareness was among the priorities highlighted at the un meeting.
但要推進這項全球工作，我們需要新的全球機構來負責完成。
to carry out that global effort, however, we need a new global institution that really is up to the task.
NANBU作為一家國際非政府機構，可以從容面對多數跨國製藥企業，並在國內遊說或政治壓力面前得到保護。
nanbu, as an international ngo, would be able to cope with the transnational nature of most drug companies, while being protected from nationallevel lobbying or political pressure.
抗生素耐藥菌是一種全球威脅，因此不能僅靠國內政策加以應對。
antibioticresistant bacteria represent a global threat, and therefore cannot be addressed with national measures alone.
世界各國必須共同思考和行動，以保護抗生素為人類帶來的巨大的健康和福利收益。
the world must think and act together to preserve the huge gains to human health and wellbeing that antibiotics have enabled.
對耐藥性的公平之戰
a fair fight against antimicrobial resistance
布萊頓 — — 現有抗菌藥的效果正在逐漸喪失。
brighton existing antimicrobial drugs are becoming ineffective.
如果任由目前趨勢繼續下去，我們可能重溫抗生素髮明之前坐視感染性疾病成為主要殺手的境況。
if current trends continue, we could end up reliving conditions before the discovery of antibiotics, when infectious diseases were major killers.
迎接耐藥菌發起的挑戰絕非易事，這需要大規模投資研發新的抗菌藥，還要為確保藥物有效性建立起控制及限制新療法的醫療制度。
meeting the challenge of drugresistant microbes will be difficult. it will require not only major investments in research and development of new antimicrobial drugs, but also a system to control and restrict new treatments, in order to preserve their efficacy.
就像應對氣候變化問題一樣，國際協調行動是任何有效策略的基礎。
as with the response to climate change, an effective strategy will require international coordination.
尤其是必須協調藥企 、政府付費機構和全球窮人的關係。
in particular, the needs of pharmaceutical companies must be reconciled with those of government payers and the global poor.
事實上，成功的關鍵在於鼓勵窮人參與。
indeed, engaging the poor will be crucial to any effort.
中低收入國家是耐藥菌的重要滋生地。
low and middleincome countries are an important source of drugresistant organisms.
住房擁擠、衛生條件差和免疫系統受損無論因為營養不良還是HIV等慢性感染，均為傳染病的蔓延提供了肥沃的土壤。
crowded housing, poor sanitation, and compromised immune systems, whether owing to malnutrition or chronic infections such as hiv, provide fertile ground for contagion.
抗生素質量低劣並常被誤用使細菌有了產生耐藥性的機會。
antibiotics are often misused or lowquality, providing bacteria the opportunity to develop resistance.
大量抗生素同時被應用於畜牧業。
large volumes of antibiotics are also used in animal husbandry.
此外，各國農村及城市間顯著改善的交通基礎設施也導致耐藥基因迅速在世界各地傳播。
meanwhile, greatly improved transportation infrastructure between rural and urban areas and between countries means that resistant genes quickly become part of a global pool.
在很多容易感染傳染病的國家，政府的醫療保健系統都無法滿足需求，於是這當中的差距就由從醫療專家到非正規供應商的一系列遊離於監管體系之外的供應商來負責彌補。
in many vulnerable countries, the government healthcare system cannot meet demand, and a variety of providers are attempting to bridge the gap. these range from medical specialists to informal providers, who work largely outside the regulatory framework.
這樣的制度外安排確有好處。
these patchwork systems do have benefits.
例如孟加拉國最近的一項研究表明由租攤經營的所謂“鄉村醫生”所提供的抗生素對降低產後敗血症和兒童肺炎的死亡率都有幫助。
a recent study in bangladesh, for example, concluded that antibiotics provided by socalled village doctors, often operating from market stalls, contributed to declines in mortality from postnatal sepsis and childhood pneumonia.
但也有相當多證據表明所提供藥品質量參差不齊，並且也經常出現濫用。
but there is also considerable evidence that the drugs being provided are of varying quality and are frequently taken unnecessarily.
很多時候患者都未能按療程服藥。
too often, patients do not purchase a full course of treatment.
一種對策是制定並執行立法僅憑醫生處方購買抗生素。
one response could be to enact and enforce laws that make antibiotics available only on a doctors prescription.
但這樣可能嚴重限制窮人獲取抗生素的渠道，提高感染死亡率，因此既難以執行又在政治上無法接受。
however, this could end up severely limiting poor peoples access to antibiotics, leading to higher death rates from infections, making it politically unacceptable and thus difficult to enforce.
替代方法是制定透過非正式渠道改善抗生素治療的新策略。
a better alternative would be to develop new strategies to improve antibiotic treatments that are provided through informal channels.
首先要投資獲取常見抗感染藥的可靠監測資料。
for starters, investment is needed to generate reliable surveillance data on the drugs that are effective against common infections.
治療指引必須涵蓋上述資訊，並將其分發給所有抗生素供應者。
treatment guidelines must incorporate this information and be given to all providers of antibiotics.
此外，必須以合理價格提供高質量的抗生素。
meanwhile, highquality antibiotics must be made available at affordable prices.
必須從市場上消除假冒產品，並在政府、藥企和公民團體間建立合作監管機制來控制質量。
counterfeit products must be identified and removed from the marketplace, and a regulatory partnership between governments, the pharmaceutical sector, and citizens groups must be developed to control for quality.
必須透過批次採購等方式以確保藥品低價；在某些情況下，可能有必要發放公共補貼。
prices must be kept low through bulk procurement in some cases, public subsidies may be necessary.
降價措施需要配合有關規定來防止濫用。
measures to reduce prices will need to be complemented by efforts to discourage overuse.
推出全療程組合藥物創新包裝可以簡化治療決策。
innovations in packaging, perhaps providing full courses of appropriate combinations of drugs, could simplify treatment decisions.
同樣，發展低成本診斷技術可以減少僅以症狀為依據的治療需求。
likewise, development of lowcost diagnostic technologies could help diminish the need to provide treatment on the basis of symptoms alone.
最大的挑戰是鼓勵抗生素供應商改變其行為。
the biggest challenge will be to encourage providers of antibiotics to change their behavior.
這需要認證、修改支付機制和鼓勵中介機構參與提供技術支援並監控效果。
this will require measures such as accreditation, modification of payment mechanisms, and the involvement of intermediary organizations to give technical support and monitor performance.
上述機構可以包括非政府組織、宗教機構、社會企業家和藥物分銷企業。
these organizations could include ngos, religious organizations, social entrepreneurs, and companies that distribute drugs.
這些活動不太可能取得商業利益，因此政府、慈善機構和藥品生產商的支援就變得十分必要。
these activities are unlikely to be commercially sustainable, and thus will require support from governments, philanthropies, and perhaps drug producers.
與此同時，必須將正確使用抗生素的可靠資訊和建議傳達給公眾。
in the meantime, the public must receive reliable information and advice on the proper use of antibiotics.
如果民眾大都依賴自身資源來應對疾病這一點就顯得尤為重要。
this is particularly important where citizens rely largely on their own resources to cope with health problems.
落實系統化的抗生素應用改革需要建立國家和全球聯盟。
implementing a systemwide change in the use of antibiotics will require the creation of national and global coalitions.
必須以制定反映患者和社團需求的醫療工作者和藥企基本行為準則為核心目標。
one core aim must be to establish basic standards of conduct for health workers and drug companies that reflect the needs of patients and communities.
政府必須在此過程中發揮有效作用；研製、生產和銷售藥物和診斷技術的企業將積極探索促進合作。
governments will need to build their capacity to play an effective role in this process, and companies that develop, produce, and distribute drugs and diagnostic technologies will have to contribute actively to the search for collaborative solutions.
人類從中受益的前提是必須以公正、可持續的方式管理抗生素。
only if we manage antiobiotics in a fair and sustainable way will we be able to benefit from them at all.
民粹主義的反民主之心
the antidemocratic heart of populism
聖地亞哥 — — 參加國際貨幣基金組織10月初年度會議的代表普遍認為 ： “ 假設共和黨人不顧性騷擾和侮辱性言論提名了像特朗普這樣的反貿易主義者，就有可能導致民粹保護主義者入主白宮。
santiago many of the men and women who turned out for the annual meeting of the international monetary fund in early october were saying something like this imagine if the republicans had nominated someone with the same antitrade views as trump, minus the insults and the sexual harassment.
”
a populist protectionist would be headed to the white house.
弦外之音是美國和歐洲的左右翼民粹主義勢力崛起是全球化及其負面影響的直接後果：相關負面影響包括失業和中產階級收入停滯。
the underlying view is that rising populism on the right and the left, both in the united states and in europe, is a straightforward consequence of globalization and its unwanted effects lost jobs and stagnant middleclass incomes.
達沃斯的與會代表不喜歡這個結論，但他們卻以皈依者般的熱情接受了它。
davos men and women hate this conclusion, but they have embraced it with all the fervor of new converts.
但還有另一種更具說服力的觀點：雖然經濟停滯可以助推選民進入民粹主義陣營，但經濟形勢低迷不是政治混亂的必要和充分條件。
yet there is an alternative and more persuasive view while economic stagnation helps push upset voters into the populist camp, bad economics is neither a necessary nor a sufficient condition for bad politics.
恰恰相反，普林斯頓大學政治學家穆勒在其新著中提出：民粹主義是代議制民主“永遠無法擺脫的陰影 ” 。
on the contrary, argues princeton political scientist janwerner mueller in his new book populism is a permanent shadow on representative democracy.
民粹主義的本質不是稅收（也不是就業或收入平等 ） 。
populism is not about taxation or jobs or income inequality.
它的本質是代表權 — — 誰能以何種形式代表民眾說話。
it is about representation who gets to speak for the people and how.
民主倡導者往往為民主高唱讚歌。
advocates of democracy make some exalted claims on its behalf.
比如亞伯拉罕·林肯在葛底斯堡提出“民有、民治、民享的政府。
as abraham lincoln put it at gettysburg, it is government of the people, by the people, for the people.
”但現代代議制民主 — — 或者任何一種民主 — — 都難免不符合這樣的說法。
but modern representative democracy or any democracy, for that matter inevitably falls short of these claims.
四年一次在大選中為黨派機器確定的候選人投票很難讓人聯想起林肯高談闊論的內容。
voting in an election every four years for candidates chosen by party machines is not exactly what lincolns lofty words call to mind.
穆勒提出，民粹主義者的目標是實現義大利民主理論家貝爾託·波比奧所謂破碎的民主承諾。 穆勒稱民粹主義者的言行“就像民眾可以達成一致共識 ， . . .
what populists offer, mueller says, is to fulfill what the italian democratic theorist norberto bobbio calls the broken promises of democracy.
就像他們是一個人那樣 ， . . . 就像只要民眾選出合適的代表，就可以把命運牢牢控制在自己的手中。
populists speak and act, claims mueller, as if the people could develop a singular judgment,...as if the people were one,...as if the people, if only they empowered the right representatives, could fully master their fates.
民粹主義的基礎是有毒三元組：否定複雜性、反多元主義和扭曲代表形式。
populism rests on a toxic triad denial of complexity, antipluralism, and a crooked version of representation.
我們多數人都認為社會選擇非常複雜，對今後措施存在不同的看法是自然和合理的。
most of us believe that social choices build more schools or hospitals?
但民粹主義者卻否認這一點。
stimulate or discourage international trade?
正如拉爾夫·達倫多夫曾經說過的那樣，民粹主義是簡單；而民主是複雜。
liberalize or restrict abortion? are complex, and that the existence of a plurality of views about what to do is both natural and legitimate. populists deny this.
在民粹主義者看來，只有一種正確的觀點 — — 那就是民眾的看法。
as ralf dahrendorf once put it, populism is simple democracy is complex. to populists, there is only one right view that of the people.
如果真的如此，自由民主的複雜機制及其對授權和代表性的強調都是不必要的。
if so, the complex mechanisms of liberal democracy, with its emphasis on delegation and representation, are all unnecessary.
議會不需要無休無止的辯論：民眾的統一意志可以輕易地以一次統一投票的形式表達。
no need for parliaments endlessly debating the unitary will of the people can easily be expressed in a single vote.
因此民粹主義者熱衷於公民投票。
hence populists love affair with plebiscites and referenda.
英國脫歐，還記得嗎？
brexit, anyone?
不是隨便哪個人都可以代表民眾。
and not just anyone can represent the people.
他們宣揚絕對代表。
the claim is to exclusive representation.
還記不記得特朗普在共和黨全國代表大會上的自吹自擂 ： “ 我靠一己之力就可以解決它。 ”
remember trumps boast in his address to the republican national convention i alone can fix it.
亞里士多德告訴我們，政治永遠關乎道德。
politics is always about morality, aristotle told us.
但民粹主義者喜歡穆勒所謂特定的政治道德解讀。
but populists favor what mueller calls a particular moralistic interpretation of politics.
那些對世界看法正確的人是道德的；其他人都是腐敗政治精英的走狗，因此都不道德。
those who hold the right view about the world are moral the rest are immoral, lackeys of a corrupt elite.
這恰恰是委內瑞拉統治者烏戈·查韋斯宣揚的觀點。
that was exactly the rhetoric of the late venezuelan ruler hugo chvez.
他那一套失敗後，查韋斯將國家經濟搞糟後反正可以把責任推到美帝國主義身上。
when that failed, and when chvezs sank his countrys economy, there was always us imperialism to blame.
因此民粹主義是一種身份政治。
so populism is a kind of identity politics.
其本質是我們反對他們。
it is always us against them.
從這個角度看，民粹主義並非技術官僚和精英發現的對民主的有效矯正，就像馬琳·勒龐、拉斐爾·科雷亞、雷德普·塔伊普·埃爾多安或形形色色的西方知識分子希望你相信的那樣。
viewed in this light, populism is not a useful corrective to a democracy captured by technocrats and elites, as marine le pen, rafael correa, recep tayyip erdoan, or assorted western intellectuals want you to believe.
恰恰相反，它本質上具有反民主色彩，因此能夠威脅到民主本身。
on the contrary, it is profoundly antidemocratic, and hence a threat to democracy itself.
那麼我們該怎麼做？
what is to be done?
我的處方（不是穆勒的，而是我的）是民主派必須（而且能夠）在他們擅長的領域擊敗民粹主義者。
my take the prescription is my own, not muellers is that democrats must and can beat populists at their own game.
有毒三元組可以轉化為有益的元素。
the toxic triad can become salutary.
首先必須承認局勢的複雜性。
first, acknowledge complexity.
讓選民像被欺騙一樣厭惡的只有一件事：就是像對孩子一樣對他們。
the only thing that upsets voters as much as being lied to is being treated like babies.
艱辛生活的民眾必須知道世界是複雜的。
people who lead challenging lives know that the world is complex.
他們並不介意有人這樣說。
they do not mind being told that.
他們本來就是成年人，應當以成年人的方式同他們對話。
they appreciate being spoken to as the grownups they are.
其次，不要將多種觀點和身份當作需要解決的技術性問題。
second, do not treat diversity of views and identities as a problem calling for a technocratic solution.
相反，尊重上述多樣性符合社會深層次道德特徵的要求。
rather, make respect for such diversity a profoundly moral feature of society.
事實上，我們並不完全相同但我們可以和平共處是一項偉大的民主成就。
the fact that we are not all the same and we can still get along is a tremendous democratic achievement.
我們應當大力宣傳它。
make the case for it.
不要相信令人厭倦的陳詞濫調，認為民粹主義者才訴諸情感，而民主派必須是理智的。
and do not fall for the tired clich that reason is for democrats and emotion is for populists.
我們必須以激發情感的方式來宣傳多元化民主。
make the case for pluralistic democracy in a way that inspires and stirs emotion.
第三，捍衛 — — 並且升級 — — 代議制。
third, defend and update representation.
僅在複雜的技術性事務中利用委託。
leave delegation to complex technical matters.
利用現代技術讓其他選擇 — — 特別是貼近日常生活的選擇 — — 更貼近於投票者。
take advantage of modern technologies to bring other choices particularly those having to do with the fabric of daily life closer to voters.
收緊競選融資法律、更嚴格地規範遊說並推進平權行動以確保代表來自民眾併為民眾服務。
tighten campaign finance laws, regulate lobbying better, and enforce affirmativeaction measures to ensure that representatives are of the people and work for the people.
僅靠採取上述措施，還無法確保實現民主所有的破碎承諾。
these measures alone will not ensure that all of democracys broken promises are fulfilled.
但我們不能期望靠一系列簡單行動來解決複雜問題。
but we cannot expect a single set of simple actions to solve a complex problem.
我們也不能認為僅靠一己之力就可以解決它。
nor can we believe that we alone can fix it.
如果我們這麼認為，我們就成了民粹主義者。
if we believed that, we would be populists.
為了保護民主，這恰恰是我們應當避免的。
for the sake of democracy, that is precisely what we should not be.
左派的退位
the abdication of the left
隆達，西班牙 — — 隨著世界在英國退歐的餘波衝擊下動盪，經濟學家和決策者漸漸明白他們嚴重低估了現有全球化形勢的脆弱程度。
ronda, spain as the world reels from the brexit shock, it is dawning on economists and policymakers that they severely underestimated the political fragility of the current form of globalization.
正在席捲全球的民眾反抗浪潮採取的形式相互重疊而多樣化：重新強調地方和國家身份、要求加強民主控制和問責、拒絕中間政黨和不信任精英與專家。
the popular revolt that appears to be underway is taking diverse, overlapping forms reassertion of local and national identities, demand for greater democratic control and accountability, rejection of centrist political parties, and distrust of elites and experts.
出現這樣的反彈是可以預見的。
this backlash was predictable.
某些經濟學家，包括我本人在內，的確警告過在現有的管理、穩定及合法化市場制度的邊界以外推進經濟全球化的後果。
some economists, including me, did warn about the consequences of pushing economic globalization beyond the boundaries of institutions that regulate, stabilize, and legitimize markets.
金融貿易超級全球化本意是創造無縫銜接的世界市場，但卻撕裂了國內社會。
hyperglobalization in trade and finance, intended to create seamlessly integrated world markets, tore domestic societies apart.
更出人意料的是人們果斷採取了右傾的政治對策。
the bigger surprise is the decidedly rightwing tilt the political reaction has taken.
歐洲各國主要是民族主義者和本土民粹主義者顯露崢嶸，而左翼只在希臘和西班牙等少數地區有所斬獲。
in europe, it is predominantly nationalists and nativist populists that have risen to prominence, with the left advancing only in a few places such as greece and spain.
美國右翼煽動家唐納德·特朗普成功地取代了共和黨當權派，而左翼份子伯尼·桑德斯卻未能打敗中間派的希拉里·克林頓。
in the united states, the rightwing demagogue donald trump has managed to displace the republican establishment, while the leftist bernie sanders was unable to overtake the centrist hillary clinton.
正在崛起的新興當權派極不情願的達成共識：全球化加劇了階級分裂，拉大了有資源和有能力利用世界市場者和不具備上述能力者之間的鴻溝。
as an emerging new establishment consensus grudgingly concedes, globalization accentuates class divisions between those who have the skills and resources to take advantage of global markets and those who dont.
收入和階級分化，相對於以種族、民族或宗教身份為基礎的分化，傳統上會強化左翼政治勢力。
income and class cleavages, in contrast to identity cleavages based on race, ethnicity, or religion, have traditionally strengthened the political left.
那麼左翼勢力究竟為什麼沒能實現政治挑戰全球化？
so why has the left been unable to mount a significant political challenge to globalization?
答案之一是其他全球化“衝擊”被移民問題掩蓋了。
one answer is that immigration has overshadowed other globalization shocks.
人們感受到來自文化傳統截然不同的貧困國家的大批移民和難民湧入加劇了身份分化，而極右翼政客可以駕輕就熟地利用這樣的現狀。
the perceived threat of mass inflows of migrants and refugees from poor countries with very different cultural traditions aggravates identity cleavages that farright politicians are exceptionally well placed to exploit.
因此從特朗普到馬琳·勒龐等右翼政治家在重新確立國家地位的主張中摻入大量反穆斯林象徵主義也就毫不奇怪了。
so it is not a surprise that rightist politicians from trump to marine le pen lace their message of national reassertion with a rich dose of antimuslim symbolism.
拉美民主國家提供了一種很能說明問題的對照。
latin american democracies provide a telling contrast.
全球化在上述國家主要表現為貿易和外資衝擊，而不是移民衝擊。
these countries experienced globalization mostly as a trade and foreigninvestment shock, rather than as an immigration shock.
全球化幾乎等同於所謂的華盛頓共識政策和金融開放。
globalization became synonymous with socalled washington consensus policies and financial opening.
中東和非洲移民問題仍十分有限，在政治上並不突出。
immigration from the middle east or africa remained limited and had little political salience.
因此在巴西、玻利維亞、厄瓜多和最具災難性的委內瑞拉等拉美國家，民粹主義迴歸是以左翼形式完成的。
so the populist backlash in latin america in brazil, bolivia, ecuador, and, most disastrously, venezuela took a leftwing form.
歐洲右翼迴歸的兩個主要除外特例 — — 希臘和西班牙 — — 情況是類似的。
the story is similar in the main two exceptions to rightwing resurgence in europe greece and spain.
在希臘，主要的政治斷點是歐洲機構和國際貨幣基金組織所強制推行的緊縮政策。
in greece, the main political fault line has been austerity policies imposed by european institutions and the international monetary fund.
而在西班牙，直到不久前多數移民還來自文化相似的拉美國家。
in spain, most immigrants until recently came from culturally similar latin american countries.
極右翼勢力在其他地方快速發展的溫床在上述兩國都是不存在的。
in both countries, the far right lacked the breeding ground it had elsewhere.
但拉美和南歐的狀況或許暴露了左翼勢力一個更大的弱點：那就是缺少重塑21世紀資本主義和全球化的明確計劃。
but the experience in latin america and southern europe reveals perhaps a greater weakness of the left the absence of a clear program to refashion capitalism and globalization for the twentyfirst century.
從希臘的激進左翼聯盟到巴西工黨，左翼勢力除收入轉移等改良政策外，都未能提出經濟上可行且政治上受歡迎的想法。
from greeces syriza to brazils workers party, the left has failed to come up with ideas that are economically sound and politically popular, beyond ameliorative policies such as income transfers.
所以經濟學家和技術官僚很大程度上要為此負責。
economists and technocrats on the left bear a large part of the blame.
他們不僅沒能為左翼改革計劃作出貢獻，反而很輕易地讓位給市場原教旨主義並全盤接受了其核心原則。
instead of contributing to such a program, they abdicated too easily to market fundamentalism and bought in to its central tenets.
更糟的是，他們在關鍵時間節點領導了超全球化運動。
worse still, they led the hyperglobalization movement at crucial junctures.
歐盟、經合組織和國際貨幣基金組織將資本自由流動 — — 尤其是短期資本流動 — — 奉為政策標準可能是近幾十年來對全球經濟最致命的政策。
the enthroning of free capital mobility especially of the shortterm kind as a policy norm by the european union, the organization for economic cooperation and development, and the imf was arguably the most fateful decision for the global economy in recent decades.
哈佛商學院教授艾儒蔚（ Rawi Abdelal）已經證明，20世紀80年代末及90年代初推動這項工作的不是自由市場理論者，而是像（歐盟委員會）雅克·德洛爾和（經合組織）亨利·沙夫蘭斯基這樣與法國社會黨有緊密聯絡的法國技術官僚。
as harvard business school professor rawi abdelal has shown, this effort was spearheaded in the late 1980s and early 1990s not by freemarket ideologues, but by french technocrats such as jacques delors at the european commission and henri chavranski at the oecd, who were closely associated with the socialist party in france.
同樣，在美國完成這項工作的是與親凱恩斯主義民主黨有關的勞倫斯·薩默斯等大力推進放鬆金融管制的技術官僚。
similarly, in the us, it was technocrats associated with the more keynesian democratic party, such as lawrence summers, who led the charge for financial deregulation.
法國社會黨技術官僚似乎從20世紀80年代初密特朗未能成功的凱恩斯主義試驗中得出結論，認為國內經濟管理任務是不可能完成的，而且沒有其他真正的措施能夠取代金融全球化。
frances socialist technocrats appear to have concluded from the failed mitterrand experiment with keynesianism in the early 1980s that domestic economic management was no longer possible, and that there was no real alternative to financial globalization.
能夠遵循的最佳路線圖是制定歐洲及全球規則，而不是坐視德美等強國強制推行他們自己的規則。
the best that could be done was to enact europewide and global rules, instead of allowing powerful countries like germany or the us to impose their own.
好訊息是左翼學術真空正在得到填補，現在已經沒有任何理由相信“沒有其他選擇”的專制舉措。
the good news is that the intellectual vacuum on the left is being filled, and there is no longer any reason to believe in the tyranny of no alternatives.
左翼政界人士越來越沒有理由不去借鑑“可敬的”經濟學學術力量。
politicians on the left have less and less reason not to draw on respectable academic firepower in economics.
舉幾個例子：安娜特·阿德馬蒂和西蒙·約翰遜一貫主張激進的銀行改革；托馬斯·皮克特和託尼·阿特金森提出了各式各樣的針對國內不平等的政策；馬里亞納·馬祖卡託和張夏準開創性地指出調動公共部門以促進包容性創新的方法； 約瑟夫·斯蒂格利茨和何塞·安東尼奧·奧坎波共同提出了全球改革；布拉德·迪隆、傑弗裡·薩克斯和勞倫斯·薩默斯（就是同一個人！ ）呼籲對基礎設施和綠色經濟領域進行長期公共投資。
consider just a few examples anat admati and simon johnson have advocated radical banking reforms thomas piketty and tony atkinson have proposed a rich menu of policies to deal with inequality at the national level mariana mazzucato and hajoon chang have written insightfully on how to deploy the public sector to foster inclusive innovation joseph stiglitz and jos antonio ocampo have proposed global reforms brad delong, jeffrey sachs, and lawrence summers the very same! have argued for longterm public investment in infrastructure and the green economy.
已經有足夠的元素供左翼人士在制定綱領性經濟對策時使用。
there are enough elements here for building a programmatic economic response from the left.
左右翼勢力最關鍵的差別在於社會越分裂右翼越壯大 — — 右翼奉行“我們”和“他們”的邏輯 — — 而左翼如果取得成功卻能透過彌合鴻溝的改革來消除社會分裂。
a crucial difference between the right and the left is that the right thrives on deepening divisions in society us versus them while the left, when successful, overcomes these cleavages through reforms that bridge them.
因此才有了早期左翼改革（凱恩斯主義、社會民主主義和福利國家政策 ） — —所產生的悖論，在拯救資本主義的同時卻讓自身成為多餘的。
hence the paradox that earlier waves of reforms from the left keynesianism, social democracy, the welfare state both saved capitalism from itself and effectively rendered themselves superfluous.
如果再不出現這樣的對策，民粹主義者和極右翼團體就會趁虛而入，他們將像以前那樣領導世界，而他們的領導只能加劇分裂和引發更多衝突。
absent such a response again, the field will be left wide open for populists and farright groups, who will lead the world as they always have to deeper division and more frequent conflict.
新愚人社會主義
the new socialism of fools
伯克利—根據主流經濟學理論，全球化會“讓所有船都浮起來 ” ， 而對於廣義收入分配，幾乎沒有影響。
berkeley according to mainstream economic theory, globalization tends to lift all boats, and has little effect on the broad distribution of incomes.
但“全球化”並不只是取消關稅和其他讓本國有政治影響力的生產商擁有尋租優勢的進口壁壘。
but globalization is not the same as the elimination of tariffs and other import barriers that confer rentseeking advantages to politically influential domestic producers.
哈佛大學經濟學家丹尼·羅德里克（Dani Rodrik）頻繁指出，經濟學理論預測，消除關稅和非關稅壁壘確實會帶來淨收益；但也會造成大規模再分配，其中消除較小壁壘所帶來的再分配相對淨收益更大。
as harvard university economist dani rodrik frequently points out, economic theory predicts that removing tariffs and nontariff barriers does produce net gains but it also results in large redistributions, wherein eliminating smaller barriers yields larger redistributions relative to the net gains.
出於目的的不同，全球化也有所不同。
globalization, for our purposes, is different.
它應該被理解為一個過程，在這個過程中，減小運輸和通訊成本的技術進步讓世界變得日益聯動。
it should be understood as a process in which the world becomes increasingly interconnected through technological advances that drive down transportation and communication costs.
誠然，這種形式的全球化讓外國生產商以更低的成本向遙遠的市場出口商品和服務。
to be sure, this form of globalization allows foreign producers to export goods and services to distant markets at a lower cost.
但它也為另一方開啟了出口市場，降低了成本。
but it also opens up export markets and reduces costs for the other side.
最終，消費者以更少的前買到了更多的東西。
and at the end of the day, consumers get more stuff for less.
根據標準經濟學理論，只有在一國的出口所需要的生產要素與其進口截然不同時，才會發生再分配。
according to standard economic theory, redistribution only comes about when a countrys exports require vastly different factors of production than its imports.
但當今全球經濟中並不具備這樣的不同。
but there are no such differences in todays global economy.
在美國，金融收支盈餘意味著更多的美國人從事建築工人、資本品生產者和護士和家庭健康助手等工作。
in the united states, a balanceofpayments surplus in finance means that more americans will be employed as construction workers, capitalgoods producers, and nurses and home health aides.
類似地，服務業盈餘意味著較多的美國人不僅僅在鋼筋玻璃幕牆大廈裡從事高學歷（和高薪）的諮詢工作，也在黃石國家公園外的汽車旅館裡當門衛和清潔工。
similarly, a surplus in services means that more americans will work not only as highly educated and wellremunerated consultants in steelandglass eyries, but also as, say, janitors and housekeepers in motels outside of yellowstone national park.
與此同時，製造業赤字可能給勞動力成本相對資本較低的國家制造更多的海外製造業崗位；但它並沒有毀掉多少美國的就業，因為美國製造業已經是一個資本密集程度很高的行業。
at the same time, a deficit in manufacturing may create more manufacturing jobs abroad, in countries where labor costs are low relative to capital but it destroys relatively few jobs in the us, where manufacturing is already a highly capitalintensive industry.
斯坦福大學經濟學家羅伯特·霍爾（Robert Hall）三十年來一直在強調，在美國，汽車銷售員比製造汽車的工人數量更多。
as stanford university economist robert hall has been pointing out for three decades, more americans are employed selling cars than making them.
美國從國外進口的商品需要大量技能相對較低的勞動力生產，但他們並不會大量取代美國的低技能勞動力。
the commodities that the us imports from abroad embody a significant amount of relatively unskilled labor, but they do not displace much unskilled labor in america.
因此，至少在理論上，美國就業從流水線製造業轉向建築業、服務業和護理業可能對性別間的總體收入分配形成了而一些影響，但對階級收入分配來說並沒有。
so, at least in theory, the shift in us employment from assemblyline manufacturing to construction, services, and caretaking may have had an impact on the overall distribution of income in terms of gender, but not in terms of class.
那麼，二十一世紀為什麼還有那麼強烈的抵制全球化的情緒？
why, then, has there been such strong political resistance to globalization in the twentyfirst century?
我看到了四個原因。
i see four reasons.
首先也是最重要的是，政客將國家的問題歸咎於外國人和沒有投票權的移民是很容易的。
first and foremost, it is easy for politicians to pin the blame for a countrys problems on foreigners and immigrants who do not vote.
1890年，哈布斯堡帝國的政治家們就慣於將各種社會經濟病歸咎於猶太人。 奧地利異見者費迪南·克羅納維特（Ferdinand Kronawetter）有一個著名的觀察 ： “ Der Antisemitismus ist der Sozialismus der dummen Kerle ” ， 即反猶是愚人社會主義。
back in 1890, when politicians in the habsburg empire routinely blamed jews for various socioeconomic ills, the austrian dissident ferdinand kronawetter famously observed that der antisemitismus ist der sozialismus der dummen kerle antisemitism is the socialism of fools.
今天的反全球化也是如此。
the same could be said of antiglobalization today.
其次，全球北方國家一代人以來的既不公平，又不及預期的經濟增長，造就了強烈的政治和心理需要，必須找到替罪羊。
second, more than a generation of inequitable and slowerthanexpected economic growth in the global north has created a strong political and psychological need for scapegoats.
人們想要一個簡單的敘事來解釋為何他們沒有趕上曾經蝴蝶許諾的繁榮，以及為何越來越富有的卓越階級和其他人之間的差距這麼大，並且還在不斷擴大。
people want a simple narrative to explain why they are missing out on the prosperity they were once promised, and why there is such a large and growing gap between an increasingly wealthy overclass and everyone else.
第三，中國的經濟崛起恰逢全球北方國家難以實現充分就業的時期。
third, chinas economic rise coincided with a period in which the global north was struggling to reach full employment.
與哈耶克和安德魯· 梅隆（Andrew Mellon）的追隨者們經常宣稱的相反，經濟再調整（readjustments）並沒有發生在破產迫使勞動力和資本退出低生產率、低需求的行業時，而是發生在繁榮將勞動力和資本推向高生產率、高需求的行業時。
contrary to what the followers of friedrich von hayek and andrew mellon have always claimed, economic readjustments do not happen when bankruptcies force labor and capital out of lowproductivity, lowdemand industries, but rather when booms pull labor and capital into highproductivity, highdemand industries.
因此，新自由主義不但要求開放和競爭的市場、全球變革以及價格穩定。
thus, neoliberalism does not just require open and competitive markets, global change, and price stability.
它依賴於充分就業和幾乎永恆的繁榮，一如經濟學家凱恩斯在20世紀二三十年代所警告的那樣。
it also depends on full employment and nearpermanent booms, just as economist john maynard keynes had warned in the 1920s and 1930s.
在最近幾十年中，新自由主義秩序沒有實現其中的任何一個條件，最有可能的原因是，即使最優秀的政客在臺上，也不可能實現這些條件。
in recent decades, the neoliberal order failed to deliver either condition, most likely because doing so would have been impossible even with the best policies in place.
第四，決策者沒有用更激進的社會政策和經濟和地理再分配來足夠多地補償這一失敗。
fourth, policymakers did not do enough to compensate for this failure with more aggressive social policies and economic and geographic redistribution.
美國總統特朗普最近告訴紐約北部居民，他們應該離開該地區，去別處找工作，這無非是全球北方國家過去一代政客們的老生常談。
when us president donald trump recently told upstate new yorkers that they should leave the region and seek jobs elsewhere, he was simply echoing the past generation of centerright politicians in the global north.
全球北方國家當前的政治和經濟困境與20世紀二三十年代並沒有很大的不同。
the global norths current political and economic dilemmas are not so different from those of the 1920s and 1930s.
當時，凱恩斯就指出，關鍵在於創造和維持充分就業，這樣，大部分其他問題自然就能解決。
as keynes noted then, the key is to produce and maintain full employment, at which point most other problems will melt away.
而奧地利-匈牙利經濟學家卡爾·波蘭尼（Karl Planyi）指出，保護社會經濟權利是政府的角色。
and, as the austrohungarian economist karl polanyi argued, it is the role of government to secure socioeconomic rights.
人們認為他們有權利生活在健康的社會中，擁有穩定的工作，獲得一份隨時間不斷增加的體面收入。
people believe that they have a right to live in healthy communities, hold stable occupations, and earn a decent income that rises over time.
但這些假定的權利並不是財產權利和稀缺資源權利 — — 即新自由主義的的通貨 — — 的應有之義。
but these presumed rights do not stem naturally from property rights and claims to scarce resources the coins of the neoliberal realm.
全球金融危機和全球北方國家發生“大衰退”已經過去了十年。
it has been ten years since the global financial crisis and the start of the great recession in the global north.
政府仍然沒有修復這些事件所造成的傷害。
governments still have not repaired the damage from those events.
如果它們不盡快修復的話，愚人“XX主義”將在未來幾十年中不斷地造成嚴重破壞。
if they do not do so soon, the isms of fools will continue to wreak havoc in the decades ahead.
移民和新階級分化
immigration and the new class divide
新加坡 — — 英國的歐洲事務影子大臣帕特·麥克法登最近警告工黨黨員他們應該儘可能去接納全球經濟，而不要像對待瘟疫一樣對移民問題避之唯恐不及。
singapore the british shadow minister for europe, pat mcfadden, recently warned members of his labour party that they should try to make the most of the global economy and not treat immigration like a disease.
如他所言 ， “ 你可以從別人的痛苦中尋找滿足感，也可以給別人一個機會。
as he put it, you can feed on peoples grievances or you can give people a chance.
我認為我們的政策應當著重於給別人機會。 ”
and i think our policies should be around giving people a chance.
在這個被針對移民、銀行家、穆斯林 、 “ 自由派精英 ” 、 “歐盟官員 ” 、 世界主義者或哪怕僅有些許陌生的任何事物的不滿所佔據的世界裡，像這樣明智的看法已經十分罕有。
in a world increasingly dominated by grievances against immigrants, bankers, muslims, liberal elites, eurocrats, cosmopolitans, or anything else that seems vaguely alien such wise words are rare.
世界各國領袖應該多加聽取。
leaders worldwide should take note.
在美國，由茶黨活動分子支援的共和黨正威脅要關閉政府，理由僅僅因為奧巴馬總統為已經在美工作生活多年的非法移民提供了獲得公民身份的機會。
in the united states, republicans backed by their tea party activists are threatening to close the government down just because president barack obama has offered undocumented immigrants who have lived and worked in the us for many years a chance to gain citizenship.
英國獨立黨（UKIP）正力推一項計劃，在五年內禁止移民取得永久定居資格。
the united kingdom independence party ukip wants to introduce a fiveyear ban on immigration for permanent settlement.
俄羅斯副總理羅戈津曾經公佈了一段影片承諾要將垃圾從莫斯科“清理”出去 — — 他把主要來自前蘇聯加盟共和國的外來務工者稱之為垃圾。
russias deputy prime minister, dmitry rogozin, once released a video promising to clean the rubbish meaning migrant workers, mostly from former soviet republics away from moscow.
就連曾以寬容聞名的荷蘭和丹麥人都越來越多地投票給主張嚴懲移民的黨派。
even the once famously tolerant dutch and danes are increasingly voting for parties that fulminate against the scourge of immigration.
一貫主張可以自由侮辱穆斯林的荷蘭自由黨想要禁止所有的清真寺。
always keen to assert the freedom to insult muslims, the dutch freedom party wants to ban all mosques.
就連新加坡勢單力薄且備受騷擾的反對黨 — — 新加坡幾乎人人都是移民的後代 — — 都從迎合民眾對於移民（主要是中印移民）的不滿中汲取動力，人們認為這些移民從“本地人”手中搶走了工作機會。
and the tiny and muchharassed opposition parties in singapore a country where almost everyone is descended from immigrants are gaining traction by appealing to popular gripes about immigrants mostly from india and china who are supposedly taking jobs from natives.
美國茶黨狂熱份子、俄國沙文主義者、憂心忡忡的荷蘭和丹麥人以及新加坡左翼人士究竟有哪些共同訴求推動著這樣的反移民情緒？
what can american tea party enthusiasts, russian chauvinists, fearful dutch and danes, and singaporean leftists possibly have in common that is driving this antiimmigrant sentiment?
在經濟緊縮環境中保住工作無疑是一個嚴重的問題。
retaining ones job in a tightening economy is undoubtedly a serious concern.
但窮苦的墨西哥移民幾乎沒有威脅到支援茶黨的多數美國中年鄉村白人的生計。
but the livelihoods of most of the middleaged rural white americans who support the tea party are hardly threatened by poor mexican migrants.
英國獨立黨受歡迎的某些區域移民非常罕見。
ukip is popular in some parts of england where immigrants are rarely seen.
而許多荷蘭自由黨選民的住所並不靠近任何清真寺。
and many of the dutch freedom partys voters live nowhere near a mosque.
反移民情緒不受傳統左右翼分界的限制。
antiimmigrant sentiment cuts across the old leftright divide.
茶黨或英國自由黨支持者與真正擔心被低薪外國人搶走工作的工薪階層選民唯一的共同點是害怕跟不上迅速變化、由超國家機構主導的全球網路化世界的焦慮。
one thing tea party or ukip supporters share with workingclass voters who genuinely fear losing their jobs to lowpaid foreigners is anxiety about being left behind in a world of easy mobility, supranational organizations, and global networking.
在右翼領域，對保守黨派的支援在移民或超國家機構受益者的商業利益和受威脅團體間發生割裂。
on the right, support for conservative parties is split between business interests that benefit from immigration or supranational institutions, and groups that feel threatened by them.
從中可以找到英國保守黨如此害怕自由黨的解釋。
that is why the british tories are so afraid of ukip.
相比於經濟發展，英國自由黨領袖法拉奇更關注宣揚他的極端民族獨立。
nigel farage, ukips leader, is less concerned with economic growth than with pursuing his extreme conception of national independence.
而在左翼領域，反對種族主義及狹隘情緒者和想要保住飯碗和本土工薪階層殘存“團結”者所持的意見發生了分歧。
on the left, opinion is split between those who oppose racism and intolerance above all and those who want to protect employment and preserve solidarity for what is left of the nativeborn working class.
將移民問題所引發的焦慮僅僅視為對全球化經濟的偏見和憂慮並歸結為反動情緒而置之不理無疑是一種錯失。
it would be a mistake to dismiss anxiety about immigration as mere bigotry or apprehension about the globalized economy as simply reactionary.
民族、宗教和文化特徵（這裡缺少更準確的形容詞）正在發生轉變，雖然轉變的動力與其說是移民還不如說是不斷發展的全球化資本主義。
national, religious, and cultural identities for lack of a better word are being transformed, though less by immigration than by the development of globalized capitalism.
在新的全球經濟中，輸家和贏家都非常明確。
in the new global economy, there are clear winners and losers.
有能力在各種國際場合有效溝通的受過教育的男性和女性無疑是受益者。
educated men and women who can communicate effectively in varied international contexts are benefiting.
而缺乏必要教育或經歷的人 — — 這種人大有人在 — — 在苦苦地掙扎求助。
people who lack the needed education or experience and there are many of them are struggling.
換言之，新一輪階級分化無關貧富差異，而更多傾向於受過教育的都市精英和沒那麼世故、靈活，並且在各方面關係也沒那��豐富的鄉下人的區別。
in other words, the new class divisions run less between the rich and the poor than between educated metropolitan elites and less sophisticated, less flexible, and, in every sense, less connected provincials.
鄉下人的政治領袖（及其支持者）有時比他們所痛恨的都市精英更加富有並不能改變什麼。
it is irrelevant that the provincials political leaders and their backers are sometimes wealthier than the resented metropolitan elites.
他們仍然感到被人看不起。
they still feel looked down upon.
因此他們像所有被撲朔迷離而又令人迷惑的世界排除在外的人一樣滿懷仇恨和痛苦。
and so they share the bitterness of those who feel alienated in a world they find bewildering and hateful.
民粹主義煽動者想要挑起這樣的仇恨，痛罵那些為微薄收入賣命或者根本不工作的外國人。
populist rabblerousers like to stir up such resentments by ranting about foreigners who work for a pittance or not at all.
但其實更令本土民眾沮喪的是少數族裔和移民的相對成功。
but it is the relative success of ethnic minorities and immigrants that is more upsetting to indigenous populations.
這就解釋了奧巴馬遭人仇恨的原因。
this explains the popular hostility toward obama.
美國人知道不久以後白人將成為少數，有色人種將越來越多地身居要職。
americans know that, before too long, whites will be just another minority, and people of color will increasingly be in positions of power.
此時，所有茶黨黨員和像他們一樣的人所能做的只是大喊 ， “ 把國家還給我們！ ”
at this point, all tea partiers and others like them can do is declare, we want our country back!
當然，這個要求根本不可能。
of course, this is an impossible demand.
如果不想像波斯尼亞那樣引發全境範圍內的大規模血腥種族清洗，美國人和其他人除了習慣生活在越來越多樣化的社會里之外其實別無選擇。
short of unleashing massive and bloody ethnic cleansing bosnia, on a continental scale americans and others have no choice but to get used to living in increasingly diverse societies.
同樣，經濟全球化的效果也無法消除。
likewise, economic globalization cannot be undone.
但監管可以而且理應得到改善。
but regulation can and should be improved.
歸根結底，有些東西仍然值得保護。
after all, some things are still worth protecting.
我們不想讓文化、教育、生活方式或工作完全處在市場力量的創造性破壞之下有著充分的理由。
there are good reasons not to leave culture, education, lifestyles, or jobs completely exposed to the creative destruction of market forces.
麥克法登已準確地找到了的全球化挑戰的核心解決方案：那就是賦予民眾“謀取全球化世界利益的工具 ” ， 從而使“高度互聯的世界更好地為人們服務 ” 。
mcfadden has pinpointed the central solution to globalizations challenges giving people the tools to reap the benefits of the globalized world, thereby making the connected world work better for people.
問題是上述呼籲更有可能吸引高學歷、已經掌握優勢的群體，而不是那些在今天全球經濟中感覺權利被剝奪的失意者。
the problem is that this call is more likely to appeal to the highly educated, already privileged classes than to those who feel disenfranchised in todays global economy.
這個擺在日益代表都市精英利益的左翼政黨面前的問題十分嚴重。 與此同時，鄉村民粹主義者正在推動傳統的保守派人士在民眾仇恨的黑暗領域轉向右翼。
this is a serious problem for political parties on the left, which increasingly seem to be speaking for the metropolitan elites, while provincial populists are pushing traditional conservatives further to the right by fishing in the dark waters of popular resentment.
全球合作問題生死攸關
global cooperation as a lifeanddeath issue
倫敦 — — 最近英國投票脫歐所產生的不確定性已經嚴重衝擊全球市場，而且一直牢牢佔據著報紙的頭版頭條。
london the uncertainty generated by the united kingdoms recent vote to leave the european union which has sent shockwaves through global markets has been dominating headlines.
但當我們準備迎接新的政治考驗時，絕不能忽視我們已經面臨的挑戰，尤其是與經濟效益和政治穩定不相稱的細菌耐藥性上升（AMR）所帶來的全球健康挑戰。
but, as we prepare to face new political trials, we must not lose sight of the challenges we already face, especially global health challenges like the rise of antimicrobial resistance amr, which has no regard for economic performance or political stability.
現在的情況是，每年約有700,000人死於耐藥菌感染。
as it stands, an estimated 700,000 people are losing their lives to drugresistant infections each year.
截止2050年，該資料可能上升到每年1000萬，累計給世界GDP造成的損失高達100萬億美元。
by 2050, this figure could skyrocket to ten million per year, at a cumulative cost to world gdp of 100 trillion..
為避免出現這樣的後果，今年5月，我所領導的《細菌耐藥性上升評論》公佈了應對上述感染的策略，就確保必要的新抗生素開發和將現有抗生素更有效的用於人類健康和農業生產提出了建議性方案。
to avoid that outcome, in may the review on amr that i lead published its strategy for tackling such infections, laying out proposals to ensure the development of the necessary new antibiotics, and to use existing antibiotics more efficiently in humans and agriculture.
在我們所建議的十大幹預措施中有4項尤為重要：
of the ten major interventions we proposed, four are particularly important
·       發起一場針對不同地區特點的全球運動，以提高對細菌耐藥性上升問題的公眾認識。
launch a global campaign, tailored for different regions, to improve public awareness of amr.
·       透過為成功新藥的研發企業提供一次性市場準入獎勵解決目前新抗生素研發領域的市場失靈現象，同時確保全球都能公平地享受到研發成果。
address the market failure in the development of new antibiotics by introducing lumpsum marketentry rewards to developers of successful new drugs, while ensuring global access.
·       推進創新並改善診斷技術應用，以支援抗生素的高效應用。
advance innovation and improve use of diagnostic technology to support more efficient use of antibiotics.
·       落實旨在減少農業及人類醫療領域抗生素不必要應用的國別目標。
implement countrylevel targets focused on reducing unnecessary use of antibiotics in agriculture and humans.
隨著最終報告的完成，評論將繼續直接敦促國際政治領導人採取行動。
with our final report complete, the review will now continue to make the international case for action directly to political leaders.
比方說，作為評論的主席，我最近在日內瓦召開的世界衛生大會上與紐約和華盛頓的聯合國及美國決策者討論了我們的建議。
for example, in my capacity as the reviews chairman, i recently discussed our recommendations at the world health assembly in geneva, and with united nations and united states policymakers in new york and washington, dc.
在上述討論中，引人矚目的是決策者對細菌耐藥性上升危險有著越來越清醒的認識。
in these discussions, policymakers growing awareness of the danger posed by amr stood out.
短短兩年前，耐藥菌感染的話題往往會遭遇像“AMR是什麼？ ”或“財政部長為什麼要負責一場醫療危機？
just two years ago, the topic of drugresistant infections would usually be met with questions like what is amr? or, why would a finance minister take charge of a health crisis?
”這樣的提問。 很少有人理解這一挑戰的規模和多面性；以及全面採取措施的必要性。
few understood the scale and multifaceted nature of the challenge, and thus the need for a comprehensive approach.
英國首相戴維·卡梅倫最初邀請我領導《細菌耐藥性上升評論》時我也曾經問過自己類似的問題。
i asked myself similar questions when british prime minister david cameron first asked me to lead the review on amr.
自那以後情況已經發生了很大改變。
the situation has changed considerably since then.
形形色色經濟和政治體制國家的決策者正在參與解決細菌耐藥性上升問題，其中某些國家已經在採取針對性措施。
policymakers from countries with a wide variety of economic and political systems are engaging on the amr problem, with some countries already taking steps to tackle it.
所有這些都給人們帶來了希望，2016年可能會啟動真正的變革。
all of this provides grounds for hope that 2016 may be the year when real change gets underway.
但希望是一回事；行動則完全不同。
but hope is one thing action is another.
雖然高層就細菌耐藥性上升問題舉行的會議和講話傳達了正確的精神，但如果從今年9月召開的二十國及聯合國峰會開始，我們不能成功將現有勢頭轉化為具體行動，那麼會議和講話就沒有任何意義。
while highlevel meetings and speeches about amr send the right message, they will mean nothing if we do not manage to translate the current momentum into concrete action, beginning at the g20 and un meetings this september.
雖然最近的討論表明上述會議很有可能達成協議，但上述協議能否匹配問題的規模仍具有極大的不確定性。
and while my most recent discussions suggest that agreements are likely to be reached at both of these meetings, it is far from certain that they will match the scale of the problem.
在20國峰會上，必要的協議應著眼於制定一套全球機制，為經濟實惠、使用方便高效的全球新抗生素市場重新注入活力。
at the g20, the needed agreement should focus on developing a global mechanism to reinvigorate the market for new antibiotics that are globally affordable, accessible, and used as efficiently as possible.
而聯合國的目標應當是真正落實“使用方便而非過剩”的口號，簽署一份減少農業不必要使用抗生素的協議，併發起一場全球宣傳運動。
at the un, the goal should be to turn the mantra of access, not excess into a reality, with an agreement to reduce the unnecessary use of antibiotics in agriculture, and to spearhead a global awareness campaign.
為新抗生素及診斷方法研發投入更多資金以應對細菌耐藥性上升同樣至關重要。
increased funding for research and development of new antibiotics and diagnostics to fight amr is also vital.
重要的是，協議必須長出牙齒。
crucially, the agreements must have teeth.
各國應自主制定目標以適應自身獨特的需求和環境，但必須加入某些條款，以確保各方盡到自己的努力。
countries should set their own objectives to fit their particular circumstances and needs, but there must be some provisions to ensure that all are pulling their weight.
首先，應當把解決細菌耐藥性上升問題納入更廣泛的經濟發展戰略，其中包括落實聯合國可持續發展目標。
for starters, efforts to fight amr should be incorporated into broader economicdevelopment strategies, including the implementation of the un sustainable development goals.
此外，應定期衡量目標的進展狀況，這不僅是要讓決策者、企業和醫療系統各負其責，也是要讓他們的成功可以被其他國家所仿效。
moreover, progress should be measured, not only so that policymakers, companies, and health systems can be held accountable, but also so that others can emulate their successes.
要想達到目的，我們或許需要計算細菌耐藥性上升影響的全新指標。
to this end, we may need new metrics for calculating the impact of amr.
雖然這聽上去技術性很強（事實也的確如此 ） ， 但現實情況是最著名的細菌耐藥性問題專家認為確定共同指標可以改變各國制定其自身目標的方法，並使我們在未來若干年內能夠更好地衡量進步。
while this sounds technical and it is, the reality is that top amr scientists think that agreeing on common measurements could change the way individual countries set their own targets and improve our capacity to measure progress in the coming years.
最後，為了防止政治目標和人物變化，我們需要在抗擊細菌耐藥性上升過程中設定不變的倡導者。
finally, to account for changing political priorities and personalities, we need a constant champion in the fight against amr.
比方說，可以指定一名聯合國細菌耐藥性上升問題特使，負責持續宣傳解決問題的重要性以及監督各國完成自己的目標。
for example, a un envoy on amr could be appointed, to continue making the international case for addressing the issue and to challenge countries to meet their targets.
沒有這樣對解決細菌抗藥性上升問題一以貫之的提醒，更不要說及時公佈進展狀況，世界各國就有可能受到其他問題干擾，從而錯失這次推進必要改革以阻止耐藥菌感染上升的轉瞬即逝的機遇。
without such a consistent reminder of the need to tackle amr, not to mention transparency about progress, the world could become sidetracked and miss the rapidly closing window of opportunity to deliver the changes needed to stop the rise of drugresistant infections.
過去幾年來，政府、企業和國際組織在應對細菌耐藥性上升問題上已經取得了重大進步。
over the last couple of years, governments, industry, and international organizations have made important strides in meeting the amr threat.
但現在需要我們做出真正艱難的決策。
but the really hard decisions must be taken now.
如果想要避免細菌耐藥性上升這場慢動作車禍，我們的領導人必須立即採取規避行動。
if we are to prevent the slowmotion car crash of rising amr, our leaders must take evasive action now.
我們知道應該做些什麼；現在我們必須身體力行。
we know what we have to do now we must get on with doing it.
和國際貨幣基金組織一起解決抗生素耐藥性
tackling amr with the imf
倫敦—本月是聯合國抗生素耐藥性（AMR）高階別會議召開一週年，該聯合國會議由英國的獨立AMR評估幫助組織。 對我來說，去年的這個時刻令人無比光榮。
london this month is the first anniversary of the united nations highlevel meeting on antimicrobial resistance, which the united kingdoms independent review on amr helped to bring about.
因為我是AMR評估主席，也因為我的團隊和英國總醫務官薩利·戴維斯（Sally Davies ） 。
that moment last year was very gratifying for me, as the chairman of the review, as well as for my team and the uks chief medical officer, sally davies.
去年的高階別會議決議，成員國代表將在兩年後再次開會評估進展情況 — — 因此，下一次會議是在2018年9月。
last years highlevel meeting resolved that memberstate delegates are to reconvene for a progress assessment after two years so, in september 2018.
會議還號召成立一個機構間協調小組，在兩年的時間裡指導遏制AMR的工作。
the meeting also called for the establishment of an interagency coordination group to guide efforts in the fight against amr during that twoyear period.
小組由我負責召集，由非常有責任心的人士領導。
from what i have gathered, the group is being led by deeply committed individuals.
在更廣的範圍上，國家和國際層面的決策者也開始將更多注意力集中在AMR的威脅上。
and, more broadly, policymakers at the national and international levels have begun to pay more attention to the threat of amr.
事實上，聯合國高階別會議舉行後，G20也做出了崇高的遏制AMR 承諾。
in fact, since the un highlevel meeting, the g20 has also made notable commitments in the battle against amr.
在7月的G20德國漢堡峰會上，各國政府同意成立“研發合作中心 ” ， 著手逐步停止將抗生素應用於農業。 農業生產上使用抗生素促進牲畜生長。
at the g20 summit in hamburg, germany, in july, governments agreed to establish an rd collaboration hub, and to begin to phase out antibiotics in agriculture, where producers use them to promote animal growth.
英國AMR評估建議增加20億美元的AMR初期研究經費，因此，建立研發中心的措施非常值得歡迎。
the uk review recommended that an additional 2 billion be earmarked for earlystage research into amr, so the creation of an rd hub is very welcome.
但限制在農業中使用抗生素的協議意義更加重大。
but the agreement to limit the use of antibiotics in agriculture was even more significant.
在過去，G20主要成員國一致拒絕做出這樣的承諾。
in the past, key g20 member states have resisted such commitments.
而在作為聯合國高階別會議基礎的檔案中，農業也沒有提及，原因是擔心因此導致最終協議胎死腹中。
and in the texts that served as a foundation for the un highlevel meeting, agriculture wasnt even mentioned, owing to fear that it would render any eventual agreement dead on arrival.
聯合國和G20所邁出的步伐令人鼓舞。
the steps that the un and the g20 have taken are encouraging.
但遏制AMR的鬥爭遠遠沒有結束，反而可能才剛剛開始。
but the fight against amr is hardly over, and has probably only just begun.
放眼未來，最大的挑戰之一在於個體國家和多邊組織，比如聯合國自身。
looking forward, one of the biggest challenges will be holding to account individual countries and multilateral organizations, such as the un itself.
我們如何確定政府和機構會兌現自己的豪言壯語？
how will we confirm that governments and institutions have followed through on their lofty declarations?
首先，我們可以著眼於經濟學和公共衛生的交叉互動。
for starters, we can look at the intersection of economics and public health.
國際機構有很多方式可以撬動經濟政策槓桿，大大降低傳染病暴發的機率，提高脆弱國家對這一風險的抵抗力。
there are many ways that international institutions can use economicpolicy levers to reduce significantly the probability of infectiousdisease outbreaks, and to increase vulnerable countries resilience to such risks.
在我看來，國際貨幣基金組織（IMF）應該起到領導作用。
to my mind, the international monetary fund should take the lead.
彼得·桑茲（Peter Sands）和他的同事們在2016年5月的《柳葉刀》雜誌上所發表的研究表明，傳染病爆發會造成巨大的經濟成本，但它們很少甚至沒有作為評估宏觀經濟風險的因素被考慮到。
as peter sands and his colleagues show in a may 2016 study in the lancet, infectiousdisease outbreaks have farreaching economic costs, and yet they are rarely, if ever, factored into assessments of macroeconomic risk.
IMF已經有了針對各國經濟健康的定期評估，金融市場分析對此非常重視。
the imf already conducts regular reviews of countries economic health, and financial markets give significant weight to its analyses.
為了經濟健康，也為了公共衛生，IMF同樣可以在追蹤各國AMR進展方面做出出色表現。
for the sake of economic as well as public health, the fund would do well to start tracking countries progress in the fight against amr as well.
十年多前，歐盟便已經宣佈將禁止將抗生素用於促進牲畜生長。
the european union declared more than ten years ago that it would fully phase out the use of antibiotics for animal growth promotion.
但除了偶爾有調查記者關注此事，還有誰真正深入到各成員國，調查這一目標的進展情況？
but who, other than the occasional investigative journalist, has ever actually delved into eu member states progress toward that goal?
在英國，我的AMR評估同僚和我們的建議所引起的政府反應引線深刻，特別是在減少抗生素處方、防止住院傳染和將農業中的抗生素用量限制在50毫克/千克牲畜水平方面。
in the uk, my review colleagues and i were quite impressed by the governments formal policy response to our recommendations, especially with respect to reducing antibiotic prescriptions, preventing hospitalacquired infections, and limiting the use of antibiotics in farming to 50 milligrams per kilogram of livestock.
在過去的一年中，我在一些積極研究AMR威脅問題的英國大學發表公開演講。
over the past year, i have given public talks at some of the british universities that are actively working on the amr threat.
們鼓勵我比過去更多地去會見一些該問題的學術研究者。
i have been encouraged to see more academic researchers pursuing this topic than in the past.
但透過提問聽眾，我意識到很少有人瞭解政府的政策反應。
but when i have quizzed my audiences, i have come to realize that hardly anyone knows about the governments policy response.
這可能只是因為我的聽眾們不瞭解情況；但我對此有所懷疑。
this could mean that my audiences are simply uninformed but i doubt that.
更有可能的情況是政府沒有兌現它的承諾。
what is more likely is that the government has not yet followed through on its commitments.
IMF是非常理想的解決問題者，它可以將該問題列為其常規經濟評估的一部分。
the imf is ideally suited to get to the bottom of this question as a part of its routine economic assessments.
它的經濟分析對於不太富裕的國家價值更高，在這些國家，防止傳染病暴發可以對長期經濟增長起到直接提振作用。
and its analyses would be even more valuable to less wealthy countries, where preventing outbreaks of infectious diseases could directly boost longterm economic growth.
在聯合國高階別會議迎來一週年之際，我的最後一項擔憂是決策者仍然沒有批准旨在鼓勵開發新藥和新診斷方法的市場進入獎勵經費。
one last concern that i have on this first anniversary of the un highlevel meeting is that policymakers still need to agree on a source of funding for the marketentry rewards intended to encourage the development of new drugs and diagnostics.
這些創新將是防止和發現AMR的關鍵，而刺激這些創新的激勵機制正日益被視為正確的方法。
such innovations will be crucial for preventing and detecting amr, and an incentive mechanism to stimulate them is increasingly regarded as the right way to go.
在這方面，IMF也能夠提供非常寶貴的建議。
that, too, is a topic on which the imf could provide invaluable advice.
醫學的社會科學
the social science of medicine
達沃斯—20實際80年代，當我還是一位醫科學生時，我在新幾內亞的巴布亞（Papua）得了瘧疾。
davos when i was a medical student in the mid1980s, i contracted malaria in papua new guinea. it was a miserable experience.
這是一段可怕的體驗。
my head ached.
我頭痛發燒，並出現貧血。
my temperature soared. i became anemic.
但我吃了藥，並好了起來。
but i took my medicine, and i got better.
這不是一段愉快的體驗，但感謝高效廉價的瘧疾藥，我從未陷入險境。
the experience wasnt pleasant, but thanks to cheap, effective malaria drugs i was never in very much danger.
這些把我治癒的藥片 — — 氯喹如今已不再有用。
the pills that cured me, chloroquine tablets, do not work anymore.
即使在我服用它們的時候，世界許多地區的導致瘧疾的寄生蟲已經擁有了氯喹抗藥性。 巴布亞紐幾內亞是這些藥片還能管用的最後幾個地方之一，而即使在那裡，氯喹的藥效也是每況愈下。
even at the time i was taking them, the parasite that causes malaria had already become resistant to chloroquine in many parts of the world papua new guinea was one of the last places where the pills continued to be effective, and even there they were losing their potency.
如今，氯喹已經基本從我們的藥品清單中消失。
today, chloroquine has basically disappeared from our medical arsenal.
病原體對抗生素和其他抗菌藥的抗藥性越來越強，這正在成為當代醫療的最大危機 — — 而這一危機無法單靠科學解決。
the growing capacity of pathogens to resist antibiotics and other antimicrobial drugs is turning into the greatest emerging crisis in contemporary health care and it is a crisis that cannot be solved by science alone.
其他藥品正在步氯喹的後塵。
other pharmaceuticals are following in chloroquines wake.
結核菌、大腸桿菌、和沙門氏菌的多抗藥性菌株已經司空見慣。
multidrugresistant strains of tuberculosis, e. coli, and salmonella are now commonplace.
大部分淋病是不可治癒的。
most gonorrhea infections are untreatable.
超級病菌，如具有甲氧西林抗藥性的金黃葡萄球菌（MRSA）和艱難梭菌，正在迅速繁衍。
superbugs, like methicillinresistant staphylococcus aureus mrsa and clostridium difficile, are proliferating.
在印度，2013年因抗生素無效的傳染病而令58,000 新生兒死亡。
in india, antibioticresistant infections killed more than 58,000 newborns in 2013.
如今，瘧疾往往透過青蒿素（一種中國藥草總提煉的藥物）和其他抗瘧疾藥物一起使用治療。
today, malaria is often treated with a combination of artemisinin a drug derived from a chinese herb and other antimalarial drugs.
但這些革命性藥品極有可能步氯喹的後塵成為明日黃花；抗藥瘧疾菌株已經在東南亞進入記錄。
but these revolutionary medicines are now in danger of following chloroquine into obsolescence resistant strains of malaria have been documented in southeast asia.
這不僅僅是一個醫學問題；這是一場潛在的經濟災難。
this is more than a medical problem it is a potential economic disaster.
以經濟學家奧尼爾（Jim O’Neil）牽頭進行的抗生素抗藥性研究（Review on Antimicrobial Resistance）指出，如果當前趨勢持續，抗藥性傳染病將在2050年奪走1 000萬人的生命，在未來35年中給全球經濟帶來100多萬億美元的損失。
research commissioned by the review on antimicrobial resistance, headed by the economist jim oneill, has calculated that if current trends continue, drugresistant infections will kill ten million people a year by 2050 and cost the global economy some 100 trillion over the next 35 years.
甚至如此嚴重的預測也有可能大大低估了情況，因為它只包括了用傳染病所造成的生命和福祉衡量的直接損失。
even that dramatic prediction may be a substantial underestimate, as it includes only the direct costs in terms of lives and wellbeing lost to infections. many other aspects of modern medicine also rely on antibiotics.
接受化療的癌症患者是為了用它們抑制非如此就會摧毀他們羸弱的免疫系統的細菌。
cancer patients receiving chemotherapy take them to suppress bacteria that would otherwise overwhelm their weakened immune systems.
許多如今被視為常規手段的外科收入，包括人工關節和剖腹產，只有在抗生素能夠預防偶發感染的情況下才能實施。
many surgical operations now considered routine, including joint replacements and caesarean sections, can be performed safely only when antibiotics prevent opportunistic infections.
抗藥性的源頭在早已是眾所周知的進化論。
the origins of drug resistance are a wellunderstood matter of evolution.
如果病原體被暴露在有選擇的毒性藥物的壓力之下，最終它們會適應這種藥物。
if pathogens are exposed to the selective pressure of toxic drugs, eventually they will adapt.
由我擔任總裁的惠康基金會（Wellcome Trust）投資了數億美元用於研究這些機制、改善診斷和創造新藥。
the wellcome trust, which i lead, has invested hundreds of millions of dollars into researching these mechanisms, improving diagnoses, and creating new drugs.
為了有效解決問題，這一努力必須擴大到科學領域之外，進入與傳統上與醫學並不相關的領域。
in order to address the problem effectively, this effort must be extended beyond the realm of biological science to areas not traditionally associated with medicine.
不論是富國還是窮國，我們都在系統性濫用抗生素。
in rich and poor countries alike, we have become systematic abusers of antibiotics.
對付抗藥性的關鍵在於拖延病原體的適應。
the key to combating resistance is to delay the rate at which the pathogens can adapt.
但是，由於過多地開出抗生素處方盒無法完成必要的療程，我們正在讓細菌獲得恰好能鼓勵抗藥性的藥量。
but, by overprescribing antibiotics and failing to complete the required courses of treatment, we are exposing germs to just enough medicine to encourage resistance.
因此，我們實際上在幫助細菌接種，形成對我們希望用來對付它們的藥物的免疫力。
in effect, we are vaccinating germs against the drugs we want to use against them.
這是因為我們一直幾乎完全把抗生素看成是一種消費品 — — 我們要求醫生給我們開出處方，並在我們感到合適的時候停藥。
that is because we have come to regard antibiotics almost as consumer goods ours to demand from doctors, and ours to take or stop taking as we see fit.
即使是最瞭解情況的患者也會無用這些出色的藥物。
even the most informed patients misuse these wonder drugs.
英國的研究發現，哪怕是知道抗藥性如何發展的人，也常常會在沒有處方的情況下服用抗生素或把自己的藥給家庭成員，從而加劇了抗藥性問題。
research in the united kingdom has found that even people who understand how resistance develops often contribute to the problem by taking antibiotics without a prescription or giving their drugs to members of their family.
改變這一破壞性行為需要我們更好地理解其背後的社會和文化因素。
changing such destructive behavior will require that we better understand the social and cultural factors that drive it.
歷史學、心理學、社會學、人類學、經濟學、市場研究和社會營銷等學科都能有所助益。
disciplines like history, psychology, sociology, anthropology, economics, market research, and social marketing can help.
不僅抗生素抗壓性問題是如此。
this is true not only for antimicrobial resistance.
埃博拉疫情等疫情的爆發也是如此。
it also applies to outbreaks like the ebola epidemic.
與病毒抗爭需要我們理解病毒的生物學、其傳播的傳染病學，以及可能使用哪些藥物和疫苗來對付它。
combating the virus requires knowledge about its biology, the epidemiology of its transmission, and the drugs and vaccines that could potentially be deployed against it.
但這也需要理解讓傳染病在賴比瑞亞、獅子山和幾內亞肆虐的行為因素。
but it also requires an understanding of the behaviors that have allowed infection to spread in liberia, sierra leone, and guinea.
解釋這些社會為何如此脆弱需要了解地區的最近歷史和明白為何那裡的人對公共當局極不信任。
explaining what made these societies so vulnerable requires learning about the regions recent history and understanding why people there are deeply distrustful of public authorities.
患者隔離和死者安全下葬時遏制埃博拉的關鍵，但這兩項措施的實施都需要顧及文化敏感性 — — 而不僅僅是它們背後的科學解釋。
isolation of patients and safe burial of the dead are crucial to containing ebola, but both need to be introduced with cultural sensitivity not just explanations of the science behind them.
今天的公共衛生大威脅具有深遠的經濟影響。
todays great publichealth threats have profound economic consequences.
實現它們所造成的風險的最小化需要認識到它們與社會、行為和文化因素互動。
minimizing the risks they pose requires recognizing that they are intertwined with the social, behavioral, and cultural landscape.
科學提供了強大的工具。
science provides powerful tools.
但我們需要比科學更多的東西才能有效使用這些工具。
but we need more than science to use these tools effectively.
抗菌素耐藥性評估之戰中我們現狀如何?
where are we in the fight against amr?
倫敦 — — 為紀念英國政府抗菌素耐藥性評估小組（AMR）成立兩週年（我曾有幸擔任評估小組的負責職務 ） ， 我和評估小組的另外兩位成員安東尼·麥克唐納和威爾·霍爾共同出版了一本名叫《超級細菌：抗菌鬥爭的一場軍備競賽》的新書。
london to mark the second anniversary of the british governments review on antimicrobial resistance amr, which i had the honor of chairing, two members of the review team anthony mcdonnell and will hall and i have published a new book superbugs an arms race against bacteria.
在這本書中，我們探討了評估小組推薦的十大幹預舉措 — — 我將這些舉措稱之為“十誡 ” — —同時還考量了迄今為止所取得的進展，以及仍需完成哪些工作。
in it, we discuss the reviews ten recommended interventions what i call the ten commandments while considering the progress made so far, and the work that still needs to be done.
新書的開篇部分詳細闡述了我們對細菌和耐藥性的理解，並指出有證據表明耐藥性的發展現在可能比我們預想的要快得多。
the first part of the book provides a detailed history of our understanding of bacteria and drug resistance, and points to evidence that drug resistance may now be rising faster than we had assumed.
例如，被普遍視為其他抗菌素失效後最後一種可用抗生素的粘菌素，由於在動物飼養中的過度使用，特別是在中國，現在正在快速失效。
for example, colistin, which is generally regarded as one of the last usable antibiotics in humans after others have failed, is losing its effectiveness, owing to overuse in animal farming, notably in china.
同樣令人不安的是，我們越來越頻繁地看到關於耐藥淋病菌株的報道。
and, equally disturbing, reports of drugresistant strains of gonorrhea are becoming more frequent.
在評估報告中，我們預測如果任由目前趨勢持續下去，到2050年每年可能有1，000萬人死亡，從2015年算起給全球經濟產出共造成約100萬億美元的損失。
in the review, we predicted that if current trends continue, ten million people could die every year by 2050, at a loss of some 100 trillion in global economic output since 2015.
但現在有理由擔心情況可能會變的更糟。
but now there is reason to fear that the situation could turn out even worse.
為了避免這種情況出現，本書的第二部分著重探討解決方案，並彙集了我們採訪的評估小組許多專家的看法。
to ensure that it does not, the second part of the book focuses on solutions, and compiles expert viewpoints from many of those we interviewed for the review.
我們所推薦的三項“供給側”干預措施中有兩項已經取得了進展，這一點是積極的。
on a positive note, there has been progress on two of the three supply interventions that we recommended.
首先，早期研發資金正在增加。
first, financing for earlystage research and development is growing.
就在不久前， 英中兩國政府、威康信託基金、美國生物醫學高階研究與發展管理局（BARDA）以及丹麥製藥企業諾和諾德聯合成立了新的資助計劃。
just recently, new joint funding initiatives were launched by the british and chinese governments, the wellcome trust, the united states biomedical advanced research and development authority barda, and the danish pharmaceutical company novo.
如果這樣的支援力度能夠維持下去，那麼評估小組建議的在未來五年內再增加20億美元的研發經費就是可行的。
if this support is sustained, the reviews recommendation of 2 billion in additional rd funding over the next five years will be within reach.
其次，專注抗菌素耐藥性研究的研究人員數量似乎正在增加。
second, the number of researchers working on amr seems to be growing.
事實上，我總喜歡開玩笑說在英格蘭北部，抗菌素耐藥性評估研究中心現在可能比按照政府的北方動力計劃同意交易權下放的城市還要多。
in fact, i like to joke that in northern england, amr research centers probably now outnumber the cities that have agreed to devolution deals under the governments northern powerhouse plan.
上述兩個地區所取得的進展讓我期待其他地區也能取得類似的進展。
the progress made in these two areas gives me hope that similar advances can be made elsewhere.
但取得進一步進展需要政府和行業領袖少空談、多行動。
but further progress will require less talk and more action from government and industry leaders.
製藥業尤其如此 — — 這是我們所提出的第三條供給側干預措施所針對的目標。
that is especially true of the pharmaceutical industry the target of the third supply intervention we proposed.
製藥業不能僅關注短期利潤，而必須進一步加大研發投資並生產新的治療藥物。
rather than focusing solely on shortterm profit margins, the industry must invest more in rd and the production of new treatments.
據我所知，全球前25家最大製藥企業的代表在今年達沃斯世界經濟論壇年會即將舉行之際見面討論抗菌素耐藥性評估，並同意就此問題保持進一步接觸。
