at any rate, experience indicates that exiting the euro while preserving the freedom of capital movements is little more than a fantasy.
一些觀察人士建議，鑑於阿根廷事件的教訓，在重新引入本國貶值貨幣時，只能將其運用在工資和一些特定產品的定價上，同時不能完全拋棄歐元。
some observers suggest, based on argentinas precedent, that countries should introduce their own weaker currency to denominate wages and selected prices without leaving the euro.
我認為這不可行。
we believe this analogy is misconstrued.
當時的阿根廷在放棄連繫匯率制度之前的2001年確實發行了一種代用貨幣，以此滿足財政需求和保持兌美元的穩定匯率。
while argentina did issue quasimoney in 2001 before abandoning the currency board, this money was conceived to meet fiscal needs and remained stable visvis the dollar.
實際上，可以想象，一旦代用貨幣貶值，這種雙貨幣機制很難避免兌換成幣值較低的可能性，這個想法最終以失敗告終。
indeed, it is hard to imagine how this dualcurrency scheme could have avoided the consequences of converting to a weaker currency if the quasimoney had depreciated, as the ideas current promoters intend.
阿根廷退出鎖定美元事件是一場災難，它導致大量的合同違約，財富重新分配，破產，儲戶擠兌存款，匯率限制，短期內對資本流動的嚴格限制。
argentinas exit from its dollar peg was a traumatic experience, concentrating contract violations, wealth redistribution, defaults, bank runs, exchange restrictions, and severe limitations on capital movements into a short period of time.
即便如此，這也會比引入一個新希臘“德拉克馬”要好的多。
even so, it was simpler than introducing a new drachma would be for, say, greece.
因為阿根廷貨幣局從來沒有取締過比索，即便最糟糕的時候，比索的需求還是客觀存在。
because argentinas currency board never eliminated the peso as the main means of transactions, the basis for demand for it was there at the time of the blowup.
相比於退出歐元的國家而言，他們將不得不為新貨幣創造出需求 — — 這將是更加混亂糟糕的事情。
euro defectors, by contrast, would need to promote demand for the new currency from scratch a much messier and nastier process altogether.
里約成績單
a rio report card
紐約 — — 全世界優秀的科學出版物之一《自然》剛剛趕在下週舉行的里約+20可持續發展首腦會議前公佈了措辭嚴厲的成績單。
new york one of the worlds preeminent scientific publications, nature, has just issued a scathing report card in advance of next weeks rio20 summit on sustainable development.
1992年首屆里約地球峰會簽署的三項偉大條約執行成績如下：氣候變化－F，生物多樣性－F，防治荒漠化－F。 人類究竟還能否避免被開除球籍的厄運？
the grades for implementation of the three great treaties signed at the first rio earth summit in 1992 were as follows climate change f biological diversity f and combating desertification f. can humanity still avoid getting itself expelled?
整整一代人早已明白世界需要改變發展道路。
we have known for at least a generation that the world needs a course correction.
我們需要更多地利用風能、太陽能和地熱發電等低碳替代能源，而不能繼續依靠化石燃料來推動世界經濟。
instead of powering the world economy with fossil fuels, we need to mobilize much greater use of lowcarbon alternatives such as wind, solar, and geothermal power.
我們需要調整農業及漁業生產以適應環境的承載能力，而不能在毫不顧忌對其他物種影響的情況下狩獵、捕魚和砍伐樹木。
instead of hunting, fishing, and clearing land without regard for the impact on other species, we need to pace our agricultural production, fishing, and logging in line with the environments carrying capacity.
我們需要結束極端貧困並降低世界最貧困地區快速增長的生育率，而不能坐視全球最弱勢群體得不到計劃生育，教育和基本醫療保健等服務。
instead of leaving the worlds most vulnerable people without access to family planning, education, and basic health care, we need to end extreme poverty and reduce the soaring fertility rates that persist in the poorest parts of the world.
簡言之，我們需要認識到今天的70億人口在本世紀中葉可能達到90億，所有人在高科技驅使的能源密集型全球經濟中都擁有非常密切的聯絡，因此我們作為整體掌握著前所未有的毀壞​​地球生命支援系統的能力。
in short, we need to recognize that with seven billion people today, and nine billion by midcentury, all interconnected in a hightech, energyintensive global economy, our collective capacity to destroy the planets lifesupport systems is unprecedented.
但通常個人行為的後果離我們的日常生活如此遙遠，以致於我們可能在渾然不覺中跌下懸崖摔得粉身碎骨。
yet the consequences of our individual actions are typically so far removed from our daily awareness that we can go right over the cliff without even knowing it.
我們開啟電腦和電燈時，並不瞭解會造成多少碳排放。
when we power our computers and lights, we are unaware of the carbon emissions that result.
我們用餐時，也不知道不可持續的耕作導致了多少森林砍伐。
when we eat our meals, we are unaware of the deforestation that has resulted from unsustainable farming.
當數十億件微不足道的小事共同造成地球另一面爆發饑荒和洪水，折磨馬裡和肯亞等旱災頻發地區最貧困民眾的時候，很少有人對全球網路的危險圈套有最基本的認識。
and when billions of our actions combine to create famines and floods halfway around the world, afflicting the poorest people in droughtprone mali and kenya, few of us are even dimly aware of the dangerous snares of global interconnectedness.
20年前，世界試圖透過條約和國際法解決上述現實問題。
twenty years ago, the world tried to address these realities through treaties and international law.
1992年首屆里約峰會達成的協議用心良苦：深思熟慮、高瞻遠矚，熱心公益，並集中關注全球重點問題。
the agreements that emerged in 1992 at the first rio summit were good ones thoughtful, farsighted, publicspirited, and focused on global priorities.
但協議卻沒有能夠拯救人類。
yet they have not saved us.
上述條約籠罩在我們日常政治、幻想和媒體週期的陰影之下。 外交官年復一年地參與會議落實這些條約，但卻擺脫不了忽視、延誤和爭論合法性的結果。
those treaties lived in the shadow of our daily politics, imaginations, and media cycles. diplomats trudged off to conferences year after year to implement them, but the main results were neglect, delay, and bickering over legalities.
二十年來，我們付出的努力只換來三項不及格的成績。
twenty years on, we have only three failing grades to show for our efforts.
那還有沒有其他方法？
is there a different way?
國際法涉及律師和外交官，但卻沒有在可持續發展的前沿領域吸引工程師、科學家和社團領導人的參與。
the path through international law engages lawyers and diplomats, but not the engineers, scientists, and community leaders on the front lines of sustainable development.
到處充斥著有關監督、約束性義務、附件一及非附件一國家和成千上萬其他法律條文的技術性條款，但卻沒有為人類提供一種語言來討論自身的生存。
it is littered with technical arcana about monitoring, binding obligations, annexi and nonannexi countries, and thousands of other legalisms, but has failed to give humanity the language to discuss our own survival.
我們擁有數以千計的檔案，但卻無法坦率地進行溝通。
we have thousands of documents but a failure to speak plainly to one other.
我們想不想拯救自己和孩子？
do we want to save ourselves and our children?
我們為什麼不這樣說？
why didnt we say so?
我們必須在里約+20峰會上果斷地表述清楚，進而解決問題並採取行動，而不是繼續喋喋不休地爭吵和自我保護。
at rio20 we will have to say so, clearly, decisively, and in a way that leads to problemsolving and action, not to bickering and defensiveness.
由於政治家順應民意而不是領導民意，因此不能指望當選官員在公眾不知情的情況下拯救公眾，而必須由公眾自身明確地提出生存要求。
since politicians follow public opinion rather than lead it, it must be the public itself that demands its own survival, not elected officials who are somehow supposed to save us despite ourselves.
政界沒有幾個人可以稱得上英雄，因此根本不可能等待政治家做出決策。
there are few heroes in politics waiting for the politicians would be to wait too long.
因此里約最重要的成果不是新條約、約束性條款或者政治承諾，而是呼籲在全世界採取行動。
the most important outcome in rio, therefore, will not be a new treaty, binding clause, or political commitment. it will be a global call to action.
世界各國異口同聲地要求將可持續發展置於全球思想和行動的中心，尤其是協助年輕人應對三重底線帶來的挑戰 — — 即經濟福祉、環��可持續性和社會包容 — — 如何應對上述挑戰將決定他們時代的特色。 里約+20峰會可以協助他們達到目的。
around the world, the cry is rising to put sustainable development at the center of global thinking and action, especially to help young people to solve the triplebottomline challenge economic wellbeing, environmental sustainability, and social inclusion that will define their era. rio20 can help them to do it.
我們需要的不是新條約，而是里約+20峰會採用能激勵一代人採取行動的全套可持續發展目標，也叫SDG。
rather than a new treaty, let us adopt at rio20 a set of sustainable development goals, or sdgs, that will inspire a generation to act.
正如千年發展目標讓我們認識到極端貧困並促成了前所未有的抗擊艾滋病、結核和瘧疾的全球行動，SDG可以讓今天的年輕人清醒地認識到氣候變化、生物多樣性喪失以及荒漠化災害。
just as the millennium development goals opened our eyes to extreme poverty and promoted unprecedented global action to fight aids, tuberculosis, and malaria, the sdgs can open the eyes of todays youth to climate change, biodiversity loss, and the disasters of desertification.
透過敦促人們站在行動的前沿，我們仍然可以兌現之前簽署的三項里約協議。
we can still make good on the three rio treaties, by putting people at the forefront of the effort.
結束極端貧困；建設脫碳能源系統；放慢人口增長；促進可持續糧食供應；保護海洋、森林和旱地；以及糾正我們這個時代存在的不平等能夠激勵一代人去發揮價值，解決問題。 從矽谷到聖保羅到班加羅爾再到上海，工程師和技術高手對拯救世界的想法全都胸有成竹。
sdgs to end extreme poverty decarbonize the energy system slow population growth promote sustainable food supplies protect the oceans, forests, and drylands and redress the inequalities of our time can galvanize a generations worth of problemsolving. engineers and technology wizards from silicon valley to so paolo to bangalore to shanghai have worldsaving ideas up their sleeves.
世界各地的大學是有意為各自所在的團體和國家解決實際問題的大批學生和教師的大本營。
universities around the world are home to legions of students and faculty intent on solving practical problems in their communities and countries.
而至少好的企業知道除非自己成為解決方案的一部分，否則將無法蓬勃發展並激勵自己的工人和消費者。
businesses, at least the good ones, know that they cant flourish and motivate their workers and consumers unless they are part of the solution.
世界正準備採取行動。
the world is poised to act.
里約+20峰會可以促成一代人邁出行動的腳步。
rio20 can help to unleash a generation of action.
我們勉強還有時間將F變成A，並透過這次人類的終極考試。
there is still time, just barely, to turn the fs to as, and to pass humanitys ultimate test.
武器，或是同盟？
arms or allies?
發自里加 — — 當許多拉托維亞人還在為法國向俄羅斯出售兩棲攻擊艦而吃驚不已時，其他歐盟成員國卻已開始將俄羅斯視為潛在的軍火買家了。
riga it should surprise no one that many in latvia view the sale by france of fullyequipped assault warships to russia with grave concern. other european union member states seem to be looking increasingly towards russia as a potential purchaser of military equipment.
但歐盟和北約成員國這種提升非盟國兵力投送能力的舉動是否明智？
but is it wise for eu and nato members to enhance the capacity of nonallies to project their military power?
畢竟俄羅斯入侵喬治亞還僅僅是兩年半以前的事，甚至至今仍佔據著這個北約所謂“潛在未來成員國”的一部分領土。
after all, only two and a half years ago, russia invaded georgia, a country that nato had named as a potential future member, and has occupied part of it ever since.
歐盟理事會針對武器出口行為的共同立場對所有成員國都具有法律約束力。
the eu councils common position on arms exports is legally binding on all eu states.
當然，對武器出口控制以及許可的許可權和責任則屬於成員國自身，而非歐盟機構。
of course, competence and responsibility for armsexport controls and licensing rests with member states, not eu institutions.
事實上在“瓦森納安排 ” （ 全球33個國家建立的常規武器和軍/民雙用途物資及技術出口控制機制）下，各成員國可以自行決定是否出口武器。
indeed, under the wassenaar arrangement, a decision on exports is the sole responsibility of each participating state.
歐盟在武器出口方面的共同立場為我們帶來了更多的資訊交流，更高的透明度以及更密切的磋商，同時也協調了與武器出口控制相關的一系列條約和規程。
implementation of the common eu position on arms exports has led to more exchanges of information, greater transparency, and closer consultation. it has also harmonized exportcontrol arrangements and procedures.
但這一機制的潛力仍未能完全發揮出來。
but there are obvious limits to what can be achieved.
磋商目前還僅限於兩國之間，同時缺乏指導磋商的相關行為準則 — — 也不要求達成任何關於武器出口決策的最後協議。
consultations are currently a bilateral matter, with no rules governing how they should be conducted and no requirement that any final agreement on armsexport decisions be reached.
因此這一磋商機制的有效性也極難評估。
the effectiveness of this consultation mechanism is difficult to evaluate.
依照共同立場條款，某一國頒發武器出口許可證之前必須與曾經拒絕頒發類似許可證的另一成員國進行磋商。
according to the common positions provisions, before a member state grants an export license, it should consult with any member state that has previously denied a similar license.
但相關條款卻並未明確說明這種磋商究竟要達到何種程度。
but the common position does not specify the extent to which another member state should be consulted.
更重要的是，它並不要求武器出口國與其他可能關注該項出口的國家進行磋商。
more importantly, it does not require the armsexporting member state to consult with any other member state that might have concerns.
於是對第三國的武器出口問題就一直困擾著歐盟。
as a result, arms exports to third countries remain a contentious issue within the eu.
而該問題的核心則是各成員國之間的核心利益衝突 — — 歐洲各大武器廠商之間的競爭，還有防務市場的戰略重要性（尤其是牽涉到各國外交政策的時候 ） — —以及特別強調增強團結與磋商機制的里斯本條約
at the heart of the matter is a conflict between the individual member states national interests the competitiveness of european defenserelated companies and the strategic importance of defense markets when linked to national foreign policy and the lisbon treaty, which refers specifically to enhanced solidarity and consultation.
如果我們希望遵重里斯本條約精神的話，那麼團結必須被視為一個重要的政治工具，並以此實現一個服務於集體利益的歐洲防禦政策。
if the lisbon treaty is to be respected, solidarity must be viewed as a political tool for moving towards a european defense policy that works for the common good.
而各國在技術轉讓方面對各自國家政策的追求則與該目標背道而馳。
pursuing solely national policies on technology transfer runs contrary to that goal.
因此必須出臺相關法則來對磋商機制進行更清晰的闡述，而出口武器的歐盟成員國必須與所有利益相關成員國進行協商，而不僅限於那些曾簽發（或禁止）類似許可證的國家。
clearer rules for the consultation mechanism need to be elaborated, and armsexporting eu member states should consult all other member governments that might have concerns, not only those that have previously issued or denied an export license.
透過各方對第三國行為的可預見性和穩定性達成共識的方式，歐盟可以最終構建一個共同的武器出口政策。
the eu could work towards a common armsexport policy by seeking a shared understanding of the predictability and stability of thirdparty countries.
但對第三國武器出口共同政策的制定程序不可孤立執行，同時還需要建立一個共有且具備國際競爭力的歐洲防務市場。
developing a common policy on arms exports to such countries should go hand in hand with the creation of a common and internationally competitive european defenseequipment market.
這意味著與非歐盟成員國的合作不應對歐盟內部的團結和共同原則造成損害。
this means that cooperation with noneu countries should not be to the detriment of solidarity and common rules within the eu.
儘早進行磋商有助於消弭誤解 — — 這些誤解通常會在媒體的添油加醋下不斷加深，即便交易還遠未達成 — — 並因此增強歐盟成員國之間的團結一致。
consulting at an early stage would help manage misperceptions often fueled by reports in the media long before deals are concluded and thus strengthen convergence and unity among eu member states.
在各成員國意見不一的情況下，歐盟應當扮演一個更重要的角色。
giving the eu a greater role in situations where member states views differ should also be considered.
比如成員國可以在政治和安全委員會內部就某些敏感或爭議性事務進行協商。
for example, member states could consult on sensitive or contentious issues within the political and security committee.
這將增強歐盟理事會共同立場的影響力，更何況這一立場已經對軍事技術和裝置的出口管制提出了大概的原則。
this would strengthen the eu councils common position, which already defines general rules for the control of exports of military technology and equipment.
對北約來說，盟國之間的磋商問題已經在《北大西洋公約》的第4條中進行了界定 ： “ 無論何時任何一締約國認為締約國中任何一國領土之完整，政治獨立或安全遭受威脅，各締約國應共同協商。 ”
as for nato, the question of consultations among allies is addressed in article 4 of the north atlantic treaty, which states that, the parties will consult together whenever, in the opinion of any of them, the territorial integrity, political independence, or security of any of the parties is threatened.
但上述第四條僅僅是針對即將到來的威脅。
but article 4 does not relate only to imminent threats.
一個北約成員國的決策可以影響到其他盟國。
decisions taken by a nato country can have implications for other allies.
對第三國的軍事裝備和技術轉讓可能影響到區域安全，並因此要對威脅態勢進行重新評估。
the transfer of military equipment and technology to third countries could affect regional security and prompt a revision of threat assessments.
北大西洋理事會顯然可以作為一個增進成員國團結，消除成員國對各種威脅的恐懼並避免誤解的論壇而存在。
the north atlantic council would seem an obvious forum within which to enhance solidarity among members, reassure member states that have perceptions of greater vulnerability, and avoid misperceptions.
在更底層級上，政治和夥伴關係委員會和/或國家軍事力量主管會議可以用作初步磋商。
at a lower level, the political and partnership committee andor the conference of national armaments directors could be used for initial consultations.
這些事務與所有盟國都利益攸關，因此討論也不應侷限於兩個國家之間。
these issues are of concern to all allies, so discussions should not be confined to bilateral agendas.
武器貿易和技術轉讓無疑會引發眾多道德和倫理問題，因此也必須在盟國之間進行公開且增強信心的討論。
arms sales and technology transfers inevitably raise complex moral and ethical questions. that is all the more reason to seek open, confidencereinforcing discussions among allies.
如果眾多重要機構都被排除在外的話，團結是無法實現的。
solidarity cannot be achieved when our most important institutions are excluded.
事實上，歐盟和北約曾經做出的某些最危險的決策，都是那些事前未被公開討論過的決定。
indeed, some of the most dangerous decisions taken in both the eu and nato are those that are not openly discussed beforehand.
邁向免疫的世界
toward an immunized world
阿布扎比/紐約—對一名孩子來說，接種疫苗只要幾秒鐘（大概還要搭上幾滴眼淚 ） 。
abu dhabinew york for a child, receiving a vaccine takes just a moment and perhaps a few tears.
但這幾秒種對於讓他獲得健康的生命起點、讓全球健康和發展目標獲得進步來說是至關重要的。
but such moments are crucial for getting children off to a healthy start in life, and for advancing progress on global health and development goals.
與阿布扎比太子阿勒納哈揚（Mohamed bin Zayed bin Sultan Al Nahyan）一起，我們將論述第一屆旨在確保所有兒童都能獲得疫苗的全部好處的全球峰會的巨大意義。 此次峰會將於本週在阿布扎比舉行。
along with mohamed bin zayed bin sultan al nahyan, crown prince of abu dhabi, we attach great importance to the worlds first global summit, being held this week in abu dhabi, aimed at ensuring that all children have access to the full benefits of vaccines.
疫苗為人們提供終生保護。
vaccines protect people for a lifetime.
它們是改善世界的最廉價的投資。
they are one of the most costeffective investments we can make to improve our world.
疫苗讓我們根除了天花，幾乎根除了小兒麻痺症，從麻疹、白喉、破傷風和其他致命致殘疾病手中拯救了數百萬兒童。
vaccines have eradicated smallpox, pushed polio to the verge of eradication, and saved millions of children from measles, diphtheria, tetanus, and other deadly and disabling diseases.
由於疫苗的作用，5歲前夭折的兒童數量從1960年的2000萬降至2011年的690萬，而且這是在地球人口大量增長的條件下實現的。
thanks in large part to the power of vaccines, the number of children dying before the age of five has fallen from 20 million in 1960 to 6.9 million in 2011, despite a large increase in global population.
疾病會侵蝕一國所擁有的最寶貴財富：人民的能量和天才。
disease saps the greatest asset that any country possesses the energy and talent of its people.
對於尋求立足全球經濟的窮國來說，代價尤其沉重。
this is an especially harsh loss for poor countries seeking to gain a foothold in the global economy.
而若兒童健康，家庭就能從沉重的醫療負擔中擺脫，將更多的錢用於食品和教育。
but when children are healthy, families are freed from the burden of costly medical care, allowing them to spend more on food and education.
健康的孩子能穩定地上學，獲得更好的學習能力，將來成為生產率更高的成年人。
healthy children attend school more regularly, are better able to learn, and become more productive adults.
新研究表明，疫苗能改善孩子的認知發展，提高勞動力生產率，有助於一國的總體經濟增長。
new research shows that vaccines improve cognitive development in children, raise labor productivity, and contribute to a countrys overall economic growth.
但超過2200萬的孩子缺少獲得基本疫苗的手段，而基本疫苗在高收入國家已是理所當然的福利。
yet more than 22 million children lack access to the basic vaccines that people in highincome countries take for granted.
這些孩子生活在最貧窮、最偏遠的社群，患病風險也最高。
these children live in the poorest and most remote communities, where the risk of disease is highest.
生於低收入國家的孩子在5歲前夭折的可能性比高收入國家孩子高18倍。
a child born in a lowincome country is 18 times more likely to die before reaching the age of five than a child in a highincome country.
結束這一不平等狀況是歷史上最大、最成功的減貧專案 — — 千年發展目標的核心。
ending this inequity is at the heart of historys largest and most successful antipoverty push the millennium development goals.
2000年，各國領導人齊聚聯合國，定下了八個千年發展目標，一致同意減少一半的極端貧困和飢餓、戰勝病魔、改善水安全和衛生、擴大教育、賦予女孩和婦女更多權利。
the eight mdgs were adopted in the year 2000, when leaders meeting at the united nations agreed to cut extreme poverty and hunger by half, fight disease, improve water safety and sanitation, expand education, and empower girls and women.
成就是斐然的，但仍有很多事情有待完成 — — 而現在距離2015年的最後時限已經不足1000天了。
there have been remarkable gains, but there is still much to do and fewer than 1,000 days of action left until the 2015 deadline.
全球免疫覆蓋面的增加將加速推動千年發展目標的實現併為2015年之後的發展日程的成功創造動力。
raising global immunization coverage will speed progress toward the mdgs and generate momentum toward a successful post2015 development agenda.
代表世界衛生組織194個成員國的世界衛生大會形成了一致的共同願景 — — 被稱為疫苗十年（Decade of Vaccines ） — —將打造沒有疫苗可防疾病的世界，讓免疫的全部好處抵達每一個人，不管他是誰、身處何方。
the world health assembly, representing the world health organizations 194 member countries, has endorsed a shared vision known as the decade of vaccines of a world free from vaccinepreventable diseases, with the full benefits of immunization reaching all people, regardless of who they are or where they live.
根除小兒麻痺症將是實現這一願景的一大里程碑。
eradicating polio will be a milestone on our path to realizing this vision.
峰會將釋出一個新的、全面的計劃，世界將有一個明確的路線圖在2018年建成沒有小兒麻痺症的世界。
with a new, comprehensive plan to be introduced at the summit, the world will have a clear roadmap for creating a poliofree world by 2018.
該計劃將與我們提高麻疹、肺炎和冠狀病毒等疾病的免疫覆蓋面的總體努力齊頭並進。
the plan works hand in hand with our overall efforts to raise immunization coverage against other diseases like measles, pneumonia, and rotavirus.
事實上，我們正在目睹強大的免疫系統保護我們在消滅小兒麻痺症的戰爭上的勝利，提供一個接觸世界最脆弱母親和兒童、為他們帶去新疫苗和基本醫療服務的平臺。
indeed, we are seeing how strong immunization systems protect our gains against polio and provide a platform for reaching the worlds most vulnerable mothers and children with new vaccines and primary health care.
如果我們成功，到這個十年末，我們將拯救2000多萬條生命，預防近10億例疾病，光是治療成本就能節省120億美元。
if we are successful, by the end of the decade we will save more than 20 million lives, prevent nearly one billion cases of illness, and save almost 12 billion in treatment costs alone.
而在讓人們擺脫疾病負擔的過程中，我們還能解放不可估量的人類潛力。
and, in the process of freeing people from the burden of disease, we will unlock immeasurable human potential.
千年發展目標和疫苗十年證明，齊心合力的全球發展目標能產生深遠不同。
the mdgs and the decade of vaccines prove that focused global development objectives can make a profound difference.
它們證明了把聯合國、政府、發展機構、公民社會、基金會和私人部門聯絡在一起的合作的力量有多大。
they show the power of partnerships that bring together the united nations, governments, development agencies, civil society, foundations, and the private sector.
在未來1000天裡，我們的進步將以我們在拯救最貧困、最脆弱人類家庭成員方面做了些什麼來衡量。
over the next 1,000 days and beyond, our progress will be measured by what we have done to improve the lives of the poorest and most vulnerable members of the human family.
讓我們從再次承諾實現所有孩子都能獲得受疫苗保護的公平起點的共同願景開始。
let us start by recommitting ourselves to realizing the shared vision of a world in which all children get a fair start in life with the protection of vaccines.
這一代人會感謝我們 — — 未來一代又一代人亦然。
this generation will thank us and so will many generations to come.
自大與權威
arrogance and authority
發自華盛頓特區 — — 最近耳邊充斥的都是各大歐美央行主管們對自身在2008~2010年危機中所作所為的評價 ： “ 咱們幹得不錯。
washington, dc it is increasingly common to hear prominent american and european central bankers proclaim, with respect to the crisis of 20082010, the following verdict we did well.
”在他們眼裡，正是一系列維護金融系統的政府行為協助穩定了整個局勢。
their view is that the various government actions to support the financial system helped to stabilize the situation.
而美聯儲的資產收購行為既然已經獲得了盈利（並隨後上繳了美國國庫 ） ， 那又什麼可指摘的呢？
indeed, what could be wrong when the united states federal reserves asset purchases may have actually made money which is then turned over to the us treasury?
但用這種思維來界定這一事務其實是有問題的：往輕了說，是被一時的錯覺遮了耳目；往重了說，這將催生出一種傲慢自大的偏見，最終腐蝕中央銀行得以構建其權威的基石 — — 公信力。
but to frame the issue in this way is, at best, to engage in delusion. at worst, however, it creates an image of arrogance that can only undermine the credibility on which central banks authority rests.
事實上，那場危機的真正成本根本無法用任何中央銀行的賬面盈虧來衡量 — — 也無法用美國財政部問題資產救助計劃（Troubled Asset Relief Program）的一系列行動是賺是虧來進行評估。
the real cost of the crisis is not measured by the profit and loss statement of any central bank or by whether or not the troubled asset relief program tarp, run by the treasury department, made or lost money on its various activities.
如果要說真正的成本，那就是僅美國就失去了800萬份工作，就業率也從最高峰下跌了6 % — —這也是與1945年後歷次衰退最大的不同之處 — — 如今距離危機爆發已經過去31個月了，失業率依然徘徊在低於最高峰5%的水平上。
the cost is eight million jobs in the us alone, with employment falling 6 from its peak and in a major departure from other post1945 recessions remaining 5 below that peak today, 31 months after the crisis broke in earnest.
另一項成本則是私人部門手中不斷增加的聯邦政府淨債務額 — — 該指標是計算政府債務的最準確手段。
the cost is also the increase in net federal government debt held by the private sector the most accurate measure of true government indebtedness.
對比美國國會預算辦公室在危機前（2008年1月）和危機後釋出的中期預測，這一債務的增加額相當於GDP的40 % ， 足以令人震驚不已了。
comparing the us congressional budget offices mediumterm forecasts before in january 2008 and after the crisis, this debt increase is a staggering 40 of gdp.
事實上，導致美國如今的財政危機（以及可能進一步傷害許多民眾的政府支出削減）的原因其實很簡單：各大銀行的危機使美國民眾付出了巨大的代價，並在全球範圍內造成了巨大的負面影響。
indeed, the reason there is a perceived fiscal crisis in the us today along with spending cuts that will further hurt many people is simple the banks blew themselves up at great cost to the american people, with major negative global implications.
美國和其他一些國家所出現的大部分公共債務並非源自於無節制的財政刺激政策，而是來自於本次衰退所引發的稅收銳減（加上布什政府為最富有的那批人減稅，經費不足的老年醫療保健藥物財政補貼，還有靠借債維持的阿富汗和伊拉克戰爭都嚴重削弱了美國的遠期財政前景 ） 。
most of the publicdebt increase in the us and elsewhere is not due to any kind of discretionary fiscal stimulus its all about the loss of tax revenue that comes with a deep recession. and the bush administrations tax cuts for the wealthiest, unfunded medicare prescription benefit, and debtfinanced wars in afghanistan and iraq have severely weakened the longterm fiscal outlook.
最後一項成本則是數百萬無家可歸者和被擾亂的生活，有些影響甚至將持續一輩子。
finally, the cost of the crisis is millions of homes lost and lives damaged, some permanently.
但問題不在於美聯儲或是其他中央銀行是否應當設法阻止本國銀行系統的崩潰。
the issue is not whether the fed, or any central bank, should seek to prevent the collapse of its countrys banking system.
如果想了解銀行危機的惡劣影響，最佳的範例莫過於1930年代（也是伯南克擔任美聯儲主席之前的研究領域 ） 。
to see the severe effects of a banking crisis, look no further than the 1930s, a period that ben bernanke studied in detail before he became fed chair.
如果在任何特定時期只有兩個選擇：要麼政府出手，要麼坐視其崩潰，那麼前者將是必然的選擇。
if the choice at any particular moment is to provide support or let the system collapse, you should choose support.
但在更廣泛的意義上，正如亞特蘭大聯邦儲備銀行主席丹尼斯·洛克哈特（Dennis Lockhart）上星期在該機構組織的一個公共論壇上所指出的那樣，我們不應試圖執行一個構建在“私人得益公眾受損”原則之上的銀行系統，更可況這些損失大多由一些效率極低的行為方式所造成，而且毫無公平可言。
but, more broadly, as dennis lockhart, president of the atlanta federal reserve bank, said last week at a public conference organized by his institution, we should not seek to operate a system based on the principle of private gains and public losses. and these losses are massively skewed in ways that are grossly inefficient, in addition to being completely unfair.
相反私人得到的好處則可以透過管理人員津貼的數額來直接計算得出。
the private gains can be measured most directly in the form of executive compensation.
從2000年到2008年，全美前14家金融機構的管理者總共獲得了大約26億美元的現金津貼（包括工資，分紅和股票出售在內 ） 。
from 2000 to 2008, the people running the top 14 us financial institutions received cash compensation salary, bonus, and the value of stock sold of around 2.6 billion.
到如今，前五位收入最高的人合共收取了近20億美元，而他們恰巧也是構建了整個高風險資產架構並險些將金融系統推入深淵的始作俑者：山迪·維爾（建立了花旗集團，該集團在他離職不久後就爆發了危機 ） 、 漢克·保爾森（大規模擴充套件了高盛集團業務並說服國會允許投資銀行採取更高投資槓桿，然後又搖身一變到美國財政部赴任去協助拯救這些銀行 ） 、 安傑羅·莫茲洛（創立美國國家金融服務公司Countrywide financial corp . ， 是濫發抵���貸款的主要推手 ） ， 迪克·福德和傑米·卡尼（分別是雷曼兄弟和貝爾斯登的送葬者 ） 。
of this amount, around 2 billion was received by the five bestpaid individuals, who were also central to creating the highly risky asset structures that brought the financial system to the edge of the abyss sandy weil built citigroup, which blew up shortly after he left hank paulson greatly expanded goldman sachs, lobbied for allowing more leverage in investment banks, then moved to the us treasury and helped save them angelo mozilo built countrywide, a central player in irresponsible mortgage lending dick fuld ran lehman brothers into the ground and jimmy cayne ran bear stearns into the ground.
相比之下公眾的損失則極為巨大：如果僅僅用聯邦政府的債務增長來評估的話，大概60億美元。
the public losses are massive in comparison roughly 6 trillion, if we limit ourselves just to the increase in federal government debt.
但那些銀行大佬們卻依然堅持自己應當被允許運營更高槓杆的全球業務，並基於企業股票回報率來向他們支付報酬 — — 無論出現任何風險。
and leading bank executives still insist that they should be allowed to run highly leveraged global businesses, in which they are paid based on their return on equity unadjusted for any risk.
為此有一批全球最頂尖的獨立金融研究者也正以長遠而嚴謹的眼光觀察這類事務，而我們近幾年的研究顯示情況比想象中更糟（詳見斯坦福大學商學院教授安娜特·阿德瑪蒂Anat Admati的網頁 ） 。
the worlds top independent financial minds have looked long and hard at these arrangements, and, given what we have learned in recent years, have found them worse than wanting see the web page of anat admati at stanfords graduate school of business for the details.
在他們看來，大銀行應具備更多的準備金 — — 大概應占其資本總額的30 % 。
in their view, the big banks should be funded much more with equity perhaps as much as 30 of their capitalization.
但銀行家們則強烈反對這一建議（因為這很可能減少他們的收入 ） ， 而中央銀行管理者們也持有類似的立場（他們都被銀行家的抗議所說服了 ） 。
but bankers strongly reject this approach because it would likely lower their pay, as do central bankers because they are too much persuaded by the protestation of bankers.
如能有一個由遠離政界的專業人士來運作的獨立中央銀行，那是有許多好處的。
there are many advantages to having an independent central bank run by professionals who can keep their distance from politicians.
但當掌管這些金融機構的人都堅持自己在危機中做得很好，宣稱所有問題都會解決，放任那些引發危機的金融巨鱷們逍遙法外，那麼他們的公信力也將不可避免地受到損害。
but when the people at the apex of these institutions insist that the crisis response went well, and that everything will be fine, even as the financial behemoths that caused the crisis lumber forward, their credibility inevitably suffers.
這一切都應當令中央銀行管理者們感到憂心，因為公信力就是他們的一切。
that should worry central bankers, because their credibility is pretty much all they have.
畢竟美國憲法並不保證美聯儲的獨立。
the us constitution, after all, does not guarantee the feds independence.
國會創造了美聯儲，也可以解散它。
congress created the fed, which means that congress can uncreate it.
透過忽視高槓杆大銀行所可能造成的危害，一場“壞事變好事”的危機神話帶來的，僅僅是中央銀行身上的不斷累積政治壓力而已。
by assuming away the damage that highly leveraged megabanks can do, the myth of a good crisis merely makes political pressure on central banks all the more likely.
人工智慧和全球化
artificial intelligence and globalization
今天的常規看法是：印度和中國的崛起將成為21世紀推動全球就業和薪酬的唯一重要因素。
todays conventional wisdom is that the rise of india and china will be the single biggest factor driving global jobs and wages over the twentyfirst century.
富裕國家的高薪勞動者將會看到：自己的競爭優勢在來自亞洲、拉美、甚至有一天也會包括非洲的極其吃苦耐勞的能幹競爭者的侵蝕之下不斷減弱。
highwage workers in rich countries can expect to see their competitive advantage steadily eroded by competition from capable and fiercely hardworking competitors in asia, latin america, and maybe even some day africa.
這是件好事，充分展現了權力政治和人類生活的戲劇性。
this is a good story, full of human drama and power politics.
但是我更想知道：今後幾十年內，是否會有另外一個因素對我們的職業生涯造成更大的影響：這個因素就是人工智慧應用的指數級增長。
but i wonder whether, even within the next few decades, another factor will influence our work lives even more the exponential rise of applications of artificial intelligence.
我對人工智慧的接觸範圍非常狹窄：那就是有著500多年曆史的國際象棋運動。
my portal to the world of artificial intelligence is a narrow one the more than 500yearold game of chess.
你可能對早就被公認為終極智慧運動的象棋毫無興趣。
you may not care a whit about chess, long regarded as the ultimate intellectual sport.
即便如此，過去10年來國際象棋界令人驚歎的發展也足以引起你的關注。
but the stunning developments coming out of the chess world during the past decade should still command your attention.
國際象棋在人工智慧的研究中一直是核心環節。
chess has long been the centerpiece of research in artificial intelligence.
儘管從原則上看，國際象棋是可解的運動，但其計算的複雜程度幾乎超出了所有人的想象。
while in principle, chess is solvable, the games computational complexity is almost incomprehensible.
如果有人說在國際象棋比賽中走棋的方法比宇宙中的原子還要多，也只是稍有誇張而已。
it is only a slight exaggeration to say there are more possible moves in a chess game than atoms in a universe.
20世紀大多數時候，程式設計師們在設計能與頂尖人類選手較量的國際象棋電腦時顯然都未獲成功。
for most of the twentieth century, programmers were patently unsuccessful in designing chess computers that could compete with the best humans.
人類國際象棋大師的直覺、想象和排序能力輕易就可以勝過電腦的橫衝直撞。
a human chess masters ability to intuit, visualize, and prioritize easily prevailed over the brute force approach of computers.
電腦在一點一滴地逐漸進步，但要與頂尖的人類高手較量似乎還相去甚遠。
the computers gradually improved, but they still seemed far inferior to the top humans.
至少我們是這麼認為的。
or so we thought.
而後，在1997年，在那個註定要作為現代人類的豐碑載入史冊的時刻，IBM的“深藍”電腦戰勝了世界象棋冠軍卡斯帕羅夫（Gary Kasparov ） ， 令世界為之震驚。
then, in 1997, in what will surely long be remembered as a historical milestone for modern man, ibms deep blue computer stunned the world by defeating the world champion garry kasparov.
也許驕傲的卡斯帕羅夫受到的震動比任何人都大，他一口咬定IBM的團隊肯定做了手腳。
proud kasparov, who was perhaps more stunned than anyone, was sure that the ibm team must have cheated.
他以諷刺的口吻告訴記者，他感到“上帝之手”在指引著他的電腦對手。
he sarcastically told reporters that he sensed the the hand of god guiding his silicon opponent.
但IBM的團隊沒有作弊。
but the ibm team had not cheated.
相反，透過把獨創性的軟體和強大的平行運算能力結合在一起，他們成功地締造出一臺以矽晶片為介質的實體，這臺機器掌握瞭如此精密微妙的運算技巧，以至於全世界所有的國際象棋大師（包括我本人在內）都大吃一驚。
rather, through a combination of ingenious software and massive parallel computing power, they had produced a siliconbased entity capable of such finesse and subtlety, that international chess grandmasters worldwide including me were simply amazed.
1997年後，電腦已經如此進步，以至於程式設計師們可以把戰勝人類當作小菜一碟。
since 1997, the computers have only gotten better, to the point where computer programmers no longer find beating humans a great challenge.
你說這只是一場遊戲？
only a game, you say?
也許你是對的，但讓我告訴你：30年前我專業從事國際象棋的時候（我曾經代表美國隊參加國際象棋世界冠軍迴圈賽 ） ， 我感到自己可以透過看別人的棋譜瞭解那個人的個性狀況，國際象棋的業餘愛好者也不例外。
perhaps, but let me tell you this when i played professional chess 30 years ago i once represented the united states in the world chess championship cycle, i felt i could tell a lot about someones personality by seeing a sampling of their games, even those of an amateur.
不久以前，我還可以輕易地對電腦和真人對手加以區分。
until a short while ago, i could certainly distinguish a computer from a human opponent.
如今一切都發生了變化。
now everything changed like lightning.
電腦甚至可以模擬著名的真人棋手¾包括他們的缺點¾電腦都能模擬得惟妙惟肖，只有專業棋手（有時甚至只有另一臺電腦！ ）才能看出其中的差別。
the machines can now even be set to imitate famous human players including their flaws so well that only an expert eye and sometimes only another computer! can tell the difference.
半個多世紀以前，人工智慧領域的教父阿蘭·圖靈（Alan Turing）提出大腦的功能可以全部歸結為數學運算，而且終有一天，電腦能夠達到人類的智慧。
more than half a century ago, the godfather of artificial intelligence, alan turing, argued that the brains function could all be reduced to mathematics and that, someday, a computer would rival human intelligence.
他提出實現終極人工智慧的佐證是真人在進行對��時，無法知曉與自己對話的其實是一臺電腦。
he claimed that the ultimate proof of artificial intelligence would be met if a human interrogator were unable to figure out that he was conversing with a computer.
“圖靈測試”被視作人工智慧研究領域的聖盃。
the turing test is the holy grail of artificial intelligence research.
對我來講，象棋比賽是一種邏輯會話。
well, for me, a chess game is a conversation of sorts.
而且在我看來，今天已有的電腦程式與圖靈測試的要求幾乎相差無幾。
from my perspective, todays offtheshelf computer programs come awfully close to meeting turings test.
從幾次網上對弈所瞭解的情況看，我很難發現其中的差別。
over the course of a small number of games on the internet, i could not easily tell the difference.
沒錯，今天的電腦還沒有達到斯坦利·庫布里克（Stanley Kubrick）導演在其代表作《2001：太空漫遊》中塑造的瘋狂電腦HAL所能達到的水準，更不用說《終結者》系列影片中阿諾德·施瓦辛格（Arnold Schwarzenegger）式的機器人了。
true, todays computers have not evolved to the level of the deranged chessplaying hal in the filmmaker stanley kubricks masterpiece 2001 a space odyssey, much less arnold schwarzeneggerlike droids from the terminator movies.
但電腦現有的水準已經足以令人毛骨悚然。
but the level that computers have reached already is scary enough.
接下來會發生什麼？
whats next?
我覺得自己作為經濟學教授的地位一點都不穩固！
i certainly dont feel safe as an economics professor!
我毫不懷疑地確信：本世紀晚些時候，人們可以買到袖珍教授¾沒準還帶有教授的全息影像¾就像今天購買袖珍卡斯帕羅夫象棋電腦那樣易如反掌。
i have no doubt that sometime later this century, one will be able to buy pocket professors perhaps with holographic images as easily as one can buy a pocket kasparov chess computer today.
讓我們回頭看看印度和中國。
so lets go back to india and china.
全球化在上個世紀的多數時候都快速發展， 近20年來的發展更是尤為迅速。
globalization proceeded at a rapid pace through much of the last century, and at a particularly accelerated rate during its last two decades.
但多數證據顯示：技術變革能夠比貿易更有效地推動全球薪酬格局的發展。
yet the vast body of evidence suggests that technological changes were a much bigger driver in global wage patterns than trade.
也就是說，技術，而非貿易，才是21世紀經濟的主題（當然，這兩者相互影響，貿易刺激技術發展，推動技術傳播，但這恐怕更多的是一種文字遊戲 ） 。
that is, technology, not trade, was the big story of the twentiethcentury economy of course, the two interact, with trade helping to diffuse and stimulate technology, but this is a matter of semantics.
我們能否確定這個世紀會發生變化？
are we so sure that it will be different in this century?
人工智慧能否徹底取代外包和製造業遷移所設下的咒語？
or will artificial intelligence replace the mantra of outsourcing and manufacturing migration?
棋手們其實早已知道這個問題的答案。
chess players already know the answer.
第二次機器時代的教育
education in the second machine age
慕尼黑—人工智慧曾經僅限於科幻小說，但如今正在改變我們的生活。
munich artificial intelligence, once confined to the realm of science fiction, is changing our lives.
汽車自己會駕駛。
cars are driving themselves.
無人機可以設定程式用於遞送包裹。
drones are being programmed to deliver packages.
計算機正在學習診斷疾病。
computers are learning to diagnose diseases.
經濟學家埃裡克·布萊恩約爾弗森（Erik Brynjolfsson）和安德魯·邁克菲（Andrew McAfee）在他們的新書中將這些最新進步描述為他們所謂的“第二次機器時代”開始的例子。
in a recent book, the economists erik brynjolfsson and andrew mcafee describe these recent advances as examples of the beginning of what they call the second machine age.
這個名字 — — 第一次機器時代是工業革命 — — 暗示了一個劃時代的變化。
the very name the first machine age was the industrial revolution suggests an epochal shift.
事實上，如果預言可信，這些技術進步能夠給我們的生活帶來深遠影響。
and, indeed, if the predictions are to be believed, these technological advances could have profound implications for the way we live.
一個普遍的預測是，隨著越來越先進的機器人開始取代工人，勞動力成本將變得越來越不重要，製造業將回流富裕國家。
one common forecast is that as evermore advanced robots substitute workers, the cost of labor will become less important, and manufacturing will move back to rich countries.
另一個預測是日益智慧的機器將減少對高階技能的需求，擁有這些技能所帶來的經濟優勢也將因此縮水。
another is that increasingly intelligent machines will reduce the demand for advanced skills, and that the economic advantage of having these skills will decline as a result.
這兩個假說的第一個仍然有些牽強。
the first of these two hypotheses remains farfetched.
但有證據表明第二個假說正在成為現實，對現代經濟面臨全球化挑戰的應對方式造成著巨大影響。
but there is evidence that the second has already started to come to pass, with serious implications for the way that modern economies have attempted to meet the challenges of globalization.
誠然，有大量非正式證據表明“回岸 ” （ reshoring）正在發生 — — 即就業崗位從低薪酬國家重新回到高薪酬國家。
to be sure, there has been plenty of anecdotal evidence of reshoring the relocation of jobs from lowwage countries to highwage economies.
蘋果公司正在把一些製造業務從中國遷回矽谷；Airtex設計集團正在將一部分紡織生產從中國遷回美國。
apple is shifting some manufacturing from china to silicon valley airtex design group is moving part of its textile production from china back to the united states.
普華永道管理諮詢公司對384家歐元區企業的最新調查中，三分之二的受訪者表示在過去一年中實施了一些回岸動作，50%的受訪者表示準備在明年這樣做。
in a recent survey of 384 firms in the eurozone by the management consultancy pricewaterhousecoopers, twothirds of the respondents said that they had reshored some activities during the past year, and 50 plan to do so in the next.
但資料並沒有表現出回岸訊號。
but when one looks at the data, there is no sign of reshoring.
事實上，趨勢仍與回岸背道而馳。
indeed, the trend is continuing in the opposite direction.
離岸自2008年全球金融危機引發大衰退以來有所下降，但隨後馬上發生了反彈，並加速超過了危機前水平。
offshoring dropped during the great recession that followed the 2008 global financial crisis, but quickly rebounded, accelerating past precrisis levels.
眼下，製造業迴歸富裕國家仍然只是預言而不是結果。
for the moment, the return of manufacturing to rich countries remains a prediction, not an outcome.
評估第二個假說更加複雜。
evaluating the second hypothesis is more complicated.
咋一看，證據支援對高階技能需求下降的可能性。
at first glance, the evidence supports the possibility that demand for advanced skills is falling.
在過去17年中，除了美國和德國，所有西方國家高技能工人和非高技能工人之間的薪酬差都有所縮小。
with the exceptions of the us and germany, the wage gap between skilled and unskilled workers has been declining in all western countries in the last 17 years.
一個可能的解釋是歐洲教育水平超過了技術變化的速度，高階技能出現了過度供給。
one possible explanation is that education levels in europe outstripped the pace of technological change, oversupplying the market for advanced skills.
在奧地利，擁有大學文憑或同等學力的人口比例在1996到2012年間增長了250 % 。
in austria, the share of people with a university degree or its equivalent increased by 250 between 1996 and 2012.
在英國和義大利，這一比例接近翻番。
in the united kingdom and italy, it almost doubled.
在西班牙，該比例上升70 % ， 法國則是60 % 。
in spain, it jumped by 70, and in france by 60.
相反，美國和德國高等教育學歷擁有者比例只是略微升高了25 % 。
by comparison, in the us and germany, the share of the population with a tertiary education rose by a more modest 25.
但是，另一個可能是高技能和非高技能工人薪酬差距縮小體現了機器的日益智慧化。
it is also possible, however, that the drop in the wage gap between skilled and unskilled workers represents competition from increasingly intelligent machines.
在這方面，美國是一個典型。
here, the us is a case in point.
自世紀之交以來，美國的教育入學率只是略有增加，因此，我們應該預期薪酬差距會顯著增加，就像20世紀八九十年代那樣。
because educational attainment has been advancing only modestly in the us since the turn of the century, we would expect the wage gap to be rising steeply, as it did in the 1980s and 1990s.
相反，薪酬差距基本保持不變，增加的是高技能工人的失業率，2000—2012年，該指標在美國和英國增加了一倍。
instead, it has remained largely unchanged, and it is the unemployment rate among skilled workers that is on the rise, doubling in the us and the united kingdom from 2000 to 2012.
20世紀80年代前，大約70%的收入屬於勞動收入，30%為資本收入。
until the 1980s, about 70 of income went to labor income and 30 to capital income.
但是，自此以後，收入歸屬勞動的比例在所有富裕國家都有所下降。
but, since then, the share of income going to labor has declined in all rich countries.
如今這一比例為GDP的58 % 。
it is now at about 58 of gdp.
根據經濟學家盧卡斯·卡拉巴波尼斯（Loukas Karabarbounis）和布倫特·尼曼（Brent Neiman）的研究，這一下降有一半要歸因於更加廉價的資訊科技，資訊科技的廉價化讓企業得以用計算機取代工人。
according to research by the economists loukas karabarbounis and brent neiman, half of this decline is the result of cheaper information technology, which has enabled firms to replace workers with computers.
影響是嚴重的。
the implications are serious.
如果這些確實是第二次機器時代的第一批訊號，有可能我們正在打一場錯誤的戰爭。
if these are indeed the first signs of the second machine age, it is possible that we have been fighting the wrong battle.
隨著人力資本稀缺日益變得不重要，教育的快速��張也許並非如我們所願的那樣是全球化挑戰的答案。
as the scarcity of human capital declines in importance, the rapid expansion of education may not be the answer to the challenges of globalization that we hoped it would be.
人工智慧的前途和陷阱
the promise and pitfalls of ai
布魯塞爾 — — 與任何革命性的趨勢一樣，人工智慧（AI）的崛起同樣帶來了重大的機遇和難以應對的挑戰。
brussels like any transformative trend, the rise of artificial intelligence ai poses both major opportunities and significant challenges.
但其中最嚴重的可能並不是最常討論的風險。
but the gravest risks may not be the ones most often discussed.
據麥肯錫全球研究院（MGI）最新研究顯示，人工智慧具備顯著提高整體經濟生產率的潛能。
according to new research from the mckinsey global institute mgi, ai has the potential to boost overall economic productivity significantly.
即使考慮到過渡成本和競爭效應，截至2030年它也可以使總產量增加13萬億美元，同時每年提高全球GDP 1.2%左右。
even accounting for transition costs and competition effects, it could add some 13 trillion to total output by 2030 and boost global gdp by about 1.2 per year.
這將超過 — — 或至少也能與過去通用技術的經濟影響力相媲美，包括19世紀的蒸汽動力、20世紀的工業製造以及21世紀的資訊科技。
this is comparable to or even larger than the economic impact of past generalpurpose technologies, such as steam power during the 1800s, industrial manufacturing in the 1900s, and information technology during the 2000s.
也許人工智慧最讓人們擔憂的問題是其未來取代的崗位可能比創造的更多。
perhaps the most discussed concern about ai is the prospect that intelligent machines will replace more jobs than they create.
但麥肯錫全球研究院的研究顯示，長期來看，人工智慧的採用或許並不會對淨就業產生重大的影響。
but mgis research found that the adoption of ai may not have a significant effect on net employment in the long term.
截至2030年，對該行業的追加投資可以貢獻5%的就業崗位，而其所創造的增量財富可以推升勞動力需求，實現就業率再提高12 % 。
extra investment in the sector could contribute 5 to employment by 2030, and the additional wealth created could drive up labor demand, boosting employment by another 12.
但儘管整體狀況十分樂觀，不好的訊息也同樣存在。
but while the overall picture is positive, the news is not all good.
首先，感受人工智慧的好處可能需要時間 — — 尤其是在生產率方面。
for one thing, it is possible that it will take time for ais benefits particularly with regard to productivity to be felt.
事實上，麥肯錫全球研究院的研究表明截止2030年，人工智慧對增長的貢獻可能是今後五年的3到5倍。
indeed, mgis research suggests that ais contribution to growth may be three or more times higher by 2030 than it is over the next five years.
上述結果與所謂的索洛計算機悖論相一致：生產率的提升落後於技術進步 — — 這是數字革命期間一個值得關注的現象。
this is in line with the socalled solow computer paradox productivity gains lag behind technological advances a notable phenomenon during the digital revolution.
部分原因是，起初，經濟體面臨高額的落地和轉型成本，而這種成本往往會被人工智慧對經濟影響的研究忽略掉。
this is partly because, initially, economies face high implementation and transition costs, which estimates of ais economic impact tend to ignore.
麥肯錫國際研究院的模擬研究表明，未來五年這些成本將佔到潛在總收益的80 % ， 而到2030年卻將下降至潛在總收益的1/3左右。
mgis simulation suggests that these costs will amount to 80 of gross potential gains in five years, but will decline to onethird of those gains by 2030.
人工智慧革命另外一個令人不安的潛在特徵是它所產生的效益不太可能得到公平的分配。
the more troubling potential feature of the ai revolution is that its benefits are not likely to be shared equitably.
由此帶來的“人工智慧差異”將進一步強化數字差異己經造成的經濟不平等和破壞競爭的鴻溝。
the resulting ai divides will reinforce the digital divides that are already fueling economic inequality and undermining competition.
上述差異可能來源於三個領域。
these divides could emerge in three areas.
第一個差異很有可能出現在公司層面。
the first divide would emerge at the company level.
充分採用人工智慧技術的創新型前沿企業可以在現在到2030年這段時間內實現現金流量翻倍 — — 這樣的結果很有可能導致聘用更多工人。
innovative, leadingedge companies that fully adopt ai technologies could double their cash flow between now and 2030 an outcome that would likely entail hiring many more workers.
這些企業將遠遠拋下那些不願或不能以同等速度採用人工智慧技術的企業。
these companies would leave in the dust those that are unwilling or unable to implement ai technologies at the same rate.
事實上，完全不採用人工智慧技術的企業可能因市場份額的喪失而面臨20%左右的現金流下降，從而致使他們面臨裁員的壓力。
in fact, firms that do not adopt ai at all could experience a 20 decline in their cash flow as they lose market share, putting them under pressure to shed workers.
第二個差異關乎到技能。
the second divide concerns skills.
人工智慧技術的普及將使勞動力需求從可以輕易實現自動化或平臺外包的重複性任務過渡到更多依賴社交或認知驅動。
the proliferation of ai technologies will shift labor demand away from repetitive tasks that can more easily be automated or outsourced to platforms, toward socially or cognitively driven tasks.
麥肯錫全球研究院模型顯示以重複性操作和低數字技術含量為特徵的職務可能從佔就業總人數的40%下降到2030年的僅30%左右。
mgis models indicate that job profiles characterized by repetitive tasks and little digital knowhow could fall from some 40 of total employment to near 30 by 2030.
同時，需要非重複性勞動或高水平數字技術的工作很可能從約40%上升至50%以上。
meanwhile, the share of jobs entailing nonrepetitive activities or requiring highlevel digital skills is likely to rise from some 40 to more than 50.
這樣的轉變可能導致工資差距拉大，約13%的工資總額可能轉向需要高水平數字技術的非重複性工作，因為上述領域的收入增加。
this shift could contribute to an increase in wage differentials, with around 13 of the total wage bill potentially shifting to nonrepetitive jobs requiring highlevel digital skills, as incomes in those fields rise.
從事重複性和低數字技術類職務的員工可能遭遇到工資停滯甚至減少，導致他們在工資總額中的比率從33%下降到20%左右。
workers in the repetitive and lowdigitalskills categories may experience wage stagnation or even reduction, contributing to a decline in their share of the total wage bill from 33 to 20.
第三項人工智慧差異在不同國家間已經非常明顯，並且勢將進一步擴大。
the third ai divide among countries is already apparent, and seems set to widen further.
這些國家，其中絕大多數為發達國家，將自身定位為人工智慧領導者，與今天相比可能獲得20~25%的額外經濟收入，而新興經濟體可能僅增加5~15 % 。
those countries, mostly in the developed world, that establish themselves as ai leaders could capture an additional 2025 in economic benefits compared with today, while emerging economies may accrue only an extra 515.
發達經濟體在人工智慧應用方面具有顯著的優勢，因為他們在落實此前的數字技術方面能夠更進一步。
the advanced economies have a clear advantage in adopting ai, because they are further along in the implementation of previous digital technologies.
他們還有極強的動機來採用人工智慧技術：低生產率增長、人口老齡化和勞動力成本相對較高。
they also have powerful incentives to adopt ai low productivity growth, aging populations, and relatively high labor costs.
相比之下，許多發展中經濟體的數字設施嚴重不足，創新和投資能力薄弱，而且缺乏牢固的技術基礎。
by contrast, many developing economies have insufficient digital infrastructure, weak innovation and investment capacity, and thin skills base.
再加上低工資的動機抑制效應和充足的生產力追趕空間，這些經濟體似乎不太可能在人工智慧應用領域與那些發達國家夥伴保持同步。
add to that the motivationdampening effects of low wages and ample space for productivity catchup, and it seems unlikely that these economies will keep pace with their advanced counterparts in ai adoption.
這些人工智慧差異的興起和擴大並不是不可避免的。
the emergence or expansion of these ai divides is not inevitable.
尤其是發展中經濟體可以選擇採用前瞻性的思維方法，包括強化其數字基礎並積極鼓勵人工智慧應用。
in particular, developing economies can choose to take a forwardthinking approach that includes strengthening their digital foundations and actively encouraging ai adoption.
同時，為了確保滿足不斷變化的工作需求，企業可以在支援低技術群體的教育升級和持續學習方面發揮更加積極的作用。
and, to ensure that their changing workplace needs are met, firms can take a more active role in supporting educational upgrading and continuous learning for lowerskill people.
而且，這些差異的存在也並不一定只起到消極作用。
moreover, these divides are not necessarily a negative development.
將資源重新分配給業績更好的企業可以使經濟發展更加健康，從而使它們在面對來自其他國家的競爭時更具有競爭優勢。
the reallocation of resources toward higherperforming companies makes economies healthier, potentially providing them with new competitive advantages visvis other countries.
但上述差異所造成的風險絕對不容低估。
but the risks posed by these divides should not be underestimated.
遠見和毅力對於人工智慧革命的成功至關重要，因為它在帶來長期收益之前將會造成短期的痛苦。
vision and perseverance are essential to make the ai revolution work, because it will bring shortterm pain before longterm gains.
如果上述痛苦出現在人工智慧收益分配不均且令民眾倍感沮喪的背景下，可能就會引發對技術的強烈抵制，而同樣的技術在不同的情況下本來是可以創造出提高生產率、增加收入和催生就業需求的良性迴圈的。
if that pain occurs against a backdrop of frustration with the unequal distribution of ais benefits, it may trigger a backlash against technologies that could otherwise produce a virtuous cycle of higher productivity, income growth, and employmentboosting demand.
發展中世界的AI憧憬
the promise of ai in the developing world
倫敦—數字趨勢觀察家們的一個常見誤解是發展中國家消費者沒有從技術進步中獲益。
london a common misperception among observers of digital trends is that consumers in developing countries do not benefit from advances in technology.
不管是擁有最新款智慧手機，還是“僱用”機器人清掃機，獲得創新的能力是富國和窮國之間最醒目的差異之一。
whether it is owning the latest smartphone or employing robot cleaners, the ability to access innovation is one of the most visible differences between rich and poor countries.
這一差距因為人工智慧（AI）的出現而變得更加顯著。
this gap has become even more pronounced since the advent of artificial intelligence ai.
比如，絕大部分家用“智慧音箱 ” ， 如亞馬遜的Alexa，都銷往了富裕國家。
for example, the vast majority of home smart speaker personal assistants, like amazons alexa, are shipped to wealthy countries.
2017年，超八成的全球智慧音箱出貨量銷往北美。
in 2017, over 80 of global smart speaker shipments were to north america.
但儘管技術可能深化全球不平等，也有能力減輕全球不平等。
but while technology can deepen global inequality, it also has the potential to mitigate it.
這是因為，AI能夠實現許多電器無法實現的功能；它還有可能掀起全球南方醫療、減災、金融、物流、教育和商業服務的實現方式革命。
this is because ai can do much more than power appliances it can also revolutionize the way health care, disaster relief, finance, logistics, education, and business services are delivered in the global south.
放眼全球，AI已經開始改變發展中國家。
around the world, ai is already transforming developing countries.
在尼泊爾，機器學習勾勒並分析震後重建需求。
in nepal, machine learning is mapping and analyzing postearthquake reconstruction needs.
在整個非洲，AI輔導幫助年輕學生追趕功課。
across africa, ai tutors are helping young students catch up on coursework.
人道主義援助機構運用大資料分析最佳化如何為逃離衝突和其他困境的難民實現供給。
humanitarian aid agencies are using big data analytics to optimize the delivery of supplies for refugees fleeing conflict and other hardships.
在我的祖國印度，農民用AI應用改善莊家產量，提高利潤。
and in my country, india, rural farmers use ai applications to improve crop yields and boost profits.
這些創新讓我們越來越接近實現聯合國在消除貧困、消除醫療不平等、提高入學普及、遏制全球變暖等關鍵問題上的可持續發展目標。
innovations like these bring us closer to achieving the united nations sustainable development goals on issues like eradicating poverty, ending healthcare inequality, increasing access to schooling, and combating global warming.
而AI可以為人類進步做出的貢獻，人們只利用了九牛一毛。
and yet the world is just scratching the surface of what ai can do for human progress.
要充分利用AI的力量推動發展，我們必須找到新的應用方法。
to harness ais full power to advance development, we must find new ways to apply it.
比如，在正確的支援下，可以用無人機向發展中國家的偏遠醫院運送藥品補給。
for example, with the right support, the skies above developing countries could be filled with drones delivering medical supplies to remote hospitals.
盧安達農村已經在這麼做，該國衛生部和矽谷科技初創企業Zipline進行了獨到的合作，幫助難以進入地區的診所實現簡訊預定血漿，並在幾分鐘內透過空投投送。
this is already happening in rural rwanda, where a unique partnership between the health ministry and zipline, a silicon valleybased tech startup, is giving doctors in hardtoreach clinics the ability to order blood by text message, and then have it arrive by parachute in a matter of minutes.
該計劃自2016年10月開始實施以來，投送時間已經縮短了五倍，拯救了數百人的生命。
since the program launched in october 2016, delivery times have been cut by a factor of five, and hundreds of lives have been saved.
儘管如此，諸如此類的AI創新固然令人印象深刻，但絕非理所當然。
still, while ai innovations like this one are impressive, we cannot take them for granted.
除非我們能夠克服普遍存在的錯誤擔憂 — — AI 弊大於利，否則科技公司為全球南方所帶來的令人難以置信的進步將日益放緩。
unless we counter the misplaced but wellpublicized fears that ai disruptions will be worse than the rewards, the incredible progress that technology companies are making in the global south will be slowed.
可以採取諸多措施避免這一結果。
there are a number of steps that can be taken to avoid this outcome.
首先，諸如聯合國“良性AI”運動這樣的計劃，旨在實現關於如何透過技術讓人道工作受益的對話，應該獲得決策者的全力支援。
for starters, programs like the uns ai for good campaign, which is aimed at fostering dialogue on the beneficial use of technology for humanitarian work, must receive the full support of policymakers.
我們這些參與技術開發的人士也必須不斷地辨別哪些專案、計劃、智庫和組織能夠從與AI企業的合作中獲益，就像盧安達的Zipline那樣。
those of us involved in technology development must also continue to identify the projects, initiatives, think tanks, and organizations that would benefit from cooperation with ai firms like zipline in rwanda.
但最重要的是，關於出於人道主義目的的AI開發的對話，不能只在援助組織、慈善機構和政府間進行。
but, most important, conversations about developing ai for humanitarian purposes cannot be conducted in isolation by aid organizations, charities, and governments.
科技投資者也必須參與其中。
technology investors must also have a seat at the table.
長期以來，科技創業家注意力集中在解決全球北方的問題，而忽視了傳統上與發展中國家相關的問題。
for too long, technology entrepreneurs have focused on solving problems in the global north, while ignoring issues traditionally associated with developing countries.
但移動技術正在開啟新的機會大門，如今，將AI方案的目標對準西方國家之外的地區在人道和商業上都很有意義。
but mobile technology is opening new doors of opportunity, and it now makes humanitarian and business sense to target ai solutions far beyond western countries.
因此，我成立了規模1億美元的投資公司Rewired，支援參與解決重要社會問題的初創AI和機器人企業。
that is why i established rewired, a 100 million investment vehicle that supports embryonic ai and robotics firms engaged in addressing important social issues.
Rewired公司與機器知覺領先企業合作 — — 機器感知即機器人理解和解讀物理世界的能力。
rewired works with firms at the vanguard of machine perception the ability of robots to understand and interpret the physical world.
我們投資的公司致力於複製人類嗅覺、開發平價靈敏假肢、創造改善製造流程的便攜機器等領域。
we have invested in companies that are working to replicate human smell, to develop affordable and dexterous prosthetics, and to create portable machines designed to improve manufacturing processes.
我們的目標是為潛力企業提供資金，改善世界各國的生活質量。
our goal is to fund technologies with the potential to enhance quality of life in every country around the world.
我相信，這將是AI的一致特徵。
and that, i believe, will be ais unifying characteristic.
我們今天所創造的機器不但能夠盈利；還能讓我們距離解決某些世界最大挑戰更近一步。
the machines we create today will not only be profitable they will also bring us closer to solving some of the worlds biggest challenges.
經濟學家和科學家對長期增長的不同看法
economists vs. scientists on longterm growth
發自劍橋 — — 大多數經濟預測者在很大程度上對人工智慧方面的近期進展（例如去年12月DeepMind自學國際象棋程式所展示的巨大飛躍）不甚重視，認為這對長期趨勢增長影響甚微。
cambridge most economic forecasters have largely shrugged off recent advances in artificial intelligence for example, the quantum leap demonstrated by deepminds selflearning chess program last december, seeing little impact on longerterm trend growth.
即使美國十年期債券利率在過去幾個月內已經上漲了0.5 % ， 但這種悲觀情緒無疑是實際（排除通脹因素後）利率仍然極低的原因之一。
such pessimism is surely one of the reasons why real inflationadjusted interest rates remain extremely low, even if the bellwether us tenyear bond rate has ticked up half a percentage point in the last few months.
如果這種供給側悲觀情緒持續存在的話，美國最近的大規模稅收和支出計劃只可能會進一步提高通脹率，而不是提振投資。
if supplyside pessimism is appropriate, the recent massive tax and spending packages in the united states will likely do much more to raise inflation than to boost investment.
即使降低企業稅率是有道理的（儘管在減稅額方面仍然存在問題 ） ， 但依然有足夠的理由去反對美國近期的財政政策。
there are plenty of reasons to object to recent us fiscal policy, even if lowering the corporatetax rate made sense albeit not by the amount enacted.
最重要的是，我們生活在一個不平等日益加重，勞動佔收入份額相對資本不斷下降的時代。
above all, we live in an era of rising inequality and falling income shares for labor relative to capital.
政府需要做更多 — — 而不是更少 — — 來重新分配收入和財富。
governments need to do more, not less, to redistribute income and wealth.
很難知道美國總統特朗普在宣稱他的政策將實現高達6％的增長（除非他談論的是物價而不是產量！ ）時腦子裡究竟在想什麼。
it is hard to know what us president donald trump is thinking when he boasts that his policies will deliver up to 6 growth unless he is talking about prices, not output!.
但如果通脹壓力真的變成了現實，目前的增長可能會比預測者和市​​場認定的持續長得多的時間。
but if inflationary pressures do indeed materialize, current growth might last significantly longer than forecasters and markets believe.
總之經濟學家悲觀情緒的著眼點就是長期增長。
in any case, the focus of economists pessimism is longterm growth.
他們的立場是基於這樣的信念：發達經濟體不可能重複美國1995~2005年（其他先進經濟體也隨後跟進）所享有的活力，更不用說1950和1960年代那種好日子了。
their stance is underpinned by the belief that advanced economies cannot hope to repeat the dynamism that the us enjoyed from 19952005 and other advanced economies a bit later, much less the salad days of the 1950s and 1960s.
但是懷疑者應該考慮這樣一個事實：許多來自各個領域的科學家卻不是這樣看。
but the doubters ought to consider the fact that many scientists, across many disciplines, see things differently.
尤其是那些年輕的研究人員會認為，即使投入實際應用還需要很長時間，但基礎知識的進步簡直是在一日千里。
young researchers, in particular, believe that advances in basic knowledge are coming as fast as ever, even if practical applications are taking a long time to develop.
事實上，一個微小但有影響力的群體一直在鼓吹匈牙利裔美國數學家約翰·馮·諾依曼的“奇點”理論 — — 有一天思維機器會變得如此複雜，以至於它們能夠在沒有任何人為干預的情況下發明其他機器，突然之間科技將呈現指數式的發展。
indeed, a small but influential cult touts the hungarianamerican mathematician john von neumanns singularity theory. someday, thinking machines will become so sophisticated that they will be able to invent other machines without any human intervention, and suddenly technology will advance exponentially.
如果是這樣，或許我們更應該擔心的是比人類精神所能接受程度更快的物質增長所帶來的倫理和社會影響。
if so, perhaps we should be far more worried about the ethical and social implications of material growth that is faster than humans can spiritually absorb.
對人工智慧的焦慮主要集中在不平等和工作的未來。
the angst over ai mostly focuses on inequality and the future of work.
但是正如科幻作家長期以來一直警告我們的那樣，矽基“生命”形式誕生所帶來的潛在威脅才是真正值得害怕的。
but as science fiction writers have long warned us, the potential threats arising from the birth of siliconbased life forms are truly frightening.
搞清楚誰才是對的絕非易事：在長期預測方面經濟學家和科學家都出過洋相。
it is hard to know who is right neither economists nor scientists have a great track record when it comes to making longterm predictions.
但眼下如果拋開人與機器之間存在你死我活鬥爭的可能性，未來五年生產率將大幅提升的預測似乎是站得住腳的。
but right now, and leaving aside the possibility of an existential battle between man and machine, it seems quite plausible to expect a significant pickup in productivity growth over the next five years.
鑑於經濟增長的主要組成部分是勞動人口 ， （ 公共和私人）投資以及在新理念指導下“生產力 ” — —特定投入所能生產出的產品 — — 的提升。
consider that the main components of economic growth are increases in the labor force, increases in investment both public and private, and productivity, namely the output than can be produced with a given amount of inputs, thanks to new ideas.
在過去的10~15年中，發達經濟體在這三個方面都乏善可陳。
over the past 1015 years, all three have been dismally low in the advanced economies.
由於出生率下降，勞動力增長急劇放緩，即使是特朗普上臺之前的美國也無法依靠移民來彌補。
labor force growth has slowed sharply, owing to declining birth rates, with immigration failing to compensate even in pretrump america.
婦女湧入勞動力隊伍對促進二十世紀後半葉的增長髮揮了重要作用。
the influx of women into the labor force played a major role in boosting growth in the latter part of the twentieth century.
雖然政府可以做更多的事情來支援女性參加工作和同工同酬，但是現在這種優勢在很大程度上已經被髮揮殆盡了。
but now that has largely played out, although governments could do more to support female labor force participation and pay equity.
同樣，自2008年金融危機以來（除中國之外的）全球投資已經崩潰，拉低了潛在增長。
similarly, global investment has collapsed since the 2008 financial crisis though not in china, lowering potential growth.
同時各地的生產率增長紛紛下降，在美國相對1990年代中期的科技熱潮時期大約下降了一半。
and measured productivity growth has declined everywhere, falling roughly by half in the us since the tech boom of the mid1990s.
難怪全球實際利率如此之低，而危機後的鉅額儲蓄能找到的投資機會日益稀少了。
no wonder global real interest rates are so low, with high postcrisis savings chasing a smaller supply of investment opportunities.
不過，最好的選擇是人工智慧以及其他新技術最終將對增長產生比迄今為止更大的影響。
still, the best bet is that ai and other new technologies will eventually come to have a much larger impact on growth than they have up to now.
眾所周知，企業可能需要很長時間才能重新設計生產流程來利用新技術：鐵路和電力是兩個主要的例子。
it is well known that it can take a very long time for businesses to reimagine productive processes to exploit new technologies railroads and electricity are two leading examples.
全球增長的抬頭可能成為變革的催化劑，為企業投資和引進新技術創造激勵機制，其中一些將取代勞動力，從而抵消勞動力增長放緩的影響。
the pickup in global growth is likely to be a catalyst for change, creating incentives for firms to invest and introduce new technologies, some of which will substitute for labor, offsetting the slowdown in the growth of the workforce.
隨著金融危機的後遺症日漸消退，人工智慧也許開始發力，未來幾年美國產出增長趨勢可能會保持強勁（當然出現經濟衰退也是可能 ） 。
with the aftereffects of the financial crisis fading, and ai perhaps starting to gain traction, trend us output growth can easily stay strong for the next several years though, of course, a recession is also possible.
對於各國央行行長來說，實際全球利率可能因此產生的上漲將會非常棘手。
the likely corresponding rise in real global interest rates will be tricky for central bankers to navigate.
在最好的情況下，他們將能夠“順勢而行 ” ， 正如艾倫·格林斯潘在1990年代的著名做法的那樣，儘管這次可能會產生更多的通脹。
in the best case, they will be able to ride the wave, as alan greenspan famously did in the 1990s, though more inflation is likely this time.
而底線在於政策制定者和市場都不應認定過去十年的緩慢增長會被帶入下一個階段。
the bottom line is that neither policymakers nor markets should be betting on the slow growth of the past decade carrying over to the next.
但這可不是個一面倒的好訊息。
but that might not be entirely welcome news.
如果科學家們是對的，我們可能會對自己所獲得的增長感到後悔。
if the scientists are right, we may come to regret the growth we get.
勾勒人工智慧的未來
mapping the future of ai
布萊頓—人工智慧（AI）已經在人類經濟和社會中起著重要作用，而在未來幾年，它的作用還將更加重大。
brighton artificial intelligence already plays a major role in human economies and societies, and it will play an even bigger role in the coming years.
因此，思考AI的未來就是要承認未來就是AI。
to ponder the future of ai is thus to acknowledge that the future is ai.
這部分要歸因於“深度學習”方面的進步。 深度學習使用20世紀80年代開始理論化的多層神經網路。
this will be partly owing to advances in deep learning, which uses multilayer neural networks that were first theorized in the 1980s.
有了當今更加強大的計算能力和儲存容量，深度學習已經具備現實可行性。 2016年Go擊敗世界冠軍，這讓深度學習應用獲得了全世界的關注。
with todays greater computing power and storage, deep learning is now a practical possibility, and a deeplearning application gained worldwide attention in 2016 by beating the world champion in go.
商業企業和政府都希望採用這項技術在各種“大資料”中尋找有用的模式。
commercial enterprises and governments alike hope to adapt the technology to find useful patterns in big data of all kinds.
2011年，IBM的沃森（Watson）標誌了另一座AI分水平，它在“危險！ ” （ Jeopardy ! ） 遊戲中擊敗兩位前冠軍。
in 2011, ibms watson marked another ai watershed, by beating two previous champions in jeopardy!, a game that combines general knowledge with lateral thinking.
這項遊戲需要結合一般知識和橫向思考。 另一項更加重大的發展是“物聯網”的出現，隨著更多裝置、家用電器、可穿戴裝置和公共場合感測器連入網路、開始隨時傳播訊息，物聯網還將繼續成長。
and yet another significant development is the emerging internet of things, which will continue to grow as more gadgets, home appliances, wearable devices, and publiclysited sensors become connected and begin to broadcast messages around the clock.
老大哥不會看著你，但萬億小大哥也許會看著你。
big brother wont be watching you but a trillion little brothers might be.
除了這些創新，我們還可以期待看到無數我們曾經稱為“專家系統”的例子：AI應用在各種專業領域輔助乃至取代人類專業人士。
beyond these innovations, we can expect to see countless more examples of what were once called expert systems ai applications that aid, or even replace, human professionals in various specialties.
類似地，機器人將勝任此前無法自動化的任務。
similarly, robots will be able to perform tasks that could not be automated before.
目前，機器人已經可以完成人類在倉儲方面的幾乎所有工作。
already, robots can carry out virtually every role that humans once filled on a warehouse floor.
考慮到這一趨勢，毫不奇怪一些人預測將出現所謂的“奇點 ” ， AI系統將超越人類智慧，智慧化地改善自身。
given this trend, it is not surprising that some people foresee a point known as the singularity, when ai systems will exceed human intelligence, by intelligently improving themselves.
到了這一步 — — 不管是2030年還是本世紀末 — — 機器人將真正接管，而AI將把戰爭、貧困、疾病甚至死亡拋入歷史的垃圾堆。
at that point, whether it is in 2030 or at the end of this century, the robots will truly have taken over, and ai will consign war, poverty, disease, and even death to the past.
對於所有這些，我要說的是：繼續做夢。
to all of this, i say dream on.
人工一般智慧（AGI）仍然是一個白日夢。
artificial general intelligence agi is still a pipe dream.
它太難掌握。
its simply too difficult to master.
儘管它有朝一日可能會成為現實，但顯然不會是可預見的未來。
and while it may be achieved one of these days, it is certainly not in our foreseeable future.
但我們仍然可以看到不少重大發展，其中許多讓我們對未來充滿希望。
but there are still major developments on the horizon, many of which will give us hope for the future.
比如，AI可以為更多人提供可靠的法律建議，並且成本非常低廉。
for example, ai can make reliable legal advice available to more people, and at a very low cost.
它可以幫助我們治療目前不可治癒的疾病，擴大可信醫療建議的普及面，而不需要增加醫學專家人數。
and it can help us tackle currently incurable diseases and expand access to credible medical advice, without requiring additional medical specialists.
在其他領域，我們應該對未來保持審慎悲觀 — — 不是說反烏托邦。
in other areas, we should be prudently pessimistic not to say dystopian about the future.
AI對軍事、個人隱私和就業造成了令人擔憂的影響。
ai has worrying implications for the military, individual privacy, and employment.
自動武器已經存在，並且最終將具備自動遴選目標的能力。
automated weapons already exist, and they could eventually be capable of autonomous target selection.
隨著政府和跨國企業越來越容易獲得大資料，我們的個人資訊日益危險。
as big data becomes more accessible to governments and multinational corporations, our personal information is being increasingly compromised.
而隨著AI接管更多的常規活動，許多職業將被去技能化（deskilled）和取代。
and as ai takes over more routine activities, many professionals will be deskilled and displaced.
工作本身的性質也將發生改變，我們可能需要考慮提供“全民收入 ” ， 如果稅基仍然足夠提供資金的話。
the nature of work itself will change, and we may need to consider providing a universal income, assuming there is still a sufficient tax base through which to fund it.
AI的另一個不同但同樣令人擔憂的影響是它可能成為一對一人際聯絡的替代品。
a different but equally troubling implication of ai is that it could become a substitute for oneonone human contact.
舉一個日常的例子，想象一下你想打電話給一個真人，卻被自動選單轉來轉去。
to take a trivial example, think about the annoyance of trying to reach a real person on the phone, only to be passed along from one automated menu to another.
有時候，你之所以煩惱，只是因為你無法在沒有人類智慧干預的情況下獲得你需要的答案。
sometimes, this is vexing simply because you cannot get the answer you need without the intervention of human intelligence.
或者，這令你心情沮喪，因為你不再能夠向人類同胞表達你的感覺，而人類能夠理解你的情緒甚至與你感同身受。
or, it may be emotionally frustrating, because you are barred from expressing your feelings to a fellow human being, who would understand, and might even share your sentiments.
其他例子沒有那麼日常，而我特別擔心用來當作老年人“看護者”或“陪伴者”的計算機。
other examples are less trivial, and i am particularly worried about computers being used as carers or companions for elderly people.
平心而論，連上網際網路、提供個性化應用的AI系統可以提醒和娛樂孤獨的人，也可以監測這些人的重要訊號，在必要時向醫生或家庭預警。
to be sure, ai systems that are linked to the internet and furnished with personalized apps could inform and entertain a lonely person, as well as monitor their vital signs and alert physicians or family members when necessary.
居家機器人可以在從冰箱中取食物和完成其他家務方面派上巨大的用場。
domestic robots could prove to be very useful for fetching food from the fridge and completing other household tasks.
但AI系統能否提供真正的看護或陪伴完全是另一個問題。
but whether an ai system can provide genuine care or companionship is another matter altogether.
認為這可能的人覺得自然語言處理可以勝任這一任務。
those who believe that this is possible assume that naturallanguage processing will be up to the task.
但“任務”還包括關於個人記憶的充滿感情的對話。
but the task would include having emotionallyladen conversations about peoples personal memories.
AI系統或許能夠從人的用語、聲調、停頓和表情中識別有限的感情，但它不可能匹配合理的人類反應。
while an ai system might be able to recognize a limited range of emotions in someones vocabulary, intonation, pauses, or facial expressions, it will never be able to match an appropriate human response.
我可能說“很抱歉你傷心了 ， ” 或者“這真是太好了！
it might say, im sorry youre sad about that, or, what a lovely thing to have happened!
”但這些語句在字面上毫無意義。
but either phrase would be literally meaningless.
一個焦躁不安的人可能被這些語句“安撫 ” ， 但他們的人格尊嚴會付出怎樣的代價？
a demented person could be comforted by such words, but at what cost to their human dignity?
當然，另一條路是繼續讓人類扮演這些角色。
the alternative, of course, is to keep humans in these roles.
機器人不取代人，而是作為人的助手。
rather than replacing humans, robots can be human aids.
如今，許多與身心看護有關人際互動崗位被低估了。
today, many humantohuman jobs that involve physical and emotional caretaking are undervalued.
在理想情況下，這些崗位應該在未來獲得更多的尊重和報酬。
ideally, these jobs will gain more respect and remuneration in the future.
但也許這只是一廂情願。
but perhaps that is wishful thinking.
說到底，AI的未來（future of AI ） — —我們的AI未來（AI future ） — —是光明的。
ultimately, the future of ai our ai future is bright.
但它越是光明，投下的陰影也越大。
but the brighter it becomes, the more shadows it will cast.
來自古希臘的人工智慧警鐘
an ai wakeup call from ancient greece
斯坦福—在關於人工智慧（AI）的影響的討論中，有人動輒拿出潘多拉魔盒的希臘神話。
stanford in discussions about the implications of artificial intelligence ai, someone almost always evokes the ancient greek myth of pandoras box.
在這個故事的現代童話版裡，潘多拉的形象是一位悲劇的好奇青年女子，開啟了一個被封印的罐子，不小心放出了人類永恆的苦難。
in the modern fairytale version of the story, pandora is depicted as a tragically curious young woman who opens a sealed urn and inadvertently releases eternal misery on humankind.
就像逃脫瓶中的妖怪，衝出穀倉的馬匹，駛出站臺的列車，這則神話也已經成為陳詞濫調。
like the genie that has escaped the bottle, the horse that has fled the barn, and the train that has left the station, the myth has become a clich.
但是，真正的潘多拉的故事非常契合AI和機器學習的爭論。
and yet the actual story of pandora is far more apropos to debates about ai and machine learning than many realize.
它教導我們，最好聽取關心人類未來的“普羅米修斯”的建議，而不是輕易被短期利益矇蔽雙眼的“厄庇墨透斯”的意見。
what it shows is that it is better to listen to prometheans who are concerned about humanitys future than epimetheans who are easily dazzled by the prospect of shortterm gains.
作為最古老的希臘神話之一，潘多拉的故事最早記錄出現在距今2,500多年的荷馬時代。
one of the oldest greek myths, the story of pandora was first recorded more than 2,500 years ago, in the time of homer.
在最原始的敘事中，潘多拉並不是受到誘惑開啟封禁之罐的純真少女。
in the original telling, pandora was not some innocent girl who succumbed to the temptation to open a forbidden jar.
相反，詩人赫西奧德告訴我們，潘多拉是“後天養成，而非先天生成。
rather, as the poet hesiod tells us, pandora was made, not born.
”潘多拉是全能神宙斯的命令，指定發明之神赫淮斯托斯設計了殘酷的正規化，她是一個人形機器人，有一副迷人少女的外表。
having been commissioned by allpowerful zeus and designed to his cruel specifications by hephaestus, the god of invention, pandora was a lifelike android created to look like a bewitching maiden.
她的使命是誘騙凡人以顯示劣根性 ： “ 紅顏禍水 ” 。
her purpose was to entrap mortals as a manifestation of kalon kakon evil hidden in beauty.
潘多拉的名字意為“所有禮物 ” ， 表明她是眾神共同的產物。
pandoras name means all gifts, and reflects the fact that all of the gods contributed to her composition.
她產生於赫淮斯托斯的煉爐，赫爾墨斯護送這位令人神魂顛倒的“女人”來到地球，把她包裝成厄庇墨透斯的新娘。
after her creation in hephaestuss forge, hermes escorted the ravishing young woman down to earth and presented her as a bride to epimetheus.
她的嫁妝就是那個包含了更多“禮物”的封禁的命運之罐。
her dowry was the fateful sealed jar containing more gifts.
厄庇墨透斯是普羅米修斯的兄弟。 反抗巨人普羅米修斯領導了 — — 也有故事說是他創造了 — — 人類。
epimetheus was brother to prometheus, the rebel titan who championed and, by some accounts, created humankind.
普羅米修斯擔心人類顯而易見的缺陷，因此教會男人和女人如何負責地使用火和其他工具。
prometheus was concerned with humans obvious vulnerability, so he taught men and women how to use fire and other tools responsibly.
但這觸怒了暴君宙斯，了不起的技術是他眼中的禁臠。
but this enraged zeus, a merciless tyrant who jealously guarded his exclusive access to awesome technologies.
作為懲罰，宙斯將普羅米修斯綁在一塊岩石上，派出他的無人機一樣的老鷹 — — 也產生自赫淮斯托斯的熔爐 — — 啄食他的肝臟。
as punishment, zeus bound prometheus to a rock and sent his dronelike eagle also forged by hephaestus to feed on his liver.
至於潘多拉，她被刻意設計出來懲罰人類接受普羅米修斯的禮物。
for her part, pandora was deliberately devised to punish humankind for accepting the gift of fire from prometheus.
本質上，她是一個迷人的雌性人工智慧，沒有父母，沒有童年記憶，也沒有任何情感，不會老也不會死。
essentially a seductive ai fembot, she had no parents, childhood memories, or emotions of any kind, nor would she ever age or die.
她的設定要完成一個狠毒的任務：潛伏在人間，解除罐子的封印。
she was programmed to carry out one malevolent mission to insinuate herself in an earthly setting and then unseal the jar.
但這尚不是故事的全部。
but that is still not the whole story.
帕累託告訴我們，普羅米修斯的名字意為“遠見 ” ， 因為和他無憂無慮的兄弟厄庇墨透斯（名字意為“向後看 ” ） 不同，他永遠向前看。
as plato tells us, prometheuss name means foresight, because he was always looking ahead, unlike his carefree brother, epimetheus, whose name means hindsight.
兄弟兩人中，普羅米修斯更加理性，也顯得更加偏執，他試圖警告厄庇墨透斯不要接受宙斯的危險禮物。
as the more rational and justifiably paranoid of the two, prometheus tried to warn his brother not to accept zeuss dangerous gift.
但厄庇墨透斯被潘多拉迷得神魂顛倒，毫無防備地讓她走進了他的生活。
but epimetheus was charmed by pandora and heedlessly welcomed her into his life.
隨後他才認識到自己犯了一個可怕的錯誤。
only later did he come to realize his terrible error.
因此，潘多拉的流行形象 — — 驚恐地後退，看著各種妖魔鬼怪逃出罐子 — — 是現代的發明。
the popular image of pandora reeling back in horror as a cloud of evil swarms out of the jar is thus a modern invention.
最後希望也從罐子中飛出安撫人類的靈魂的令人作嘔的橋段亦然。
so, too, is the cloying image of hope emerging from the vessel last to soothe mens souls.
在古典希臘戲曲中，潘多拉形象是一臺狡猾的機器：最著名的潘多拉瓶繪把她畫成一位年輕女性，站姿僵硬，帶著神秘莫測的微笑。
in classical greek renditions, pandora is depicted as a cunning automaton the most famous vase painting of her shows a young woman standing stiffly with an uncanny smile.
此外，在古代，希望被人格化為一位名叫厄爾皮斯的年輕女性，常常意味著缺乏遠見。
moreover, in antiquity, hope was personified as a young woman named elpis, and usually stood for a lack of foresight.
希望絕不是什麼福音，而是象徵著無法向前看或在可能的結果中做出明智的選擇；她代表著一廂情願，而不是維持生活的樂觀。
rather than a boon, hope signified an inability to look ahead or choose sensibly among possible outcomes she represented wishful thinking, not lifesustaining optimism.
對希臘人來說，她無非是劣根性的另一種表象：釋放到人類頭上的美麗的魔鬼。
and for the greeks, she was just another manifestation of kalos kakon a beautiful evil that had been unleashed upon humans.
因此，至少有一位古代藝術家把厄爾皮斯/希望畫得像極了潘多拉，帶著傻笑。
hence, at least one ancient artist depicted elpishope, much like pandora, with a smirking grin.
AI/機器學習正在迅速演變為技術“黑箱 ” ， 潘多拉的封禁之罐的象徵也有了新的含義。
with aimachine learning quickly evolving into a black box technology, the symbol of pandoras sealed jar has taken on new meaning.
要不了多久，AI決策系統的操作邏輯不但使用者無法理解，就連創造者也無法理解。
soon, the operational logic of ai decisionmaking systems will be inscrutable not just to their users, but also to their creators.
於其他威脅一樣，AI系統被邪惡之徒入侵或被恐怖分子和暴君利用的可能性很大。
among other threats, the possibility that ai systems will be hacked by malign actors, or deployed by terrorists and tyrants, now looms large.
Facebook創始人馬克·扎克伯格（Mark Zuckerberg）麻省理工學院的安德魯·邁克菲（Andrew McAfee ） 、 微軟的程麗麗（Lili Cheng）和其他AI樂觀派像我們保證，AI會帶來巨大的益處，但我們仍然會不經意地想起厄庇墨透斯和厄爾皮斯。
when facebook founder mark zuckerberg, mits andrew mcafee, lili cheng of microsoft, and other ai optimists assure us that ai will bring great benefits, one cannot help but think of epimetheus and elpis.
我們真的應該信任人類能調整和解決AI所造成的問題嗎？
should we really trust humanity to adjust and troubleshoot the problems posed by ai as they arise?
似乎更明智的做法是聆聽當代普羅米修斯，如已故的史蒂芬·霍金、微軟創始人比爾·蓋茨，以及2017年發聲討論武器化AI和機器人的威脅的其他115位科技領袖。
it seems wiser to heed modernday promethean thinkers such as the late stephen hawking, microsoft founder bill gates, and the 115 other tech leaders who in 2017 spoke out about the threat of weaponized ai and robotics.
“留給我們行動的時間已經不多了 ， ” 他們警告 ， “ 一旦潘多拉的盒子被開啟，就再也難以關上。
we do not have long to act, they warned. once this pandoras box is opened, it will be hard to close.
”此外，這些普羅米修斯的擔心收到了谷歌聯合創始人謝爾蓋·布林和喬安娜·布萊森（Joanna Bryson）和帕特里克·林（Patrick Lin）等人工智慧倫理學家人的遙相呼應，他們警告不可貿然接受AI的禮物，必須先想好如何控制它們。
moreover, these prometheans concerns have been echoed by google cofounder sergey brin and ai ethicists such as joanna bryson and patrick lin, who caution against recklessly accepting ais gifts before figuring out how to control them.
最新民調錶明，真正在開發AI系統的人，對AI的潛在益處的樂觀態度大幅下降。
recent polls suggest that optimism about the potential benefits of ai has dropped significantly among those who are actually developing ai systems.
對AI工作原理的理解將帶來更加現實的預期。
an understanding of how ai works would seem to correlate with more realistic expectations.
不是盲目的希望，而是基於知識和經驗的遠見應該決定我們如何管理這項技術及其於我們的關係的未來。
rather than blind hope, foresight based on knowledge and experience should govern how we manage the future of this technology and our relationship with it.
站在人工智慧革命的風口浪尖
on the cusp of an ai revolution
舊金山 — — 過去三十年來，消費者已經從激動人心的技術進步中獲益匪淺。
san francisco over the last 30 years, consumers have reaped the benefits of dramatic technological advances.
在很多國家，大多數人揣在口袋裡的個人電腦比二十世紀八十年代的大型計算機運算能力更強。
in many countries, most people now have in their pockets a personal computer more powerful than the mainframes of the 1980s.
高中時我用來開發遊戲的Atari 800XL電腦其微處理器擁有3，500個電晶體；而今天我的iPhone 上執行的電腦其電晶體數達到20億個之多。
the atari 800xl computer that i developed games on when i was in high school was powered by a microprocessor with 3,500 transistors the computer running on my iphone today has two billion transistors.
當時，1GB的儲存裝置耗資100,000美元，而且有冰箱大小；今天它幾乎不花錢，尺寸也以毫米計量。
back then, a gigabyte of storage cost 100,000 and was the size of a refrigerator today its basically free and is measured in millimeters.
即使取得了如此大的進步，我們仍然可以在整個星球 — — 包括所有人和物 — — 聯網的過程中期待更快的進步。
even with these massive gains, we can expect still faster progress as the entire planet people and things becomes connected.
已經有50億人使用移動裝置，超過 30億人可以接入網際網路。
already, five billion people have access to a mobile device, and more than three billion people can access the internet.
未來若干年，500億件物品 — — 從燈泡到冰箱、道路、服裝等諸如此類 — — 也將連線到網際網路。
in the coming years, 50 billion things from light bulbs to refrigerators, roads, clothing, and more will be connected to the internet as well.
每過一代人左右，新興技術就會出現融合，某種革命性的技術因此而誕生。
every generation or so, emerging technologies converge, and something revolutionary occurs.
比方說，成熟的網際網路、廉價的頻寬和檔案壓縮，以及蘋果標誌性的iPhone使得像Uber , 、 Airbnb、 YouTube、Facebook和Twitter這樣的企業重新定義移動客戶體驗。
for example, a maturing internet, affordable bandwidth and filecompression, and apples iconic iphone enabled companies such as uber, airbnb, youtube, facebook, and twitter to redefine the mobilecustomer experience.
現在我們正站在另一次大規模融合的風口浪尖上：大資料、機器學習和不斷提高的計算能力將很快使人工智慧（AI）無處不在。
now we are on the cusp of another major convergence big data, machine learning, and increased computing power will soon make artificial intelligence, or ai, ubiquitous.
人工智慧符合愛因斯坦的那句格言，即天才能將複雜事物簡單化。
ai follows albert einsteins dictum that genius renders simplicity from complexity.
因此，在世界本身越來越複雜的同時，人工智慧將成為21世紀的決定性技術，就像微處理器是二十世紀的決定性技術一樣。
so, as the world itself becomes more complex, ai will become the defining technology of the twentyfirst century, just as the microprocessor was in the twentieth century.
消費者已經每天都在與人工智慧打交道。
consumers already encounter ai on a daily basis.
谷歌利用機器學習來自動完成搜尋查詢，並且往往能夠準確預測某個人要找什麼。
google uses machine learning to autocomplete search queries and often accurately predicts what someone is looking for.
Facebook 和Amazon 利用預測演算法在使用者閱讀或購買經歷的基礎上完成推薦工作。
facebook and amazon use predictive algorithms to make recommendations based on a users reading or purchasing history.
人工智慧是無人駕駛汽車的核心部件 — — 無人駕駛技術現在可以避免碰撞和交通堵塞 — — 人工智慧也是像谷歌DeepMind AlphaGo等遊戲系統的核心部件，這臺電腦年初在一場五局三勝制的比賽中擊敗了韓國圍棋高手李世石。
ai is the central component in selfdriving cars which can now avoid collisions and traffic congestion and in gameplaying systems like google deepminds alphago, a computer that beat south korean go master lee sedol in a fivegame match earlier this year.
鑑於人工智慧的廣泛應用，今天的所有企業都必須要將它們融入自己的產品和服務；否則，他們將無法與利用資料蒐集網路改善使用者體驗和輔助商業決策的企業展開競爭。
