舉債豪賭
betting with the houses money
許多人都在問為何美元還沒有崩潰。
many people have been asking why the dollar hasnt crashed yet.
美國會為十數年以來那一連串巨大的貿易逆差買單嗎？
will the united states ever face a bill for the string of massive trade deficits that it has been running for more than a decade?
加上過往的逆差所產生的利息，僅2006年的賬單就超過8000億美金—約為美國國民生產總值的6.5 % 。
including interest payments on past deficits, the tab for 2006 alone was over 800 billion dollars roughly 6.5 of us gross national product.
更令人吃驚的是，美國的負債相當於包括中國、日本、德國和歐佩克國家等在內的所有貿易順差國家儲蓄總餘額的三分之二強。
even more staggeringly, us borrowing now soaks up more than twothirds of the combined excess savings of all the surplus countries in the world, including china, japan, germany, and the opec states.
外國人在美國的投資罕有豐厚回報。
foreigners are hardly reaping great returns on investing in the us.
正相反，他們所獲得的回報通常比投資國外的美國人所得要低得多。
on the contrary, they typically get significantly lower returns than americans get on their investments abroad.
在這個股價和房價瘋長的時代，日本和中國的央行正掌握著價值兩兆美金的低息債券。
in an era in which stock and housing prices are soaring, the central banks of japan and china are holding almost two trillion dollars worth of lowinterest bonds.
其中大部分是美國國庫券和抵押貸款。
a very large share of these are us treasury bonds and mortgages.
這項對美國納稅人的鉅額補貼，在很多方面堪稱世界上最大規模的外國援助專案。
this enormous subsidy to american taxpayers is, in many ways, the worlds largest foreign aid program.
如果美國的競爭優勢如此虛弱，那麼又是什麼魔力在支援美元呢？
if americas competitive position is so weak, what magic is holding up the dollar?
大多數頭腦清楚的分析家都一直預測著美元相對其貿易伙伴國貨幣的穩定貶值趨勢，特別是相對於亞洲和新興市場國家的貨幣。
most sober analysts have long been projecting a steady trend decline in the dollar against the currencies of americas trading partners, especially in asia and emerging markets.
那麼，為什麼還沒有出現更多的調整呢？
so why hasnt more adjustment taken place already?
當然，第一個答案就是貿易加權的美元已經貶值—自其高峰的2002年初以來已實際貶值15 % 。
the first answer, of course, is that the tradeweighted dollar has fallen by more than 15 in real terms since its peak in early 2002.
然而，美國的赤字仍然居高不下，甚至自那時起還有所上升。
yet the us deficits have persisted, and even risen, since then.
真正的驅動因素有兩層。
the real driving force has been twofold.
第一層，也是最重要的，是美國政府和消費者已經陷入了一場從不停歇的消費狂潮。
first and foremost, americas government and consumers have been engaged in a neverending consumption binge.
在消費者方面，這是不難理解的。
on the consumer side, this is quite understandable.
隨著置業率超過80 % ， 房價在過去十年裡的歷史性成長的事實已經廣泛深入美國中產階級。
with over 80 home ownership, the epic boom in housing prices of the last ten years has spread deep into the american middle class.
雖然股權更為集中化，但許多美國中產階級仍然從他們的養老金中間接獲益。
equity holdings are somewhat more concentrated, but many middle class americans have still benefited indirectly through their pension funds.
總體上看，經過了近25年令人難以置信的繁榮（其間只被兩次輕微的經濟衰退打斷 ） ， 大多數美國人對他們的經濟情況充滿信心。
overall, after almost 25 years of stunning prosperity, punctuated by only two mild recessions, most americans feel pretty confident about their economic situation.
失業率處在週期性的低點，經濟情況也比現代歷史上的任何時候都要穩定。
unemployment is at a cyclical low, and the economy appears to be less volatile than at any point in modern history.
所以即便是在美國經濟增長漸入低速期時，私人消費仍然旺盛的情況也就不足為奇了。
so it is not surprising that private consumption continues to hold up even as us economic growth has shifted into lower gear.
人們在過去十幾年來享受了如此豐厚的資本收益，以至於他們似乎感覺像只贏不陪的賭徒。
people have enjoyed such huge capital gains over the past decade that most feel like gamblers on a long winning streak.
現在，他們認為自己是在用賭場（或“他們”賭場）的錢賭博。
by now, they see themselves as playing with the houses or their houses money.
要明白為什麼美國政府在週期性經濟繁榮的情況下依然繼續保持預算赤字就不那麼容易了。
it is less easy to rationalize why the us government is continuing to run budget deficits despite a cyclical boom.
當一個財政上負責的政府發動戰爭時，它通常會縮減國內支出，並提高稅收。
when a fiscally responsible government launches a war, it typically cuts back on other domestic expenditures and raises taxes.
而布什政府卻反其道而行之。
the bush administration did the opposite.
這可能不是好的經濟學手段，但在一定時期內卻是一項不錯的政治戰略。
it may not be good economics, but the strategy proved to be good politics, for a time.
不幸的是，新的民主黨主導的國會似乎對此不以為然。
unfortunately, it is unlikely the new democratic majority in congress will do much about it.
當然，孤掌難鳴。
of course, it takes two to tango.
為了讓美國經濟在世界上帶赤字執行，其它國家必須願意提供能自動抵銷的等量儲蓄。
in order for the us economy to run deficits with the world, other countries must be willing to spin off a counterbalancing supply of savings.
美聯儲主席Ben Bernanke的一句名言曾將美國全部的經常賬目赤字歸罪於“全球性的儲蓄過剩 ” 。
ben bernanke, the us federal reserve chairman, once famously pinned the whole us current account deficit on a global savings glut.
但更為準確的說法是全球投資不足，雖然全球經濟增長趨向放慢，但投資卻趨向提升。
but it would be more accurate to say that there is global investment shortfall, with investment trending downwards despite the upward trend in global growth.
造成這種投資不足的因素有很多，但可能最主要的一點是在向許多發展中國家投資的過程中有不少中期的制度性障礙。 在這些國家裡現在似乎長期投資的回報最高。
this investment shortfall is due to many factors, but perhaps the main one is that there are substantial mediumterm institutional roadblocks to investment in many developing countries, where longterm returns now seem to be by far the highest.
其直接的結果就是資金被暫時停泊在低投資回報率的美國，雖然這不會是一個長期趨勢。
the net result is that money is being parked temporarily in lowyield investments in the us, although this cannot be the longrun trend.
那麼，美元的未來趨��如何？
what then is future of the dollar?
只要現在的情況持續下去，再加上強勁的全球經濟增長和驚人的宏觀經濟穩定性，美國就能夠繼續舉債並維持貿易赤字而不會馬上遭遇後果。
as long as the status quo persists, with strong global growth and stunning macroeconomic stability, the us can continue to borrow and run trade deficits without immediate consequence.
隨著時間的推移，美元仍會貶值，但幅度可能不會大於每年兩個百分點。
over time, the dollar will still decline, but perhaps by no more than a couple of percent per year.
但不論如何也不難想象美元崩潰的情景。
nevertheless, it is not hard to imagine scenarios in which the dollar collapses.
恐怖主義、中國經濟增長放緩、或中東暴力衝突的突然升級都可能完全破壞現有的經濟局面。
nuclear terrorism, a slowdown in china, or a sharp escalation of violence in the middle east could all blow the lid off the current economic dynamic.
從原則上講，我們也可以想象美元升值的情況。 但總體上看，這不大可能出現。
in principle, one can also think of scenarios in which the dollar shoots up, but overall these seem less likely.
總而言之，美國貿易平衡多年以來逆風執行的情況，也同樣可能發生在美元上。
in sum, the fact that the us trade balance has defied gravity for so many years has made it possible for the dollar to do so, too.
但總有一天，美國還是得要節儉度日。
but some day, the us may well have to pay the bill for its spendthrift ways.
當那一天到來時，美國人最好祈禱他們的債主們還會像今天一樣樂於接受美元。
when that day arrives, americans had better pray that their creditors will be as happy to accept dollars as they are now.
謹防俄羅斯笑裡藏刀
beware of smiling bears
華沙 — —
warsaw remember the partnership and cooperation agreement pca, aimed at enshrining commonlyshared values between russia and the european community? signed in 1994 during the hopeful early days of russias firstever democracy, the pca was bolstered in 1999 by the creation of the european unions common security defense policy csdp.
還記得旨在發揚俄羅斯與歐共體“共同價值”的《夥伴關係與合作協定 》 （ Partnership and Cooperation Agreement，PCA）嗎？
both sides often refer to this desire to forge closer relations as a strategic partnership.
該協定簽訂於1994年，彼時俄國剛剛進入民主社會，充滿著希望。 1999年，PCA因歐盟共同安全和防務政策（Common Security Defense Policy，CSDP）的建立而得到進一步強化。
but as french president nicolas sarkozy and german chancellor angela merkel meet russian president dmitri medvedev in deauville, it would be wise to recognize that the kremlin appears to be changing the terms of this nascent relationship.
締約雙方都意欲打造更加緊密的“戰略合作伙伴”關係。 但從法國總統薩科齊和德國總理默克爾與俄羅斯總統梅德韋傑夫在多維爾（Deauville）的會面中不難看出，俄羅斯對於這一誕生沒多久的關係已經發生了態度轉變。
in the wake of russias apparent departure from democratization during vladimir putins presidency, and of the wars in chechnya and georgia, the eu has adopted increasingly cautious language, sounding less optimistic about the prospects of a real partnership.
在普京總統任期內，俄羅斯發生了明顯的去民主化，對車臣和喬治亞戰火連連，這使得歐盟對俄羅斯的態度越來越謹慎，對雙方實質關係的前景也不再像以前那樣樂觀。
thus, the european security strategy, adopted in 2004, says only that, we should continue to work for closer relations with russia, a major factor in our security and prosperity. respect for common values will reinforce progress towards a strategic partnership.
因此，2004年生效的歐洲安全戰略（European Security Strategy）僅僅提到“我們就應該繼續致力於加強與俄羅斯的緊密關係，這是關係到我們安全與繁榮的一大重要因素。 尊重共同價值有利於促使雙方締結戰略合作伙伴關係。
russias august 2008 invasion of georgia produced a sterner variation no strategic partnership is possible if the values of democracy, respect for human rights, and the rule of law are not fully shared and respected.
俄羅斯在2008年8月對喬治亞出兵使形勢急轉直下。
russians, meanwhile, are struggling to reconcile their disparate views on europe. some profess to be sick and tired of dealing with brussels bureaucrats.
“如果民主的價值、人權的尊重、法治的精神不能得到完全的承認和尊重，就不可能建立任何戰略合作伙伴關係。 ”
as konstantin kosachev, chairman of the russian dumas foreign relations committee, put it, in germany, italy, france, we can achieve much more.
而俄羅斯則忙於調和自己與歐洲迥異的價值觀。
kosachev and others do not believe that the eu is committed to serious talks on hard security, a russian imperative and with good reason.
部分俄羅斯人坦誠“對與布魯塞爾官僚打交道感到厭倦。
how to deal with russia on security issues particularly on energy security is one of the most divisive issues facing the eu.
”俄羅斯杜馬外交關係委員會主席康斯坦丁·科薩切夫（Konstantin Kosachev）稱 ： “ 在德國、義大利和法國，我們能夠取得更大的成果。
despite their commitment to speak to russia with one voice, various eu countries negotiate with russia bilaterally whenever possible especially over lucrative business contracts, congregating under the eu umbrella only when necessary.
”
that gives russia great scope to play one country against another.
科薩切夫等人認為歐盟不會與俄羅斯就“硬”安全問題 — — 俄羅斯的當務之急 — — 進行嚴肅探討。
russia, meanwhile, harbors deep disappointment with the west for its actions after communisms collapse. during the gorbachev era, it was assumed that the west would stick to the essence of its cold war containment policies.
這自有道理。 在歐盟，如何處理與俄羅斯有關的安全問題 — — 尤其是能源安全問題 — — 可謂眾說紛紜。
russians expected that, once their country was seen to be no longer confrontational and expansionist, it would be treated as a legitimate partner, not as a defeated enemy.
按理，歐洲應該以一個聲音與俄羅斯對話，但實際上，歐盟各國一有機會就會與俄羅斯進行雙邊協商（特別是在利潤豐厚的商業合同事務上 ） ， 只是在萬不得已的情況下才會統一打出歐盟的旗幟。 這使得俄羅斯可以遊刃有餘地各個擊破。
it would retain its status alongside the united states on the world stage, its territorial integrity would be unquestioned, and it would be left to manage its domestic affairs without outside interference or criticism.
而俄羅斯對西方在蘇聯解體後的行徑懷著深深的不滿。 在戈爾巴喬夫時代，俄羅斯認為西方會堅持冷戰時期的遏制政策。
growing resentment toward the west has reinforced russian leaders enduring penchant for the concepts of great powers and spheres of influence, and the belief that international relations is a zerosum game, in which others gain is russias loss.
俄羅斯人希望，一旦俄羅斯不再採取對峙和擴張主義態勢，西方就應該視其為合法合作伙伴而不是被打倒在地的敵人。
thus, they cannot accept that more robust multilateral institutions, confidence, cooperation, and interdependence could assure international security.
俄羅斯應該能夠維持其在世界舞臺上與美國平起平坐的地位，俄羅斯領土完整應該是毋庸置疑之事，而俄羅斯如何處理民主事務完全是內政，不應受到任何外部干涉和批評。
on the contrary, russias loss of superpower status is completely unacceptable.
對西方日益不滿的情緒使得俄羅斯領導人開始著眼於“超級大國 ” 、 “勢力範圍”等概念，相信國際關係是一場零和遊戲，西方之所贏即俄羅斯之所輸。
economic growth during the putin years, combined with the defeat of georgia which was regarded in russia as the beginning of a great political comeback provided the confidence needed to embrace efforts to remodel the transatlantic security architecture.
因此，他們不再接受強大的多邊機構、信心、合作以及相互依存可以保證國際安全的觀點。 相反，俄羅斯失去超級大國地位是不可容忍的。
medvedevs proposed transatlantic security treaty would enshrine the principle of avoiding external force to resolve national disputes, which would rule out international intervention in the conflicts affecting the northern caucasus, including chechnya.
普京時代的經濟增長與對喬治亞的勝利一道 — — 在俄羅斯人看來，出兵喬治亞意味著俄羅斯在政治上的重新崛起 — — 使俄羅斯充滿了信心，欲重塑大西洋兩岸安全模式。
the status quo would be reinforced further by the principle that no country may increase its security to the detriment of another. but it is unclear who decides what is detrimental.
梅德韋傑夫版的跨大西洋安全條約將強化外部勢力不應干涉國內糾紛的原則，這將把對北高加索地區（包括車臣）衝突的國際干預擋在俄羅斯國門之外。
worse, the freedom to join military treaties, stipulated in the helsinki accords of 1975 and in other major international agreements like the charter of paris for a new europe or the charter for european security, is ominously omitted. the expansion of military alliances, such as nato, would be declared a threatening measure.
俄羅斯還有更進一步的打算，認為一國不能為了自己的安全而損壞他國利益。 到底由誰來定義什麼是“損壞”目前還不清楚。
europe should react to this russian proposal, first, by acknowledging that russia has a critical role to play in transatlantic security, and that it should be treated not only with caution, but also with respect.
但是，由1975年《赫爾辛基協定 》 （ Helsinki Accords）和其他國��協定 — — 如建設新歐洲（New Europe）的《巴黎憲章 》 （ Charter of Paris）和《歐洲安全憲章 》 （ Charter for European Security ） — —所規定的自由加入軍事條約的權利，梅德韋傑夫的計劃隻字未提。
at the same time, a range of institutions already deals with the issue osce, the natorussia council, and the euroatlantic partnership council, to name but a few.
北約等軍事聯盟的擴張將被俄羅斯視為威脅手段。
these existing institutions might need to be reinvigorated and fortified, but there is no need for more of them.
首先，應該承認俄羅斯在跨大西洋安全事務上的關鍵作用。 歐洲不應該僅僅防範俄羅斯，更應該尊重它。
second, the principle of the indivisibility of european and us security, so fundamental during the cold war, remains valid.
同時，已經存在的安全事務機構 — — 歐安組織（OSCE ） 、 北約-俄羅斯理事會（NATO-Russia Council）以及歐洲-大西洋合作伙伴理事會（Euro-Atlantic Partnership Council）等等 — — 應該得到強化，而為此設定新機構則沒有必要。
security initiatives should therefore first be discussed bilaterally within the natoeu framework only then should a common position be presented at the osce. speaking to russia with one voice is absolutely essential.
其次，冷戰中至關重要的歐洲與美國安全榮辱與共的原則仍有必要性。
third, the idea implicit in medvedevs plan that russia should have veto power over all securityrelated decisions of nato or the eu must be rejected.
因此，安全措施應該首先在北約-歐盟框架內進行雙邊討論，在此基礎上形成一個OSCE共同立場。 以一個聲音與俄羅斯對話至關重要。
given that russias own new military doctrine presents nato as a potential threat, its leaders can logically claim that nato enlargement undermines russian security.
第三，對梅德韋傑夫計劃的如意算盤 — — 俄羅斯應該對所有北約或歐盟安全相關決定擁有否決權 — — 必須嚴詞拒絕。
russia should nonetheless be consulted on all major security issues. natorussia consultation during the drafting of the latest nato strategic concept is a good example an approach that russia itself rejected before adopting its new military doctrine.
俄羅斯自己的軍事新思維將北約列為潛在威脅，因此其領導人宣稱北約東擴會威脅俄羅斯安全再自然不過了。
consultations on the medvedev plan should also include other former sovietbloc countries, such as ukraine.
北約-俄羅斯在最近的《北約戰略概念 》 （ NATO Strategic Concept）問題上的磋商就是很好的例子 — — 讓俄羅斯在接受軍事新思維之前自己把它給拒絕了。 在梅德韋傑夫計劃問題上的協商應該將其他前蘇聯加盟國 — — 如烏克蘭 — — 也包括進來。
the best way to proceed on the medvedev plan would be an osce declaration similar to the one adopted in istanbul in 1999 that is, a political resolution, not a legally binding treaty.
處理梅德韋傑夫計劃的最佳方式是效仿1999年的伊斯坦布林OSCE宣言 — — 即採取政治解決方案，而不是法律限制條約。
according russia more formal recognition as a great power might help eu and us efforts to engage its leaders in a serious security dialogue.
給予俄羅斯正式超級大國地位可能有助於歐盟和美國就重大安全問題與俄羅斯領導人展開對話。 但不能和俄羅斯簽署任何協議，因為俄羅斯是否會踐行所做的按國際標準行事的承諾還未可知。
but no treaty should be signed so long as the sincerity of russias commitment to the norms of international behavior remains in doubt.
福島之後
beyond fukushima
維也納—一年前日本福島災難性事故以來，核電變得更加安全了。
vienna nuclear power has become safer since the devastating accident one year ago at fukushima, japan.
在未來幾年中，只要政府、核電站運營商和監管者做好自己的工作，核電的安全性將繼續提高。
it will become safer still in the coming years, provided that governments, plant operators, and regulators do not drop their guard.
福島事故是由史上最嚴重的地震和海嘯引起的。
the accident at fukushima resulted from an earthquake and tsunami of unprecedented severity.
但是，日本當局也 承認，人事和組織方面的不力也是事故的重要原因。
but, as the japanese authorities have acknowledged, human and organizational failings played an important part, too.
比如，日本的核監管當局不夠獨立，核電站的運營方東京電力公司也不夠強大。
for example, japans nuclear regulatory authority was not sufficiently independent, and oversight of the plant operator, tepco, was weak.
在福島核電站，用於維持關鍵安全功能 — — 如冷卻核反應堆和乏燃料棒 — — 的後備電源沒有得到合適的維護。
at the fukushima site, the backup power supply, essential for maintaining vital safety functions such as cooling the reactors and spent fuel rods, was not properly protected.
應對嚴重事故的培訓做得不夠充分。
training to respond to severe accidents was inadequate.
福島核電站和日本都缺少綜合緊急響應的能力。
there was a lack of integrated emergencyresponse capability at the site and nationally.
人事和組織不力絕不是日本獨有的問題。
human and organizational failings are not unique to japan.
福島事故不啻向所有使用核電的國家敲響了警鐘。
fukushima was a wakeup call for all countries that use nuclear power.
該事故引起了深刻的反思，人們意識到，安全大過天，決不能存在僥倖心理。
it prompted serious soulsearching and recognition that safety can never be taken for granted anywhere.
此次事故的關鍵起因也已被查明。
key causes of the accident have been identified.
事實上，全世界的政府、監管者和核電站運營商已開始吸取教訓。
indeed, governments, regulators, and plant operators around the world have begun learning the right lessons.
魯棒的國際和安全行為計劃已開始實施。
a robust international nuclear safety action plan is being implemented.
因此，再次發生如福島這樣嚴重的核災難的可能性已經被降低了。
as a result, the likelihood of another disaster on the scale of fukushima has been reduced.
那麼，到底是哪些地方有了變化？
what, exactly, has changed?
也許最重要的一點是安全規劃中的最壞情形假設被徹底地重新修訂了。
perhaps most importantly, the worstcase assumptions for safety planning have been radically revised.
在福島，核反應堆經歷了9.0級的地震，遠高於其設計抗震能力。
at fukushima, the reactors withstood a magnitude 9.0 earthquake far more powerful than they were designed to tolerate.
但該核電站並沒有設計抵抗14米巨浪的能力，結果，巨浪在一小時之內就摧毀了防護海塘。
but the plant was not designed to withstand the 14meterhigh tsunami waves that swept over its protective sea wall less than an hour later.
福島事故發生後，全世界核設施都加強了多重嚴重自然災害（如地震和海嘯）的防護。
in the aftermath of fukushima, defenses against multiple severe natural disasters, including earthquakes and tsunamis, are being strengthened at nuclear facilities all over the world.
採取的措施包括：改善應對長期停電的準備、維護備用電源以及在發生嚴重事故的情況下確保冷卻水的可獲得性。
measures are being taken to improve preparedness for prolonged power outages, protect backup power sources, and ensure the availability of water for cooling even under severe accident conditions.
全球核安全標準正在被重新修訂。
global nuclear safety standards are being reviewed.
國家和國際緊急響應能力正在升級。
national and international emergencyresponse capabilities are being upgraded.
核電站運營商和國家監管者正在受到更嚴格的詳細檢查。
plant operators and national regulators are being scrutinized more critically.
各國正在開放核電站，接受過多更徹底的國際安全檢查。
countries are opening their plants to more amp160and more thorough international safety reviews.
儘管發生了福島事故，但全球核電用量將在2未來20年中穩步增長，只是增長速度比先前預計的有所下降。
despite the accident, global use of nuclear power looks set to grow steadily in the next 20 years, although at a slower rate than previously forecast.
其中的原因並沒有改變：對能源的需求在上升，對氣候變化、波動的化石燃料價格和能源供給安全性的擔憂也在與日俱增。
the reasons for this have not changed rising demand for energy, alongside concerns about climate change, volatile fossilfuel prices, and the security of energy supplies.
世界要想同時實現可持續能源供給和限制溫室氣體兩大目標是非常困難的，除非核電能在全球能源消費中佔據重要一席。
it will be difficult for the world to achieve the twin goals of ensuring sustainable energy supplies and curbing greenhouse gases unless nuclear power remains an important part of the global energy mix.
國際原子能機構預計，到2030年，全球開機發電的核反應堆將從現在的437座的基礎上增加90座。
the international atomic energy agency expects at least 90 additional nuclearpower reactors to join the 437 now in operation globally by 2030.
一些國家在福島事故後放棄了核能計劃或減小了核能計劃的規模，但核電的主要消費國 — — 中國、印度、俄羅斯等國 — — 並沒有停止雄心勃勃的核電擴張腳步。
although some countries abandoned or scaled back their nuclear energy plans after fukushima, major users of nuclear power, such as china, india, and russia, are going forward with ambitious expansion plans.
其他國家也有不少（主要是發展中國家）正在考慮引入核電。
many other countries, mainly in the developing world, are considering introducing nuclear power.
不管是老使用者還是新使用者，核安全都是至關重要的考慮因素。
nuclear safety is of the utmost importance to both established users and newcomers.
該問題同樣關係到已決定放棄核電的國家，因為那裡的核電站還將執行幾十年，退役後也將面臨核廢料安全置放的問題。
it matters to countries that have decided to phase out nuclear power, because their plants will continue to operate for decades and will need to be decommissioned, with nuclear waste stored safely.
該問題同樣關係到明確反對核電的國家，因為它們的鄰國在使用核電站。
and it matters to countries that are firmly opposed to nuclear power, as many of them have neighbors with nuclearpower plants.
計劃建造新核電專案的國家必須認識到，這是一個極具挑戰性的目標，是一項長期工程。
countries planning new nuclearpower programs must recognize that achieving their goals is a challenging, longterm undertaking.
它們需要投入大量時間和資金訓練科技人員和工程師、成立真正獨立且資金充裕的監管者，還要建設必要的技術基礎設施。
they need to invest considerable time and money in training scientists and engineers, establishing genuinely independent, wellfunded regulators, and putting in place the necessary technical infrastructure.
從這個方面看，不少國家仍需努力趕上。
some countries still have shortcomings in this regard.
儘管如此，與流行的感覺相反，核電在安全記錄上總體來說相當優秀。
nonetheless, contrary to popular perception, nuclear power has a good overall safety record.
與福島核電站所採用的那一代反應堆相比，眼下在建的新核反應堆採用了強化的主動和被動安全設施。
new reactors being built today incorporate significantly enhanced safety features, both active and passive, compared to the fukushima generation of reactors.
但是，為了重新贏得並維持公眾信心，政府、監管者和運營商必須公佈核電的好處和風險，在出問題時誠實承認。
but, in order to regain and maintain public confidence, governments, regulators, and operators must be transparent about the benefits and risks of nuclear power and honest when things go wrong.
日本是世界上最發達的工業國之一，既然它都免不了出現福島這樣的事故，那麼在核安全問題上絕對不能心存僥倖。
the fact that an accident such as fukushima was possible in japan, one of the worlds most advanced industrial countries, is a reminder that, when it comes to nuclear safety, nothing can be taken for granted.
自滿將招來慘重的代價。
complacency can be deadly.
過去12個月以來所實現的安全性改進只是個開始。
the safety improvements seen in the past 12 months can only be a start.
我們決不能因為福島事件逐漸從記憶中消失而回到“老方一帖”的狀態。
we must not slip back into a business as usual approach as fukushima recedes from memory.
從傳染病談開去
beyond pandemics
紐約 — — 世界衛生組織現已正式宣佈將H1N1流感病毒列為全球流行病毒。
new york the world health organization has now officially declared the h1n1 flu virus to be a global pandemic.
世界各國政府、國際組織和民眾正在與病毒進行鬥爭。
governments, international organizations, and people around the world are rightly focused on fighting it.
H1N1病毒以如此快的速度傳播到幾乎所有大洲凸顯出人類的相互依存程度。
the speed with which the h1n1 virus has spread to almost every continent highlights our mutual interdependence.
今天，疾病對一個國家的影響最終會波及到所有國家。
nowadays, the impact of disease in one country is ultimately felt by all.
因此，應對傳染病的有效對策必須以全球團結和文明對待自身利益為基礎。
any effective response, therefore, must be grounded in a sense of global solidarity and enlightened selfinterest.
我們必須意識到人類的命運是休慼相關的。
we must recognize, yet again, that we are all in this together.
當一種新疾病席捲全球的時候，疫苗和抗病毒藥物的使用不能只侷限在有錢人當中。
when a new disease sweeps the world, access to vaccines and antiviral medicines cannot be limited to those who can pay for them.
如果貧窮國家不健康，富裕國家也很難獨善其身。
wealthy nations cannot hope to remain healthy if poorer nations do not.
我們必須公開迅速地共享病毒樣本和相關資訊。
virus samples and information must be shared openly and quickly.
政府和大型製藥企業必須確保貧困國家也能得到所需的醫療物資。
governments and major pharmaceutical companies must be sure that poorer nations receive the medical supplies they need.
在迎接今天挑戰的時候，我們還必須放眼未來。
even as we cope with todays challenge, however, we must look ahead.
拋開此次疾病流行不論，幾乎可以肯定在未來的道路上還隱藏著其他危機 — — 而且後果可能更嚴重。
beyond this pandemic, there almost certainly lurks another down the road potentially far more serious.
在我們動員起來迎接影響世界民眾、特別是貧困人群的其他健康挑戰的時候，我們也必須遵守同樣的團結原則。
the same principles of solidarity must guide us as we mobilize to meet the other health challenges that afflict the world populations, and the poorest in particular.
放眼世界，每一分鐘就有一名女性死於分娩。
around the world, one woman dies every minute in childbirth.
10多億人仍患有被人忽略的熱帶疾病 — — 這些疾病通常很容易預防和控制。
more than a billion people continue to suffer from neglected tropical diseases often easy to prevent and easy to control.
就像我們曾經消滅天花一樣，我們也能消滅其他熱帶疾病。
just as we once eliminated smallpox, so can we eliminate others.
我們還必須記住有60%的世界人口死於癌症或心臟病等非傳染性疾病。
it also bears remembering that 60 of the worlds population dies of noncommunicable illnesses such as cancer or heart disease.
這也解釋了為什麼在談到國家發展和穩定時，我們如此關注健康，特別是最脆弱人群的健康，以及為什麼在危機紛至沓來的時刻，本週我們仍要在紐約探討健康話題。
that is why, in speaking about development and the stability of nations, we place such emphasis on health, particularly of the most vulnerable, and why, at a time of multiple crises, we will take up the issue of health this week in new york.
繼續投資於全球健康無論從挽救生命還是節約開支的角度講意義都十分重大。
continuing to invest in global health makes sense both in terms of lives and dollars saved.
健康的人生產率高。
healthy people are more productive.
他們較少因病休假。
they take fewer days off work.
他們壽命更長、受教育更多、普遍生子較少但質量較高，因為他們對已有子女投入較多。
they live longer, go further in school, and tend to bear fewer and more prosperous children as they invest more in the children they do have.
研究表明醫療投資可以產生六倍的經濟回報。
studies have shown that investments in health care can yield a sixfold economic return.
這裡僅舉一例：產婦和新生兒死亡估計已造成每年150億美元的生產率損失。
to offer but one example the global impact of maternal and newborn deaths has been estimated at us15 billion a year in lost productivity.
但當困難襲來的時候，健康投資通常會首先受到威脅。
and yet, when hard times hit, spending on health is often among the first things to be cut.
在此前的經濟衰退期，特別是在發展中經濟體，通常只有富人才能享受到最高水平的醫療服務，而窮人則通常除了孤軍奮戰沒有其他選擇。
during past recessions, especially in developing economies, the best care has tended to go to the wealthy the poor, too often, have been left to fend for themselves.
但任何社會的社會和經濟健康都取決於社會全員的身體狀況。
but the social and economic health of any society depends on the physical health of all its members.
當政府削減貧困群體基本醫療開支的時候，整個社會最終會付出更高的代價。
when governments cut back on primary health care for their poorer citizens, the entire society ultimately pays a high price.
今天，非洲、拉美和亞洲大部分地區仍然未能從以前經濟低迷期所犯的錯誤中恢復。
today, large parts of africa, latin america, and asia have still not recovered from mistakes made during previous economic downturns.
沒有什麼比投資於婦女衛生更加重要。
nothing is more important than investing in maternal health.
尤其是在最貧困國家，女性構成了社會的基本單位。
in the poorest countries, especially, women make up the fabric of society.
她們超出比例地承擔著種地、挑水、撫養教育子女、照顧病人的職責。
disproportionately, they farm the land, carry the water, raise and educate the children, and care for the sick.
因此投資於婦女衛生應當成為最重要的任務。
investing in maternal health should thus be a high priority.
但在所有千年發展目標中，婦女衛生是最晚實現的目標。
yet, of all the millennium development goals, maternal health is the slowest to be achieved.
因此，2005年全世界死亡率是每100，000例活產兒有400例產婦死亡 — — 這一資料從1990年來幾乎從未改變過。
as a result, worldwide mortality rates in 2005 were 400 maternal deaths per 100,000 live births barely changed since 1990.
非洲的比例是每100，000例中有900例。
in africa, the ratio is 900 per 100,000.
這個數字背後的殘酷現實是：很多年輕母親們正死於缺少多數人在二十一世紀已經習以為常的服務 — — 那就是負擔得起的醫療保健服務。
the harsh reality behind these figures is this mothers, very often young, are dying for lack of what most of us take for granted in the twentyfirst century access to affordable health care.
婦女保健同樣是醫療體系運轉是否正常的晴雨表。
maternal health care is also a barometer of how well a health system functions.
如果婦女能進入醫院和診所，她們死於分娩的可能性就會大大降低。
if women have access to hospitals and clinics, they are less likely to die in childbirth.
這些醫院和診所同樣能減輕其他原因造成的疾病和死亡負擔。
these hospitals and clinics in turn reduce the burden of illness and deaths from other causes as well.
未能集中資源和政治意願結束這場無知的悲劇是不可原諒的。
failure to mobilize the resources and muster the political will to put an end to this senseless tragedy would be unforgivable.
我們已經在其他許多領域中取得了進展。
we have made progress on so many other fronts.
再過幾年我們就可以消滅瘧疾死亡病例。
we are within a few years of ending deaths from malaria.
群眾免疫已基本實現了脊髓灰質炎絕跡。
mass immunization has largely eliminated polio.
多虧有口服補液和改善飲用水及衛生條件的新計劃，我們在治療痢疾和其他寄生蟲病時也取得了顯著的進步，並在1990到2007年間使五歲兒童的死亡率降低了27 % 。
thanks to new programs of oral rehydration and improved water and sanitation, we have seen marked gains in treating dysentery and other parasitic diseases, contributing to a 27 decline between 1990 and 2007 in mortality rates for children under five.
是的，世界正面臨著四十多年來的第一次流感肆虐。
yes, the world faces its first influenza pandemic in more than 40 years.
我們必須警惕病毒變異。
we must remain on guard against changes in the virus.
我們還必須做好準備，迎接對世界某些營養不良、艾滋病和其他嚴重疾病流行區域的可能大相徑庭的挑戰。
we must also be prepared for potentially different impacts in parts of the world where malnutrition, hivaids, and other serious health conditions are prevalent.
簡言之，我們必須保持警惕，繼續積極推進傳染病管理。
in short, we must remain vigilant and continue actively to manage this pandemic.
同時，傳染病提醒我們應當採取更大範圍的思考和行動。
at the same time, the pandemic reminds us that we need to think and act beyond it.
只有這樣我們才能真正保護我們的人民、我們的國家、我們的經濟和我們的全球社會。
only by doing so can we truly protect our people, our countries, our economy, and our global society.
超越革命理想的破滅
beyond revolutionary disillusion
所有的革命最終都會從民眾的興奮轉入理想的破滅。
prague all revolutions, in the end, turn from euphoria to disillusion.
在團結和自我犧牲的革命氣氛中，人們趨向於認為當他們取得勝利的時候，人間天堂就指日可待了。
in a revolutionary atmosphere of solidarity and selfsacrifice, people tend to think that when their victory is complete, paradise on earth is inevitable.
當然，從來就沒有過天堂，而且，失望很自然地隨之而來。
of course, paradise never comes, and naturally disappointment follows.
在當今的烏克蘭，橙色革命成功一年多一點以後，烏克蘭人民準備選舉新一屆議會的時候，就會發生這種情況。
that seems to be the case in ukraine today, as its people prepare to vote for a new parliament little more than a year after their successful orange revolution.
後革命的理想破滅，特別是在反對共產主義的革命之後的理想破滅（烏克蘭的情況則是反對後共產主義革命）紮根於人們的心理。
postrevolutionary disillusion, especially after the revolutions against communism and in ukraine's case revolution against postcommunism is rooted in psychology.
新的形勢給大多數人帶來了新的挑戰。
new circumstances imposed new challenges for most people.
以前，國家決定一切。 許多人，特別是中年和老年人，開始把自由視為負擔，因為自由帶來的是持續不停的自我決定。
formerly, the state decided everything, and many people, particularly in the middle and older generation, began to see freedom as a burden, because it entailed continuous decisionmaking.
我有時候把這種心理上的厭倦和我自己的獄後生活作比較。 多年來我渴望自由。
i have sometimes compared this psychological ennui to my own postprison situation for years i yearned for freedom, but, when finally released, i had to make decisions all the time.
但是，當我最終被釋放的時候，我不得不總是來為自己作決定。 當一個人突然間每天面對許多選擇的時候就會開始感覺頭疼，而且有時候會無意識地想要回到監獄。
confronted suddenly with many options every day, one starts to feel a headache, and sometimes unconsciously wants to return to prison.
這一種憂鬱症可能是無法避免的。
this depression is probably inevitable.
但是在社會層面來講，隨著新一代的成長，它最終被克服。
but, on a societal scale, it is eventually overcome, as new generations grow up.
實際上，在蘇聯解體15年後，一種新的宣洩看起來正在進行，而烏克蘭的橙色革命就是其中的一部分。
indeed, 15 years after the disintegration of soviet union, a new catharsis seems underway, and ukraines orange revolution was part of that.
正如烏克蘭如此清楚地所表明的那樣，從共產主義中自我解放的程序從定義上來講是同大規模的私有化聯絡在一起的。
as ukraine so clearly shows, the process of selfliberation from communism was, by definition, associated with a gigantic privatization.
很自然地，舊權貴的成員們憑藉他們的內線訊息和關係取得了私有化了的財產的大部分。
naturally, members of the old establishment, with their inside knowledge and connections, gained much of the privatized property.
這一“不可避免”的程序毒化了政治生活和媒體，進而導致一種奇怪的有限自由局面以及類似黑手黨那樣的環境。
this inevitable process poisoned political life and the media, which led to a strange state of limited freedom and a mafialike environment.
後共產主義世界的情況各國均不相同，但是成長在這些社會中的新的一代人現在看起來對此不耐煩了。
the shadings differed from country to country in the postcommunist world, but the new generations rising in these societies now seem to be fed up with it.
烏克蘭的橙色革命以及喬治亞的玫瑰革命看起來都驗證了這一點。
ukraines orange revolution, as well as georgias rose revolution, seems to confirm this.
二十世紀八十年代末期以及九十年代早期的革命針對的是專制的共產政權，現在這些革命的目的是要消除這種類似黑手黨似的後共產主義。
while revolutions in the late 1980s and early 1990s were directed against totalitarian communist regimes, nowadays they aim to get rid of this mafiatype postcommunism.
但是，為了讓這一改變不可逆轉，一個真正獨立和不受腐敗侵襲的司法體系是至關重要的。
but to make the change irreversible, a truly independent and incorruptible judiciary is essential.
在與政治有關的案件中，很多情況下並沒有認真審理從而得出好不模稜兩可的結論。
too often in politically connected cases, suspicions and charges of wrongdoing are not pursued to an unambiguous conclusion.
這是可以理解的，因為共產司法體系受到操縱來服務於政權，而數以萬計的法官則不可能一夜之間就被更換掉。
this is understandable the communist justice system was manipulated to serve the regime, and thousands of judges cannot be replaced overnight.
回到蘇聯時代是不可能的，儘管這一點很清楚，但是，有些人把烏克蘭民眾的理想破滅歸咎於俄國的影響。
although it is clear that a return to the old soviet union is not possible, some blame russian influence for the disillusion in ukraine.
是的，俄國政策中有許多令人擔憂的地方，大多數情況下是因為俄國從來就不知道何去何從。
yes, there are some alarming elements in russian policy, mostly because russia has never really known where it begins and where it ends.
它要麼佔領要麼掌控著其他許多國家，現在，它極為不情願地應付失去所有這些國家。
it either owned or dominated many other nations, and now it is only with grudging reluctance dealing with the loss of them all.
俄國總統普京的某些言論看起來對蘇聯時代很懷舊。
some of russian president vladimir putins statements seem to recall the soviet era with nostalgia.
的確，他最近說蘇聯解體是一個悲劇性的錯誤。
indeed, he recently called the disintegration of the soviet union a tragic mistake.
但是，懷戀蘇聯與俄羅斯傳統的大國情懷聯絡要遠遠大於與共產主義的聯絡。
but soviet nostalgia has far more to do with russias traditional great power ambitions than with communism.
我相信，俄羅斯應該明白無誤地宣告、而且國際社會應該明白無誤地對俄羅斯宣告，俄羅斯的邊界是確定的、不會受到懷疑，因為邊界爭議時大多數衝突和戰爭的根源。
russia, i believe, should clearly say and the international community should clearly say to russia that it has defined borders that will not be questioned, because disputed borders lie at the core of most conflicts and wars.
在另一方面，我並不想把普京妖魔化。
on the other hand, i dont want to demonize putin.
他可能會把石油低價賣給與其親近的人，例如白俄羅斯的獨裁者盧卡申科，而堅持以市場價格出售給其他人，但是他也只能如此而已。
he may lower oil prices for someone close to him, like belarus dictator alexander lukashenko, and insist on a market price for someone else, but thats basically all he can do.
我並不看到除此以外還會有什麼嚴重的衝突。
i don't envision any serious conflict beyond that.
融入西方的許諾是使得衝突看似不可能的一個原因，因為這不僅是一個地理上的問題，也是共同價值觀和文化的問題。
the promise of western integration is one reason that conflict seems impossible, for it is a question of geography as much as shared values and culture.
烏克蘭屬於聯合的歐洲政治實體；烏克蘭所信奉的以及在其歷史中植根的價值觀本質上是歐洲式的。
ukraine belongs to a united european political entity the values that ukraine endorses and that are embedded in its history are european to the core.
捷克的經驗表明，實施歐盟所有的法令條例以便做好準備入盟需要時日。
the czech experience shows that implementing all of the european unions norms so as to be ready to qualify for membership takes some time.
但是在原則上來講，烏克蘭也同樣可以成功。
but in principle, ukraine can succeed as well.
對於烏克蘭和北約來講情況大體也是如此。
much the same is true for ukraine and nato.
建立在共同規則、標準以及價值觀念基礎之上的夥伴關係是現代安全的中心。
partnerships based on shared rules, standards, and values are the heartbeat of modern security.
而且，北約確定了一個文明的領域，當然這並不是說北約就是高人一等。
moreover, nato in a way defines the sphere of a civilization, which of course doesnt mean that natos community is better than any other.
但是，只要人們有願望，而且對於人們來說具有歷史性的意義，加入北約就是不錯的事情。
but its a community that is good to belong to provided that people want it and that it makes historical sense for them.
北約成員資格規定了義務，因為可能會出現這樣一種情況，而且我們已經經歷了，那就是北約響應聯合國的呼籲，在北約以外、例如種族屠殺正在進行的地方實行軍事幹預。
nato membership carries obligations, because situations may arise and we have already experienced them when nato follows a united nations appeal and conducts an outofarea military intervention where, for example, genocide is being committed.
換句話說，如同歐盟成員資格一樣，北約的成員資格是有代價的。
in other words, nato membership, like eu membership, comes at a price.
但是，我認為有益之處要遠遠大於可能的不利之處。
however, i think that the advantages far outweigh any possible disadvantages.
烏克蘭人民要自己作出決定，並進而克服後革命時代的理想破滅。
it is up to ukrainians to decide this for themselves and thus to overcome postrevolutionary disillusion.
死刑辯論之外
beyond the death penalty debate
中國判處原藥監局局長死刑再度引發了有關死刑的國際爭論。
chinas decision to execute the head of its drug regulatory agency has rekindled international debate about capital punishment.
這個問題由來已久，可以追溯到波拉圖時代，按照波拉圖“定律 ” ， 必須要對犯下重罪的人處以死刑。
it is an ageold question, one that harks back to plato, who in his laws saw the need to punish by death those who commit egregious crimes.
死刑支援派通常會羅列三種論點，來為國家審批殺人者死刑進行辯護。
supporters of capital punishment usually put forward three arguments to justify statesanctioned killing of those who take the life of another.
首先是“以眼還眼，以牙還牙”的古老原則。
first, there is the old law of an eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth.
用伊曼努爾·康德（Immanuel Kant ） 、 而不是某位德克薩斯州州長的話說，沒有任何一種其他刑罰“足以伸張正義 ” 。
in the words of immanuel kant, not some texas governor, no other penalty is capable of satisfying justice.
其次是實用主義的論調：死刑能夠阻止罪犯進行謀殺。
then there is a utilitarian argument capital punishment deters many criminals from murder.
不僅如此，對殺人犯執行死刑可以有效地防止重犯：如果從監獄中獲釋，他們可能會再次行兇。
furthermore, killing murderers prevents recidivism if released from prison, they might kill again.
第三點理由同樣出於實用主義考慮，但質量卻沒有那麼高：對殺人犯執行死刑而不是由社會出錢把他們終生養在監獄裡，可以為國家節省下大筆的開支。
the third argument is also utilitarian, although of a lower quality the state saves money by killing murderers instead of keeping them in prison for life at the expense of the community.
死刑廢除派也提出了兩條道德理由作為回應。
abolitionists respond with two ethical arguments.
首先，在現代社會里，刑罰的目的不僅是為了淵淵相報，也是為了讓犯人改過自新，使他們能夠在社會中與他人和諧相處。
first, in a modern democracy, punishment must be not only retributive, but should also try to rehabilitate the criminal in order to enable him to live in society with other human beings.
儘管這個理由非常充分，但對現代監獄有了解的人卻認定很多犯人並不那麼容易悔過，他們這樣的態度很難全部歸咎於現有的關押條件。
but, while this is a compelling argument, those who know modern prisons recognize that many inmates are not susceptible to improvement a fact that cannot be attributed only to conditions of detention.
第二條道德理由來自於“不可殺人”的聖經訓誡，這條訓誡同樣也禁止國家殺人。
the second ethical argument is based on the commandment thou shalt not kill which also enjoins the state from killing.
但事實上國家可以藉助毀滅性力量、或者是戰爭和叛亂來阻止嚴重罪行的發生，在這樣的極端事例面前，這條理由實際也很難成立。
but this argument is undermined by the fact that the state can resort to lethal force to prevent serious crimes, or to fight a war or rebellion.
實用性理由同樣也是死刑反對者的法寶。
opponents of the death penalty also rely on utilitarian arguments.
死刑無法逆轉。
the death penalty is irreversible.
如果最終證明犯人是無辜的，人們也無法讓他死而復生。
if a convict turns out to be innocent, his execution cannot be undone.
不僅如此，死刑廢除派還質疑死刑的震懾效果。
moreover, abolitionists assail the deterrent effect of the death penalty.
修西得底斯（Thucydides）在講述雅典人討論該對叛亂的密提林人（Mytilenians）施以何種懲罰的故事時，指出“很多犯罪行為的法定判決都是死刑，但人們卻仍然大著膽子甘願冒險，也就是說一旦認準了某個特定的方向，法律的威嚴或者其他形式的恫嚇都不可能阻止人們去犯罪行兇。
thucydides, in recounting the athenians discussion of what penalty to impose on the rebellious mytilenians, noted that the death penalty has been laid down for many offenses, yet people still take risks when they feel sufficiently confident it is impossible for human nature, once seriously set upon a certain course, to be prevented from following that course by the force of law or by any other means of intimidation whatsoever.
犯罪學家用實實在在的資料表明，在對罪犯執行死刑的美國各州，嚴重犯罪並沒有任何減少的跡象。
criminologists have shown, statistically, that in us states where convicts are executed, serious crimes have not diminished.
其他犯罪學家認為上述發現如果理由充分，就應該適用於所有的刑事規則：刑法設立的禁區時時都在被人打破。 但如果根本沒有這些禁區，犯罪行為就會更為猖獗。
other criminologists argue that this finding, if wellfounded, should then apply to any criminal law every day, criminal prohibitions are infringed yet if we did not have such prohibitions, crimes would be even more rampant.
因此在他們看來，死刑至少可以對人類行兇傾向起到抑制的作用。
in their view, capital punishment serves at least to restrain the homicidal leanings of human beings.
有關死刑的爭論至此就歸結為相互矛盾的道德和功利觀點之間的交流和碰撞。
so the death penalty debate boils down to an exchange of conflicting ethical and utilitarian views.
但我們不應該三緘其口、置身事外。
but we should not sit idly by and refrain from taking sides.
比如我就認定死刑從根本上破壞了以尊重生命和人類尊嚴為基礎的人權學說。
i, for one, believe that the death penalty radically negates the doctrine of human rights, which is founded on respect for life and the dignity of human beings.
但無論你反對死刑與否，都可以從這場辯論中汲取到兩個教訓。
but, whether or not you oppose the death penalty, two lessons can be drawn from the debate.
首先，爭取人類尊嚴和對生命尊重的鬥爭如同任何一場人權鬥爭一樣，受到民主社會全體成員的頑強推動，而個人為推動人權所付出的努力要遠遠超過國家。
first, the fight for human dignity and respect for life, as with any struggle for human rights, is set in motion and tenaciously pursued by members of civil society, by individuals more than by states.
它所代表的是一個理性的時代，1764年切薩雷·貝卡利亞（Cesare Beccaria）在一份僅有幾頁的發展手冊中首次提出了這樣的概念，並竭力倡導廢除死刑。
it was a representative of the age of reason, cesare beccaria, who first advocated in 1764, in a few pages of a seminal booklet, the abolition of capital punishment.
實際上，國家逐漸放棄古老的原則多虧少數思想家和積極分子的功勞。
indeed, it is thanks to a few thinkers and activists that states have gradually moved away from ageold tenets.
正如康帕內拉（Tommaso Campanella）在幾個世紀前寫到的那樣 ： “ 改變歷史的首先是言論，其次才是武力。 ” 偉大的哲學家康帕內拉一生大部分時間都在囹圄中渡過，並且由於他的思想而受盡折磨。
as tommaso campanella, a great philosopher who spent much time in prison and was tortured because of his ideas, wrote a few centuries ago, history is changed first by the tongue and then by the sword.
在當今世界，也存在像大赦國際和拯救該隱這樣的組織極力敦促國家取消死刑。
nowadays, it is associations such as amnesty international and hands off cain that push states to abolish capital punishment.
第二個教訓是有關死刑的爭論不該吸引我們全部的注意力。
the second lesson is that the death penalty debate should not absorb all our attention.
如果我們要廢除絞刑，那麼也該為預防犯罪和反對監獄虐待犯人努力進行鬥爭。
if we intend to abolish the gallows, we should also fight for the prevention of crime and against the inhumanity of many prisons.
歸根結底，如果犯人受到可恥的非人道虐待，那麼用監禁來取代電刑又有什麼實際意義呢？
after all, what is the point of suggesting imprisonment as an alternative to electrocution, if inmates are subjected to inhuman and degrading treatment?
很多犯人用自殺（自我執行死刑）的方式來逃避在獄中所受的非人道待遇，��此我們怎能視而不見？
how can we ignore that a high number of inmates commit suicide selfinflicted capital punishment to escape the inhumanity of their imprisonment?
今天許多國家不僅透過法律懲戒的方式進行殺戮，而且還以國際或國內戰爭或任由饑荒蔓延的方式開展謀殺和大規模屠殺，我們又怎能麻木不仁？
how can we ignore that many states today kill not only through legal punishment, but also by murdering and massacring in international or civil wars, or by allowing starvation?
簡言之，反對死刑不應該是終極目的，因為它只是爭取人類尊嚴大規模鬥爭中的要素之一。
in short, opposition to the death penalty cannot be an end in itself, for it is only one element of a more general fight for human dignity.
加沙停火之外
beyond the gaza ceasefire
特拉維夫－終於，期盼已久的以色列和哈馬斯在加沙地帶上的停戰變成了現實。
tel aviv finally, the longsought truce between israel and hamas in the gaza strip has become a reality.
取得這樣的不穩定狀態並不容易。
reaching this uneasy state has not been easy.
幾個月以來，明智而負責的人們勸誡以色列接受位於加沙的哈馬斯領導層提出的停火協定，但是以色列政府利用各種藉口，堅決地予以拒絕。
for months, wise and responsible people had exhorted israel to accept the ceasefire that the hamas leadership in gaza had proposed. but israels government, using all kinds of pretexts, stubbornly resisted.
以色列官員們聲稱“停戰協定會削弱巴勒斯坦總統阿布·馬讚的威望 ” ， 彷彿在東耶路撒冷建立的新以色列定居點以及拒絕拆除以前的非法定居點沒有削弱他的威望一樣；或者他們辯稱“哈馬斯並不承認以色列這個國家 ” ， 彷彿和阿拉伯國家以及巴勒斯坦解放組織在過去60年裡達成的停戰協定都是基於他們對以色列的承認，而不是基於一個指導以色列多年的簡單道德原則－即為我們和我們的敵人暫停敵對狀態－那樣。
a truce would weaken palestinian president abu mazen, officials claimed, as if the construction of new israeli settlements in east jerusalem and the refusal to dismantle previous illegal ones had not already weakened him. or they argued that hamas does not recognize the state of israel, as if other ceasefire agreements with the arab states and the plo in the last 60 years had been based on recognition of israel, rather than on a simple ethical principle that has guided israel for many years, namely to gain, for us and our enemies, a pause in hostilities.
但是，最終，理性戰勝了空想和猶豫，以色列和哈馬斯簽署了一個停火協定，我們只能為因為長期不簽署停戰協定而造成的時間損失和雙方不必要的苦難感到遺憾。
in the end, however, logic prevailed over escapism and hesitation, a ceasefire was signed, and we can only regret all the time that was lost and the unnecessary suffering on both sides.
在這場幾乎長達一個世紀的戰爭中，記住這樣一個原則是很重要的：巴勒斯坦人是以色列的鄰居，他們將和以色列人肩並肩的永遠生活在一起。
in this war, which has been going on for nearly a century, it is important to keep one principle in mind the palestinians are israels neighbors and will live side by side with israelis forever.
因為這個簡單的事實，這裡的軍事考慮就要和那些相距很遠的國家之間的衝突中的軍事考慮非常不同。
because of this simple fact, the military considerations are very different from those in a conflict between countries that are distant from each other.
喋血的記憶，不管這血是以色列人的還是巴勒斯坦人的，都鮮明地留在兩國人民的腦中。
memories of spilled blood, be it israeli or palestinian, remain vivid in the hearts of both peoples.
因此，立即停止敵對狀態比一個空想的長期“投降條約”更為重要。
an immediate break in the hostilities is therefore more important than a chimerical longterm capitulation.
在簽署停戰協定後的五天內，已經有五枚卡薩姆型火箭被髮射到以色列境內，這暗示了該協定的不穩定。
the launch of five qassam rockets into israel five days after the signing of the truce suggests its precariousness.
所以，這個停戰協定能持續並演化成為一個持久的狀態嗎？
so can it last and evolve into something durable?
該停戰協定的反對者預言－甚至是希望－它很短命。
opponents of the truce predict, indeed, wish that it will be shortlived.
但是即使是懷疑主義者也懷有許多希望。
but even skeptics nourish many hopes.
確實，如果這個新停戰協定僅僅是技術上的，如果不進行穩定和鞏固該協定的努力，它又會變成一長串痛苦事件中的另一個。
to be sure, if this new truce is merely technical, if efforts are not made to stabilize and consolidate it, it could become just one another in a long string of bitter episodes.
但是，所有擔心在加沙發生“巨大的以色列攻擊”的人都應該努力鞏固這個協定並創造一個緩和緊張的氣氛，從而隨著時間的推移，能在這種氛圍裡與巴勒斯坦當局達成一個和平協定。
but all who had feared a great israeli offensive in gaza should make every effort to strengthen the truce and create a climate for relaxing tensions that could, with time, lead to a peace agreement with the palestinian authority.
那麼，為了實現這一點要做些什麼呢？
so what should be done to bring this about?
首先，以色列和巴勒斯坦領土之間的邊境交界處應為病人、學生和家庭成員被封鎖分開的家庭重新開放。
above all, border crossings between israel and the palestinian territories should be reopened for the sick, for students, and for families whose members were separated by the blockade.
其次，應該為巴勒斯坦工人到以色列工作設定一個慷慨的額度（並且，隨著時間的推移，增加額度 ） － 確實，他們應被允許在最受火箭襲擊影響的加沙周圍的農業中心工作。
second, a generous and, with time, growing quota should be set for palestinian laborers to work in israel indeed, they must be allowed to work in the very agricultural centers around gaza which were the most affected by the rocket attacks.
巴勒斯坦人在以色列工作對雙方都有好處，也比來自遙遠國家並在以色列過著孤立的生活的外國人好，這些外國人很孤獨並且經常處於被開除的威脅之下。
palestinians working in israel are good for both sides, and better than the foreigners who come from distant lands and live an isolated life in israel, solitary and under constant threat of expulsion.
巴勒斯坦工人每天晚上都會回家，不會變得與他們正常的生活狀態疏離。
palestinian workers, who go back home every night, do not become alienated from their normal life.
將來來自加沙的工人，有道德上的權利在以色列謀生，他們將會自然地成為維護停戰協定的支持者。
future workers from gaza, having a moral right to earn their living in israel, will become natural supporters of the maintenance of the truce.
此外，過去成為敵對狀態犧牲品的工業建設專案應該重新開始，並透過阿拉伯國家的參與使其在哈馬斯眼中更具合法性。
furthermore, past industrial projects that fell victim to the hostilities should be revived and made more legitimate in the eyes of hamas through the participation of the arab state.
以色列在約旦河西岸消滅哈馬斯恐怖分子的行動也應該停止－或者至少在可能的情況下最大限度的減少這樣的行動－並且允許巴勒斯坦當局用他們自己的方法來對付他們。
the killing by israel of hamas terrorists in the west bank should also be stopped or at least limited as much as possible and the palestinian authority should be permitted to deal with them in their own way.
最重要的是，我們必須確保停戰具有它自己的力量。
above all, we must assure that the armistice has its own dynamic.
在戰爭狀態中，人們習慣了現狀並不能作其他的想象，但是當緊張局勢得到緩解後，再次拿起武器的想法會變得令人痛苦和不能忍受，因為它意味著回到常見和恐怖的苦難經歷中。
in a state of war, people get used to the status quo and cannot imagine anything else. but when tensions relax, the idea of taking up arms again becomes painful and unsupportable inasmuch as it means a return to the familiar and terrible experience of suffering.
所以，這個停戰協定不應該被看作是一個具有一些法律意義的檔案，而應該被看作是一個需要照顧、澆水、施肥和保護的幼小植物，以至於能成長為一棵強壯繁茂的大樹，不會因為偶爾的卡薩姆型火箭或零星的手榴彈而被連根拔起。
so this truce must be seen not as a piece of paper with some legal significance, but as a young plant that needs to be tended to, watered, nursed, and protected, so that it grows into a strong and robust tree that cannot be uprooted with an occasional qassam rocket or a stray grenade.
超越性別差距
beyond the gender gap
去年春天，經濟學家雜誌曾經鼓吹“女性勢力”就是世界經濟的推動力量。
last spring, the economist trumpeted womanpower as the driving force for the world economy.
但是，如果歐洲經濟要想變得更為具有競爭力以及創新力，婦女僅僅大量進入勞動力市場還是不夠的。
but if europes economy is to become more competitive and innovative, it is not enough that women enter the labor market in droves.
為了充分利用婦女才能的果實，她們還必須在公營部門和私營部門居於最高的職務。
to reap the full fruits of womens talents, they must be in more top jobs, too, both in the public and private sector.
西歐的婦女長久以來已經消除了同她們的男性同齡人在教育上的差距。
women in western europe have long since bridged the education gap with their male peers.
在大學裡，女生不僅在人數上超過男生，而且她們也比男生成績要好，最為顯著的是在數學、物理以及資訊科學方面。
women not only outnumber men at universities they also outperform them, most notably in math, physics, and information science.
但是女生在學術上的成就並未增加婦女在最高職務上的存在。
but female students academic achievements have not increased womens presence in top jobs.
在歐洲，婦女在企業董事會中的比例在百分之十以下，在政府和學術界最高職務上也是一樣。
in europe, the percent of women on corporate boards remains in single digits, as is true of the top ranks of government and academia.
在美國的企業官員中幾乎每五個人就有一個人是女性，而在歐洲大陸，在公司董事會中婦女和男子的比例是一比二十或者更低。
while in the united states almost one out of five corporate officers are women, in mainland europe the female to male ratio on company boards is one to twenty or worse.
在科學界，這一局面稍微好一點。
the situation is only slightly better in science.
在歐洲，每十名教授中有一人是女性。
one of every ten professors in europe is a woman.
在美國，這一比例再一次對婦女更為有利。 在美國大學中，超過20%的教授是女性。
in the us, the ratio is once again more favorable to women, with more than 20 of professors at american universities being female.
歐洲無法在中國和印度兩國崛起、其自身人口老齡化的時候浪費寶貴的人力資本。
europe cannot afford to waste valuable human capital at a time when china and india are on the rise and its own population is aging.
首批嬰兒潮已經到達退休年齡，勞動力在歐洲的大部分地區將會馬上萎縮。
the first baby boomers have reached retirement age, and the labor force will soon be shrinking in most parts of europe.
歐洲為了承擔人口老齡化的成本以及維持其經濟強國的地位就必須大幅度增加勞動力的總體參與。
to cover the costs of aging and maintain its position as an economic power, europe must increase overall labor participation considerably.
父親們不僅能夠、而且必須在撫養孩子上承擔更大的責任；家務中的很大一部分完全可以由市場得到滿足。
not only can and must fathers assume a greater role in child rearing a large part of homemaking is perfectly suitable to be met by the market.
正如經濟學家斯科塔和弗里曼所指出的那樣，職業婦女每週工作時間並不一定比兼職工作婦女或者居家母親們要長。
as economists ronald schettkat and richard freeman have pointed out, career women do not necessarily work more hours per week than women with parttime jobs or stayathome moms.
相反，她們往往把某些家務，例如購買雜貨、做飯以及清潔等外包出去。
instead, they tend to outsource activities like grocery shopping, cooking, and cleaning.
如果歐洲婦女在更高質量的工作中工作更長的時間，那麼，這將會刺激像清潔和托兒等服務性工作，從而降低低技能工人的失業率。
if women in europe work more hours in better quality jobs, it will stimulate demand for service jobs like cleaning and child care, thus reducing unemployment among lowskilled workers.
而且，高質量女性勞力供應的增加不會像勞工移民那樣引發額外的醫療和養老金成本。
moreover, the increased supply of highquality female labor will not incur additional healthcare and pension costs, unlike labor immigration.
無論是居家母親還是在外從事帶薪工作的婦女都是要使用這些福利補助的。
women use those benefits anyway, whether they are stayathome moms or perform paid work outside the home.
由於人們壽命延長，生育降低，所以，父母撫養孩子所花費的精力比過去要少。
because people live longer and procreate less, raising and caring for children requires less of a parents life than it used to.
婦女可以在不錯過生育的情況下謀求最高的職位，而且，她們的成功將會鼓勵職位較低的婦女，因為女性經理往往會落實更為考慮性別的錄用政策，而且是強大的楷模。
women should be able to aspire to top jobs without squandering their fertility, and their success would encourage women in lowerranking positions, because female managers tend to implement more genderconscious hiring policies and serve as strong role models.
歐洲受過教育的婦女的職業進步的障礙根源在於企業文化、性別偏向以及成見，而不是赤裸裸的歧視。
obstacles to the professional advancement of educated women in europe is rooted in corporate culture, gender biases, and stereotyping, rather than outright discrimination.
群體能動阻礙全部由男性組成的公司董事會包含婦女，即使單個董事成員會支援這一決定。
group dynamics prevent company boards that consist solely of males from including women, even if members individually would support such a decision.
而且，那些提升到更高職位的婦女由於居於少數地位，其知名度容易受到損害而螺旋狀下降。
moreover, those women who do reach higherranking positions are susceptible to a visibilityvulnerability spiral, owing to their minority status.
只要女性被認為是弱勢性別，那麼，男女都會將其自有的損害感覺適用到女性候選人上。
as long as women are perceived to be the weaker sex, men and women alike will project their own feelings of vulnerability onto the female candidate.
只有婦女在高階職位中獲得大量位置，這種排斥性的群體能動才能夠得到克服。
such exclusionary group dynamics can be overcome only by attaining a critical mass of women in highranking positions.
這樣做有許多好處。
the benefits of doing so would be enormous.
研究結果表明，如果公司的高階管理層中有眾多的婦女，就會比那些在頂層中婦女寥寥無幾的公司更為盈利。
studies show that companies with more women in senior management are more profitable than those with few women at the top.
多樣化的管理就意味著更好的管理。
diversified management means better management.
在公營和私營部門的最高職位中包含更多的婦女根本性地改變決策程序，因為婦女往往降低繁文縟節的重要性並且直接溝通，從而克服組織上的妨礙。
including more women in top positions, both in the public and private sector, changes decisionmaking processes fundamentally, because women tend to play down the importance of formalities and communicate directly, thereby overcoming organizational blockages.
因此，一個決定性的親婦女的戰略將會為歐洲創造新的勢頭，能夠使其與美國和亞洲競爭。
a decisive prowomen strategy would thus create new momentum for europe, allowing it to compete with the united states and asia.
今年年初，挪威透過立法，要求所有的公司董事會中兩性至少佔有40 % 。
at the start of this year, norway enacted legislation that requires that both sexes be represented by at least 40 on all corporate boards.
這一性別規則也適用於公營部門。 不符合這一規則的公司有可能會有被法院下令解散的風險。
companies that do not meet the new gender rules, which also apply to the public sector risk being dissolved by court order.
西班牙首相薩帕特羅最近提議在商界和政界實施類似的標準。
spains prime minister, jos zapatero, recently proposed similar standards for gender balance in business and politics.
挪威現在樹立了一個良好的範例。 這是超越在許多公司和機構中依然盛行的性別偏見和成見文化的最佳做法，歐洲應該予以效仿。
norway has set an excellent example one that all of europe should follow as the best way to transcend the culture of gender bias and stereotyping that is still prevalent in many companies and institutions.
但是婦女自身也應當調整。
but women, too, must adjust.
現實是，最高職位要求每週工作超過兩天，而且工作時間也與學校時間不吻合。
the reality is that top jobs require more than two workdays a week, and they do not coincide with school hours.
承擔長久以來一直屬於男子的責任要求婦女放棄那些阻礙她們從低職位更進一步的任務。
assuming the responsibilities that have long belonged to men requires that women let go of the tasks that have prevented them from advancing beyond lowranking positions.
建國方案之外的方案
beyond the twostate solution
發自紐黑文 — — 隨著中東動盪加劇，巴勒斯坦人的命運似乎已被外交界拋在了腦後。
new haven as the turmoil in the middle east worsens, the fate of the palestinians seems to have been put on the diplomatic back burner.
的確，儘管美國國務卿約翰·克里（John Kerry）奮力斡旋，但巴勒斯坦以色列兩地分別建國的方案自以色列於2014年在加沙地區執行“防護之刃”軍事行動後就陷入了垂死狀態。
indeed, the twostate solution has been on lifesupport since israels 2014 operation protective edge in gaza, despite us secretary of state john kerrys heroic efforts to revive it.
而對於該地區和其他地方的許多人來說，這一方案早就宣告不治了。
many in the region, and elsewhere, now believe that it is dead.
但這又引發了一個新問題。
but that raises a new problem.
既然建國大業變得遙不可及，那麼遲早有一天會有大批巴勒斯坦人要求在以色列大選中獲得投票權。
with statehood seemingly out of reach, it will be only a matter of time before large numbers of palestinians begin demanding the right to vote in israeli elections.
針對這項權利的鬥爭將會異常激烈。
that fight will be intense.
因為以色列人之所以能在兩國方案上堅持那麼久，在一定程度上就是因為這可以避開巴勒斯坦人的選舉權問題。
israelis embraced the idea of two states for so long partly to keep palestinian enfranchisement off the table.
那麼這一新興秩序如何才能變得更具包容性的和合法性？
how can the emerging order become more inclusive and legitimate?
可以說那些構成建設性前進方案的要素就隱藏在眾人的目光之下。
elements of a constructive way forward are hiding in plain sight.
以色列與約旦於1994年簽署了和約後不久，時任以色列外長的希蒙·佩雷斯（Shimon Peres）提出建設跨境經濟合作區以鞏固該協議，並以此建成了佔地346英畝，橫跨海法附近約旦河段以色列和約旦兩岸的經濟特區 — — 約旦通商工業園。
shortly after israel signed its 1994 peace treaty with jordan, thenforeign minister shimon peres proposed a crossborder joint economic zone to solidify the agreement. this became the jordan gateway industrial park jgip, a 346acre special economic zone sez occupying the israeli and jordanian banks of the jordan river near haifa.
由以色列實業家索羅米·福格爾（Shlomi Fogel）主導的該工業園最近經​實現了大幅增長。
championed by israeli industrialist shlomi fogel, the jgip has recently experienced marked growth.
以色列政府在2013年為園區提供了3400萬美元資金，而自2001年以來都在很大程度上執掌著該專案的約旦則提供了持續的財政支援。
israels government contributed 34 million in 2013. jordan, which has largely directed the project since 2001, provides ongoing fiscal support.
與世界其他地方的經濟特區一樣，園區內的企業可以享受稅收和關稅的減免以及其他經濟利益。
as with sezs elsewhere around the world, the industries in the park are exempt from taxes and tariffs and enjoy other economic benefits.
這種模式應該擴大到某種涵蓋以色列人和巴勒斯坦人的政治特區，並以此取消雙方之間的隔離區。
this model should be expanded to include special political zones spzs that erode divisions between israelis and palestinians.
這些特區可以沿著以色列和約旦河西岸及加沙地帶之間的邊界建立，並實現比依賴外來勞工的約旦工業園更為全面的整合。
spzs could be created along the borders between israel and the west bank and gaza. they should be more fully integrated than the jgip, which depends on outside labor.
在政治特區的人們實際上會將自身視為一個新秩序的縮影。
people in the spzs would effectively constitute themselves as microcosms of a new order.
特區內的企業主可以是以色列人，巴勒斯坦人，或是雙方合資，而工人將來自隔離區的兩側。
spz businesses could be owned by israelis, palestinians, or jointly, and workers would come from both sides of the divide.
但是這些人都得是特區的居民，而他們所享有的所有權和管治權都將隨著居住時間的延長而按比例增加。
but everyone would have to live in the spz, in which they would receive ownership shares and governance roles that would grow in proportion to the length of their tenure.
特區應該分別從以色列政府和巴勒斯坦權力機構處享有高度的政治自治。
spzs should enjoy high degrees of political autonomy from the israeli government and the palestinian authority.
特區內將建設包括學校，市政服務和醫療設施在內的居民基礎社會，使其基本實現自給自足。
residential infrastructure, from schools to municipal services and medical facilities, would be built in the zones, making them substantially selfsufficient.
日常治理將留給區內居民，因為這些人會因特區的興旺而獲得經濟利益，也擁有不斷保持這些雙邊社群融合一體的動力。
daytoday governance would be left to residents, who would have an economic interest in the spzs vitality, as well as incentives to sustain integrated binational communities.
美國最大的住宅綜合體公社城（Co-Op City）也是一個可供借鑑的模式。
coop city, the largest residential complex in the united states, is a suggestive model.
在一家社群型企業的主導下，公社城內包含了學校，商店和私人執法部門。
directed by a communitybased corporation, coop city contains schools, stores, and private law enforcement.
這種基於共同利益的住房開發模式近年來在美國遍地開花，其中一部分吸引力就來自於居民參與感的增強。
such commoninterest housing developments cids have grown in the us in recent years. part of the attraction is enhanced participation.
而在中東地區，這類方案可以催生一系列族群間合作的新形式。
in the middle east, such arrangements could foster new forms of interethnic cooperation.
安保將會是主要問題。
security would be a major concern.
一開始，特���周邊將設有類似西岸和加沙地區的邊檢站。
initially, spz perimeters would have checkpoints like those for crossing into the west bank and gaza.
但由於人們無需每日進出，也就舒解了迄今為止一直困擾著跨境經濟特區的一道難題。
but people would not need to come and go on a daily basis, an albatross that has bedeviled crossborder sezs until now.
類似於公社城和大學校園所僱傭的自治型安保力量將負責維持內部秩序。
autonomous forces, similar to those employed by cids and university campuses, would maintain internal order.
這一點與約旦通商工業園不同 — — 以色列和約旦都保持著對約旦河兩岸各自領域的控制。
this differs from the jgip, where israel and jordan maintain control over their respective spheres on either side of the jordan river.
政治特區應位於邊界兩側的交通要道附近，但遠離宗教聖地，定居點和具有重要戰略意義的軍事設施。
spzs should be located near transportation on both sides of the border, but away from religious shrines, settlements, and strategically important military installations.
可能的地點包括曾經計劃過的位於西岸地區圖爾卡雷姆和荷茲利亞之間的卡杜裡工業園，以及加沙城外的卡爾尼工業區。
possible sites include the onceplanned khaddourie industrial park between tulkarem in the west bank and herzliya, and the karni industrial zone outside gaza city.
這個想法無需說服選民或極端分子就能推行,也無需強制移民或拆除定居點。
the idea need not be sold to electorates or extremists to go forward. nor need it uproot people.
對於那些渴望到終結當前政治停滯局面並避免以色列不可避免地滑向因人口構成而導致的種族隔離制度的人來說,這是極富吸引力的建設性替代方案。
spzs will be attractive to those who are hungry for constructive alternatives to the prevailing political stagnation and the inexorable, demographydriven drift toward israeli apartheid.
那些進入政治特區的人們將積極致力於讓特區順利運轉起來。
those who move into spzs would be actively committed to making them work.
如果最初的特區取得了成功，就會有壓力創造更多的。
if the early spzs succeed, there will be pressure to create others.
事實上，跨境政治特區最終可能在被佔領土內的複製和以色列境內，包括拉馬拉和特拉維夫這樣的城市。
indeed, crossborder spzs might eventually be replicated within the occupied territories and in israel proper, including cities like ramallah and tel aviv.
大部分工作都將由居民們建立的社群來完成,但外界也可以提供幫助。
much will depend on the communities that the residents create. but outsiders can help.
如同約旦工業園那樣，政治特區將為特區內外的投資者提供機會，讓人們可以從和平中獲利。
as with the jgip, spzs would provide opportunities for investors from the region and beyond to contribute to, and profit from, peace.
他們能享受當地的稅收減免，也許也會從他們自己的政府處得到支援。
they would receive local tax breaks, and maybe also support from their own governments.
美國可以帶頭，正如它在在埃及和約旦建立經濟特區那樣。
the us could take the lead, as it has done with sezs in egypt and jordan.
各國政府和慈善家可以提供種子基金。
governments and philanthropists could provide seed grants.
對於約旦工業園來說，運作的目標應當樹立別人也想模仿的最佳實踐榜樣。
as with the jgip, the goal should be to model best practices that others will want to imitate.
目前已經有參與者表達了成為政治特區企業家的正式意願。
there are already serious players poised to become spz entrepreneurs.
比如上文提到的福格爾就屬於屬於一個名為"打破僵局"的組織，而該組織則由一群致力於推進和平的巴勒斯坦和以色列商界領袖組成。
fogel belongs to breaking the impasse bti, a group of prominent palestinian and israeli business leaders committed to advancing peace.
該組織由巴勒斯坦商業巨頭穆尼比·馬斯里（Munib al-Masri）和以色列高科技億萬富翁貝納約西·瓦迪（Yossi Vardi）於2012年7月成立，擁有300名成員，下屬企業佔以色列​​和巴勒斯坦國內生產總值的30％以上。
established by palestinian magnate munib almasri and israeli tech billionaire yossi vardi in july 2012, bti has some 300 members, whose companies account for at least 30 of israeli and palestinian gdp.
換言之，他們擁有足夠影響力和資源來推動政治特區的第一波浪潮。
in other words, they have the influence and resources to instigate a first wave of spzs.
第一個政治特區必須證明經濟政治的聯姻可誘發其他手段無法實現的合作。
the first spzs must demonstrate that a marriage of economics and politics can induce collaboration that would not be possible otherwise.
以色列政府和巴勒斯坦權力機構必須發揮推動作用。
israels government and the palestinian authority must play facilitating roles.
但是政府只是後坐的乘客，真正的驅動者將是那些企業家，致力地區和平的國際友人，以及 — — 也是最重要的 — — 那些願意付出自己的汗水去實現一種新和平嘗試的普通巴勒斯坦人和以色列人。
but they will mostly be in the back seat of a venture driven by entrepreneurs, external friends of regional peace, and most important the individual palestinians and israelis who make the sweatequity commitment to become a new kind of pioneer for peace.
如果他們能成功的話，兩國方案的破產可能被證明是因禍得福。
if they succeed, the death of the twostate solution might prove to be a blessing in disguise.
老大哥谷歌
big brother google?
莫斯科-ampquot;谷歌違背了其'不作惡'的座右銘ampquot ; 。
moscow google violates its dont be evil motto.
如果你用谷歌搜尋這句話，你可以找到人們對這一說法的爭論（這對谷歌來說是加分的 ） ， 而我最近也參加了這場辯論。
to googles credit, if you google that sentence, you can find reference to a debate on that claim that i took part in recently.
事實上，我與谷歌的關係是複雜的。
as it happens, i have a complex relationship with google.
我曾多次以各種身份支援過谷歌-無論是作為私人賓客、還是作為谷歌所資助的非政府組織ampquot;停止惡意軟體ampquot;公司的顧問團成員、或是作為在其舉辦的活動上發言的嘉賓。
i have fed at its trough many times as a personal guest as an advisory board member of stop badware, an ngo it sponsors and as a speaker at its events.
我還是23andMe公司的董事會成員，這個公司是由谷歌的創始人之一Sergey Brin 的妻子和他人共同創立的。
i also sit on the board of 23andme, cofounded by the wife of google cofounder sergey brin.
但我也是俄羅斯Yandex的董事會成員，它是世界上為數不多的能在本地市場打敗谷歌的公司之一；我還是WPP公司的董事會成員，它是全球性的廣告/營銷公司，因與谷歌競爭而聞名。
but i also sit on the boards of yandex in russia, one of a small number of companies around the world who beat google in their local markets, and of wpp, a worldwide advertisingmarketing company famous for its rivalry with google.
最後我想說的是，我質疑任何形式的權威的高度集中。
finally, im suspicious of concentrations of power of any kind.
因此，我很高興有這個機會讓我澄清我的想法。
so i welcomed the chance to clarify my thinking.
我在這場辯論中的立場是反對方：即谷歌並沒有違背其座右銘。
i took the con side of the debate google does not violate its motto.
但是，我覺得將來有一天，是可能出現谷歌會這樣做的危險。
however, i do think there is a danger that someday it could.
危險在於谷歌所代表的資訊的高度集中-這或許是權威的高度集中。
the danger lies in the concentration of information arguably a concentration of power that google represents.
谷歌不僅是為使用者在網路上搜尋現存的資訊時指明瞭方向，而且還收集使用者行為的資訊，而這些資訊穀歌是不與外界分享的。
google doesnt merely point users to existing information on the web it also collects information that it doesnt share about its users behavior.
如果你能用谷歌搜尋的規律來跟蹤流感爆發和預測一部電影的商業前景的話，那麼，你也可以用它來預測市場走勢甚至是革命的爆發嗎？
if you can use patterns in google searches to track flu outbreaks and predict a movies commercial prospects, can you also use it to forecast market movements or even revolutions?
即使如果谷歌只是為了自己的利益而使用個人資訊（無論這麼說是什麼意思） 的話，它仍然是政府很感興趣的一個目標。
even if google uses personal information only for their benefit whatever that means, it represents an attractive target for governments.
事實上，谷歌一般都會與政府提出的提供個人資訊的要求進行抗爭。
in fact, google generally fights government requests for personal information.
（是雅虎，而不是谷歌，曾把個人資訊提供給中國政府，而致使一名部落格作者入獄。 ）
it was yahoo, not google, that gave personal information to chinas government, which then jailed a blogger.
其次，谷歌已經成為事實上的資訊看門人，以至於如果你的網站在谷歌排名不高，那你就會像一棵樹那樣，在森林中無聲無息地倒下。
google has become a de facto gatekeeper of information, to the extent that if your site is not highly ranked by google, you are like the tree falling in the forest with no one to hear it.
尋找資訊的人們可以自由地繞過谷歌而使用其它工具，這也沒有關係，可人們並沒有這樣做。
it doesnt matter that people seeking information are free to bypass google and use other tools they dont.
那麼資訊是怎樣等同於力量的呢？
so how does information equal power?
，典型的由資訊所提供的積極的力量，是披露資訊而帶來的威懾力。
the active power that information provides is typically the threat of exposure.
在一個詭秘、不透明且獲取資訊的渠道有限的世界裡，這種資訊尤其會給你帶來力量。
such information gives you power primarily in a secretive, opaque world where access to information is limited.
但一般來說，資訊的自由流動能減少權威的集中。
but generally, the free flow of information reduces the concentration of power.
因此，我們最好讓谷歌披露的資訊更自由地被公眾獲取，而不是去壓制或監管這些資訊。
so, rather than suppressing or regulating the information that google uncovers, we are better off making it more freely available.
一個對其使用者-搜尋使用者、廣告商、投資者和政府-負責的谷歌可能是能在今天相對開放的市場裡做更多益事的好公司。
a google that is accountable to its users searchers, advertisers, investors, and governments is likely to be a better outfit that does more good in todays relatively open market.
總之，沒有任何監控體系能比目前充滿利益衝突的混亂世界更讓我信任。
in short, there is no regulatory system that i trust more than the current messy world of conflicting interests.
無論谷歌所面臨的短期誘惑是什麼-操縱搜尋結果、使用私人資訊或仗勢欺人-很清楚的是，如果經不住這些誘惑，谷歌就可能在這個它一舉一動都備受關注的世界裡損失巨大。
whatever shortterm temptations it faces to manipulate its search results, use private information, or throw its weight around google, it is clear, could lose a lot by succumbing to them in a world where its every move is watched.
同時，谷歌不僅僅是避免邪惡;他還積極地對抗邪惡。
meanwhile, google is not merely avoiding evil it actively fights against it.
例如，谷歌與審查制度所做的抗爭-它透過行動，而不是喊口號。
for example, google fights censorship by doing, not by shouting.
谷歌不是採取站在一邊大聲譴責審查制度的邪惡作為其抗爭的方法，而是在中國的地雷中摸索出一條路-它與一家佔有政治關係優勢的對手進行競爭，並禮貌地告訴使用者，他們搜尋到的內容並不總是事情的全貌。
rather than stand on the sidelines and proclaim censorship evil, it is picking its way through the landmines in china competing with a politically wellconnected rival and politely letting its users know that they arent always getting the whole picture.
總之，谷歌正在改變什麼是人們可以知道的期望值-甚至在美國也如此，雖然那裡沒有正式的資訊審查，但政府造成的模糊以及不透明的企業，以及此類的情況確是存在。
in short, google is changing expectations about what people can know even in the united states, where formal censorship is absent, but government obfuscation, opaque corporations, and the like are not.
此外，在以妨礙資訊獲得而使谷歌遭受非議的國家裡，當某些資訊被封鎖時，谷歌會指出這些資訊的缺失 ， - 谷歌要讓人們知道，此資訊是存在的但他們無法獲得它。
moreover, in countries where google is criticized for blocking access to information, it points out the informations absence when something is blocked letting people know that it exists but that they cant have access to it.
另一方面，每當有人在中國用谷歌搜尋資訊並得到搜尋結果後-比如搜尋某產品的優劣情況，以及不受政府喜歡的某個人的詳細情況-他一定會想，ampquot;為什麼不是所有的資訊都能查得到？
on the other hand, every time someone in china googles something and gets an answer a products good and bad points, the details about someone the government does not like he must wonder, why cant i get this kind of information about everything?
ampquot;谷歌的出現，使人們開始期望能獲得任何事情的資訊。
with google, people start to expect answers about everything .
一丁點的透明度就肯定會帶來更多的透明度。
a little transparency inevitably leads to more.
不是現在就要求取消審查制度-這個夢想不現實-而谷歌正透過削弱政府對資訊的控制而努力朝這個夢想邁���。
rather than demand an end to censorship now an impossible dream google is working to make that happen by eroding government control over information.
另外，從純粹的實用角度來看，谷歌使這個世界變得更有效率。
moreover, from a purely practical point of view, google makes the world more efficient.
買家和賣家都可以相互找到對方，中小學生可以找到完成功課所需的資料，生病的人可以找到保健資訊。
buyers and sellers can find one another, schoolchildren can find information needed for their homework, and sick people can find health information.
真正的邪惡威脅，我認為在於ampquot;國際治理ampquot;的誘惑 –例如，一個稱為世界資訊中心的險惡的多邊政府機構。
the real threat of evil, i think, lies in the temptations of international governance say, a sinister multilateral government body called the world information center.
儘管名字聽上去好聽，但現實中可能是官僚主義盛行，而且容易受世界上最糟而不是最好的政府的控制，並沒有創新能力。
nice as it sounds, the reality is likely to be ridden with bureaucracy, susceptible to control by the worst of the worlds governments rather than its best ones, and incapable of innovation.
例如， ICANN，一個為域名系統制定政策的機構，我是其創辦的主席。
take, for example, icann, the body that sets policy for the domain name system.
我想沒有人認為它是成功的。
i was its founding chairman, and i dont think anyone considers it a success.
幸好可以彌補的是，人們普遍認為它不具合法性，因此它幾乎沒有什麼權威。
its saving grace is that it is widely considered illegitimate and therefore has little power.
相比之下，谷歌把它所做的事情做得很有效，因此它的搜尋結果就有合法性。
by contrast, google is effective at what it does, and therefore has the legitimacy of results.
但它沒有強制力，因為任何人都可以自由地嘗試另一搜尋引擎。
but it has little coercive power, because anyone is free to try an alternative.
谷歌唯一的選擇就是做得比競爭對手更優秀。
its only option is to be better than the competition.
這些問題目前正被討論，本身就是個好現象-這讓谷歌和關注它的人們保持不鬆懈。
the fact that these issues are being debated is a good sign in itself keeping google and its watchers on guard.
幸運的是，多疑的記者們、強大的政府和緊張的競爭對手們都看著谷歌的一舉一動，並希望它抵制住許多誘惑。
fortunately, a wary press corps, powerful governments, and nervous competitors watch its every move, hoping the company to fight its many temptations.
濫用權威是邪惡的，但權威本身卻不邪惡。
abuse of power is evil, but power itself is not.
監控、西藏和四川地震
big brother, tibet, and the sichuan earthquake
上海 - - 西藏騷亂時媒體受到嚴加管束，而接下來在四川毀滅性地震中，媒體對於有些人而言好像放開了報導。
shanghai tight media control of the unrest in tibet has been followed by what, to some, looks like far more open coverage of the devastating earthquake in sichuan province.
這是中國媒體戰略的改變，還是僅僅一個短期戰術變化？
is this a change in chinas media strategy, or just a short term change in tactics?
在西藏危機的後半階段，這一問題在中國輿論中十分突出。
this question stands out in view of chinese public opinion in the latter phase of the tibet crisis.
令西方媒體驚愕不已的是，全世界的中國人都憤怒譴責對西藏騷亂的偏向報導。
much to the consternation of the western media, chinese people worldwide lashed out against its allegedly biased coverage of the tibetan riot.
大量的海外華人和留學生走向街頭，抗議他們所感受到的西方媒體報導的偏見。
throngs of chinese expatriates and students took to the streets, protesting the prejudice they perceived in western media reports.
憤怒的年輕人甚至建立了像Anti-cnn.com那樣的網站來表達憤怒。
angry youngsters even founded web sites such as anticnn.com to express their outrage.
西方報導曾經因其準確性而受到讚揚，而且儘管對四川地震大量死亡富有同情心的報導或許在某些程度上挽回了西方媒體的聲譽，但是現在全中國好像都不信它們了。
western reporting, once commended for its veracity, now seems discredited across china, although sympathetic coverage of the loss of life in sichuan may have redeemed the western media somewhat.
甚至連中國的自由派人士也承認西方記者使用剪接的影象和虛假的字幕證明中國的嚴厲統治，從而在西藏問題上出現了大錯。
even chinese liberals admit that western journalists blundered badly in tibet, using cropped images and false captions as evidence of china's heavyhanded rule.
中國流行的入口網站天涯發表一個帖子甚至說“有限新聞網和中央電視臺是一丘之貉。
one sarcastic posting on china's popular web portal tianya even went so far as to say that cnn is of the same ilk as cctv china central television.
它們都對公正報導誇誇其談。
both talk grandiosely and profusely about impartiality.
具有諷刺意味的是，兩個到頭來都是偽君子。 ”
ironically, both turn out to be hypocrites.
人們可以說這一趨勢對中國並不好。
one can argue that this trend bodes ill for china.
但是悲觀不得其所。
but pessimism is misplaced.
大多數中國怒氣都指向偏向的報導，而非整體西方媒體。
much of the chinese wrath is directed at biased reports, not at western media in general.
而且要是仔細看看中國人對西藏騷亂和四川地震是如何反應的話，就可以發現切實跡象，也就是中國人正在接受更大程度的言論自由。
and when one looks more closely at how chinese responded, both to the unrest in tibet and the sichuan earthquake, one sees tangible signs that the chinese are embracing a greater degree of free speech.
例如，儘管在拉薩實行了新聞封鎖，中國的網際網路使用者還是突破了新聞管治。
despite a news blackout during the riots in lhasa, for example, chinese internet users managed to dodge the countrys censorship.
儘管他們憎惡對中國國家通訊社新華社的導向言聽計從，對於西方媒體錯誤處理事件同樣也是很輕蔑。
much as they loathed domestic publications for blindly following the guidelines of xinhua, chinas state news agency, they were similarly contemptuous of western media that mishandled the story.
結果，那些把網際網路作為新聞來源的人清醒了，原來無論西方還是中國的報導都不是十全十美的。
as a result, those chinese who use the internet as a source for news awakened to the fact that no account chinese or western is flawless.
這種懷疑是民主思維的基本特徵，或許在推動政府在四川地震事件上更為開放上發揮了作用。
such skepticism, which is a fundamental attribute of the democratic mind, may have played a role in pushing the government toward more openness in sichuan.
確實，四川許多學校建築被夷為平地引發了網民的憤慨。 他們質疑當地幹部，這些是否是不合格的建築標準或者甚至是臭名昭著的“豆腐渣工程”才導致了學生的大量死亡。
indeed, the fact that many school buildings were flattened in sichuan prompted an outcry from netizens, who grilled local officials about whether it substandard building codes or even a notorious toufuzha construction scandal, namely, jerrybuilt projects, that had led to the disproportionate number of dead pupils.
在不斷加重的公共調查下，政府官員不得不保證那些責任人將會受到懲處。
under mounting public scrutiny, government officials felt compelled to promise that those responsible will be brought to justice.
中國的網際網路使用者以往被動地接收資訊，現在和以往不一樣了。 經過幾年接觸類似人權和民主的概念，他們敢於質疑根深蒂固而又含糊不清的觀點，即使是打破舊有觀念也在所不惜。
unlike in the past, when chinese internet users passively received information, years of exposure to concepts such as human rights and democracy have emboldened them to challenge entrenched yet dubious views, even if it means iconoclasm.
中國的受眾已經厭倦了中央電視臺的歌功頌德，也厭倦了西方媒體簡單化、沒有新聞背景的報導。
chinese audiences are as fed up with the glowing encomiums broadcast by cctv as they are with the simplistic, contextfree reporting of western media.
中國民眾夾在兩者中間，於是越發自己篩選真相。
caught in the middle, chinese increasingly sift for the truth on their own.
的確，有許多人試圖把自己有關西藏騷亂事件的版本向外界展示，反駁無論是中國還是西方正統的說辭，並且在YouTube和英國廣播公司的留言板上張貼評論和上載錄影。
many, indeed, tried to present to the outside world their own version of the tibet story, rebutting the orthodox narrative be it chinese or western and posting comments and footage on youtube and the bbc's bulletin board.
而且，由於他們不斷要求解釋，一些西方媒體終於承認了錯誤。
moreover, due to their repeated queries for explanation, a few western media outlets eventually owned up to their mistakes.
中國政府意識到獨立的民間運動可能讓中國百姓相信政府的宣傳所不能達到的事情，於是就放開了最初對西藏報導的禁令。
after chinas government became aware that independent grassroots movements could convince ordinary chinese where government propaganda had failed, it lifted its initial ban on reporting on tibet.
中國的網際網路審查人員經常被稱為“網路奶媽 ” ， 他們也不是那麼頻繁地阻擋敏感的文章了。
net nannies as chinas internet censors are often dubbed blocked sensitive articles less frequently.
中國政府明顯地開始意識到掩蓋和拒不改變的侷限性，或許也意識到來允許某種程度的自由言論的好處。
chinas government has apparently begun to appreciate the limitations of coverups and stonewalling, and perhaps also the merits of allowing some room for free speech.
這種渴求沒有偏見的資訊表明了網際網路給中國政局帶來的巨大變化。
this thirst for unbiased information highlights the dramatic change that the internet has brought to chinas political landscape.
如今，政府不再獨攬資訊以及處理資訊的權利。
nowadays, the government no longer monopolizes information and the right to process it.
富有見地的部落格吸引的點選要遠遠超過官方喉舌。
insightful bloggers attract considerably more clicks than do official mouthpieces.
一個“虛擬民間社會”正在形成。
a virtual civil society is in the making.
但是網路積極行動主義是否會在不受政府操縱或者西方媒體矇騙的情況下成熟成為要求言論自由的全面行動呢？
but can web activism mature into a fullblown campaign for free speech without being manipulated by the government or blindfolded by western media?
其答案可能是混雜的。
the answer may prove to be mixed.
無疑，民族主義熱情尤其推動了大眾反對西方媒體的強烈反彈，這正中政府的下懷。
admittedly, the fierce popular backlash against western media was partially motivated by nationalist ardor, which played into the governments hands.
網際網路要比冷靜分析更加可以進行煽動。
the internet can foster more demagoguery than sober analysis.
但是防止這一情形的最佳方式就是創造一種對立的觀點可以自由交鋒的環境，從而讓真相最終取勝。
but the best way to prevent this is to create an environment in which opposing views can clash freely, enabling truth ultimately to triumph.
在政府方面，四川更為開放的媒體可能只不過是一種姿態來安撫西藏動亂以及聖火傳遞的混亂。
on the governments part, the more open media in sichuan may be mere posturing to appease critics after the tibet upheaval and the scuffle over the olympic torch.
政府是否願意直接處理偽劣基礎工程可以驗證它是否果真容忍更為自由的言論。
the governments willingness to address squarely questions about shoddy infrastructure will be a key test of the genuineness of its supposed new found tolerance of freeish speech.
儘管言論自由並非解決中國重重難題的靈丹��藥，但是隻有確立了言論自由，中國的進步才會持續。
although free speech is no panacea for chinas woes, only when it is established will the countrys progress be sustainable.
儘管北京監管人員時刻監控，網際網路正在中國播撒自由言論的種子。
despite the watchful eyes of big brother in beijing, the internet is sowing the seeds of free speech in china.
這也許是西藏和四川危機中最為重要的教訓。
that may be the most important lesson of the crisis in tibet and sichuan.
透過集團公司刺激增長
the conglomerate way to growth
美國劍橋—生產更多同樣的東西無法讓國家變富。
cambridge countries do not become rich by making more of the same thing.
改變產品和生產方式才能讓國家變富。
they do so by changing what they produce and how they produce it.
生產新東西才能讓國家增長；簡言之，國家需要創新。
they grow by doing things that are new to them in short, they innovate.
許多國家改變增長戰略以反映這一洞見。
many countries have been altering their growth strategies to reflect this insight.
但它們因為最偉大但不典型的成功例子分散了注意力。
but they are being distracted by some of the greatest but atypical examples of success.
我們都知道史蒂夫·喬布斯、比爾·蓋茨和馬克·扎克伯格 — — 這些20出頭的大學輟學者建立了數十億美元規模的公司，站在了全球創新的最前沿。
we all have heard of steve jobs, bill gates, and mark zuckerberg twentysomething college dropouts who built billiondollar companies at the cutting edge of global innovation.
我們聽說過許多賺取億萬美元的創業企業 — — Instagram、Skype、YouTube、Tumblr，還有最近的Waze。
we have heard of the many startups that they and others acquired for hundreds of millions of dollars instagram, skype, youtube, tumblr, and, most recently, waze.
既然如此，為何不效仿這些成功者？
so why not emulate these successes?
主要的問題在於這些例子都是軟體行業的個例，對經濟中的其他部分來說遠不能成為成功藍圖。
the main problem is that these examples are peculiar to the software industry, which provides a woefully insufficient blueprint for the rest of the economy.
軟體行業是獨特的，因為其進入壁壘極低，並且可以透過網際網路進入現成的巨大市場。
the software industry is unique, because it has unusually low barriers to entry and ready access to a huge market through the internet.
創業企業通常只是善於程式設計、靈光一現的黃口小兒。
a startup is typically just a group of kids with a good idea and programming skills.
他們所需要的全部投入是寫程式碼的時間。
all they need is time to write the code.
孵化器為他們提供空間、法律顧問服務，幫助聯絡潛在客戶和投資者。
incubators provide them with space, legal advice, and contacts with potential clients and investors.
但想象一下鋼鐵、汽車和肥料公司 — — 或者度假區、醫院和銀行。
but consider a steel, automobile, or fertilizer plant or a tourist resort, a hospital, or a bank.
這些組織要複雜得多，起始規模要大得多，前期投資要多得多，並且需要集中多元化的熟練專業團隊。
these are much more complex organizations that must start at a much larger scale, require much more upfront investment, and need to assemble a more heterogeneous team of skilled professionals.
這絕非年輕的大學輟學者生來就能脫穎而出的，因為他缺少經驗、組織和這些企業所要求的資本。
