在蘇聯和兩極世界消失後，勝利的西方資本主義在唯一的世界霸主美國的領導下，稱霸全球政治，甚至統治全球經濟。
after the disappearance of the soviet union and the bipolar world order, victorious western capitalism, under the leadership of the only world power, the united states, reigned supreme in global politics, and even more so in the global economy.
好像沒有任何事情和任何人能夠阻止擁有超過之前所有財富的市場經濟在全球範圍內的勝利 — — 直到2008年9月15日，這個日子是雷曼兄弟倒閉和全球金融體系走向崩潰的開始。
nothing and no one, it seemed, could stem the global triumph of the market, with its transcendence of all previous limits on wealth that is, until september 15, 2008, the fateful date when lehman brothers went bust and the meltdown of the global financial system began.
當驚慌失措的世界正在努力估測這次全球金融危機的後果並減輕其影響的時候，下一個黑天鵝的叫聲已經清晰可見：全球氣候災難。
while a distraught world is still trying to fathom the consequences of this global crash and to mitigate its impact, the call of the next black swan can already be heard the global climate disaster.
人們往往對於巨大危機發生的可能固執地否認或者不予重視，這也許是人的本性之一。
it seems to be part of human nature willfully to deny the possibility of great crises, or at least to downplay them.
“不可能”或者“不會那麼糟的”是兩個我們常常依賴的慣用套詞。
impossible or it wont be all that bad are the two magic formulae on which we tend to rely.
甚至下一個黑天鵝已然清晰可見的時候，我們仍拒絕吸取已經發生的黑天鵝事件的教訓。
and we refuse to learn the lesson of the black swan even when the next one is already visible for all to see!
雖然當今的一代在過去不到20年的時間內目睹了兩個未曾想象的百年難遇的危機，但是我們對於即將到來的氣候災難以及之後更嚴重的可預見的後果，卻是集體性的置若罔聞。
although the generations alive today have witnessed two completely unexpected crises of epic proportions within the last 20 years, we indulge in a shocking collective repression of a climate disaster with far more serious and foreseeable consequences.
但是，其實將全球氣候和經濟危機的結果聯絡起來的話，我們可以找到一種解決這兩個問題的方法。
but, in fact, by linking the answers to the global climate and economic crises, we can find a way out of both.
解決氣候危機的方法我們已經找到，資金不是問題，技術也還可以（即使有些地方還不足，也可進一步發展 ） 。
the solutions to the climate crisis are already well known, the money is available, and so are the technologies, or where they arent, they could be developed.
我們所欠缺的就是全球主要政治人物戰略的眼光和堅決的行動。
what is lacking is the strategic vision and determined action of the major political players.
對於經濟危機來說，數十億美元、歐元、日元或者人民幣的的政府救援和財政刺激計劃已經被計劃或執行以阻止全球經濟的進一步下滑。
as for the economic crisis, bailouts and stimulus packages on the order of billions of dollars, euros, yen, or yuan have been planned or implemented to stem the further slide of the global economy.
但是，如果以大蕭條的經驗正確的話，危機的教訓是：羅斯福新政執行的計劃最多隻是使得經濟不再繼續下滑，逐漸企穩而已。
but, while references to the great depression are justified, the lesson of that crisis, and of the new deal, is that effective programs can at best cushion the fall and bring about stabilization.
真正的經濟復甦 — — 這可能是個壞訊息 — — 只能來自於之後的第二次世界大戰和冷戰。
the real economic recovery and this is the bad news came only with wwii and the long cold war that followed.
如果不用戰爭來解決眼下的經濟衰退的話，國際組織應該考慮使用抗擊全球氣候危機的辦法，因為全球化仍在繼續，這大大增加了對於世界氣候的威脅。
rather than relying on war as an economic megaproject to end todays recession, the international community should bet on the fight against the climate crisis, because globalization will continue, rapidly increasing the threats to the worlds climate.
1929年，大約只有20億多一點的人口生活在這個星球上；而今天，大約有67億人，到2050年將會有90億人。
in 1929, there were slightly more than two billion people living on the planet today, there are 6.7 billion, and in 2050 there will be nine billion.
由於全球化和新通訊技術，所有這些人都會為標準化的生活（可能略有差異）而奮鬥，這會導致全球生態系統的過渡擴張。
all of them, thanks to globalization and new communication technologies, will strive for the same standard of living, give or take, which will necessarily lead to an overstretched global ecosystem.
是否能使用煤或者核能的問題已經不再恰當了：如果沒有在可再生能源上的突破，全球能源的需求將不能得到滿足，更別提一個新的切爾諾貝利事件的危險了。
the question of whether to use coal or nuclear power is simply no longer apposite without a breakthrough in renewable energies, global energy demand cannot be met, not to mention the dangers of a new chernobyl.
這些今天已經有所顯現：中國已經做好世界最大的核能計劃，而且其每年所建造的火電廠的發電量大體相當於整個英國電網的容量。
where this will lead the world can be seen even today china already has the worlds most ambitious scheme for expanding nuclear energy, and every year it builds coalfired power plants whose electricity output is roughly equivalent to the capacity of the entire british power grid!
因此氣候危機的黑天鵝已經將要到來。
so the black swan of the climate crisis is already preparing to land.
抗擊氣候危機對於全球經濟來說不亞於一場綠色革命，這是21世紀的戰爭般的巨大計劃。
to fight the climate crisis effectively demands nothing less than a green revolution of the global economy, the megaproject of the twentyfirst century.
只有富裕的工業國例如歐洲，美國和日本才能夠負擔得起在新興國家的必要投資。
only the rich industrial nations of europe, america, and japan can afford to pay for the necessary investments in emerging countries.
但是這個綠色革���不僅僅只是花錢，還要有相關法律與標準與之配套。 例如，政治監管和新的技術，還有意味著新經濟機會的新產品和新市場。
but this green revolution must be about more than spending money it must also be about laws and standards, i.e. about political regulation and new technologies, as well as new products and markets, which mean new economic opportunities.
今年，一項新的全球氣候協議將在哥本哈根進行商討，目的是取代京都議定書。
this year, a new global climate agreement will be negotiated in copenhagen to replace the kyoto protocol.
這是有效阻止下一個黑天鵝到來的機會。
this is effectively the last chance to prevent the next black swan from landing.
但是我們必須知道，哥本哈根必須是復甦全球經濟的一次絕佳的機會。
but we must understand that copenhagen is also a big chance to revive the global economy.
作為所有21世紀相關國家代表的20國集團應該將哥本哈根的成功視作其直接責任的一部分。
all of the relevant powers of the twentyfirst century are represented in the g20, and they should see the success of copenhagen as part of their direct responsibility.
這次不同於倫敦的20國集團會議，他們應該充分做好他們的工作 — — 不僅僅是為了保護我們的氣候，也是為了重振全球經濟。
this time, unlike at the london g20 meeting, they should do the job properly both to protect our climate and to reboot the global economy.
布萊爾的歐盟災難
blairs eu disaster
法國和荷蘭選民否決歐盟憲法提案後，全世界都知道歐洲專案陷入了深深的困境。
when voters in france and the netherlands turned down the proposal for a constitution for the european union, the world knew that the european project was in deep trouble.
上週有關歐盟中期預算的激烈爭執再次明白無誤地證明了這個判斷。
last weeks bruising battle over the mediumterm future of the unions budget has confirmed that verdict with a vengeance.
這次爭執也使英國6個月的歐洲理事會主席任期黯然結束，讓人們再次看清了長久以來英國在歐盟內部形單影隻的尷尬處境。
it also brought to a sorry close the uks sixmonth presidency of the european council, confirming britains longstanding reputation as the oddmanout in the european union.
這兩個問題的關係盤根錯節，密不可分。
the two events are intimately connected.
法荷選民並沒有明確說出反對憲法提案的原因，但很多評論家都認為他們是在對歐盟突然吸納10個新成員國的做法進行抗議，這些新成員國主要包括來自中東歐的貧困國家。
french and dutch voters did not say why they voted against the planned constitution. but many commentators believe that they were protesting against what they perceived as the precipitate admission of ten new member states, mainly much poorer countries from central and eastern europe.
選民們尤其擔心工作會被成群結隊的東歐移民搶走，價格低廉的波蘭管道工是當時東歐移民在歐洲人心目中的普遍形象。
in particular, voters were afraid that their jobs would be lost to hordes of eastern immigrants, exemplified in the image widely quoted at the time, of the lowcost polish plumber.
當然，具有諷刺意味的是：歐盟15個老成員國中的絕大多數都拒絕讓新成員國立即全面地進入西歐勞務市場。
the irony, of course, was that most of the 15 old member states had refused to give the new members full and immediate access to the western job markets.
但無論如何，抗議已經為時太晚：10個東歐國家已經取得了歐盟成員的地位。
but in any event, it was too late to protest the ten eastern states had already been granted membership of the union.
但現在這25個成員國必須面對擴盟帶來的財政後果，這種後果不僅體現在未來7年內歐盟預算的總體數量，還體現在誰將付出而誰將獲益。
but now the 25 member states must deal with the financial consequences of that enlargement, not just in the overall size of the european union budget for the next seven years, but in who pays and who benefits.
具體地講，核心問題是原有成員國願意為促進發達程度較低的新成員國經濟發展付出多大的代價。
in particular, the central issue is how far the old member states are willing to pay to boost the less developed economies of the new members.
這種情況最終變成了英國、法國和新成員國三方之間的角力。
in the event, it turned into a threeway battle between britain, france and the new member states.
過去，預算的絕大部分都用於農業或者落後地區的發展。
traditionally, a large majority of the budget has gone either on agriculture or on the development of backward regions.
而實際上，這意味著會有大批的資金流入法國這樣的農業生產大國，或者像希臘和葡萄牙這樣的相對貧困的國家。
in practice, this has meant large flows of money either to big agricultural producers, like france, or to poorer member states, like greece and portugal.
在這兩個方面，新成員國都將從歐盟系統獲得巨大的補助。
on both counts, the new member states expected to benefit substantially from the eu system.
過去，英國是歐盟系統財政領域最大的輸家。 因為儘管農業佔到了歐盟開支的三分之二，英國的農業規模卻很有限，因此得到的農業補助也微乎其微。
in the past, the big loser from the eu system, in budgetary terms, was the uk for while agriculture accounted for two thirds of all eu spending, the uk had a small farm sector, and therefore received small farm payments.
英國人很早就抱怨遊戲規則的不公，尤其考慮到英國還屬於歐盟內部相對貧困的國家。 1984年，瑪格麗特·薩切爾執政的保守黨政府提出並獲得了歐盟的批准，英國對歐盟的淨稅額自此大幅度降低。
the british long complained of the unfairness of these rules, especially in view of the fact that the uk was one of the relatively poorer member states and in 1984, margaret thatchers conservative government demanded, and got, a massive rebate on its net contribution to the eu budget.
今天，整個局面有了3個方面的改變。 歐盟的農業政策開始實行改革，農業撥款佔歐盟預算的份額也從60%下降到了40 % 。
today, the situation has changed in three important respects.
近幾年來英國的經濟增長比其它多數歐盟成員國要快得多，早已進入了歐盟富裕國家的行列，即便與法、德兩國相比也毫不遜色。 而新成員國的經濟狀況即便與舊成員國中最窮的相比依然相去甚遠，因此英國在談判確定的預算額度中負有不可推卸的道義責任。
eu farm policy has started to be reformed, and its share of the eu budget has fallen from over 60 to 40 britain has for several years enjoyed significantly faster economic growth than most other member states, so that it is now one of the richer eu countries, even compared with france and germany and the new member states are so much poorer than even the poorest of the old members, that they have an unanswerable moral case for a generous share of whatever budget could be negotiated.
6個月前談判開始時，恰逢英國接任歐洲理事會主席職務。
when negotiations started six months ago, it was britains turn to take over the presidency of the european council.
英國首相托尼·布萊爾向歐洲議會宣佈自己是“充滿熱情的歐洲支持者 ” ， 他的這一表態轟動了整個歐洲政界。
tony blair, british prime minister, electrified the world of european politics by telling the european parliament that he was a passionate proeuropean.
英國的歐洲朋友們早就期待這樣的表態，自從布萊爾1997年當選後他們就毫無結果地苦苦等候。
this was a message for which britains european friends had long been hoping, and for which they had waited in vain since blairs election in 1997.
當然，過去8年布萊爾從未在英倫諸島表達過這樣的觀點。
certainly, he had never expressed any such sentiment inside the british isles during the previous eight years.
由於英國自始至終堅持吸納中東歐國家加入歐盟，人們可能會認為布萊爾政府在預算談判中也會對新成員國表現出相應的慷慨。
since britain had been one of the most insistent advocates of enlargement of the eu to the candidates from central and eastern europe, one might have expected that the blair government would have wished to be correspondingly generous to the newcomers in the conduct of the budgetary negotiations.
開始時，這似乎是英國政府的既定戰術。
at first, this seemed to be the british governments chosen tactic.
出乎所有人的預料，英國提出可以放棄部分財政優惠，從而在道義上贏得了主動。 但兌現承諾的條件是歐盟其它國家（比如法國）同意對歐盟農業政策進行根本的改革。
against all expectations, it struck a morally advantageous posture by offering to surrender some part of its budget rebate, but only if the rest of the european union i.e. france, in particular would agree to fundamental reforms of eu farm policy.
英國花了很長時間才明白：希拉剋是個倍受秸難的軟弱總統，任期持續到2007年但卻掌握不了實權，他沒有能力接受這樣的討價還價。
it took some time before the british came to understand that since president jacques chirac is a beleaguered lameduck president, who will remain in office but not in power until 2007, he is in no position to agree to any such bargain.
因此當英國人認清這種嚴酷的現實後，他們在談判中丟擲了鼠目寸光、強詞奪理的可悲提議，目的主要是以犧牲新成員國的利益為代價，維護英國自身的狹隘利益。
so when the british came to terms with this harsh reality, they played out the lamentable endgame of their management of the negotiations with smallminded cheeseparing and logicchopping offers, all designed primarily to safeguard narrow british interests, mainly at the expense of the new member states.
對於6個月前開始的主席任期，聽慣了布萊爾“充滿熱情的親歐洲人士”的漂亮口號，這恐怕是一個令人哀傷的結局。
it is a sad conclusion to a presidency, launched sixmonths ago, with blairs claim that he was a passionate proeuropean. yet the full text of his speech tells it all.
布萊爾支援歐洲，但不支援現在的歐洲。
blair is in favour of europe but not this europe.
他希望成為歐洲政治的組成部分，但前提是其它歐盟國家遵循英國提出的經濟和社會改革模式。
he wants to be a part of a political europe but only if the other member states follow britains model of economic and social reform.
問題是經濟和社會改革純屬於國家責任，超出了歐盟所能管轄的範疇。 如果法德兩國要進行社會改革，那也只能是法德選民和政治家的事情。
the problem is that economic and social reform are purely national responsibilities, and do not lie within the competence of the union if there is to be economic and social reform in france and germany, that is a matter exclusively for french and german voters and politicians.
只有當歐盟成為真正的聯盟，上述���題才有可能成為歐洲事務。
it could only be a european matter, if the eu were a real federation.
那麼布萊爾是不是聯邦主義者？
is blair a federalist, then?
不！
heavens, no!
他只是個輕率的民族主義份子，沉浸在民族主義份子低俗小報製造出來的恐怖氛圍中。
he is merely an unthinking nationalist, living in terror of the nationalist yellow tabloid press.
那麼他為什麼說自己是個熱情的歐洲支持者？
so why does he say he is a passionate proeuropean?
原因是這個問題他連想都沒想過。
because he has not thought about the question for one moment.
布萊爾在歐洲進退兩難
blairs european dilemma
託尼·布萊爾在第三次競選中大獲全勝。
tony blair has achieved a remarkable third successive electoral victory.
但是工黨在下議院中劇減的席位，布萊爾本人受損的個人聲譽，意味著他的政治地位受到嚴重創傷。
but his sharply reduced majority in the house of commons, and his damaged personal reputation, mean that his political position is seriously weakened.
結果，可憐的他不得不著手於眼前的挑戰，最難應付的就是歐盟的新憲法。
as a result, he will be poorly placed to handle the challenges ahead, the most intractable of which will be the european unions new constitution.
歐盟25國去年簽署的憲法本身並不是一個大問題。
the constitution, adopted by the 25 member states last year, is not, in itself, a big deal.
它就部長聯席會中的多數決投票引進了一些重大改進，賦予歐洲議會更多權力。
it introduces some significant improvements for majority voting in the council of ministers. it gives some more powers to the european parliament.
它還包含了一本基本權利憲法，這也許有助於平衡各成員國的外交政策。
it includes a charter of fundamental rights. it might help harmonize the foreign policies of the member states.
但是它不是一份革命性的檔案。
but it is no revolutionary document.
按照正常的英國憲法慣例，政府應當根據下議院的投票批准憲法；在最近的這次大選之前，政府擁有的多數支援對透過這項憲法應該綽綽有餘。
according to normal british constitutional practice, the government would be expected to ratify this constitution by a vote in the house of commons and, until the recent general election, the governments huge majority should have been more than sufficient.
但是，被圍困在有關這場不得人心並且可能是非法的伊拉克戰爭的是非爭論中的布萊爾，認為他可以拖到2006年（那可是很長一段時間）再批准，這樣就可避免在Westminster的麻煩，並建議舉行全民公投來批准它。
but blair, beset by controversy over the unpopular and possibly illegal war in iraq, thought he could avoid trouble at westminster by postponing ratification until 2006 that is, a comfortably long time in the future, and proposing that it be carried out by popular referendum.
不幸的是，就當前情況來看，這是一場布萊爾不會贏得的全民投票，因為所有的選票都顯示絕大多數人堅決反對歐洲憲法。
unfortunately, as things stand, this is a referendum that blair will not win, because all polls show a large and solid majority against the european constitution.
布萊爾政府也許指望發生在國外的事件能救他們一把。
blairs government may hope to be rescued by outside events.
法國將在本月底就憲法舉行全民公決，在英國看來，法國的一聲“不”也許就能解決他們的問題。
france will hold a referendum on the constitution for the end of this month, and a french no, the british seem to think, might make their problem go away.
因為人們普遍認為，如果法國反對憲法，那麼憲法就不會生效，那麼英國也就不需要舉行什麼公投了。
for the general expectation is that if france rejects the constitution, the constitution would be dead, and no british referendum would be needed.
如果布萊爾打著這樣的如意算盤的話，他就錯了。
if this is blairs calculation, he is mistaken.
事實上，這正是過去半個世紀中英國在他們與歐洲關係問題上一直在犯的錯誤。
moreover, it is the kind of mistake that the british have been making in relations with europe for the past halfcentury.
最近法國的一些民意測驗表明大部分人支援憲法。
some recent french polls now show a majority in favor of the constitution.
但是即使法國投了否決票，那也不會解決英國的問題：相反，它還會加速一場在法國及全歐洲範圍內的有關歐盟未來的嚴重政治危機 — — 這正是英國五十年來試圖避免的那一種危機。
but even if the french do vote no, that will not solve the british problem on the contrary, it will precipitate a major political crisis, in france and across europe, concerning the future of the eu the type of crisis that the british have spent fifty years trying to evade. for if the constitution is indeed dead, what happens next?
沒有任何一個歐盟領導國家會對英國對這一問題的看法感興趣。
none of the leading members of the union will be interested in britains views on this question.
自託尼·布萊爾1997年掌權以來，他在歐洲大受歡迎，成為自約二十五年前英國首相Edward Heath之後最為親歐的英國首相。
when tony blair swept to power in 1997, he was widely welcomed throughout europe as the most proeuropean british prime minister since edward heath a quarter of a century earlier.
他說法語，看起來和英國海峽兩岸的鄰里都相處融洽；更為重要的是，他看起來認同支援歐洲整合。
he spoke french and seemed at ease with britains neighbors across the channel more importantly, he seemed to sympathize with european integration.
但是八年之後，歐洲看得更明白了。
eight years on, europe knows better.
現在所有人都很清楚，布萊爾從內心深處反對一個政治更加整合的歐洲概念。
it is now clear to all that blair is fundamentally opposed to the idea of a more politically integrated europe.
過去四年中，他不僅在讓英國置身於單一歐洲貨幣之外，並在他的競選活動中明確表明，他不希望英國在今後五年中加入歐盟。
not only has he kept britain out of the single european currency over the past four years, he made it clear during the election campaign that he does not expect the uk to join the euro during the next five years either.
偶爾，布萊爾會對在外交和國防政策上進行更多的歐洲性合作表現出濃厚興趣。
occasionally blair flirts with the idea of more european cooperation on foreign policy and defense.
但是過去的三年卻證明，比起任何一種與歐洲團體的合作，他事實上更喜歡對布什的戰爭政策俯首帖耳。
but the past three years proved in practice that he prefers subservience to the war policy of president bush to any sense of community with europe.
簡而言之，布萊對和他所有的前任一樣反對歐洲計劃。
in short, blair is as opposed to the european project as all his predecessors.
法國與英國最本質的差異之一就是大部分的法國主流政治精英長期以來都是明確親歐的。
one fundamental difference between france and britain is that most of the mainstream political elite in france has long been broadly proeuropean.
如果法國選民投了否定票，那與其說是反對憲法，還不如說是反對法國總統希拉剋的投票，或者是他們對歐盟擴大至中歐的訊號表示出的焦慮。
if the french electorate votes no, it will be much less a vote against the constitution than a protest vote against president jacques chirac, or an expression of anxiety about the implications of the eus enlargement to central europe.
相比之下，布萊爾無法贏得這場關於歐洲憲法的公投，不僅僅因為憲法確確實實受到所有廣大媒體的反對，也因為不管是布萊爾還是任何其他英國重要政治領導人都從來沒有說過歐洲整合的好話。
by contrast, blair cannot win a referendum on the constitution, not only because it is opposed by virtually all the popular press, but also because neither he nor any major political leader in britain has ever had a good word to say about european integration.
法國的一票否決票所引發的歐盟未來方向的危機可能會持續一段時間。
the crisis over the unions future direction triggered by a french no vote could last for some time.
但是如果英國人認為憲法就這樣消逝了，認為這樣故事就結束了，那麼他們就是在自欺欺人。
but if the british imagine that the constitution will just die, and that that will be the end of the story, they are deceiving themselves.
相反，他們會發現他們已經像歐洲其他國家一樣被捲入了一場有關歐盟目標的重要討論之中。
on the contrary, they will find themselves embroiled, like the rest of europe, in a fundamental debate about the objectives of the union.
那時他們就會被迫在公眾面前明確選擇他們所要的歐洲型別，這將會引發他們與鄰國之間的爭執。
they will then be forced to make public and explicit choices about the sort of europe that they want, and this will put them at odds with their neighbors.
最終，法國和其他歐盟領導成員國有可能去探尋不同的工作方法來實現一個政治更加整合的歐洲。
in the end, the french and other leading member states are likely to explore alternative ways of working towards a more politically integrated europe.
這個方法最可能運用到的體系機制就是將那些正要加入或謀求加入歐元區、想要屬於一個更為團結的歐洲的國家分組。
the most plausible institutional mechanism for this alternative way forward will be the existing grouping of those member states that have wanted to belong to a more united europe by joining, or seeking to join, the euro zone.
如果憲法被否決��，選擇遠離分組的英國也許會發現他們把自己放在了一個更遠的歐洲外圈之中。
if the constitution is rejected, the british, having chosen to stay out of that grouping, may find that they have maneuvered themselves into an even more remote outer circle of europe.
要責備的是經濟學家，而不是經濟本身
blame the economists, not economics
劍橋 — — 當今世界經濟面臨著崩潰的邊緣，對經濟學家的批評之聲也日漸興起，甚至有人認為他們是導致此次經濟危機的同謀。
cambridge as the world economy tumbles off the edge of a precipice, critics of the economics profession are raising questions about its complicity in the current crisis.
還是讓我們來聽聽經濟學家自己的說法吧。
rightly so economists have plenty to answer for.
經濟學家一直都提倡金融秩序的自由性，幾乎異口同聲地反對“政府的過度監管 ” ， 認為自由的金融可以促進社會的繁榮。
it was economists who legitimized and popularized the view that unfettered finance was a boon to society. they spoke with near unanimity when it came to the dangers of government overregulation.
由於是以所謂專業的身份 — — 當時好象大家也是這麼認為的 — — 他們掌握了一定的話語權，甚至可以進入權力的核心。
their technical expertise or what seemed like it at the time gave them a privileged position as opinion makers, as well as access to the corridors of power.
除了魯裡埃爾·魯比尼和羅伯特·希勒之外，很少有經濟學家對即將到來的金融危機發出預警。
very few among them notable exceptions including nouriel roubini and robert shiller raised alarm bells about the crisis to come.
恐怕更為糟糕的是，他們對如何擺脫經濟危機也沒有提出建設性的辦法。
perhaps worse still, the profession has failed to provide helpful guidance in steering the world economy out of its current mess.
對於凱恩斯主義者的經濟刺激計劃來說，經濟學家的觀點從“絕對必須”到“沒有效率而且有害 ” ， 真是無所不包。
on keynesian fiscal stimulus, economists views range from absolutely essential to ineffective and harmful.
在對金融的監管方面，經濟學家們不乏有一些好的建議，但也沒有達成什麼共識，過去他們一致地大力鼓吹“金融中心論”的好處，而現在，大家幾乎各自一詞，努力都出了自己的良方。
on reregulating finance, there are plenty of good ideas, but little convergence. from the nearconsensus on the virtues of a financecentric model of the world, the economics profession has moved to a neartotal absence of consensus on what ought to be done.
難道經濟學要有一個大的變革麼？
so is economics in need of a major shakeup?
難道我們要燒燬現在的教科書而從頭再來麼？
should we burn our existing textbooks and rewrite them from scratch?
當然不是，如果沒有經濟學家們的分析，我們現在都還不能意識到目前所面臨危機的本質。
actually, no. without recourse to the economists toolkit, we cannot even begin to make sense of the current crisis.
例如，為什麼中國的外匯儲備積累會引起俄亥俄州的房貸過剩？
why, for example, did chinas decision to accumulate foreign reserves result in a mortgage lender in ohio taking excessive risks?
如果你不懂得運用行為經濟學原理，代理理論，資訊經濟學和國際經濟學等，你可能就不知道其中的關聯。
if your answer does not use elements from behavioral economics, agency theory, information economics, and international economics, among others, it is likely to remain seriously incomplete.
問題不是出在經濟學本身，而是在經濟學家身上，經濟學家們（以及聽從他們的人）過分相信自己所偏好的經濟學模型，這包括：市場是有效的；誰能掌握金融的創新，誰就可以很好地化解風險；金融行業自律是最好的監管；政府的干預是無效率且有害的。
the fault lies not with economics, but with economists. the problem is that economists and those who listen to them became overconfident in their preferred models of the moment markets are efficient, financial innovation transfers risk to those best able to bear it, selfregulation works best, and government intervention is ineffective and harmful.
他們可能忘記了其他的一些可能導致完全不同的結果的經濟學模型。
they forgot that there were many other models that led in radically different directions.
過於的自信必然是潛在的危險。
hubris creates blind spots.
如果要有什麼需要改變的的話，應該是他們的認知能力。
if anything needs fixing, it is the sociology of the profession.
教科書，至少目前運用在頂尖學府的教科書，應該是沒有問題的。
the textbooks at least those used in advanced courses are fine.
幾乎沒有經濟學家認為經濟學是把市場看作一成不變，一種單一的經濟理論不可能解釋整個市場。
noneconomists tend to think of economics as a discipline that idolizes markets and a narrow concept of allocative efficiency.
如果你只是參加一個入門的經濟學課程，或是你是一個記者，問經濟學家對當前政策的簡要評論時，你可以會得到這個粗淺的答案。
if the only economics course you take is the typical introductory survey, or if you are a journalist asking an economist for a quick opinion on a policy issue, that is indeed what you will encounter.
而當你再進一步學習經濟學課程，或是在高階研討班裡再多花一些時間，你就會得出完全不同的答案。
but take a few more economics courses, or spend some time in advanced seminar rooms, and you will get a different picture.
勞動經濟學家不僅知道工會對市場的危害，同樣也知道，在某種程度下，工會對提高生產力也有一定的好處。
labor economists focus not only on how trade unions can distort markets, but also how, under certain conditions, they can enhance productivity.
貿易經濟學家研究的是全球化對不同國家之間貿易不平衡，以及導致的後果。
trade economists study the implications of globalization on inequality within and across countries.
金融經濟學家研究的是“有效市場”理論失效的後果。
finance theorists have written reams on the consequences of the failure of the efficient markets hypothesis.
開放經濟學的宏觀經濟學家研究的是國際金融的不穩定性。
openeconomy macroeconomists examine the instabilities of international finance.
透過進一步對經濟學的研究，你就會知道市場失靈的種種表現，以及政府對市場干預的各種有效手段。
advanced training in economics requires learning about market failures in detail, and about the myriad ways in which governments can help markets work better.
宏觀經濟學家需要更為嚴格的訓練，由於他們所依賴的是嚴格理想的數學模型，和現實有明顯的區別，所以能夠分清楚專家的理論和現實世界的差距尤其重要。
macroeconomics may be the only applied field within economics in which more training puts greater distance between the specialist and the real world, owing to its reliance on highly unrealistic models that sacrifice relevance to technical rigor.
可悲的是，在目前看來，自從約翰·梅納德·凱恩斯解釋了由於市場需求的不足，經濟是如何受制於失業率的理論之後，宏觀經濟學家們並沒有什麼新的貢獻。
sadly, in view of todays needs, macroeconomists have made little progress on policy since john maynard keynes explained how economies could get stuck in unemployment due to deficient aggregate demand.
正如同布拉德•德隆和保羅•克魯格曼所說的，宏觀經濟學實際上已經在退步。
some, like brad delong and paul krugman, would say that the field has actually regressed.
經濟學是一個有著多種模型的工具 — — 每一種都代表著現實生活的某個方面，經濟學家的能力就體現在如何運用正確的模式來解決當前問題。
economics is really a toolkit with multiple models each a different, stylized representation of some aspect of reality. ones skill as an economist depends on the ability to pick and choose the right model for the situation.
經濟學的博大精深並不為公眾所知道，原因是經濟學家們有了太多的特權，經濟學的本質是列出可能解決問題的方法，以及有關聯的一些折中解決方案，而現在的經濟學家只是將自己個人的偏好加在上面，不是運用理性的分析，而是將自己的意識形態，把自己所偏好的選項提交出來。
economics richness has not been reflected in public debate because economists have taken far too much license. instead of presenting menus of options and listing the relevant tradeoffs which is what economics is about economists have too often conveyed their own social and political preferences.
更有甚之，經濟學家不願意將自己的質疑和大眾分享，更不用說對社會大眾的“教誨 ” ， 沒有一個經濟學家會認為自己的模式是完全正確的。
furthermore, economists have been reluctant to share their intellectual doubts with the public, lest they empower the barbarians. no economist can be entirely sure that his preferred model is correct.
但當他們在推銷自己的方案時候，他們會以過分自信地口吻來表達，以此說服大家。
but when he and others advocate it to the exclusion of alternatives, they end up communicating a vastly exaggerated degree of confidence about what course of action is required.
具有諷刺意味的是，當前的經濟學家們紛紛提出了自己不同觀點，可謂是五花八門，這正說明了經濟學家這個職業本身的價值所在。 經濟學的本身是提出所有解決問題的可能性，而不是給出解決問題的答案。
paradoxically, then, the current disarray within the profession is perhaps a better reflection of the professions true value added than its previous misleading consensus. economics can at best clarify the choices for policy makers it cannot make those choices for them.
當經濟學家有不同意見的時候，大家對經濟如何執行會有著更為深刻的認識，而當所有的經濟學家都發出一個聲音的時候，那就是我們該保持警惕的時候了。
when economists disagree, the world gets exposed to legitimate differences of views on how the economy operates. it is when they agree too much that the public should beware.
誰把外債當回事
bleed the foreigner
普林斯頓 — — 當前，世界正面臨重演2008金融崩潰的危險 — — 甚至更厲害。
princeton today, the world is threatened with a repeat of the 2008 financial meltdown but on an even more cataclysmic scale.
這回的震中是在歐洲，而不是美國。
this time, the epicenter is in europe, rather than the united states.
而這次出事兒的金融工具，不是高度複雜的結構性產品，而是一種最古老的金融工具 — — 政府債券。
and this time, the financial mechanisms involved are not highly complex structured financial products, but one of the oldest financial instruments in the world government bonds.
儘管有關政府和央行急著想對策，但有一種深刻的心理機制阻礙著債務問題的有序解決：我們不太把欠陌生人的債當回事兒。
while governments and central banks race frantically to find a solution, there is a profound psychological dynamic at work that stands in the way of an orderly debt workout our aversion to recognizing obligations to strangers.
如果債權人遠在他鄉又素不相識，就會有比較強的衝動，索性違約，一了百了。
the impulse simply to cut the gordian knot of debt by defaulting on it is much stronger when creditors are remote and unknown.
2007~2008年，是購房者還不起錢，如今換成了政府。
in 20072008, it was homeowners who could not keep up with payments now it is governments.
但不論是當時還是今日，債主都是遙遠的陌生人。
but, in both cases, the lender was distant and anonymous.
美國人的按揭並未留在本地銀行的賬上，而是被打包成玄奧的金融工具賣到全世界。 同樣地，希臘國債也有很大一部分攥在外國債主手裡。
american mortgages were no longer held at the local bank, but had been repackaged in esoteric financial instruments and sold around the world likewise, greek government debt is in large part owed to foreigners.
鑑於西班牙和法國在近代早期曾多次違約，而希臘自從1830年獨立以來更是習慣性違約者，有人便揣測，是不是民族性格令有些國家染上了違約的癮。
because spain and france defaulted so much in the early modern period, and because greece, from the moment of its political birth in 1830, was a chronic or serial defaulter, some assume that national temperament somehow imbues countries with a proclivity to default.
但追溯這麼漫長的歷史連貫性有些想當然，因為忽略了決定某國是否能保持債務穩健的一個關鍵因素：誰是債主。
but that search for long historical continuity is facile, for it misses one of the key determinants of debt sustainability the identity of the states creditor.
在是否按時、迅速還債的問題上，這個變數影響巨大。
this variable makes an enormous difference in terms of whether debt will be regularly and promptly serviced.
近代早期法國和西班牙經常上演的壯觀的破產鬧劇，大多數跟欠外債有關。
the frequent and spectacular early modern bankruptcies of the french and spanish monarchies concerned for the most part debt owed to foreigners.
16世紀的哈布斯堡王朝以極高利息向佛羅倫薩、日內瓦和奧格斯堡的商人借債。
the sixteenthcentury habsburgs borrowed at very high interest rates from florentine, genovese, and augsburg merchants.
“舊制度”統治下的法國也發展出相似的行為模式，總是向阿姆斯特丹和日內瓦借錢，用來打仗，16、17世紀跟西班牙人打，到了18世紀跟英國人打。
ancien rgime france developed a similar pattern, borrowing in amsterdam or geneva in order to fight wars against spain in the sixteenth and seventeen centuries, and against britain in the eighteenth.
但荷蘭和英國走的就是另外一條路。
the netherlands and britain, however followed a different path.
它們的外債遠遠不如內債多。
they depended much less on foreign creditors than on domestic lenders.
1688年英國光榮革命廢黜了信仰天主教的國王詹姆斯二世，不僅把來自荷蘭的新教徒威廉·奧倫治扶上英國王座，也把偏好內債的荷蘭模式帶到了英國。
the dutch model was exported to britain in 1688, along with the political revolution that deposed the catholic james ii and put the dutch protestant william of orange on the english throne.
事實上，光榮革命也促成了一場財政革命。
indeed, the glorious revolution enabled a revolution in finance.
尤其是議會權利的確立，使得預算從制定到執行的全過程都逃不開債權人階級的代理人的監督。
in particular, recognition of the rights of parliament of a representative assembly ensured that the agents of the creditor classes would have permanent control of the budgetary process.
他們督促國家保持財政穩健並償還債務，也連帶著保護了外國債權人的利益。
they could thus guarantee also on behalf of other creditors that the states finances were solid, and that debts would be repaid.
立憲君主制限制了宮廷的奢侈浪費和軍事冒險，這兩樣可以說是近代早期專制君主制（如法國和西班牙）的招牌。
constitutional monarchy limited the scope for wasteful spending on luxurious court life as well as on military adventure the hallmark of early modern autocratic monarchy.
簡言之，近代世界的財政革命依託於一種政治秩序 — — 債權人構成政治階級，這種秩序是後來普遍民主制的先聲。
in short, the financial revolution of the modern world was built on a political order which anteceded a full transition to universal democracy in which the creditors formed the political class.
那種模式傳播到許多國家，成為近代財政穩健的基石。
that model was transferred to many other countries, and became the bedrock on which modern financial stability was built.
二戰以後，發達國家的財政原本也是內債優先的，仍然保守著1688年的傳統。
in the post1945 period, government finance in rich industrial countries was also overwhelmingly national at first, and the assumptions of 1688 still held.
後來，事情起了一些變化。
then something happened.
隨著20世紀70年代開始的全球金融市場自由化，外國信貸資源變成可及之物。
with the liberalization of global financial markets that began in the 1970s, foreign sources of credit became available.
到了20世紀80年代中期，美國成為淨債務國，對外債的依賴程度與日俱增。
in the mid1980s, the us became a net debtor, relying increasingly on foreigners to finance its debt.
歐洲也步其後塵。
europeans, too, followed this path.
20世紀80年代兜售歐洲一體化的廣告詞，有一條就是，一體化以後借債變得更容易。
part of the promise of the new push to european integration in the 1980s was that it would make borrowing easier.
20世紀90年代，統一貨幣構想對義大利和西班牙政客的主要吸引力就在於，引入新貨幣既能壓低利率，又能開啟外國人的錢袋子，使政府可以實現廉價融資。
in the 1990s, the main attraction of monetary union for italian and spanish politicians was that the new currency would bring down interest rates and make foreign money available for cheap financing of government debt.
一直到20世紀90年代末，歐元啟動前夕，歐盟國家的國債還大都是內債：1998年，主權債務中外債比重只有五分之一。
until the late 1990s and the advent of monetary union, most government debt in the european union was domestically held in 1998, foreigners held only onefifth of sovereign debt.
歐元引入後，外債比重迅速上升。
that share climbed rapidly in the aftermath of the euros introduction.
到2008年金融危機爆發前夜，葡萄牙國債的四分之三、西班牙和希臘國債的一般、義大利國債的四成多都成了外債。
in 2008, on the eve of the financial crisis, threequarters of portuguese debt, half of spanish and greek debt, and more than 40 of italian debt was held by foreigners.
隨著外債比重上升，向外國人轉嫁債務成本的政治誘惑也越來越大。
when the foreign share of debt grows, so do the political incentives to impose the costs of that debt on foreigners.
20世紀30年代大蕭條期間及其後一段時間，世人曾有一種強烈的情緒，認為債權人就是一幫非法、敗德的吸血鬼，於是當時違約成風。
in the 1930s, during and after the great depression, a strong feeling that the creditors were illegitimate and unethical bloodsuckers accompanied widespread default.
當德意志帝國銀行行長沙赫特（Hjalmar Schacht）對富蘭克林·羅斯福說，納粹德國將要對外債違約，包括欠美國一些銀行的債務時，這位美國總統竟然一拍大腿，笑著說 ： “ 華爾街銀行家罪有應得！
even us president franklin roosevelt jovially slapped his thigh when reichsbank president hjalmar schacht told him that nazi germany would default on its external loans, including those owed to american banks, exclaiming, serves the wall street bankers right!
”請看今日歐洲，德國總理默克爾、法國總統薩科齊屢屢苛責銀行家們“愚蠢 ” ， 豈不也在縱容希臘人賴賬的決心？
in europe today, impatient greeks have doubtless derived some encouragement from excoriations of bankers foolishness by german chancellor angela merkel and french president nicolas sarkozy.
“統一貨幣需要統一財政 ” ， 這句經濟學家的老生常談，其實揭示了一條更深刻的關於債務的真理：若沒有責任共擔之心，便難有可靠之債。
the economists commonplace that a monetary union demands a fiscal union is only part of a much deeper truth about debt and obligation debt is rarely sustainable if there is not some sense of communal or collective responsibility.
只有遵循這個道理，才能打消賴賬之心，讓債務變得安全而便宜。
that is the mechanism that reduces the incentives to expropriate the creditor, and makes debt secure and cheap.
最終，歐洲只有團結起來，分擔重擔，才能平安走出當前危機。
at the end of the day, a collective, burdensharing europe is the only way out of the current crisis.
但那需將政治責任和權力大��集中起來，遠遠超越歐洲人今日所能做到之程度。
but that requires substantially greater centralization of political accountability and control than europeans seem able to achieve today.
這也就是為什麼，許多歐洲國家還只顧今天能揮霍，不管明天要還錢。
and that is why many of them could be paying much more for credit tomorrow.
失明於加沙和耶路撒冷
blind in gaza and jerusalem
倫敦 - - 我的元旦是在悉尼度過的。 我當時觀看著煙火綻放在悉尼大橋上空歡迎2009年。
london i spent the new year in sydney, watching the fireworks above the iconic bridge welcome in 2009.
而當天夜晚在加沙的爆炸則並不是打算讓哈馬斯高興，而是想要破除其在巴勒斯坦人心目中的威信。
the explosions over gaza that night were not intended to entertain, but rather to break hamas and discredit it in the eyes of palestinians.
這是最新的一次施暴行動，意在解決和平分享基督教徒稱為的聖地。
it was the latest resort to terrible violence in order to resolve how to share in peace what christians still like to call the holy land.
甘地批評聖經把“以牙還牙，以眼還眼”的報復合法化。
mahatma gandhi criticized the biblical justification of retribution, an eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth.
他認為，如果聽從這一教唆就會意味著所有人都失明。
followed through to its end, he argued, it would mean that all were blind.
在巴勒斯坦和以色列就證明了這一點。
and so it has proved in palestine and israel.
加沙和耶路撒冷都失明瞭。
blind in gaza, blind in jerusalem.
超過1400名男子、婦女和兒童喪失，另有四千多人受傷，而大部分事情都是在預料之中的。
much of what has happened was predictable, as well over 1,400 men, women, and children have died and more than 4,000 have been injured.
首先，美國給以色列的進攻予以合法化並且把責任全部推到哈馬斯身上，正如以前它把所有的責任都算在阿拉法特和法塔赫頭上一樣。
first, the united states justified the israeli assault and blamed everything on hamas, just as it used to pin all responsibility for whatever went wrong on yasir arafat and fatah.
第二，儘管法國總統薩爾科奇高調外交斡旋受人歡迎，但是歐洲在這一事件中即使不是沒有蹤影，也是無關緊要。
second, despite french president nicolas sarkozys welcome highprofile diplomacy, europe has been irrelevant, if not quite invisible.
正如以色列官員指出的那樣，歐洲人總是在那裡擺姿勢照照像而已。
as israeli officials point out, europeans are always there for the photo opportunity.
中東四方調停人布萊爾和以往一樣沒有效用。
the quartets peacemaker, tony blair, is as unctuously nugatory as ever.
他出現在有線新聞網之中，但是，從2007年他得到任命後有沒有實際訪問加沙呢？
he appears on cnn , but has he actually visited gaza since his appointment in the summer of 2007?
第三，正如以往一樣，只要有人敢於批評以色列對哈馬斯火箭襲擊反應過度及其對巴勒斯坦人的集體懲罰，以色列都指責為反猶主義。
third, as usual, israel has accused of antisemitism those who have dared to criticize its disproportionate response to hamass indefensible rocket attacks and its collective punishment of palestinians.
一位義大利的紅衣主教一時失言，就被指責為使用否認猶太人大屠殺的語言。
an italian cardinal, who admittedly spoke intemperately, was accused of using the language of holocaust denial.
那麼根據這一標準，如果我不當地批評哈馬斯的火箭襲擊，是否我也是反伊斯蘭教主義者呢？
by that standard, does my unqualified criticism of hamass rocket attacks make me an islamophobe?
湊巧的是，這次對加沙的致命攻擊發生的時候，將會成為美國最為著名的中東和平使者出版了書籍，談論如何正確解決問題。
coincidentally, the deadly attack on gaza came at the same time that a clutch of americas most distinguished wouldbe middle east peacemakers published books about how the task should properly be tackled.
這聽起來就是求職申請，在爭取奧巴馬總統的注意力。
it all sounded a bit like a series of job applications the war for president barack obamas ear.
這些專家的共識之一就是布什總統把事情搞糟了。
one thing all these experts could agree on is that president george w. bush was a disaster.
美國的政策好像是在利庫德總部裡制定的一樣。
american policy might as well have been made in likuds headquarters.
即使在最後，當聯合國安理會對加沙問題投票的時候，布什還是樂意給萊斯難堪來討好以色列總理奧爾穆特。
even at the end, when the united nations security council voted on gaza, bush was happy to humiliate condoleezza rice at israeli prime minister ehud olmerts bidding.
這些“賢人”都是克林頓和其他總統的幕僚。 他們好像都承認2000年戴維營和平提議失敗畢竟不能全部歸咎於阿拉法特。
these wise men, advisers one and all to president bill clinton and other presidents, all seem to concede that the failure of the proposed camp david accord in 2000 could not, after all, be laid solely at arafats door.
以色列前總理巴拉克也應該承擔責任。
former israeli premier ehud barak should carry his share of the blame.
而且，他們都批評克林頓時代的政策首先獲得以色列的認同，這樣就難以贏得阿拉伯人的信任和支援。
moreover, they all criticize the clintonera practice of routinely clearing americas policy positions first with israel, which is hardly likely to win arab confidence or support.
美國外交官有關和平程序的觀點總體上並不涉及有關和平協議內容的分歧。
the american diplomats arguments about process did not on the whole carry over into disagreement about the content of a peace deal. all more or less agree on this.
所有人都大體同意以下幾點。
a palestinian state within the 1967 borders, adjusted by agreement through mutual land swaps. an end to most west bank settlements.
那就是，巴以建立兩個國家；對以色列做出安全保證；透過協商互換領土調整在1967年邊境內建立巴勒斯坦國；結束大多數西岸定居點；巴勒斯坦難民不得實施“返回家園”的權利，但是給予經濟補償；對耶路撒冷的聖地建立聯合或者國際主權體系；分割耶路撒冷以便成為兩國的首都。
no right of return for palestinian refugees, but financial compensation for them. some system of joint or international sovereignty over jerusalems holy places and the division of the city so that it can become the capital of two states.
當然，這是理應發生的事情。
of course, this is what should happen.
而且我認為，在新的受人歡迎的調停國家卡達和土耳其的幫助下這依舊可能。 土耳其總理把以色列的襲擊稱為“嚴重的反人類罪行 ” 。
and i suppose that it is conceivable that it could still happen with the help of welcome new mediators like qatar and turkey, whose prime minister called israels attack a serious crime against humanity.
但是我開始懷疑是否真的可能在這一基礎上實現和平。
but i have begun to wonder whether it will really be possible to achieve peace on this basis.
法塔赫和阿巴斯總統等巴勒斯坦溫和派人物完全失去了信用。
fatah, and palestinian moderates like president mahmoud abbas, have been totally discredited.
巴勒斯坦人在整體上變得更為激進了。
palestinians on the whole have been further radicalized.
任何和解都離不開哈馬斯的參與和支援，而它卻揚言復仇。
hamas, whose engagement and support is essential for any settlement, has sworn revenge.
每天都會卻發生新的巴勒斯坦人悲劇。
every day, new palestinian sorrows strike heaven in the face.
寡婦們和死者的母親們痛哭流涕要求償命。
the widows and the mothers of the dead weep and cry out for bloody justice.
我們是否應該感到驚訝呢？
should we be surprised?
如果英國政府追求和平以及透過轟炸天主教城市摧毀北愛爾蘭的共和軍，那麼這種做法是會離間還是贏得天主教輿論？
had the british government pursued peace and the destruction of the ira in northern ireland by bombing catholic derry, would that have alienated or won over catholic opinion?
在以色列方面，那個政治領導人真正想要巴勒斯坦國家而且願意冒著伴隨試圖建立巴勒斯坦國的政治風險呢？
on the israeli side, which political leaders really want a palestinian state and are prepared to take the political risks associated with trying to establish one?
他們那個人足夠強大來應付西岸的定居者呢？
which of them are strong enough to deal with the west bank settlers?
否則就不會有和平協議。
there will be no peace settlement otherwise.
那個領導人會向美國猶太人中的極端分子講述事實呢？
which leaders will teach the facts of life to the more extreme members of the jewish diaspora in america?
以色列領導人中誰理解和解要比報復和復仇更為重要呢？
who among israels leaders understands that reconciliation is more important that retribution and revenge?
無論過去看來多麼困難，我都沒有對巴以問題感到絕望。
however tough things looked in the past, i have never felt such a sense of despair about palestine and israel.
理性被吞沒在了鮮血裡。
reason has been drowned in blood.
看起來希望的政治已經讓位給了墓地的政治。
it seems as though the politics of hope have given way to the politics of the cemetery.
可憐的巴勒斯坦，可憐的以色列。
poor palestine. poor israel.
誰可以在黑暗中點燃蠟燭呢？
who is there now who can still light a candle in the dark?
區塊鏈大謊言
the big blockchain lie
紐約—比特幣的價值從去年高點下跌了70%左右，這場所有泡沫之母已經破滅。
new york with the value of bitcoin having fallen by around 70 since its peak late last year, the mother of all bubbles has now gone bust.
更一般地說，加密貨幣已經進入了一場不那麼秘密的浩劫。
more generally, cryptocurrencies have entered a notsocryptic apocalypse.
以太幣、EOS、萊特幣和XRP等主要加密貨幣都下跌了80%多，數千種其他數字貨幣下跌了90—99 % ， 其餘更是露出了騙局的本質。
the value of leading coins such as ether, eos, litecoin, and xrp have all fallen by over 80, thousands of other digital currencies have plummeted by 9099, and the rest have been exposed as outright frauds.
因此你不必感到奇怪，八成首次貨幣發行（ICO）從一開始就是騙局。
no one should be surprised by this four out of five initial coin offerings icos were scams to begin with.
面對市場的血雨腥風，加密惡棍的支持者們躲進了最後的避難所 ： “ 區塊鏈”防線。 區塊鏈是一種分散式記賬軟體，是所有加密貨幣的基礎。
faced with the public spectacle of a market bloodbath, boosters have fled to the last refuge of the crypto scoundrel a defense of blockchain, the distributedledger software underpinning all cryptocurrencies.
區塊鏈被說成是所有問題的潛在解決妙招，不管是貧困與饑荒還是癌症。
blockchain has been heralded as a potential panacea for everything from poverty and famine to cancer.
事實上，它是人類歷史上被吹得最厲害而實際最沒用的技術。
in fact, it is the most overhyped and least useful technology in human history.
在實踐中，區塊鏈無非是外表光鮮的電子表格。
in practice, blockchain is nothing more than a glorified spreadsheet.
但它卻成了自由主義意識形態的代名詞，將一切政府、央行、傳統金融機構和真實貨幣視為邪惡的權力集中，必毀之而後快。
but it has also become the byword for a libertarian ideology that treats all governments, central banks, traditional financial institutions, and realworld currencies as evil concentrations of power that must be destroyed.
在區塊鏈原教旨主義者的理想世界裡，所有經濟活動和人際互動都必須是無政府主義或自由主義去中心化的。
blockchain fundamentalists ideal world is one in which all economic activity and human interactions are subject to anarchist or libertarian decentralization.
他們但願社會和政治生活的全部最終都落在應該是“無許可 ” （ 向所有人開放）和“無信任 ” （ 不依賴銀行等可信中介）的公共賬簿上。
they would like the entirety of social and political life to end up on public ledgers that are supposedly permissionless accessible to everyone and trustless not reliant on a credible intermediary such as a bank.
但區塊鏈並沒有催生一個烏托邦，而是帶來了我們耳熟能詳的經濟地域。
yet far from ushering in a utopia, blockchain has given rise to a familiar form of economic hell.
一些自利的白人（區塊鏈圈子裡很少有女性或少數群體）擺出一副全世界窮人、邊緣群體和無銀行服務大眾的救世主形象，宣稱無中生有地創造了數十億美元財富。
a few selfserving white men there are hardly any women or minorities in the blockchain universe pretending to be messiahs for the worlds impoverished, marginalized, and unbanked masses claim to have created billions of dollars of wealth out of nothing.
但只要想一想權力在加密貨幣“礦工 ” 、 交易所、開發者和財富所有者手中大量集中，就能看出區塊鏈與去中心化和民主根本無關；它只和貪婪有關。
but one need only consider the massive centralization of power among cryptocurrency miners, exchanges, developers, and wealth holders to see that blockchain is not about decentralization and democracy it is about greed.
比如，少數幾家公司 — — 大多位於民主窪地俄羅斯、喬治亞和中國 — — 控制著所有加密挖礦活動的三分之二到四分之三，並且都透過抬高交易成本來增加豐厚的利潤。
for example, a small group of companies mostly located in such bastions of democracy as russia, georgia, and china control between twothirds and threequarters of all cryptomining activity, and all routinely jack up transaction costs to increase their fat profit margins.
顯然，區塊鏈狂熱分子將把我們引向完全不受法律約束的匿名卡特爾，而不是信任央行和受監管的金融中介。
apparently, blockchain fanatics would have us put our faith in an anonymous cartel subject to no rule of law, rather than trust central banks and regulated financial intermediaries.
加密貨幣交易也表現出類似的模式。
a similar pattern has emerged in cryptocurrency trading.
在中心化的交易所，99%的交易會不時被駭客入侵。
fully 99 of all transactions occur on centralized exchanges that are hacked on a regular basis.
而和真實貨幣不同，一旦你的加密貨幣被入侵，就會永遠消失。
and, unlike with real money, once your crypto wealth is hacked, it is gone forever.
此外，加密開發的中心化 — — 比如，原教旨主義者們稱以太坊創始人維塔利克·布特林（Vitalik Buterin）是“生活的仁慈獨裁者 ” — —等於宣佈了所謂的“程式碼即法律”是一個謊言。 在“程式碼即法律”的幌子下，好像作為區塊鏈應用基礎的軟體堅如磐石。
moreover, the centralization of crypto development for example, fundamentalists have named ethereum creator vitalik buterin a benevolent dictator for life already has given lie to the claim that code is law, as if the software underpinning blockchain applications is immutable.
真相是開發者擁有絕對權力充當法官和陪審團。
the truth is that the developers have absolute power to act as judge and jury.
如果他們的充滿漏洞的“智慧”偽合同出了問題，發生大規模入侵，他們只需要改改程式碼，用任性的指令將失敗的貨幣“分叉”稱另一種貨幣，這表明一整套“無信任”機制從一開始就完全不值得信任。
when something goes wrong in one of their buggy smart pseudocontracts and massive hacking occurs, they simply change the code and fork a failing coin into another one by arbitrary fiat, revealing the entire trustless enterprise to have been untrustworthy from the start.
最後，加密世界的財富集中度比朝鮮還要高。
lastly, wealth in the crypto universe is even more concentrated than it is in north korea.
基尼係數1.0表示一個人控制著一國100%的收入/財富，朝鮮的基尼係數為0.86，非常不平等的美國的基尼係數是0.41，而比特幣的基尼係數高達0.88。
whereas a gini coefficient of 1.0 means that a single person controls 100 of a countrys incomewealth, north korea scores 0.86, the rather unequal united states scores 0.41, and bitcoin scores an astonishing 0.88.
應該清楚，所謂的“去中心化”根本就是控制著這個偽行業的偽億萬富翁所宣傳的神話。
as should be clear, the claim of decentralization is a myth propagated by the pseudobillionaires who control this pseudoindustry.
如今，被吸引到加密貨幣市場的散戶都輸了個底兒掉，而沒有倒閉的神油販子們作用萬貫假財，只要他們試圖套現“資產 ” ， 這筆財富就會立即蒸發。
now that the retail investors who were suckered into the crypto market have all lost their shirts, the snakeoil salesmen who remain are sitting on piles of fake wealth that will immediately disappear if they try to liquidate their assets.
至於區塊鏈本身，全世界沒有一家機構 — — 銀行、公司、非政府組織或政府機構 — — 會把資產負債表或與客戶的交易、貿易和互動記錄放在公開的去中心化點對點無許可賬簿上。
as for blockchain itself, there is no institution under the sun bank, corporation, nongovernmental organization, or government agency that would put its balance sheet or register of transactions, trades, and interactions with clients and suppliers on public decentralized peertopeer permissionless ledgers.
沒有好理由認為如此重要的財產和無價的情報應該公開記錄。
there is no good reason why such proprietary and highly valuable information should be recorded publicly.
此外，實際使用分散式記賬技術 — — 所謂的企業DLT — — 的情況，也和區塊鏈沒有什麼關係。
moreover, in cases where distributedledger technologies socalled enterprise dlt are actually being used, they have nothing to do with blockchain.
它們是私有的、去中心化的，記錄在區區幾個受控制的賬簿上。
they are private, centralized, and recorded on just a few controlled ledgers.
它們的訪問需要許可，許可只授予合格的人。
they require permission for access, which is granted to qualified individuals.
也許最重要的是，它們基於受信任的當局，它們的信譽需要時間的積澱。
and, perhaps most important, they are based on trusted authorities that have established their credibility over time.
所有這些說明 ， “ 區塊鏈”徒有其名。
all of which is to say, these are blockchains in name only.
總而言之，所有“去中心化”的區塊鏈，到了實際使用時，最終都是中心化的、有許可的資料庫。
it is telling that all decentralized blockchains end up being centralized, permissioned databases when they are actually put into use.
照此看，區塊鏈甚至還不如1979年就發明的標準電子表格。
as such, blockchain has not even improved upon the standard electronic spreadsheet, which was invented in 1979.
嚴肅的機構斷不會允許讓世界極權盜賊政權的陰影下執行的匿名卡特爾驗證交易。
no serious institution would ever allow its transactions to be verified by an anonymous cartel operating from the shadows of the worlds authoritarian kleptocracies.
因此，毫不奇怪只要傳統設定的“區塊鏈”試水，要麼被扔進垃圾箱，要麼轉變為私人有許可資料庫，無非就是加上了誤導性名字的Excel電子表格資料庫。
so it is no surprise that whenever blockchain has been piloted in a traditional setting, it has either been thrown in the trash bin or turned into a private permissioned database that is nothing more than an excel spreadsheet or a database with a misleading name.
大銀行的終結
the end of big banks
發自華盛頓特區 — — 在美國及歐盟經歷了近十年的危機，救市和改革後，金融體系 — — 無論是在這些國家和全球 — — 變得非常與2006年時的樣子非常相似。
washington, dc after nearly a decade of crisis, bailout, and reform in the united states and the european union, the financial system both in those countries and globally is remarkably similar to the one we had in 2006.
自2010年以來人們嘗試施行了多項金融改革，但總體效果卻相當有限的。
many financial reforms have been attempted since 2010, but the overall effects have been limited.
一些大銀行陷入了困境，而其他一些則取而代之。
some big banks have struggled, but others have risen to take their place.
無論是2008年全球金融危機之前還是今時今日，金融版圖上照樣是十幾個大銀行一統天下的局面。
both before the 2008 global financial crisis and today, just over a dozen big banks dominate the worlds financial landscape.
但如今金融業正發生著某種變革，而大銀行可能很快也將淪為明日黃花了。
and yet the ground is shifting beneath the financial sector, and big banks could soon become a thing of the past.
沒有幾個官員私下對金融改革的進展感到滿意。
few officials privately express satisfaction with the progress of financial reform.
不過在公開場合，他們大多都比較收斂，但明尼阿波利斯聯邦儲備銀行總裁尼爾·卡什卡利（Neel Kashkari）則最近激起了人們共鳴，因為他呼籲要對在應對那些“大而不能倒”的金融機構所導致的問題上所取得的進展進行重新評估。
in public, most of them are more polite, but the president of the federal reserve bank of minneapolis, neel kashkari, struck a chord recently when he called for a reevaluation of how much progress has been made on addressing the problem of financial institutions that are too big to fail tbtf.
卡什卡利自2006年開始在美國財政部長亨利·M·保爾森（Henry M. Paulson）手下任職。
kashkari worked for henry m. paulson in the us treasury department, beginning in 2006.
此人不僅旁觀了金融危機的全過程，更親身參與其中；2008年10月，他就任負責問題資產救助計劃的副部長，受命穩定金融體系。
he not only watched the financial crisis develop in october 2008 he became the assistant secretary responsible for the troubled asset relief program tarp, with the goal of stabilizing the financial system.
他也是一位同時在高盛（大型銀行）和太平洋投資管理公司（大型資產管理公司）工作過的共和黨人。
he is a republican who has worked at both goldman sachs a big bank and pimco a large assetmanagement company.
因此當他發表“我認為那些大銀行仍然是大而不能倒，並繼續對我們的經濟構成顯著且持續的風險。 ”這番談話時自然就引起了人們的警覺。
so people pay attention when he says, i believe the biggest banks are still too big to fail and continue to pose a significant, ongoing risk to our economy.
同時卡什卡利對2010年多德 - 弗蘭克金融改革法案的評價也是正確的。
and kashkari is correct in his assessment of the doddfrank financial reforms of 2010.
該立法以及隨之出臺的法規確實將某些事務推向了正確的方向。
this legislation and the ensuing regulations have moved some issues in the right direction.
“但考慮到另一場金融危機可能引發的龐大成本，同時這些新工具能否有效應對危機的不確定性 ， ” 他指出 ， “ 我認為我們必須認真考慮一些更大膽的，轉型性的選項。 ”
but given the enormous costs that would be associated with another financial crisis and the lack of certainty about whether these new tools would be effective in dealing with one, he argues, i believe we must seriously consider bolder, transformational options.
卡什卡利目前提議採用一個完全正確的手段：舉行公眾會議和廣泛的討論以評估大型銀行是否應該被分拆，是否這些銀行（以及其他金融機構）應被強制留置更多資產並承擔更少債務，或者是否應該徵收債務稅以遏制過度槓桿。
kashkari is now proposing exactly the right approach to hold public conferences and extensive discussions to evaluate whether large banks should be broken up, whether they and other financial institutions should be forced to fund themselves with more equity and less debt, or whether there should be a debt tax to discourage excessive leverage.
第一次會議定於4月4日召開（而筆者也是演講者之一 ） 。
the first conference will be on april 4 i will be one of the speakers.
卡什卡利只是地區性聯邦儲備銀行的12位總裁之一。
kashkari is just one of 12 presidents of regional federal reserve banks.
他同時擔任聯邦公開市場委員會委員，負責制定貨幣政策 — — 但不是在負責監督銀行監管的聯邦儲備系統理事會。
and he sits on the federal open market committee fomc, which sets monetary policy but not on the board of governors of the federal reserve system, which oversees bank regulation.
但他要求評估大而不能倒問題的呼籲將產生重大的影響，原因有三：
still, his call for an evaluation of the tbtf problem will have a major impact for three reasons.
首先，他表達的意見完全合理並符合主流，並構建於（他和其他人）對這場和其他金融危機的深厚經驗之上。
first, the views he expresses are entirely sensible and mainstream, based on deep experience his and others with this and other financial crises.
卡什卡利運用自身所處的權威角色，傳達了許多其他理性的人們在近十年來一直在試圖傳達的資訊。
kashkari is presenting from a position of authority a message that many other reasonable people have been trying to convey for nearly a decade.
其次，卡什卡利所闡述的 — — 以適當的央行語言 — — 與餘下的民主黨總統候選人在選民面前提出的觀點完全相同。
second, kashkari has articulated in appropriate centralbank language precisely the same view that the remaining democratic presidential candidates are putting before the voting public.
希拉里·克林頓為金融改革提出了一項細緻周到的計劃，將重點放在對槓桿徵稅並提高資本金要求上。
hillary clinton has a detailed and thoughtful plan for financial reform, with emphasis on taxing leverage and increasing capital requirements.
伯尼·桑德斯則傾向於分拆銀行。
bernie sanders would prefer to break up the banks.
但目標是相同的;正如卡什卡利所指出的那樣，任何這些工具都有可能讓我們到達一個更好的境地。
but the goal is the same and, as kashkari points out, any of these tools can potentially get us to a better place.
當理性的共和黨和民主黨人開始在政策上趨同時，我們就更有可能實現合理的變革。
when reasonable republicans and democrats begin to converge on policy, we are more likely to get sensible change.
第三，卡什卡利提出手段的時機與新“區塊鏈（blockchain ） ” 技術的到來恰巧同步，使得人們可能以更分散的方式來組織金融交易。
third, kashkaris timing coincides with the arrival of new blockchain technology, which makes it possible to organize financial transactions in a more decentralized way.
這種技術的各種版本要麼已經面市要麼正在開發 — — 而且都有著一個非常真實的前景，將降低大多數金融行業的交易成本。
various versions of this technology are either already available or currently under development and there is a very real prospect that this will reduce transaction costs across much of the financial sector.
我們還不知道哪個版本會最終通行，同時也有關於如何確保新標準和系統得以增強穩定性，而不是（與以前的一些金融創新那樣）產生不愉快的意外後果的熱烈討論。
we do not yet know which version will prevail, and there is active discussion about how to ensure that the new standards and systems enhance stability, rather than as with some previous financial innovations producing unpleasant unintended consequences.
最重要的是，區塊鏈技術有潛力去大幅減少 — — 或甚至消除 — — 那些可信中介機構（如大型銀行）的存在價值。
most important, blockchain technology has the potential to reduce substantially, or even eliminate, the value of being a trusted intermediary such as a large bank.
而大銀行本身也在大量注資這類技術的研發 — — 大概是希望透過限制最終放權的程度以挽救它們自身的一部分業務。
and yet the big banks themselves are pouring money into this technology presumably hoping to save at least some part of their business by limiting the degree of ultimate decentralization.
卡什卡利將帶領我們去反思 — — 並希望能結束 — — 傳統大型銀行的大而不能倒問題。
kashkari will lead the way to rethinking and, one hopes, ending the tbtf problem in traditional big banks.
在區塊鏈的世界裡，他和他的同事們會努力工作，以防止任何大而不能倒的變體死灰復燃。
in a blockchain world, he and his colleagues are likely to work hard to prevent any variant of tbtf from reappearing.
區塊鏈白日夢
the blockchain pipe dream
紐約—關於比特幣和其他加密貨幣終歸要失敗的預言總是會引來許多人替區塊鏈技術基礎辯護。
new york predictions that bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies will fail typically elicit a broader defense of the underlying blockchain technology.
誠然，這一論點說，迄今為止的大部分“初次貨幣發行 ” （ ICO）都以失敗告終，1,500多種加密貨幣也會有一大半失敗，但“區塊鏈”終將掀起金融和人類一般交易的革命。
yes, the argument goes, over half of all initial coin offerings to date have already failed, and most of the 1,500plus cryptocurrencies also will fail, but blockchain will nonetheless revolutionize finance and human interactions generally.
事實上，區塊鏈是有史以來最宣傳過度的技術。
in reality, blockchain is one of the most overhyped technologies ever.
首先你，區塊鏈不如已有資料庫高效。
for starters, blockchains are less efficient than existing databases.
如果有人說他們在“一個區塊鏈上”運營，他的意思往往是他們在做一個到處複製而成的軟體應用。
when someone says they are running something on a blockchain, what they usually mean is that they are running one instance of a software application that is replicated across many other devices.
與分散化應用相比，所需的儲存空間和計算力要大得多，延遲（latency）也要長得多。
the required storage space and computational power is substantially greater, and the latency higher, than in the case of a centralized application.
嵌入了“權益證明”或“零知識”技術的區塊鏈要求所有交易都加密查證，因此會減慢速度。
blockchains that incorporate proofofstake or zeroknowledge technologies require that all transactions be verified cryptographically, which slows them down.
使用“工作證明”技術的區塊鏈 — — 許多流行的加密貨幣採取這種方式 — — 則會產生另外一個問題：它們需要巨量能源來保證。
blockchains that use proofofwork, as many popular cryptocurrencies do, raise yet another problem they require a huge amount of raw energy to secure them.
這解釋了為何今年冰島比特幣“挖礦”作業所消耗的能源比全部冰島家庭加起來還要多。
this explains why bitcoin mining operations in iceland are on track to consume more energy this year than all icelandic households combined.
當速度/查證權衡真的划算時，區塊鏈才有意義，但這項技術的兜售可不是這麼說的。
blockchains can make sense in cases where the speedverifiability tradeoff is actually worth it, but this is rarely how the technology is marketed.
區塊鏈投資方案通常會做出異常誘人的承諾，如顛覆雲端計算等整個行業，全然不顧這項技術的顯而易見的侷限性。
blockchain investment propositions routinely make wild promises to overthrow entire industries, such as cloud computing, without acknowledging the technologys obvious limitations.
比如，有很多專案宣稱區塊鏈是分散式的無處不在的“世界計算機 ” 。
consider the many schemes that rest on the claim that blockchains are a distributed, universal world computer.
這需要假設已經擁有高效的系統處理每天數百萬筆交易的銀行有理由切換到顯著更慢、效率更低的單一加密貨幣。
that claim assumes that banks, which already use efficient systems to process millions of transactions per day, have reason to migrate to a markedly slower and less efficient single cryptocurrency.
這與我們所知的金融業軟體使用之道完全背道而馳。
this contradicts everything we know about the financial industrys use of software.
金融機構，特別是有演算法交易的金融機構，需要高速高效的交易處理。
financial institutions, particularly those engaged in algorithmic trading, need fast and efficient transaction processing.
對於這些目標，單一的全球化分散式區塊鏈（如以太坊）永遠派不上大用場。
for their purposes, a single globally distributed blockchain such as ethereum would never be useful.
另一個錯誤的假設是區塊鏈代表了新的普適協議，就像網際網路的TCP-IP協議和HTML協議。
another false assumption is that blockchain represents something akin to a new universal protocol, like tcpip or html were for the internet.
言下之意是這個或那個區塊鏈將成為未來世界大部分交易和通訊的基礎。
such claims imply that this or that blockchain will serve as the basis for most of the worlds transactions and communications in the future.
同樣地，考慮到區塊鏈的實際工作情況，這純屬無稽之談。
again, this makes little sense when one considers how blockchains actually work.
一方面，區塊鏈本身需要依賴TCP-IP等協議，因此它們如何替代後者並不清楚。
for one thing, blockchains themselves rely on protocols like tcpip, so it isnt clear how they would ever serve as a replacement.
此外，和基礎層面的協議不同，區塊鏈是“狀態性”的，這意味著它們儲存所有傳送給它們的有效通訊。
furthermore, unlike baselevel protocols, blockchains are stateful, meaning they store every valid communication that has ever been sent to them.
因此，設計良好的區塊鏈需要考慮使用者硬體的限制，防止垃圾郵件。
as a result, welldesigned blockchains need to consider the limitations of their users hardware and guard against spamming.
這解釋了為何比特幣軟體客戶端Bitcoin Core每秒鐘只處理5—7筆交易，而維薩卡每秒鐘可以可靠地處理25,000筆交易。
this explains why bitcoin core, the bitcoin software client, processes only 57 transactions per second, compared to visa, which reliably processes 25,000 transactions per second.
正如我們無法用一個集中式資料庫記錄全世界的所有交易，我們也無法在一個分散式資料庫中實現這一點。
just as we cannot record all of the worlds transactions in a single centralized database, nor shall we do so in a single distributed database.
事實上 ， “ 區塊鏈縮放”的問題或多或少仍然沒有得到解決，並在短期未來仍將保持這一狀態。
indeed, the problem of blockchain scaling is still more or less unsolved, and is likely to remain so for a long time.
儘管我們可以相當確定區塊鏈不會取代TCP-IP，但區塊鏈的一個要素 — — 如Tezos或以太坊的智慧合約語言 — — 有望最終成為具體應用的標準，正如企業版Linux和Windows之於PC作業系統。
although we can be fairly sure that blockchain will not unseat tcpip, a particular blockchain component such as tezos or ethereums smartcontract languages could eventually set a standard for specific applications, just as enterprise linux and windows did for pc operating systems.
但像目前的許多投資者那樣下注於某種“幣”和下注於採用某種更大的“協議”不是一回事。
but betting on a particular coin, as many investors currently are, is not the same thing as betting on adoption of a larger protocol.
基於我們對開源軟體使用的認識，沒有理由認為具體的區塊鏈應用對企業的價值集中在一兩種或幾種幣上。
given what we know about how opensource software is used, there is little reason to think that the value to enterprises of specific blockchain applications will capitalize directly into only one or a few coins.
第三種錯誤的觀點是認為區塊鏈將消滅對金融和其他可靠中介的需求，從而建立“無信任的”烏托邦。
a third false claim concerns the trustless utopia that blockchain will supposedly create by eliminating the need for financial or other reliable intermediaries.
這是荒謬的，原因很簡單：每一份今天存在的金融合同，都可以修改或被參與方違約。
this is absurd for a simple reason every financial contract in existence today can either be modified or deliberately breached by the participating parties.
透過自動化，用僵化的“無信任”條款將這些可能排除在商業上不可行，因為這要求所有金融協議都有100%的現金抵押，從資本成本角度，這實在過於瘋狂。
automating away these possibilities with rigid trustless terms is commercially nonviable, not least because it would require all financial agreements to be cash collateralized at 100, which is insane from a costofcapital perspective.
此外，似乎許多可能適用於金融的區塊鏈應用 — — 如證券化和供給鏈監控等 — — 仍然需要中介，因為難免有一些環境會發生未預見到的情形，要求自由裁量。
moreover, it turns out that many likely appropriate applications of blockchain in finance such as in securitization or supplychain monitoring will require intermediaries after all, because there will inevitably be circumstances where unforeseen contingencies arise, demanding the exercise of discretion.
在這種情形中，區塊鏈最重要的作用是確保交易的所有各方彼此同意其地位和各自的義務。
the most important thing blockchain will do in such a situation is ensure that all parties to a transaction are in agreement with one another about its status and their obligations.
應該立即停止區塊鏈興奮。
it is high time to end the hype.
比特幣是一隻行動遲緩、能源效率低下的恐龍，永遠無法像Excel電子表格那樣迅速廉價地處理交易。
bitcoin is a slow, energyinefficient dinosaur that will never be able to process transactions as quickly or inexpensively as an excel spreadsheet.
以太坊的計劃 — — 不安全的權益證明鑑定系統 — — 將使其很容易受到有影響力的局內人的操縱。
ethereums plans for an insecure proofofstake authentication system will render it vulnerable to manipulation by influential insiders.
瑞波幣的跨境銀行間金融轉賬技術很快就會被SWIFT打得找不著北。 SWIFT是一個世界主要金融機構已在使用的非區塊鏈服務。
and ripples technology for crossborder interbank financial transfers will soon be left in the dust by swift, a nonblockchain consortium that all of the worlds major financial institutions already use.
類似地，幾乎沒有交易成本的集中式電子支付系統 — — Faster Payments、支付寶、微信支付、Venmo、Paypal、Square等 — — 在全世界已有數十億人正在使用。
similarly, centralized epayment systems with almost no transaction costs faster payments, alipay, wechat pay, venmo, paypal, square are already being used by billions of people around the world.
今天的“幣瘋”和十九世紀工業革命前夕的鐵路瘋狂別無二致。
todays coin mania is not unlike the railway mania at the dawn of the industrial revolution in the midnineteenth century.
就其本身而言，區塊鏈算不上是一場革命。
on its own, blockchain is hardly revolutionary.
但與金融和機械程式的遠端自動化相結合後，它可以產生深遠的潛在影響。
in conjunction with the secure, remote automation of financial and machine processes, however, it can have potentially farreaching implications.
說到底，區塊鏈的使用將侷限於具體的、定義清晰的複雜應用，這些應用要求透明度和抗干擾甚於要求速度 — — 比如與無人駕駛汽車或無人機的通訊。
ultimately, blockchains uses will be limited to specific, welldefined, and complex applications that require transparency and tamperresistance more than they require speed for example, communication with selfdriving cars or drones.
至於各種幣，它們和19世紀40年代的鐵路股沒有什麼區別，將隨著泡沫 — — 就像大部分泡沫一樣 — — 的破裂而一蹶不振。
as for most of the coins, they are little different from railway stocks in the 1840s, which went bust when that bubble like most bubbles burst.
思維一律
block thinking
“多元文化”在當今世界的每一個地方，尤其是在歐洲，幾乎成了可疑的代名詞。
multiculturalism has become a suspect term almost everywhere in the world nowadays, and particularly in europe.
人們會說 ： “ 我曾經對不同的文化抱有開放以及寬容的態度，但是現在我看到它正引向何方了。
people say things like i used to be for openness and toleration of difference, but now i see where its leading.
”但是它 正 引向何方呢？
but where is it leading?
幾乎所有從寬容明顯跌落到聲名狼藉的原因都與伊斯蘭教有關。
almost every reason for tolerations apparent fall into disrepute concerns islam.
甚至是簡單的要求，就像女學生在班上戴頭巾，都突然被裝載了重大的政治性，並且被當成是必須由最高層的政府來解決的問題。
even simple requests, like that of schoolgirls to wear headscarves in class, are suddenly freighted with immense political significance and treated as issues that must be resolved at the highest level of government.
人們以及他們選舉出的領導人常常認為這些貌似清白的提議實際上是某個不祥的“暗藏的動機”的一部分。
people and their elected leaders as well often have the feeling that such seemingly innocent proposals are in fact part of an ominous hidden agenda.
那個動機就是“伊斯蘭教 ” ， 許多人想象它包含了我們每天從媒體上讀到的所有恐怖的事情：在奈及利亞北部根據伊斯蘭教教法用石頭砸死通姦的女人，在沙烏地阿拉伯砍下小偷的手，在巴基斯坦（或者甚至英國北方的城市，像布拉德福德和曼徹斯特）殺死拒絕接受包辦婚姻的女人，為自殺性人體炸彈辯護的意願。
that agenda is islam, which many imagine to include all the terrible things that we can read about in the press every day the stoning of adulterous women under sharia law in northern nigeria, the amputation of thieves hands in saudi arabia, honor killings of women who refuse arranged marriages in pakistan or even northern english cities like bradford and manchester, the willingness to justify suicide bombings.
如果你回答說想要戴頭巾去上學的女孩並非生活在奈及利亞或沙烏地阿拉伯，並且幾乎肯定不會持有在那些國家存在的瓦哈比教派的極端觀點，你肯定會被回以一種幾乎是寬容地憐憫的目光，一種為不可救藥地天真的人保留的目光。
if you reply that the girls who want to wear headscarves to school arent living in nigeria or saudi arabia, and almost certainly dont share the extreme wahhabi views found in those countries, you will be met with a look of almost indulgent pity, a look of the type reserved for the terminally nave.
或者你會被告知沙特受過訓練的伊瑪目怎樣扭住女孩子的手臂，把她們變成“伊斯蘭教”不情願的掩飾物的故事。
or you will be told stories about how saudi trained imams are twisting the girls arms, turning them into unwilling stalkinghorses for islam.
事實上，今天要按其本來面目談論頭巾完全是不可能的事情。
indeed, it is virtually impossible nowadays to talk about headscarves as an issue in its own right.
所有有關女孩子動機的社會學證據，事實上它們各不相同，因其不相干而被置之不理。
all the sociological evidence about the girls motives, which are in fact very varied, is swept aside as irrelevant.
人們唯一關心的是伊斯蘭教所帶來的威脅。
all that matters is the threat posed by islam.
這正是我所稱之為“思維一律”的典型例子，這種現象近些年在歐洲蔓延得非常快。
this is a classic example of what i call block thinking, which seems to have made huge strides in europe in recent years.
約翰·鮑文的近作《為什麼法國不喜歡頭巾》就記錄了這種轉變。
john bowens recent book why the french dont like headscarves documents this shift.
思維一律把各不相同的現實都融進一個牢不可破的聯合體中，用的兩種方式。
block thinking fuses a varied reality into one indissoluble unity, and in two ways.
第一種是對伊斯蘭教的虔誠或文化的不同表現被看成是以不同的方式表達了同一核心理念。
first, different manifestations of islamic piety or culture are seen as alternative ways of expressing the same core meaning.
第二種方式是所有的穆斯林人都被看成是支援這些核心理念的。
second, all muslims are then seen as endorsing these core meanings.
一個女孩佩戴頭巾事實上可能是對她父母以及 他們 所奉行的那種伊斯蘭教的反抗，而另一些女孩可能對伊斯蘭教非常虔誠同時對性別歧視或暴力極度反感。 但是人們從來不去關心這些可能性。
the possibility that a girl wearing a headscarf might in fact be rebelling against her parents and their kind of islam, and that others might be deeply pious while being utterly revolted by gender discrimination or violence, is lost from view.
思維一律的現象早已有之，並且我們每個人都有某種程度的思維一律。
block thinking is an ageold phenomenon, and we all do it to some degree.
但是，在另一個時代我們也許會很寬容它所帶來的後果，今天它卻可能帶有爆炸性的潛在力量，因為以這種方式思考的人最有可能按照薩默爾·亨廷頓的“文明衝突論”的觀點來看這個世界。
but, while in another age we might have been indulgent about its consequences, today it has explosive potential, because people who think in this manner are prime recruits for seeing the world in terms of samuel huntingtons theory of the clash of civilizations.
更糟糕的是，以這種方式思考的人隨後採取的行動會更把我們推向亨廷頓所描繪的惡夢般的局面。
whats worse, the way such people then act tends to edge us closer to huntingtons nightmare scenario.
他們把持有不同觀點的所有伊斯蘭教徒都統統看成是對西方的威脅，使得穆斯林更難站出來批評他們自己的思維一律者 — — 就像本·拉登，後者正在樹立他們自己的由“基督教徒和猶太教徒”組成的聯合敵人。
by treating all the varied segments of islam as nothing more than parts of a unified threat to the west, they make it harder for muslims to stand out and criticize their own block thinkers people like osama bin laden, who are building their own unified enemy, composed of christians and jews.
兩方的思維一律者都給另一方的思維一律者以援助和安慰，而伴隨這邊每一次變動他們把我們推向了更深的深淵。
block thinkers on each side give aid and comfort to block thinkers on the other side, and with each exchange they pull us closer toward an abyss.
那麼我們怎樣才能制止這種極度愚蠢的思維方式呢？
so how can we stop this madness?
思維一律者之所以如此頑固部分是因為一方對其的批評者並不為另一方對其的批評者所知曉。
block thought persists in part because its critics on each side are unknown to those on the other side.
事實上，歐洲思維一律者的批評者經常會碰到這樣的回答 ： “ 但是哪裡有批評極端伊斯蘭的穆斯林呢？ ”
indeed, how many times does a critic of european block thought meet this kind of response but where are the muslims who are criticizing extremist islam?
當然，你不太可能在巴黎記者或者更廣泛的歐洲職業政治階層的客廳裡碰到他們。
of course, one isnt likely to meet them in the drawing rooms of paris journalists or the wider european professional political class.
但是對思維一律者解釋這一點永遠不會起到讓他們真正接觸在另一面真實發生著的多層面的討論那樣的作用。
but explaining that to block thinkers will never have the impact of a real connection to the multifaceted discourse that is actually taking place on the other side.
那麼，真正的問題就是：能夠提供迫切需要的接觸的橫跨兩面的人在哪裡呢？
the real question, then, is this where are the crossover figures who can provide that urgently needed connection?
BMW與中國的司法公正
bmw's and chinese justice
在世界的大多數地方 ， " BMW" 代表著華貴奢侈和與眾不同。
in most places, the name bmw implies luxury and exclusivity.
但在中國，這一品牌卻無意間捲入了一些非常事件。 這些事件反映了普通的中國老百姓面對權勢和腐敗的無奈。
but in china, the brand has unwittingly found itself enmeshed in tales that illustrate the powerlessness of ordinary chinese against the powerful and corrupt.
第一樁醜聞發生在去年的哈爾濱，其起因是一輛滿載著大蔥的拖拉機與一輛BMW擦掛。
the first scandal occurred last year, after a tractor filled with green onions scraped the side of a bmw in harbin.
拖拉機和鍍著銀灰色金屬漆的豪華轎車的駕駛者都是45歲的婦女，但她們之間的共同點也僅止於此了：前者是位農婦，而後者則是一位富商之妻。
the drivers of both the tractor and the metallicsilver luxury car were 45yearold women, but any similarity between them ended there the former was a peasant, the latter the wife of a wealthy businessman.
在一番對峙之後，富商之妻駕車衝進街沿上越來越多的圍觀者，將農婦當場撞死並撞傷了12個圍觀者。
after a confrontation between the two, the wealthy wife drove her bmw into the growing crowd of spectators on the roadside, killing the peasant woman and injuring 12 others.
這一案件在地方法院進行審理，法官的判決結果是"意外擾亂交通秩序 " ， 撞人者被判入獄兩年並緩期執行。
the case went to the local court, where the judge ruled it an accidental traffic disturbance and gave the driver a twoyear suspended sentence.
法官的判決使得流言四起，其內容都是說法官對肇事者手下留情是因為此人的丈夫與省裡的高官有關係。
the judge's ruling spurred rumors that he went easy on her because her husband was related to senior provincial officials.
該案很快就演變成一個"富對貧"的故事並被人們廣泛引用為高層腐敗的寫照。
it quickly became a story of rich versus poor, widely cited as an example of highlevel corruption.
在接下來的幾個月裡，由於報紙和電視臺對該事件滾雪球般地報道使其成為一個全國上下共同關注的話題。
over the next few months, newspapers and television stations ran with the story as it snowballed into a national obsession.
在公眾輿論的壓力下，哈爾濱地方法院重新開庭審理了該案，但在今年三月結案時的結論也只是維持緩刑的原判。
alarmed by the public reaction, the harbin magistrate ordered the case reopened, only to have the suspended sentence confirmed when the case was closed this march.
此時，另一個發生在2003年末的，與BMW相關的事件也在幾乎永遠退出公眾視線之前，再次悄然浮現。
the big bmw story of late 2003 resurfaced quietly, before being buried again forever.
就在同一個月，一樁彩票抽獎醜聞再一次讓BMW這一品牌成為公眾關注的焦點。
that same month, a lottery scandal threw the bmw brand into the limelight once again.
陝西省負責彩票發行的官員以造假為由拒絕兌現一張中了頭獎的彩票。 這張彩票的持有人是17歲的保安劉亮，他應獲的獎品是一輛價值58，000美金的BMW轎車和120，000元現金（約合14，510美金 ） 。
lottery officials in shaanxi province rejected a winning ticket, calling it a fake and denying its bearer, a 17yearold security guard named liu liang, the grand prize of a 58,000 bmw and 120,000 yuan 14,510 in cash.
被控造假和領獎被拒使劉亮怒不可遏，以至於他爬上一塊廣告牌並威脅要縱身跳下以示清白。
liu became so angry about being accused of fraud and denied the car that he climbed atop a high advertising billboard and threatened to jump as a show of innocence.
但故事並沒有以他被警察勸服而結束。
but the story didn't end when police officers managed to talk him down.
新聞媒介仍報導著他堅持自己沒有偽造彩票的事實和 彩票中心合法拒獎的宣告。
news broadcasts covered his continued insistence that he did not forge his ticket, along with the lottery center's claims that their rejection of the ticket was legitimate.
警方終於介入了這一事件，並在一番仔細調查之後宣佈查出了真正的禍首：楊永明，一個與當地彩票發行部門簽約負責組織彩票銷售的個體商人。
the police finally stepped in and, after a careful investigation, announced that they had found the true criminal yang yongming, a private businessman whom the local lottery administration had contracted to organize ticket sales.
楊與一些政府官員合謀操縱抽獎試圖詐騙頭獎獎品。 這些官員也因瀆職而被捕。
yang had conspired with the government officials directing the lottery, who were arrested for malfeasance, to fraudulently obtain the top prizes.
在今年6月，劉亮終於得到了他應得的獎品-一輛BMW-325i型轎車和來自彩票中心的誠摯歉意。
in june liu liang finally got what he deserved a bmw325i sedan and a sincere apology from the lottery center.
如果說第一樁醜聞是個悲劇，那麼第二樁則更像是出鬧劇。
if the first scandal was a tragedy, the second was more like a farce.
但兩個事件都為我們提供了了解當代中國人心態的機會。
but both offer keys to understanding contemporary chinese psychology.
在第一樁BMW案發生之後，民間呼聲並不在於法庭對富商之妻的判刑太輕而在於普通民眾對中國的司法制度缺乏信心。
the outcry after the first bmw case was not really about the light sentence given to a rich woman, but about the lack of confidence ordinary people have in china's judicial system.
在中國，權力、金錢和關係凌駕於法律之上。
in china, power, money, and connections trump the law.
即便是在人們越來越習慣於訴諸法律的情況下，許多中國人也認為面對權勢他們不可能獲得司法公正。
even as they are becoming ever more litigious, many chinese believe that they have no hope of securing justice against the powerful.
這種心態從死亡農婦的丈夫在得到10，000美金的賠償時無動於衷的反應中可見一斑。
the apathetic response of the dead peasant woman's husband to the 10,000 in compensation he received was telling.
他表示 ： " 我不在乎法院的判決，也不在乎它是否公正。 "
i don't care about the verdict and whether it is justice or not, he said.
最為不利的後果是公眾對司法體系喪失了信任。
the most harmful consequence is the public's loss of trust in the system.
社會信任不是用金錢可以買到的。
social trust is not something you can buy with money.
如果整個社會都認為不能依靠法律維權-而必須依靠與那些有權有勢的人所建立的關係網-那麼這樣的社會是否是人們願意歸屬的社會就成為一個問題。
if an entire society believes that you cannot depend on legal rights for protection that one must instead rely on a web of relationships with those who have power and influence questions about whether such a society is livable or desirable will remain.
同樣，在第二樁BMW案中，人們沒有譴責一個腐敗的商人；他們將過失歸咎於彩票中心，一個政府機構。
similarly, in the second bmw case, people didn't blame a corrupt businessman they ascribed culpability to the lottery center, a government body.
因此他們開始懷疑一個機構，而不是某位個人-他們甚至懷疑政府本身。
so instead of mistrusting one person, they grew suspicious of an institution even of government itself.
所以，當一位執拗的青年孤身挑戰擁有眾多審計員、公證員和藉口的彩票機構時，讓人們欽佩的真正勝利者就是他這個人，而不是司法制度。
when a stubborn teenager went up against the mighty lottery authority with its army of auditors and inspectors and initial alibis, this individual, not the system, was the clear winner of the public's admiration.
劉亮或許只是一個工人階層的小孩，但他的話語中卻透出睿智。 他說仍然有一群"沉默的大多數"可以影響脆弱的中國社會的運轉方式。
liu liang may have been just a workingclass kid, but there was wisdom in his words that there is still a silent majority who can affect the workings of china's fragile society.
他拒絕了私下調解，因為他相信如果他放過了腐敗的政府官員 ， " 他們會繼續欺騙公眾。
he refused to settle privately, because he believed that if he let corrupt government officials off the hook, they'll keep scamming the public.
"在他的不懈努力及媒體的調查下，這場騙局終於真相大白。
thanks to his perseverance and the media's investigation, the fraud was laid bare.
權力的腐敗隨處可見，但像Liu這樣的個體的中國人已經形成了一股與之對抗的力量。
power corrupts everywhere, but individuals in china such as liu have come to form a countervailing force.
可即便如此，這種邊緣的力量還沒有能形成一種糾正社會不公的制度。
even so, such marginal forces do not yet constitute a system for redressing grievances.
中國的流行音樂愛好者們能夠聽任何想聽的音樂，包括麥當娜所唱的"我會動搖整個體制 " 。 普通的中國人也需要勇氣吶喊這樣的訊息。
while pop music fans in china can listen to whatever they like, including madonna singing i'm gonna shake up the system, ordinary chinese need courage to speak such messages aloud.
有一句話說得好 ： " 中國人現在需要的不是良知，而是勇氣。 "
as one saying goes, there is not want of conscience in chinese, but there is want of courage.
從透明罩到橋樑
from bubbles to bridges
倫敦—隨著上市公司年度股東大會召開季的推進，一個一直存在的問題是公司官員和大眾之間缺乏真正的對話。
london as the season in which public companies hold their annual general meetings progresses, one persistent issue is the lack of genuine dialogue between company officials and the general public.
在投資者、高管、員工以及社群展開激烈爭論和討論的場合，都給人一種各說各的感覺，一群人圍坐在董事會會議桌周圍，另一群人則集中在餐桌四周。
in place of robust debate and discussion among investors, executives, the workforce, and the community at large, the conversation seems to be taking place in different silos, with one group sitting around the boardroom table and another gathered at the kitchen table.
從外部看來，董事會常常像是一個透明罩，在這個罩子裡，平庸刻板之士做出影響成千上萬人生活的重大決定。
from the outside, a boardroom is all too often viewed as a kind of bubble where big decisions that influence thousands of lives are made by faceless people.
人們對董事會的印象是，在這裡，大筆獎金被授予高管；討價還價和人際關係比功績和努力工作更重要。
they are perceived as places where big bonuses are awarded to chief executives and where horsetrading and old boy networks are more important than merit or hard work.
隨著董事會外部人日益要求能夠問責董事會成員，開啟溝通渠道現已成為公司長期成功的關鍵。
with people outside the boardroom increasingly demanding to hold those inside it to account, opening up avenues of communication is now critical to companies longterm success.
這一轉變的一個重要特徵將是高層管理人員認識到他們無法再用“你根本不懂”為藉口將批評拒之門外。
an important feature of this shift will be the realization by highprofile executives that they can no longer afford to brush off criticism with the youjustdontunderstand defense.
他的言辭引申出一種更廣泛的感覺：CEO們“不食人間煙火 ” ， 不願或無法就尖銳問題給出真誠的回答。
his words tapped into a wider feeling that ceos are out of touch and unwilling, or unable, to respond to tough questions with sincere answers.
就連廣受尊敬的投資者巴菲特也無法免俗，他說沃倫“如果少點怒氣和妖魔化會更好。 ”
even the widely respected investor warren buffett missed the mark when he said that warren would do better if she was less angry and demonized less.
在工資差異、企業的社會責任、資料隱私以及無法提供正確的努力工作的激勵或充分懲罰失敗的獎金文化等問題上缺少真正的對話，難怪會產生擔憂和不信任。
in the absence of genuine dialogue about issues like wage discrepancy, corporate social responsibility, data privacy, and a bonus culture that does not seem to provide the right incentives for hard work or to adequately penalize failure, worries and mistrust are guaranteed to fester.
透明度不足、缺少明確性，以及缺少答案催生了一種感覺：公司常常進行可疑的交易，無法信任。
lack of transparency, absence of clarity, and a paucity of answers feeds into the perception that companies are too often engaged in dodgy dealings and cant be trusted.
最糟糕的是，溝通破裂讓董事會和餐桌的人都失去了認識到他們在討論類似的問題，有著類似的找到這些問題解決辦法的渴望的機會。
worst of all, the breakdown in communication deprives those around both the boardroom and kitchen tables of the opportunity to realize that they are talking about similar problems and share similar desires to find solutions to them.
高管和董事需要將與他們互動的人當成是對話者而不是聽眾。
chief executives and board chairs need to think of those with whom they interact as people to talk with rather than at.
能說的領導人固然好，但懂得聽的領導人更優秀。
leaders who can talk are fine but those who can listen are even better.
企業高管需要認識到，如果他們不以投資者、監管者、工人和消費者能夠理解的方式解釋他們的決策，那麼他們 — — 而不是他們的對話者 — — 才是問題。
business executives need to realize that if they cannot explain their decisions in ways that investors, regulators, workers, and consumers can understand, then they not the people with whom they are talking are the problem.
當積極投資者希望探一探公司究竟時，董事會的本能不應該是結成利益共同體，召集顧問對付積極投資者。
when activist investors want to take a look at a company, the boardroom instinct should not be to circle the wagons and call in consultants to do battle.
相反，董事會和高管團隊需要捫心自問，隨什麼他們的公司會成為目標，是否存在合理的疑慮需要解決。
