多數人指望黨對媒體的壟斷來宣傳他們的思想，比如 ： “ 請給優秀共產黨員萊斯澤克投票。 ”
most counted on the partys media monopoly to carry their message, such as it was vote lezek, a good communist.
共產黨政權以非凡的風度接受了不可避免的失敗，這一點非常值得讚揚。
to their credit, the regime accepted its inevitable loss with remarkable grace.
投票結束後當天下午3點，雅魯澤爾斯基召集了黨內高層會議。
at three p.m. on the day after the vote, jaruzelski summoned top party officials.
“我們遭到了完敗 ， ” 他說。
our defeat is total, he told them.
“必須找到政治解決的辦法。
a political solution will have to be found.
”他這麼說不是要使用暴力，也不是要竄改計票結果。
by that, he meant no violence and no doctoring the ballot count.
接受現實是共產黨人唯一的選擇。
the communists would have to live with the result.
20年後的今天，我仍然感到迷惑。
twenty years later, i remain mystified.
我們這些報導東歐問題的記者知道團結工會必將獲勝。
those of us covering eastern europe knew that solidarity would win.
我們也知道這次和平的勝利將為集團內部其他國家所仿效。
we knew, too, that its peaceful victory would be a lesson for the rest of the bloc.
對於各地反共勢力來說，波蘭的選舉結果尤其令人鼓舞。
for anticommunists everywhere, the polish election was extraordinarily encouraging.
多虧有了波蘭的榜樣，僅僅在幾天前似乎還不可能的事突然之間變得可能了。
thanks to poland, what only days before had seemed impossible was, suddenly, possible.
此外還有其他的跡象。
there were other signs.
五月，匈牙利改革者開始拆掉奧匈邊境上的圍牆 — — 鐵幕終於被挖開了一個洞。
in may, hungarian reformers began tearing down the fence along their border with austria a hole in the iron curtain.
在莫斯科，米哈伊爾·戈爾巴喬夫提出建立共同的歐洲議會，不承認干涉主義者勃列日涅夫的教條。
in moscow, mikhail gorbachev spoke of a common european house and repudiated the interventionist brezhnev doctrine.
但當柏林牆倒塌的時候，專家和世界領袖們卻異口同聲。
yet when the wall tumbled down, experts and world leaders alike were unanimous.
他們承認“我們從來沒有想到 ” 。
we never saw it coming, they confessed.
冷戰持續的時間如此之長，以致於在自由真正破繭而出前變革似乎超出人們的想象。
the cold war had lasted so long that change seemed unimaginable until freedom burst forth.
捲起鋪蓋回家
bringing it all back home
巴黎—2008年爆發金融危機後，每隔一段時間，全球決策者就會拍手相慶，認為避免了20世紀30年代的政策失誤。
paris global policymakers regularly congratulate themselves on having avoided the policy errors of the 1930s during the financial crisis that began in 2008.
在大蕭條經濟史專家、美聯儲主席伯南克的領導下，他們牢記凱恩斯思想，放鬆貨幣和財政政策以避免最壞情形發生。
led by us federal reserve board chairman ben bernanke, an economic historian of the great depression, they remembered the ideas of john maynard keynes and loosened monetary and fiscal policy to avoid the worst.
我們至今仍在收拾預算爛攤子，特別是在歐洲。 但是，2008年確實沒有成為世界末日。
we are still coping with the budgetary consequences, especially in europe, but it is true that the world did not end in 2008.
貨幣緊縮並非20世紀30年代唯一的重大政策失誤；除此之外還有保護主義復燃 — — 以30年代伊始實行的斯穆特-霍利（Smoot-Hawley）關稅法案為典型代表。
monetary tightening was not the only major policy error of the 1930s so was a retreat into protectionism, symbolized by the smoothawley tariff increases at the beginning of that decade.
經濟史家仍然在為斯穆特-霍利法案本身的集中性爭辯不休，但隨之而來的關稅戰破壞了貿易和經濟增長，讓形勢雪上加霜。
historians continue to debate the centrality of the smoothawley law itself, but the subsequent tariff war certainly damaged trade and economic growth, making a bad situation worse.
如今，政客們還喜歡說，他們避免了保護主義錯誤，但果真是這樣嗎？
todays statesmen like to say that they have avoided the protectionist error as well, but is that true?
毫無疑問，我認為短期內絕不會發生關稅戰，但放眼未來，可以看到不少危險的貿易訊號。
certainly i do not expect a tariff war to break out in the near term, but there are dangerous indicators of trade trouble ahead.
全球自由貿易談判多哈回合已經告廢，世界貿易組織現在還在寄希望於日內瓦會議，但心懷惴惴焉。
the doha round of global freetrade talks has been abandoned, and the world trade organization is now languishing by the lake in geneva, uncertain of its future.
也許多哈回合照目前的形勢看不可能獲得什麼成果，但如果沒有後續世界貿易對話跟上 — — 至少也得有個可用的安全閥 — — 則將出現新的風險。
perhaps doha was unlikely to achieve much in the current circumstances, but the absence of any continuing dialogue on world trade at worst, a useful safety valve adds a new level of risk.
人們口頭上還在談判，但要指望能有多大實際動作已經不太現實。
while people are talking, they are less likely to act precipitately.
在金融方面，越來越多的跡象表明，各國各自為政實施監管和貨幣政策的時代要捲土重來了。
in the financial arena, there are many signs of a revival of nationalistic approaches to regulation and currency policy.
危機挑戰了華盛頓共識 — — 世界正在逐步走向資本自由流動和市場決定的匯率。
the crisis challenged the washington consensus, which assumed that the world was moving gradually towards free movement of capital and marketdetermined exchange rates.
不少國家 — — 包括巴西、韓國和土耳其 — — 已經實施了多種資本管制。
several countries including brazil, south korea, and turkey have now imposed capital controls of various kinds.
就連華盛頓共識的長期實踐者IMF也承認 ， “ 在某些情況下，資本管制是合理的資本流管理工具之一 ” 。
even the international monetary fund, long the embodiment of the washington consensus, has acknowledged that capital controls are a legitimate part of the toolkit to manage capital flows in certain circumstances.
美國國會認定中國是貨幣操縱國的典型例子，但瑞士也對瑞郎的波動上限有著嚴格控制。
american congressmen view the chinese as archetypal currency manipulators, but the swiss have introduced a firm cap on the francs appreciation.
金融市場的這些反全球化早期跡象也可以在商業銀行中找到，這群全球最大的金融機構中已有一些開始迅速收縮。
these early signs of deglobalization of financial markets have their parallels in commercial banking, with some of the biggest global institutions retrenching rapidly.
花旗銀行和滙豐銀行一直是全球化急先鋒；事實上，如今，只要你坐飛機，就一定會看到後者“全世界的本地銀行”的廣告語。
citibank and hsbc had gone further than most in developing a global footprint indeed, one can hardly get on a plane nowadays without being reminded that the latter is the worlds local bank.
但這兩家銀行正在關掉多個國家的業務。
but both are closing down in many countries.
與此類似，許多其他歐洲銀行也在大力削減海外業務。
likewise, many other european banks are cutting back their overseas business sharply.
貿易金融首當其衝 — — 在這方面，歐洲銀行一直是亞洲業務的主要參與者。
the impact is particularly vivid in trade finance, where european banks have been major participants in asia.
如今它們正在快速從亞洲市場撤出，導致亞洲銀行疲於奔命，尋找填補它們留下的要命空白的辦法。
now they are in rapid retreat from that market, creating a worrying gap that asian banks are seeking to fill.
到這裡還不算完。
there is more to come.
急於籌集新資本的歐洲銀行和保險公司可能將被迫出售海外資產。
as they struggle to raise new capital, european banks and insurers are likely to be forced to sell overseas assets.
如果這僅僅表明歐洲銀行轉向更專注的可靠長期戰略的新動向，那麼倒是可以被視為良性發展。
if this were simply a sign of a new, tighter focus on viable longterm strategies, it might be regarded it as a benign development.
但有跡象表明，之所以如此是受監管變化推動，其中不乏監管保護主義。
but there are indications that the process is being driven by regulatory change, and in some cases by regulatory protectionism.
銀行要受到註冊地“母國”監管者的監督，也要受到一系列業務所在地“東道國”監管者的監督。
banks are overseen by a home regulator in their country of incorporation, and by a series of host regulators where they operate.
“母國”監管者和最後貸款人越來越擔心它們海外業務的潛在風險損失敞口。
home regulators and lenders of last resort are increasingly worried about their potential exposure to losses in banks overseas operations.
英格蘭銀行行長默文·金犀利地指出 ， “ 銀行生在全球，死在祖國。
as mervyn king, the governor of the bank of england, acutely observed, banks are global in life, but national in death.
”換句話說，一旦出了簍子，還要靠母國當局去收拾殘局。
in other words, home authorities are left to pick up the tab when things go wrong.
東道國監管者則對那些透過母公司分支在其轄區內開展業務，但沒有本地資本或本地董事會的銀行越來越忌憚。
host regulators are increasingly nervous about banks that operate in their jurisdictions through branches of their corporate parent, without local capital or a local board of directors.
因此它們堅持要求子公司化。
so they are insisting on subsidiarization.
從銀行的角度來說，這意味著資本會被困在子公司，而無法在整個網路實現最優配置。
from the banks perspective, that means that capital is trapped in subsidiaries, and cannot be optimally used across its network.
因此銀行可能寧可選擇退出。
so banks may prefer to pull out instead.
歐盟就在上演��個橋段。
a particular version of this phenomenon is at work in the european union.
作為單一市場，銀行可以隨處吸收存款而不需要獲得地方批准，只要它們獲得了其中一個歐洲國家的授權。
in the single financial market, banks are allowed to take deposits anywhere, without local approval, if they are authorized to do so in one european country.
但在冰島銀行紛紛倒閉後，英國和荷蘭當局不得不出手拯救本地存款人。
yet when the icelandic banks failed, the british and dutch authorities had to bail out local depositors.
如今，監管者已開始抑制此類跨國業務，這導致了一個難聽的新名詞 — — “去歐元化 ” 。
now regulators are discouraging such crossborder business, leading to a process with the ugly new name of deeuroization.
我們只能寄希望於這不會成為一種時尚。
we can only hope that it does not catch on.
監管者已經意識到金融反全球化之勢加速的風險，開始尋找更好的應對全球銀行巨頭倒閉的良策。
regulators, recognizing the risks of allowing financial deglobalization to accelerate, have been seeking better means of handling the failure of huge global banks.
如果銀行在出問題時可以輕鬆解決，損失可以公平地分擔，那麼監管者可以更爽快地允許它們繼續在全球開展高效經營。
if banks can be wound up easily when things go wrong, with losses equitably distributed, regulators can more easily allow them to continue to operate globally and efficiently.
因此，建立跨國解決方案框架的重大努力正在進行中。
so a major effort to construct a crossborder resolution framework is under way.
但這項工作相當繁重，美聯儲官員塔魯羅（Daniel Tarullo）承認 ， “ 清晰完整的解決方案還沒有成型。 ”
but it is uphill work, and daniel tarullo, a governor of the federal reserve, has acknowledged that a clean and comprehensive solution is not in sight.
所有這些都會成為全球化好處的嚴重威脅嗎？
does all of this amount to a serious threat to the benefits of globalization?
謹慎的回答是現在還不好說。
the cautious answer would be that it is too early to say.
也許我們所看到的僅僅是衛兵交接儀式，花旗銀行和滙豐銀行的全球地位由中國工商銀行、巴西伊塔烏聯合銀行（Itau Unibanco ） 、 俄羅斯聯邦儲蓄銀行（Sberbank）取而代之。
perhaps we are just seeing the beginnings of a changing of the guard, and that hsbc and citibank will be replaced as global players by chinas icbc, brazils itau unibanco, or russias sberbank.
但也許我們正在目睹激進凱恩斯主義捲土重來 ： “ 思想、知識、科學 … … 理應天然是國際的。
but it may be that we are seeing a revival of a less benign keynesian doctrine ideas, knowledge, science....should of their nature be international.
但商品應該本地的，存在於合理和便利的地方，而金融，那應該是國家的。 ”
but let goods be homespun wherever it is reasonably and conveniently possible and, above all, let finance be national.
將英國帶到歐洲的核心之中
bringing the uk to europes core
布魯塞爾—目前歐盟的核心國家，除最初的6個創始國外，是組成歐洲貨幣聯盟的15個國家。
brussels the european unions core countries these days, besides the original six founders, are the 15 member states that make up the european monetary union.
這些國傢俱有趨同的經濟體系和共同的貨幣及財政政策。
they have converging economies and coordinated monetary and fiscal policies.
最大的外圍國家是英國。
the big outsider is the united kingdom.
仍然有許多人希望英國加入歐洲經濟貨幣聯盟。
british emu membership remains very desirable.
如果歐盟想要突破共同的經濟和貨幣政策的界限，在發展安全防衛政策的同時發展共同的外交政策，英國必須參與。
if the eu is to progress beyond the limits of a common economic and monetary policy and develop a defense and security policy along with a common foreign policy, the uk must be on board.
英鎊和歐元之間的匯率波動擾亂了歐盟成員國之間的市場力量，有時候甚至在倫敦造成了負面衝擊。
exchangerate fluctuations between sterling and the euro disturb market forces among member states, and at times even have a negative impact in london.
從長期來看，如果歐元區開始施加更大的影響力，英國就冒著嚴重的被孤立的風險。
in the long run, the uk risks serious isolation if the euro zone starts to exert even greater power.
但是，鑑於倫敦作為國際金融中心的重要地位以及英國和50多個英聯邦國家的特殊關係，其它歐洲國家也應該理解英國要求其擁有自己的貨幣的觀點。
but other european countries must also understand british arguments in favor of the uk maintaining its own currency, given londons importance as an international financial center as well as its privileged relations with more than 50 commonwealth countries.
因此，歐元區應該為英國提供一個體面的折衷方案，允許英國成為歐洲經濟貨幣聯盟的完全成員，加入其所有的機構 — — 例如歐洲中央銀行以及部長級的歐元集團，同時在英國和第三國家關係中可以繼續使用英鎊。
the euro zone should therefore offer the uk an honorable compromise in which britain would be allowed to become a full member of the emu and take a seat in all of its institutions like the european central bank and the ministerial eurogroup, while also being able to keep the pound in its relations with third countries.
但是，歐元應該和英鎊一起被作為英國以及英聯邦國家的法定貨幣，這需要英格蘭銀行和歐洲中央銀行間的緊密合作。
the euro would, however, have to be accepted as legal tender in the uk, alongside the pound, and in the commonwealth countries, and this would demand close cooperation between the bank of england and the ecb.
這樣的折衷方案可以增加歐洲經濟貨幣聯盟在歐洲以及歐洲以外地區的影響力。
such a compromise would increase the emus weight both inside and outside europe.
建立在這樣一個核心周圍的歐洲符合我所說的“土星模式 ” ， 在這個模式中，在中間是一個巨大的行星，周圍被環形環繞著，它們遲早會合而為一。
a europe built around such a core corresponds to what i call a saturn model, with a huge planet in the middle, surrounded by rings, converging sooner or later in the center.
在模式的外圍的是過渡時期的國家，與此同時，圍繞在中心周圍的環形是仍然拒絕加入歐洲經濟貨幣聯盟的歐盟國家，或者是像羅馬尼亞和保加利亞這樣尚未滿足所有條件的國家，或者是最終的西巴爾幹半島國家和土耳其。
the outer circles are the transition countries, while the rings around the center would be eu countries that still refuse to join the emu, or do not yet fulfill all the conditions, like romania and bulgaria, or eventually the western balkan countries and turkey.
土星模式將當前關於歐盟擴大和歐洲邊界的激烈爭論置於一個完全不同的背景，因為核心國家將發現它們不再被要求接受一個被分裂成為不同類別的成員國的歐洲。
the saturn model puts the present fierce debate on enlargement and the borders of europe into a totally different context, because the core countries would no longer find themselves being asked to accept a europe divided into different classes of member states.
處於圍繞著核心國家周圍的環形上的歐盟國家是暫時的，其目的是推進完全的融合。
the positioning of eu countries on the rings around the core would be transitory, with the aim being to facilitate overall convergence.
鑑於全球化以及諸如中國和印度這樣的國家潛在的競爭導致的直接的挑戰，歐洲經濟需要變得更有創新精神。
given the impact of globalization and the direct challenge to the eu implied by competition from countries like china and india, the european economy needs to become more innovative.
如果歐盟官方能夠協調遍及歐洲的經濟和社會改革政策，這些政策會變得更有力，並且，歐盟的擴大以及幾乎擁有5億消費者的內部市場的進一步發展，可以強有力地刺激經濟行為。
economic and social reform policies throughout europe would be strengthened if the eu authorities were able to coordinate them, and eu enlargement, together with the further development of its internal market of almost half a billion consumers, could powerfully stimulate economic activity.
20世紀80年代西班牙和葡萄牙的加入就是一個生動的例子，它也是對土耳其這樣一個人口眾多的國家加入歐盟這個問題應該考慮觀點。
the accession of spain and portugal was a vivid example of that in the 1980s, and it is an argument that should be considered with respect to such a populous country as turkey.
現在，歐洲逐漸一體化已經50年了，我們有理由期望進一步的洲際合作和一體化，尤其是因為科學和技術發展的影響。
europe has been unifying gradually for 50 years now, and we can reasonably look forward to further intercontinental cooperation and integration, not least because of scientific and technological developments.
同時，我們可以期待一個成長中的大西洋共同體，因為後續的貿易自由化談判使在歐盟和美國之間發展一個自由貿易區更加容易。
at the same time, we can expect a growing atlantic community as successive rounds of trade liberalization make it easier to develop a freetrade area between the eu and the united states.
歐洲自己的經驗告訴我們，關稅聯盟必須是發展自由貿易區的第一步，然後，關稅聯盟帶來的更緊密的經濟合作遲早會迫使其成員建立具有統一的內部市場一切特徵的經濟共同體。
europes own experience has taught us that a customs union must be the first step, and that sooner or later the more intense economic cooperation that a customs union imposes will compel its members to establish an economic community that has all the characteristics of a unified internal market.
但是，當然，這只有在其成員國之間的匯率波動被消除以後才能順利執行。
but, of course, this can only function smoothly if exchangerate fluctuations between its members currencies have been eliminated.
雖然大西洋貨幣聯盟（美國和歐盟之間的聯盟）是一個長期以來的期望，然而，它僅可以作為一個未來的宏大藍圖來考慮。
although an atlantic monetary union between the us and the eu is a longterm prospect, it should be considered as a grand design for the future.
現在，歐洲的領導人和他們的選民可以在過去的歐洲和未來的歐洲之間進行選擇。
europes leaders and their voting publics now have a choice between the europe of the past and of the future.
過去的歐洲以舒曼計劃開始，它為現在的歐盟播下了種子，並在冷戰結束的時候結束。
the europe of the past began with the schuman plan, which sowed the seeds of todays eu, and concluded when the cold war ended.
這是一個建立在推進戰後的德國和法國和解，建立一個和平的歐洲以及蘇聯擴張的威脅上的一體化時代。
it was an era of integration based on the heroic drive to reconcile postwar germany and france and establish a pax europea , as well as the threatened expansion of the soviet union.
但是，在共產主義垮臺之後，歐洲的情形多多少少發生了一些逆轉：對邊界的防衛劃分被在整個大陸消除國境所取代。
but after the implosion of communism, the situation in europe was more or less reversed the defensive demarcation of borders has been replaced by the removal of frontiers across the continent.
但是，雖然戴高樂將軍曾經提到將歐洲從大西洋擴大到烏拉爾，然而，僅僅用地理概念定義歐洲漏掉了“屬於”歐洲的含義的其它標準 — — 包括歐洲的社會模式以及其建立的價值標準。
however, while general de gaulle once spoke of a europe stretching from the atlantic to the urals, defining europe in purely geographical terms omits other criteria including the european social model and the scale of values on which it is based of what it means to belong to europe.
相反，在21世紀，歐洲的使命應該是成為逐步的洲際融合和統一的槓桿。
instead, the vocation of europe in the course of the twentyfirst century should be to become the lever of stepbystep intercontinental convergence and unification.
為此目的，歐洲必須進行徹底改造，而擴大歐洲經濟貨幣聯盟的範圍是一個正確的開端。
europe must be reinvented for this purpose, and broadening the emus reach is the right place to start.
英國：沒有痛苦就沒有收穫？
no pain, no gain for britain?
倫敦—經濟史學家尼爾·弗格森（Niall Ferguson）讓我想起已故的牛津歷史學家泰勒（A.J.P. Taylor ） 。
london the economic historian niall ferguson reminds me of the late oxford historian a.j.p. taylor.
儘管泰勒在其歷史寫作中堅持試圖述說真相，但他隨時準備出於好意採取春秋筆法。
though taylor maintained that he tried to tell the truth in his historical writing, he was quite ready to spin the facts for a good cause.
弗格森也是了不起的歷史學家 — — 但在進入政治領域時有些狂妄。
ferguson, too, is a wonderful historian but equally ready to spin when he shifts into political gear.
弗格森篤信美國新保守主義，同時他頑固地排斥凱恩斯和凱恩斯主義。
fergusons cause is american neoconservatism, coupled with a relentless aversion to keynes and keynesians.
最近，英國大選剛剛落下帷幕，他又開始為財政緊縮辯護，在為《金融時報》撰寫的文章中，他說 ， “ 工黨應該把失敗歸咎於凱恩斯。 ”
his latest defense of fiscal austerity came immediately after the united kingdoms recent election, when he wrote in the financial times that, labour should blame keynes for their defeat.
弗格森的觀點就像是殘酷不仁的嚴格執行者，認為受害者還活著就說明他的方法是可行的。
fergusons argument amounts to that of a brutal disciplinarian who claims vindication for his methods by pointing out that the victim is still alive.
他為英國財政大臣喬治·奧斯本（George Osborne）辯護，說英國經濟去年增長了2.6 % （ 是“G-7經濟體中表現組好的 ” ） ，但對奧斯本給經濟復甦過程中造成的傷害隻字不提。
in pleading on behalf of british chancellor of the exchequer george osborne, he points out that the uk economy grew by 2.6 last year the best performing of the g7 economies, but ignores the damage that osborne inflicted on the economy en route to this recovery.
如今，對於這一傷害已經達成了相當大的共識。
there is now much agreement about this damage.
由奧斯本設立、評估政府宏觀經濟表現的獨立機構預算責任辦公室（Office of Budget Responsibility）剛剛估算，從2010年到2012年，緊縮導致GDP增長下降2 % ， 2010年以來的累計損失相當於GDP的5 % 。
the office of budget responsibility, the independent agency set up by osborne to assess the governments macroeconomic performance, has just concluded that austerity reduced gdp growth by 2 from 2010 to 2012, bringing the cumulative cost of austerity since 2010 to 5 of gdp.
牛津大學的西蒙·任-劉易斯（Simon Wren-Lewis）估算該損失可能高達GDP的15 % 。
simon wrenlewis of oxford university estimates that the damage might be as high as 15 of gdp.
在宏觀經濟學中心（Centre for Macroeconomics）的最新英國經濟學家意見調查中，三分之二的受訪者同意緊縮傷害了英國經濟。
in a recent poll of british economists by the centre for macroeconomics, twothirds agreed that austerity had harmed the uk economy.
而且英國不是“一個人”在戰鬥。
moreover, britain is not alone.
在2012年10月的《世界經濟展望 》 （ World Economic Outlook）中，IMF承認“財政乘數被全世界所低估。
in its october 2012 world economic outlook, the imf admitted that, fiscal multipliers were underestimated across the world.
”用大白話說就是：預測者低估了閒置產能的程度，因此也低估了財政擴張可能帶來的產出增長。
in plain english the forecasters underestimated the extent of spare capacity and hence the scope for fiscal expansion to raise output.
這是無心之失嗎？
was it an honest mistake?
或者，這是因為預測者被暗示經濟處於充分就業狀態、財政擴張的唯一結果只能是通貨膨脹的經濟模型所迷惑了嗎？
or was it because the forecasters were in thrall to economic models that implied that economies were at full employment, in which case the only result of fiscal expansion would be inflation?
現在，他們已經有了更好的瞭解，弗格森現在也應該有了更好的瞭解。
they now know better, and ferguson should now know better as well.
弗格森的狂妄有一個令人沮喪的方面，那就是他根本沒有意識到大蕭條對政府表現和商業預期的影響。
a depressing aspect of fergusons interpretation is his failure to acknowledge the impact of the great recession on government performance and business expectations.
因此，他將2014年2.6%的增長率與2009年4.3%的衰退相比較。 他稱2009年時“工黨政府的最後一個整年 ” — —好像工黨的政策導致了增長崩潰似的。
thus, he compares 2.6 growth in 2014 with the 4.3 contraction in 2009, which he describes as the last full year of labour government as though labour policy produced the collapse in growth.
類似地 ， “ 自2010年5月以後 ， [ 信心]從未跌回戈登·布朗災難般的首相生涯的最後兩年的低位 ” — —好像是布朗政府的表現導致商業信心崩潰似的。
similarly, at no point after may 2010 did confidence sink back to where it had been throughout the last two years of gordon browns catastrophic premiership as though the brown governments performance caused business confidence to collapse.
把工黨選舉失利“歸咎凱恩斯”的說法尤其怪異。
the claim that keynes is to blame for labours election defeat is peculiarly odd.
畢竟，工黨領導層在選戰中用力最多之處乃是將工黨與一切凱恩斯主義“毒藥”劃清界限。
after all, the one thing labours leadership tried hardest to do in the campaign was to distance the party from any taint of keynesianism.
也許弗格森的意思是工黨與凱恩斯結盟的過去讓他們付出了代價 — — 用他的話說，就是“他們在金融危機之前和之中的災難性治國之道。 ”
perhaps ferguson meant that it was labours past association with keynes that had damned them their disastrous stewardship before and during the financial crisis, as he puts it.
事實上，工黨最新幾屆政府絕非凱恩斯主義者；貨幣政策的目標一��是2%的通脹，財政政策的目標一直是平衡整個商業週期的預算 — — 在衰退開始前，這是標準的宏觀經濟方針。
in fact, labours most recent governments were determinedly nonkeynesian monetary policy was geared to hitting a 2 inflation target, and fiscal policy aimed at balancing the budget over the business cycle standard macroeconomic fare before the recession struck.
對他們的治國之道的最嚴厲的指責是他們認為金融市場最好自我監管 — — 而這正是凱恩斯反對的。
the most damning charge against their stewardship is that they embraced the idea that financial markets are optimally selfregulating a view that keynes rejected.
凱恩斯不是工黨失敗的原因；從很大程度上說，蘇格蘭才是。
keynes was not to blame for labours defeat in large part, scotland was.
蘇格蘭民族黨（Scottish National Party）的大獲全勝導致工黨在該地區只獲得一席。
the scottish national partys crushing victory left labour with only one seat in the country.
毫無疑問，蘇格蘭民族黨之所以大獲全勝，原因有很多，但支援緊縮絕不在此列。
there are no doubt many reasons for the snps overwhelming triumph, but support for austerity is not one of them.
（保守黨和工黨做的一樣糟糕。 ）
the conservatives did as badly as labour.
蘇格蘭第一大臣、蘇格蘭民族黨領袖尼古拉·斯特金（Nicola Sturgeon）抨擊威斯敏斯特圍繞財政整合計劃的“愉快共識 ” 。
nicola sturgeon, first minister of scotland and leader of the snp, attacked the cozy consensus around fiscal consolidation in westminster.
她正確地指出，赤字是“經濟困難的表徵，而不僅是經濟困難的原因。
the deficit, she rightly said, was a symptom of economic difficulties, not just the cause of them.
”蘇格蘭民族黨的競選口號承諾“至少在全英國增加1,400億英鎊投資於技能和基礎設施。 ”
the snp manifesto promised at least an additional 140 billion 220 billion across the uk to invest in skills and infrastructure.
因此，如果蘇格蘭民族黨依靠“凱恩斯主義”財政擴張計劃取得如此出色的成績，那麼，認為工黨若更有力地為其自身執政記錄辯護、更積極地攻訐奧斯本的財政政策就會收到更好的效果豈非有理？
this is what leaders of the labour party like alistair darling, gordon browns chancellor of the exchequer, are now saying. but they seem to have had no influence on the two architects of labours election strategy, ed miliband and ed balls, both now removed from frontline politics.
保守黨的成功做成並且做得相當聰明的是說服英格蘭人民他們只是在“收拾工黨的爛攤子 ” ， 並且，要不是緊縮，英國將“是另一個希臘 ” — —而這正是弗格森的觀點。
what the conservatives did succeed in doing, and doing brilliantly, was to persuade english people that they were only cleaning up labours mess, and that, but for austerity, britain would have gone the way of greece exactly fergusons view.
你也許會認為，所有這些都是歷史：選民已經發話。
one might conclude that all of this is history the voters have spoken.
但接受保守黨的說辭為定音是一個錯誤。
but it would be a mistake to accept the conservative narrative as the last word.
從根本上，這是宣傳手段，沒有什麼支援，倒是有破壞性的實踐效果。
it is basically a tissue of propaganda, with little support in theory and destructive effects in practice.
如果換了一個政府，這也許不重要。
this might not matter so much had there been a change of government.
但奧斯本又回到了財政大臣的位子上，承諾在未來五年採取更嚴格的削減開支。
but osborne is back as chancellor, promising even tougher cuts over the next five years.
而拜德國所賜，財政緊縮也依然是歐元區主宰觀念。
and fiscal austerity is still the reigning doctrine in the eurozone, thanks to germany.
因此，傷害還會繼續。
so the damage is set to continue.
如果沒有令人信服的反駁，我們也許不得不目睹受害者到底能承受多少痛苦。
in the absence of a compelling counternarrative, we may be fated to find out just how much pain the victims can withstand.
站不住腳的英國理由
the eclipse of british reason
柏林— 當拉力過大時，鏈條會從最薄弱的一環斷起。
berlin when placed under too much strain, chains tend to break at the weakest link.
這形象地說明了歐盟的狀況。
figuratively speaking, the same applies to the european union.
因此，全世界都會非常自然地認為，如果歐盟開始分裂，最初一定從危機深重的南歐（其中又以希臘首當其衝）開始。
so the entire world quite naturally assumed that any process of eu disintegration would start primarily in the crisisridden european south greece, first and foremost.
但是，正如英國首相卡梅倫最近所指出的，歐洲之鏈的斷環極有可能不出現在最弱的一環，而出現在最不理智的一環。
but, as british prime minister david cameron has now demonstrated, the european chain is most likely to break not at its weakest link, but at its most irrational.
英國 — — 實用主義和現實主義的發軔地，一個有著驚人鎮定和適應性的國家，一個在成功對抗納粹德國、捍衛歐洲自由之後放棄帝國地位的國家 — — 如今正在迷失方向。
the united kingdom the homeland of pragmatism and realism, a country of unflappable principles and unmatched adaptability that stoically gave up its empire after successfully defending europes freedom against nazi germany has now lost its way.
更準確滴說，它是被保守黨意識形態幻象 — — 歐盟權力可以也應該回歸英國主權 — — 帶錯了路。
more precisely, it has been led astray by the conservative partys ideological fantasy that certain eu powers can and should be returned to british sovereignty.
英國的國家利益並未改變，歐盟的根本性變化也並不對英國國家利益構成威脅。
the uks national interests have not changed, and no fundamental shifts within the eu have worked against those interests.
改變的是英國的國內政治：首相太弱，鎮不住下議院約100人的反歐洲議員（稱之為“茶話會 ” （ High Tea Party ） ） ，而保守黨政府還擔心英國獨立黨的崛起，這會導致保守黨失去右翼選票，讓工黨在大選中佔先。
what has changed is britains domestic politics a prime minister too weak to control his roughly 100 antieuropean backbenchers call them the high tea party in the house of commons, and a conservative establishment wary of the uk independence partys rise, which could cost the tories enough votes on the right to give labour an electoral advantage.
卡梅倫說，他不願看到英國離開歐盟。
cameron claims that he does not want the uk to leave the eu.
但他的戰略 — — “重議”歐盟成員國資格，然後就新協議舉行英國全民公投 — — 是兩大幻覺的產物。 其一是他可以確保產生積極結果，其二是歐盟可以也願意給出他想要的讓步。
but his strategy renegotiation of eu membership, followed by a british referendum on the new agreement is the product of two illusions first, that he can ensure a positive outcome, and, second, that the eu is able and willing to give him the concessions that he wants.
事實上，有充分的理由認為，整個過程會按自己的邏輯發展，可能出現意料之外的英國退出歐盟的結果。
in fact, there is good reason to believe that such a course would take on a dynamic of its own, possibly leading to an unintended british exit from the eu.
這將是歐盟的一次嚴重退步；對英國來說，歷史表明這一結果將是名副其實的災難。
that would be a severe setback for the eu for the british, blundering through history, it would be a veritable disaster.
毫無疑問，脫離歐盟的英國也能生存，但生存質量如何就難說了。
while britain surely would survive outside the eu, the quality of its existence is another matter.
退出歐盟會嚴重損害英國的經濟利益，既失去了單一市場，也丟掉了倫敦的金融中心地位。
by exiting the eu, the uk would severely damage its economic interests, losing both the single market and londons role as a financial center.
退出歐盟也會危害英國的地緣政治利益，不僅包括其在歐洲的利益（諷刺的是，這方面它倒是支援歐盟擴張的 ） ， 也包括其在全世界的利益，其在全球事務中的地位以及其與美國的特殊關係（美國明確表示更希望看到歐洲英國 ） 。
an exit would also harm britains geopolitical interests, both in europe where, ironically, it favors eu enlargement and, worldwide, in its global standing and special relationship with the united states which has made clear its preference for a european uk.
不幸的是，卡梅倫的歐洲政治表現記錄實在無法激起人們對他獲得不同結果的信心。
unfortunately, camerons track record in european politics does not inspire confidence in his ability to manage a different outcome.
2009年，他下令保守黨MEP退出歐洲人民黨（European People’s Party，泛歐洲的中右翼政治勢力集團 ） ， 此舉剝奪了保守黨在歐洲議會的一切影響力，而保守黨現在已與派系主義者和反啟蒙主義者處在同一陣營中。
when, in 2009, he ordered the conservative meps to withdraw from the european peoples party, the europewide grouping of centerright political forces, he merely deprived the tories now consigned to sit with the sectarians and obscurantists of any influence in the european parliament.
他削弱了英國在歐盟的地位，最終加重了黨內對歐元的疑慮
by weakening the uks position within the eu, he ended up strengthening the euroskeptics within his party.
但是，儘管卡梅倫應該知道慘痛的教訓，卻仍拋棄了理智的思路。
but, while cameron should know from grim experience what is looming, it seems that he has abandoned rational considerations.
事實上，認為歐盟會重議英國的成員資格條件 — — 這意味著德國不會反對 — — 簡直是白日做夢。
indeed, the belief that the eu would renegotiate britains membership terms which assumes, further, that germany would not object borders on magical thinking.
如此先河將被其他成員國所援引，從而意味著歐盟的末日。
such a precedent would be applicable to the other member states, which would mean the end of the eu.
儘管英國德高望重，但為了繼續其成員資格而解散歐盟實在太過荒謬。
with all due respect to the uk, dismantling the eu as the price of its continued membership is an absurd idea.
卡梅倫應該認識到，他的戰略是不可能實現的（即使他擔心對條約修飾性的修改無助於他在國內的處境 ） 。
cameron should recognize that his strategy cannot be allowed even if he fears that a few cosmetic corrections to the treaty wont help him at home.
與此同時，如果保守黨想將此作為重議眾多歐洲條約的第一步，那麼他們將有可能失去解決一個關鍵問題 — — 改革歐元區和非歐元區歐盟成員國關係 — — 的機會。
in the meantime, the tories risk losing their way on a crucial issue reform of the relationship between the eurozone and noneuro eu members if they try to use it as leverage to renegotiate the various european treaties.
英國知道，歐元的生存需要更緊密的政治一體化，也知道作為金融中心的倫敦之於英國就像核工業之於法國、汽車工業之於德國，若是歐元崩潰，將受到嚴重損害。
britain knows that the euros survival requires much closer political integration, and also that londons role as a financial center as important for the uk as the nuclear industry is for france and the auto industry is for germany would be greatly damaged if the euro should fail.
儘管沒人會期待英國在不久的將來加入歐元區，但歐盟內部的政治領導力需要明智地考量一國本身的核心利益和其他成員國的核心利益，不能把目光集中在威脅上。
although no one should expect the british to join the euro any time soon, political leadership within the eu requires the acumen to take account of the central interests of ones own country and those of the other member states without indulging in threats.
但是，這又要求充分理解這些利益，並願意在互惠基礎上合作，而這在歐洲大家庭中應是理所當然之事。
this, however, requires an adequate understanding of those interests and a willingness to cooperate on the basis of mutual trust, which should be a given within the european family.
說辭，特別是來自大國領導人的說辭，可能有用，可能不切題，也可能有害。
speeches, particularly when delivered by leaders of great nations, can be useful, irrelevant, or dangerous.
卡梅倫醞釀已久的關於歐洲的講話被一再打斷。
camerons longplanned speech on europe was postponed time and again.
也許他應該將這作為反思其立場的訊號。
perhaps he should have taken that as a sign that he should rethink his position.
他還可以這樣做，再不做就晚了。
he still can, before it is too late.
最佳起點是重讀一下丘吉爾1946年在蘇黎世的著名演講。
the best starting point would be a rereading of winston churchills famous speech in zurich in 1946.
“我們必須建設一個歐羅巴合眾國 ， ” 英國20世紀最偉大首相如是說。
we must build a kind of united states of europe, urged britains greatest twentiethcentury statesman.
如今，這仍然是我們 — — 也是英國 — — 的任務。
that remains our task and britains to this day.
英國如何改變退歐思維
how britain could change its mind about brexit
倫敦—2018年會成為英國改變脫離歐盟思維的一年嗎？
london will 2018 be the year when the united kingdom changes its mind about leaving the european union?
傳統智慧說，停止退歐是不可能的。
conventional wisdom says that stopping brexit is impossible.
但傳統智慧對特朗普怎麼說？
but what did conventional wisdom say about donald trump?
馬克龍呢？
or emmanuel macron?
或者，一開始的退歐公投呢？
or, for that matter, the original brexit referendum?
在革命年代，事件可以從不可能跨越未必能，直接變成不可免。
in revolutionary times, events can go from impossible to inevitable without ever passing through improbable.
英國退歐就是一起這樣的事件，它的逆轉則有可能是另一起這樣的事件。
brexit was such an event, and its reversal could be another.
問問尼格爾·法拉奇（Nigel Farage ） 。 他是英國獨立黨（UK Independence Party）前領導人，他突然說，2016年6月的英國退歐公投可以推翻。
just ask nigel farage, the former uk independence party leader, who has suddenly said that the june 2016 brexit referendum could be overturned.
“留歐陣營遙遙領先 ， ” 法拉奇在這個週末警告他的強硬退歐派同志們。
the remain side are making all the running, farage warned his fellow hardline leavers this weekend.
“他們在議會中是大多數，除非我們自己也組織起來，否則我們將失去英國退歐這一歷史性勝利。 ”
they have a majority in parliament, and unless we get ourselves organized we could lose the historic victory that was brexit.
投票給英國退歐和特朗普，這樣的現象在今天常常被描述為是不平等和全球化等深刻社會經濟因素的不可避免的結果。
the votes for brexit and trump are often described today as an ineluctable result of deep socioeconomic factors like inequality or globalization.
從某些角度講，這一描述是對的。
in some ways, this description is right.
2008年經濟危機後，發生某些形式的政治劇變是意料中事，我多年來一直這樣認為。
political upheavals of some kind were to be expected after the 2008 economic crisis, as i have argued for years.
但具體發生的劇變，完全不是不可避免的。
but there was nothing inevitable about the specific upheavals that happened.
和特朗普一樣，英國退歐是選民行為出現小波動的偶然結果。
brexit, like trump, was a contingent outcome of small perturbations in voter behavior.
只要1.8%的英國人投出不同的票，英國退歐現在早已是一個被忘卻的笑話。
if just 1.8 of britons voted differently, brexit would now be a forgotten jokeword.
如果希拉里·克林頓（Hillary Clinton）所多贏的三百萬張選票能夠在各州之間分佈得略有不同 ， “ 特朗普總統”現在也將和2016年1月時一樣可笑。
if hillary clintons popular majority of three million votes was distributed slightly differently among the states, the phrase president trump would be as laughable today as it was in january 2016.
要想在新的一年裡阻止英國退歐，需要發生四個類似的略微的行為變化。
to stop brexit in the year ahead, four similarly modest shifts in behavior need to happen.
公共觀點必須略微更加反對退歐決定。 目前，認為它“事後看來是個錯誤”的人要比不那麼認為的人多4 % 。
public opinion must shift slightly further against the brexit decision, which is already viewed as wrong in hindsight by a 4 point margin.
私下裡反對英國退歐的政客必須公開說出來。
politicians who privately detest brexit must speak out publicly.
理性反對政府政策必須再次被認為是民主的標誌，而不是叛國行為。
reasoned opposition to government policies must be recognized again as a hallmark of democracy, not an act of treason.
英國退歐不可避免的觀點必須消除乾淨。
and the sense that brexit is inevitable must be dispelled.
這些要求是相輔相成的關係。
these requirements are interdependent.
只有當政客感到公共觀點有所改變時，才會公開發聲；但公共觀點只有在可信的政治領導下，才會發生改變。
politicians will speak out only if they sense public opinion shifting but public opinion will shift only with credible political leadership.
如果所有的反對都被打上反民主的標籤，那麼政客就會三緘其口。
politicians are cowed into silence if all opposition is branded as antidemocratic.
而如果英國退歐看起來不可避免的話，為什麼選民還要重新思考這個問題?
and if brexit appears inevitable, why should voters bother to think again?
民意調查和焦點小組表明，不可避免感是逆轉退歐決定的最重要的障礙。
the sense of inevitability, opinion polls and focus groups show, is the most important obstacle to a reversal.
大約30%的英國選民堅決反對歐盟，他們永遠都是脫離歐盟的支持者，不管這回帶來多大的經濟代價，正如特朗普的“票倉”永遠都會支援“他們的”總統，不管他的行為如何。
about 30 of british voters oppose the eu so passionately that they will always back leaving, regardless of the economic costs, just as trumps base will always support their president regardless of how he behaves.
但只要這些死硬疑歐派無法贏得對歐洲不太在乎，當將公投視為抗議投票的20%選民，他們就無法贏得多數。
but these diehard euroskeptics would never have won a majority without some 20 of voters who cared little about europe, but treated the referendum as a protest vote.
如今，這些立場並不太堅定的選民中有很多驚愕於退歐讓人們的注意力從他們真正的怨恨物件 — — 醫療、不平等性、低工資、住房和其他問題 — — 上轉移開去。
many of these lowconviction voters are now dismayed that brexit has distracted attention from their real grievances about health, inequality, low wages, housing, and other issues.
但正是出於這一原因，他們想要不可避免的退歐儘快發生，以使國家可以回到常規軌道上來。
yet, for this very reason, they want the inevitable departure from europe to happen as quickly as possible so that the country can get back to business as usual.
現在，假設這些選民看是相信，英國退歐遠非不可避免，倒有可能永遠不會發生。
now suppose these voters began to believe that brexit, far from being inevitable, might never happen.
他們會要求政客“停止在歐洲問題上喋喋不休 ” ， 開始解決人民真正的擔憂。
they would demand that politicians should stop banging on about europe and start dealing with the peoples real concerns.
不可避免感可能因為最近在保守黨政府和工黨反對派內部政治局面的改變而消失。
the sense of inevitability could be dispelled by recent shifts in the internal politics of both the conservative government and the labour opposition.
工黨已經開始認識到，其唯一的重掌權力之路便是反對英國退歐。
labour has begun to realize that its only possible route back to power is by opposing brexit.
2017年選舉結果的詳細分析表明明，工黨出人意料的勝利幾乎完全可以歸因於出於希望“攪黃”英國退歐動機的富裕年輕選民。
detailed analysis of the 2017 election returns has shown that labours unexpected gains were due almost entirely to affluent young voters whose motivation was the hope of derailing brexit.
如果不是這些反對退歐的選民，首相梅可能將贏得被廣泛預測的一邊倒的大勝。
had it not been for these antibrexit voters, prime minister theresa may would have won the widely predicted landslide.
如果工黨黨魁傑里米·科爾賓（Jeremy Corbyn）現在成為“英國退歐侍女 ” — —布萊爾令人印象深刻的用詞 — — 不進行有效的反對，那麼這些新選民會感到遭到了背叛，工黨也將分裂為馬克思主義者和中間派，其贏得大選的希望將付之東流。
if jeremy corbyn, the labour leader, now becomes the handmaiden of brexit, in tony blairs memorable phrase, by shying away from effective opposition, these new voters will feel betrayed, the party will split between the marxists and centrists, and its hopes of ever winning a general election will be dashed.
另一方面，如果工黨決定要挑戰英國退歐，公共觀點將迅速轉變。
if, on the other hand, labour decided to fight brexit, public opinion would rapidly shift.
反對退歐將開始被認為是民主政治的自然結果。
opposition to brexit would start to be treated as a natural feature of democratic politics.
工黨將開始從政府的談判失誤中受益。
labour would start to benefit from the governments negotiating blunders.
英國退歐的不可避免感也將消失。
and the sense of brexits inevitability would vanish.
這反過來將給予親歐保守黨以勇氣。
that, in turn, would give courage to proeuropean conservatives.
如果因為工黨不高舉反對大旗而導致政府無論如何都會勝出，那麼保守黨議員就不可能反對本黨領導層。
tory mps are unlikely to vote against their party leadership if the absence of labour opposition allows the government to win anyway.
但如果工黨的一致反對創造了阻止退歐的真正的可能性，那麼將國家利益置於當派忠誠之前的保守黨議員就會因為勇氣而被歌頌，而不會因為愚蠢而被取笑。
if, however, concerted opposition from labour created a genuine possibility of stopping brexit, tory mps who put national interest ahead of party loyalty would find themselves praised for their mettle, not ridiculed for folly.
他們甚至會覺得，如果本黨與歐洲形成妥協，自己的職業生涯也會就此添彩。
they might even calculate that their own careers would prosper if their party reconciled itself to europe.
這一系列連鎖事件似乎正在啟動。
this chain of events now seems to be starting.
12月，梅輸掉了第一場重要的退歐戰役，工黨議員聯合12位保守黨叛徒透過了一份修正案，要求一切與歐盟談成的協議都需要國會法案批准。
in december, may lost her first important brexit battle, when labour mps united with 12 tory rebels to pass an amendment requiring a specific act of parliament to approve whatever deal is negotiated with the eu.
這意味著任何引起嚴重反對的退歐計劃 — — 不管是來自強硬民族主義者還是來自親歐保守黨 — — 都可以用來觸發新的公投。
this means that any brexit plan that arouses serious opposition, either from hardline nationalists or from proeuropean tories, could be used to trigger a new referendum.
隨著這一突破，第一波明確以阻止退歐為目標，而不僅僅是以透過“軟”分手協議來降低傷害為目標的嚴肅的跨黨派行動將在本月晚些時候發動。
following this breakthrough, the first serious crossparty campaign explicitly aiming to stop brexit, and not merely to mitigate damage by seeking a softer divorce deal, will be launched later this month.
要想獲得成功，這次行動需要說服幻滅的留歐派，退歐不是不可避免的。
to succeed, this campaign will need to persuade disillusioned remainers that brexit is not inevitable.
這次行動需要向抗議選民證明，不管他們的問題是什麼，退歐都不是答案。
it will need to show protest voters that whatever their problems, brexit is not the answer.
這次行動需要說服工黨政客，參與退歐合謀就是選舉自殺，還要說如親歐盟的保守黨叛徒，背叛不是徒勞。
it will need to convince labour politicians that collaboration with brexit is electoral suicide, and persuade proeu tory rebels that a rebellion would not be futile.
最後，這次行動需要歐洲領導人毫不含糊地宣告，英國有改變退歐想法的合法權利。
finally, it will need european leaders to state unequivocally that britain is legally entitled to change its mind about leaving.
這些要求非常具有挑戰性，但並非不可能。
these requirements are challenging, but not impossible.
大衛·戴維斯（David Davis）是一位支援退歐的保守黨，他目前主持著英國的退歐談判。 他曾經說 ， “ 如果民主不能改變思維，那麼它就不再是民主。
david davis, the probrexit tory who is now leading the uks brexit negotiations, once said that, if a democracy cannot change its mind, it ceases to be a democracy.
”英國仍然是一個民主國家，並且它仍然可以改變退歐思維。
britain is still a democracy, and it can still change its mind about brexit.
英國日益加深的迷茫
britains deepening confusion
倫敦 — “ 受夠了 ， ” 這是英國首相梅在倫敦橋恐怖襲擊後的宣告。
london enough is enough, proclaimed british prime minister theresa may after the terrorist attack on london bridge.
現在，形勢已經清楚，近一半在6月8日的英國大選中投票的人受夠了梅。 梅的保守黨多數地位也在選舉中消失殆盡，結果是形成了一個懸浮議會（任何政黨都沒能獲得多數 ） 。
now, it is clear, almost half of those who voted in the united kingdoms general election on june 8 have had enough of may, whose conservative majority was wiped out at the polls, producing a hung parliament with no majority for any party.
不管是“受夠了移民 ” ， 還是“受夠了緊縮 ” ， 英國選民顯然是受夠了很多事情。
whether it is enough immigrants or enough austerity, britains voters certainly have had enough of a lot.
但大選讓英國陷入了迷茫的分歧。
but the election has left britain confusingly split.
去年的英國脫歐公投表明英國存在留在歐盟-離開歐盟分歧，脫歐派略勝一籌。
last years brexit referendum on european union membership suggested a leaveremain divide, with the brexiteers narrowly ahead.
今年的大選則在這層分歧之上又加上了更加傳統的左右分歧，捲土重來的工黨利用了選民對保守黨削減預算政策的不滿。
this years general election superimposed on this a more traditional leftright split, with a resurgent labour party capitalizing on voter discontent with conservative budget cuts.
要理解由此造成的政治局面，可以想象一個田字格，四個象限分別由留歐和預算削減派、留歐和經濟擴張派、脫歐和預算削減派以及脫歐和經濟擴張派組成。
to see the resulting political terrain, imagine a twobytwo table, with the four quadrants occupied by remainers and budget cutters remainers and economic expansionists brexiteers and budget cutters and brexiteers and economic expansionists.
這四個象限無法疊加形成一致的兩個半邊，因此，很難搞清楚選民是在給哪個陣營投票。
the four quadrants dont add up to coherent halves, so its not possible to make out what voters thought they were voting for.
但可以看出選民拒絕了什麼。
but it is possible to make out what voters were rejecting.
有兩件確定的事情。
there are two certain casualties.
一是緊縮。 即使是保守黨，也表示會放棄緊縮政策。
the first is austerity, which even the conservatives have signaled they will abandon.
削減公共支出以平衡預算是基於錯誤的理論，並且在實踐中也已經失敗。
cutting public spending to balance the budget was based on the wrong theory and has failed in practice.
最能說明問題的跡象便是2010—2016年間擔任財政大臣的喬治·奧斯本（George Osborne）無法實現任何預算目標。
the most telling indicator was the inability of george osborne, chancellor of the exchequer from 2010 to 2016, to achieve any of his budget targets.
赤字應該在2015年消失，然後推遲到2017年，然後再度推遲到2020—2021年。
the deficit was to have vanished by 2015, then by 2017, then by 20202021.
如今，政府幹脆不再承諾任何日期了。
now, no government will commit to any date at all.
這些目標是基於一個概念 ： “ 可信”的赤字學見計劃將帶來足夠的商業信心，克服對削減政策本身的抑制效應。
the targets were based on the idea that a credible deficitreduction program would create sufficient business confidence to overcome the depressing effects on activity of the cuts themselves.
有人說，這些目標從來都不夠可信。
some say the targets were never credible enough.
真相是它們永遠不可能可信：赤字只有在經濟增長時才會減少，而削減預算，不管是真正的發生的還是預料中的，都會阻礙增長。
the truth is that they never could be the deficit cannot come down unless the economy grows, and budget cuts, real and anticipated, hinder growth.
現在的共識是，緊縮將復甦推遲了近三年，抑制了真實收入，也導致地方政府、醫療和教育等關鍵公共服務遭到嚴重拖累。
the consensus now is that austerity delayed recovery for almost three years, depressing real earnings and leaving key public services like local government, health care, and education palpably damaged.
因此，就等著荒謬地咬定平衡預算不放鬆的做法破產吧。
so expect the ridiculous obsession with balancing the budget to be scrapped.
從現在開始，赤字將根據經濟狀態調整。
from now on, the deficit will be left to adjust to the state of the economy.
第二件被拒絕的事情是不受限制的歐盟移民。
the second casualty is unrestricted immigration from the eu.
脫歐派要求“控制我們的國境 ” ， 這一口號被導向了來自東歐的經濟移民流入。
the brexiteers demand to control our borders was directed against the uncontrolled influx of economic migrants from eastern europe.
這一要求必須以某種形式得到滿足。
this demand will have to be met in some way.
當歐盟主要由西歐組成時，歐洲內部的移民問題可以忽略不計。
migration within europe was negligible when the eu was mainly west european.
而當歐盟開始將工資較低的前共產主義國家納入時，情況開始改變。
this changed when the eu began incorporating the lowwage excommunist countries.
隨後到來的移民緩解了 英國和德國等國家的勞動力短缺問題，也增加了移民本身的收入。
the ensuing migration eased labor shortages in host countries like the uk and germany, and increased the earnings of the migrants themselves.
但這些收益並不適用於不受限制的 移民。
but such benefits do not apply to unrestricted migration.
哈佛大學的喬治·波爾加斯（George J. Borjas）和其他人的研究表明，淨移民流入降低了競爭性本國勞動力的工資。
studies by harvard universitys george j. borjas and others suggest that net immigration lowers the wages of competing domestic labor.
波爾加斯最著名的發現表明 ， “ 馬裡艾爾人 ” — —1980年大規模集體 移民到邁阿密的古巴人 — — 對當地工作階級工資造成了抑制效應。
borjass most famous study shows the depressive impact of marielitos cubans who immigrated en masse to miami in 1980 on domestic workingclass wages.
這些擔憂長期以來一直是主權國家堅持移民管控權利的基礎。
these fears have long underpinned sovereign states insistence on the right to control immigration.
對管控的支援在東道國存在勞動力盈餘時更加強大，2008年危機以來的西歐大部就是如此。
the case for control is strengthened when host countries have a labor surplus, as has been true of much of western europe since the crisis of 2008.
支援脫歐實質上可以說就是要求回覆對英國國境的主權。
support for brexit is essentially a demand for the restoration of sovereignty over the uks borders.
這一問題的癥結在於它的政治遺產。
the crux of the issue is political legitimacy.
進入現代以前，市場基本上是本地性質，對外部人士基本關閉，哪怕是相鄰的城鎮。
until modern times, markets were largely local, and heavily protected against outsiders, even from neighboring towns.
國家市場直到現代國家出現之後才開始形成。
national markets were achieved only with the advent of modern states.
但商品、資本和勞動力在主權國家內部完全不受限制的流動需要滿足兩個條件才能成為可能：國家身份的發展，以及出現有能力在出現不利局面時提供安全的國家機關。
but the completely unrestricted movement of goods, capital, and labor within sovereign states became possible only when two conditions were met the growth of national identity and the emergence of national authorities able to provide security in the face of adversity.
這兩個條件歐盟一個都不滿足。
the european union fulfills neither condition.
歐洲人民首先是民族國家的公民。
its peoples are citizens of their nationstates first.
公民與國家之間的契約，即國家經濟的基石，無法在歐洲層面複製，因為不存在可以與之達成這個協議的歐洲國。
and the contract between citizens and states on which national economies depend cannot be reproduced at the european level, because there is no european state with which to conclude the deal.
歐盟堅持將勞動力的自由流動作為非國家成員資格的條件很不成熟。
the eus insistence on free movement of labor as a condition of membership of a nonstate is premature, at best.
這應該成為整個歐盟的規定，而不僅僅是英國脫歐協議的一部分。
it will need to be qualified, not just as part of the uks brexit deal, but for the whole of the eu.
那麼，英國大選的混亂結果會如何發展？
so how will the shambolic results of the british general election play out?
梅的首相是做不長了。
may will not last long as prime minister.
奧斯本已經說她是“女活死人 ” （ 當然，他沒有承認他的緊縮政策也是梅黯然失色的幫兇 ） 。
osborne has called her a dead woman walking of course without acknowledging that his austerity policies helped to seal her demise.
最明智的結果目前絕不可能達成：保守黨-工黨聯合政府 ， （ 比如）約翰·鮑里斯（John Boris）當首相，傑里米·科爾賓（Jeremy Corbyn）當副首相。
the most sensible outcome is currently a political nonstarter a conservativelabour coalition government, with say boris johnson as prime minister and jeremy corbyn as his deputy.
政府實施一個只包含兩項內容的兩年計劃：完成與歐盟的“軟”脫歐協議，以及在住房、基礎設施和綠色能源方面大量進行公共投資。
the government would adopt a twoyear program consisting of only two items the conclusion of a soft brexit deal with the eu and a big public investment program in housing, infrastructure, and green energy.
投資計劃的出發點是漲潮可以讓所有船都浮起來。
the rationale for the investment program is that a rising tide will lift all boats.
經濟繁榮還有一個額外的好處，就是對移民的敵意會有所減弱，於是英國可以更容易地談判明智的移民流管控政策。
and an added benefit of a thriving economy will be lower hostility to immigration, making it easier for britain to negotiate sensible regulation of migrant flows.
誰知道呢：如果談判迫使歐盟修改其自身的勞動力自由移動承諾，那麼英國脫歐將不再僅僅是英國從歐洲退出，而更像是歐盟資格條件的大修。
and who knows if the negotiations force the eu to recast its own commitment to free labor movement, brexit may turn out to be a matter less of british exit than of an overhaul of the terms of european membership.
脆弱的英國
brittle britain
倫敦—在未來一年中，哪個歐洲國家面臨最大的政治動盪和金融混亂風險？
london which european country faces the greatest risk of political instability and financial turmoil in the year ahead?
在5月7日英國大選還有不到一週之際，答案既明顯又令人震驚。
with less than a week to go before the british general election on may 7, the answer is both obvious and surprising.
作為曾經歐元危機中的政治和經濟穩定的避風港，英國即將成為歐盟政治局面最難預測的成員國。
once a haven of political and economic stability amid the turmoil of the euro crisis, the united kingdom is about to become the european unions most politically unpredictable member.
事實上，連續性幾乎可以確定從選舉結果中排除。
indeed, continuity is the one election outcome that can almost certainly be excluded.
除非民調結果出現英國歷史上最大程度的不準確性，否則組成執政聯盟的兩黨 — — 首相卡梅倫的保守黨和自由民主黨 — — 幾乎不可能贏得聯合議會多數席位。
unless opinion polls are inaccurate to a degree unprecedented in british history, the two parties comprising the government coalition, prime minister david camerons conservatives and the liberal democrats, have almost no chance of winning a combined parliamentary majority.
一個可能性 — — 根據民調結果，這一可能性略高於50 % — —是英國，撒切爾主義的誕生地和歐盟新自由主義經濟學的旗幟，很快就會出現一個決心實施自20世紀70年代以來最大增稅計劃的工黨政府。
one possibility with a probability slightly above 50 according to the polls is that britain, the birthplace of thatcherism and the eus standardbearer of neoliberal economics, will soon have a labourled government committed to the biggest taxraising program since the 1970s.
此外，拜英國選舉制度的特殊性和蘇格蘭和威爾士民族主義的興起所賜，工黨政府能否生存下去取決於經濟日程更加激進、以分裂英國為目標的政黨的支援。
moreover, because of the peculiarities of the british electoral system and the rise of scottish and welsh nationalism, a labour governments survival would depend on the support of parties with even more radical economic agendas and dedicated to dismantling the uk.
另一個情景 — — 與工黨領導的執政聯盟情形可能性幾乎相當 — — 是弱勢且不穩定的保守黨政府。
another scenario almost as probable as a labourled coalition is a weak and unstable conservative government.
從民調結果看，卡梅倫的最大希望是贏得比工黨更多的議會席位，然後試圖組建少數派政府，主要其他政黨不聯合起來反對，就能繼續執政。
to judge by the opinion polls, camerons best hope is to win more parliamentary seats than labour and try to form a minority government, which could survive as long as the other parties failed to unite against it.
這也許是可能的，因為自由民主黨和蘇格蘭民族黨（Scottish Nationalist Party）也許認為允許弱勢的保守黨政府上臺有利可圖，至少暫時如此。
this might be possible, because the liberal democrats and scottish nationalist party may see benefits in allowing a weak conservative government to remain in power, at least for a while.
但少數派保守黨政府會帶來更多不確定性和風險。
but a minority conservative government would create additional uncertainties and risks.
卡梅倫將比其他所有戰後英國領導人都更容易受到本黨異見派和極端分子的要挾，後兩者把讓英國退出歐盟視為自己的歷史使命。
cameron would be more vulnerable than any leader in postwar british history to blackmail by his own partys dissidents and extremists, who see it as their historic mission to pull britain out of the eu.
而少數派政府也將無法透過任何蘇格蘭民族黨反對的爭議立法。
and a minority government would be unable to pass any controversial legislation that the scottish nationalists opposed.
此外，英國政治制度也將無以為繼。
moreover, britains political institutions might be unable to cope.
英國的不成文憲法完全基於傳統和先例。
the uks unwritten constitution is based entirely on tradition and precedent.
這一安排永遠需要以擁有明確權力的強勢政府為前提。
that arrangement has always presupposed strong governments with clear mandates.
憲法極不適應聯合政府和少數派政府，一些法律學者甚至質疑，如果政府不出幾周或幾個月就會被推翻，那麼女王是否應該宣佈議會代表“她的”新政府？
the constitution is so poorly adapted to coalitions and minority governments that some legal scholars question whether the queen should address parliament on behalf of her new government if there is a risk that it will be toppled within a few weeks or months.
此外，儘管選舉算術意味著穩定的中間道路政府 — — 能夠保持英國當前的稅收、經濟管理和歐洲政策的政府 — — 幾乎不可能出現，但連續性仍是大部分國際商界領袖和政客所期待的結果。
and yet, although the electoral arithmetic makes a stable centrist government one that could maintain britains current policies on taxes, economic management, and europe almost impossible to imagine, continuity is the outcome that most international business leaders and politicians seem to expect.
關於這一點，最明顯的證據要數金融市場。
the clearest evidence of this can be seen in financial markets.
儘管英鎊匯率自去年9月的合1.70美元貶值了大約10 % ， 但這完全是美元強勢的結果。
although the pound has declined by about 10 from its peak of 1.70 last september, sterling weakness has simply reflected the dollars strength.
與此同時，英鎊對歐元升值了近10 % ， 而英國股價正處於歷史最高水平，英國政府債券的回報也高於美國、德國和日本。
in the same period, sterling has risen almost 10 against the euro, while british share prices have hit alltime highs and government bonds have generated better returns in britain than in the united states, germany, or japan.
什麼造成了這一對即將到來的英國政府風險的漠視 — — 在歐洲政客之間顯然也是如此？
what accounts for this apparent indifference also evident among european politicians to the looming political risks in britain?
許多國際觀察家認為政治早已不在英國佔據重要地位，因為經濟基本面良好，增長率相當健康。
many international observers believe that politics simply no longer matters much in britain, because the economy is fundamentally sound and growing at a fairly healthy pace.
但這是一種非常危險的自滿觀點。
but this is a dangerously complacent argument.
是的，2014年英國經濟增長為主要經合組織國家中最快的，失業率也只有歐盟平均水平的一半。
yes, britain recorded the fastest economic growth among the major oecd countries in 2014 and has an unemployment rate of only half the eu average.
但這些有利指標掩蓋了一個巨大的風險源：世界首屈一指的外部赤字，去年這一赤字透過總額高達1,600億美元的外部資本流入填補。
but these favorable indicators obscure a source of enormous risk one of the worlds largest external deficits, financed last year by foreigncapital inflows totaling 160 billion.
經常專案缺口相當於GDP的5.5 % ， 目前為主要經合組織國家最高，這一水平也是金融危機爆發以來長期存在的水平 — — 英國和其他國家都是如此。
the currentaccount gap, at 5.5 of gdp, is by far the highest among the major oecd countries and is at a level long associated both in the uk and elsewhere with the onset of financial crises.
只要英國身為政治穩定的安全港並且稅收政策有利於外國投資者，就不會出現吸引資本流入的問題。
as long as britain was a haven of political stability and tax policies favorable to foreign investors, it had no problem attracting capital inflows.
但英國政壇及其與歐盟關係即將發生的改變必然會引起人們關注英國經濟對外部融資的極端依賴。
but the impending shifts in britains politics and its eu relations are bound to draw attention to the economys extreme dependence on foreign finance.
工黨政府有一套專門用來對付私人外國投資者的稅收計劃，該計劃必定會影響資本流入。
a labour government, wielding tax proposals specifically designed to hit private foreign investors, would certainly discourage inflows.
但國際投資者也許同樣會因為“恐歐派”把持的弱勢保守黨政府而感到沮喪。
but international investors might be equally put off by a weak conservative government dominated by the partys europhobe wing.
無論如何，GDP增長都會隨商業信心、消費和房價的不振 — — 或者因為工黨的新稅收政策，或者因為保守黨帶來的歐盟成員資格不確定性 — — 而減速。
in either case, gdp growth is likely to slow as business confidence, consumption, and house prices suffer either from new taxes under labour or from uncertainties about eu membership under the conservatives.
另一個國際觀察家忽視如此明顯的風險的原因是他們的目光完全集中在希臘和烏克蘭你的大事件上。
another reason why international observers may be ignoring such obvious risks is that they have been preoccupied with more dramatic events in greece and ukraine.
政客、金融分析家和政治評論家的時間和注意力都是有限的。
politicians, financial analysts, and political commentators have limited time and attention.
他們傾向於關注最大最緊迫的問題，而英國政治不在此列。
they tend to focus on whatever seems to be the biggest and most urgent story, and british politics has not been it.
而許多顯然是非常老練的分析家可能再次完全陷入了一種心理否認的狀態。
then again, many apparently sophisticated analysts may simply be in a state of psychological denial.
英國商業和金融觀點調查表明，這類群體中的絕對多數期望選戰的最後幾日會出現有利於保守黨的突然轉變，形成一個穩定的執政聯盟和實現經濟和政治環境的連續性。
surveys of business and financial opinion in britain show clear majorities in these groups expecting a sudden swing toward the conservatives in the closing days of the election campaign, resulting in a stable coalition government and continuity in economic and political conditions.
發生最後一分鐘選舉傾向改變時可能的，但時間正在耗盡。
such a lastminute shift in voting intentions is possible, but the time for it is running out.
事實上，英國公眾觀點一直驚人地穩定，不僅在官方選戰期間是如此，在整個過去12個月裡一直是如此。
in fact, british public opinion has remained uncannily stable, not only during the official election campaign, but throughout the past 12 months.
預期保守黨或工黨取得組建穩定政府所需要的決定性勝利絕非理性預期。
there are simply no rational grounds for expecting either the conservatives or labour to achieve the decisive victory needed to form a stable government.
因此，即將到來的選舉將標誌著英國政治、經濟和金融不確定性時代的開始，而不是結束。
the upcoming election will therefore mark the beginning, not the end, of a period of uncertainty for british politics, economics, and finance.
即使再大的穩定信念也無法改變這一點。
no amount of lingering faith in stability will change that.
英國的混亂離婚
britains messy divorce
倫敦—在英國正式啟動自絕於歐洲政治和經濟主流的令人憂傷的談判之際，其首相梅卻拒絕使用“離婚”來描述這一事件。
london as britain formally triggers the doleful negotiations to exclude itself from the mainstream of european politics and economics, prime minister theresa may refuses to use the word divorce to describe what is happening.
我的妻子、一位退休家庭律師兼調解員認為梅也許是正確的。
my wife, a retired family lawyer and mediator, thinks may could be correct.
畢竟，我們所要退出的家庭仍然包含著我們的大量歷史和“傳家寶 ” ， 也包含了我們的未來經濟利益。
after all, the family house we are exiting still contains much of our history and family silver, as well as our future economic interest.
從這個角度講，離婚絕不是好選擇。
in that sense, divorce is scarcely an option.
英國並不像一些人認為的那樣，只是一個狹隘的島國。
britain has not been as insular an island as some people take it to be.
從在位王室（日耳曼人）到出口（絕大部分流向歐洲 ） ， 我們影響了西歐其他國家的發展，也反過來受到西歐其他國家發展的影響。
from our reigning royal family which is german to our exports overwhelmingly to europe, we have helped to shape and in our turn been shaped by developments in the rest of western europe.
我們與西歐只隔著一條區區20英里多佛海峽 — — 現在，這顯然是超寬的20英里。
we are separated by just 20 miles 33 kilometers of water these days, apparently a very wide 20 miles at the strait of dover.
那麼，我們為什麼要離開？
so why are we leaving?
原因混合了失望、錯覺、謊言和刻意作對等多種因素。
the cause is a mixture of frustration, delusion, mendacity, and bloodymindedness.
我們被灌輸，歐洲無力處理它所面臨的一些最重大的挑戰 — — 如競爭力和難民等，除非設法獲得更多的核心力量（central powers ） 。
we were fed up with europes inability to tackle some of its biggest challenges from competitiveness to immigration without seeking to acquire more central powers.
此外，我們的政治領袖多年來被對歐盟懷有敵意的人牽著走，對他們幾乎有求必應，而事實上他們的許多批評根本就是謊言的組合體。
in addition, our political leaders have for years played into the hands of those hostile to the eu, by appearing to accept any and every criticism of it, many of them a compound of falsehoods.
我們拒絕承認我們的現實：我們只是一箇中等規模的國家，早已不再能夠支配世界大部。
we refuse to see ourselves for what we are a midsize country that no longer rules much of the world.
我們過於容易地被說服相信，只有民族主義者才可能是愛國者。
we are too easily persuaded that you cannot be a patriot without being a nationalist.
我們能夠也應該管理好這場分家所帶來的後果，並且不再給我們自己平添麻煩。
we can and should manage the consequences of this breakup without bringing further woes down on our heads.
但到目前為止，分離的過程讓我們看不到多少希望。
but the process of separation thus far doesnt offer great hope.
去年6月的英國脫歐公投本身是一場災難。
the brexit referendum last june was itself a disaster.
一個代議制民主國家根本不應該轉向如此民粹主義的設計。
a parliamentary democracy should never turn to such populist devices.
即便如此，梅原本仍然可以對52%要求退出歐洲的選民說，她將把談判交給相信這一結果的大臣團隊，並及時將談判結果提交給議會和人民。
even so, may could have reacted to the 52 vote to quit europe by saying that she would hand the negotiations to a group of ministers who believed in this outcome and then put the result of the talks in due course to parliament and the people.
相反，她讓她的政府完全淪為脫歐機器，及時她本人一直想要留在歐盟。
instead, she turned the whole of her government into a brexit machine, even though she had always wished to remain in the eu.
如今，她的政府的格言是“要麼脫歐，要麼解體 ” 。
her governments motto is now brexit or bust.
悲哀的是，我們可能同時得到這兩樣東西。
sadly, we will probably get both.
那麼，接下去會怎麼樣？
so what happens next?
沒有人有頭緒。
no one has a clue.
懸崖在招手；旅鼠正在集結。
the cliff beckons the lemmings are lining up.
我們知道，我們的出口有將近一半流向歐盟，比流向整個英聯邦的出口多五倍，比流向所有金磚國家的出口多六倍。
we know that almost half our exports go to the eu, five times more than go to the entire commonwealth and six times more than to all the brics countries.
但我們卻放棄了歐盟單一市場（這要求我們接受歐洲司法管轄和勞動力自由流動）或關稅聯盟的成員資格。
but we have given up on staying in the single market which would require us to accept european jurisdiction and the free movement of labor or the customs union.
顯然，我們想要按照我們的要求與歐盟簽訂自由貿易協定，覆蓋我們主要的行業和服務。
apparently we want a freetrade agreement with the eu on our own terms, covering our main industries and services.
梅的外交大臣鮑里斯·約翰遜（Boris Johnson）認為我們在這些談判中盡佔優勢，因為歐洲想繼續賣東西給我們 — — 比如Prosecco。
mays foreign secretary, boris johnson, argues that the cards are in our hands in these negotiations, because europeans want to continue selling prosecco, for example to us.
但即使說到底，梅的大臣們說，什麼協議都不達成也無關緊要。
but anyway, mays ministers say, it doesnt matter if we have no deal at all.
我們只需要走開就是了。
we will simply walk away.
他們說，沒有協議未必是一個壞結果，因為世界渴望與我們做更多生意，隨著未來英鎊穩步貶值，與我們做生意更加有利可圖。
no deal would not necessarily be a bad outcome, they insist, because the world is eager to do more business with us, which will be cheaper in the future as sterling continues its steady decline.
所有這些，用梅不會用的話說，感覺就好像是一場非常不友好的離婚。
all of this, to return to the word may wont use, feels like a rather unamicable divorce.
談判中的每一次轉折，都伴隨著梅的保守黨的右翼以及她現在欠著巨大人情的花邊小報的衝冠仇外之怒。
every twist and turn in the talks will be accompanied by xenophobic outrage on the right wing of mays conservative party and in the tabloid press to which she is now so beholden.
真是壞透了，我們正準備破壞我們的經濟，而這將讓窮人變得更窮，有企業家精神的人變得更加脆弱。
it is bad enough that we are setting about wrecking our economy, which will make the poor poorer and even the enterprising more vulnerable.
除此之外，我們還顛覆了許多代議制民主的規則和傳統，代議制應該鼓勵尋找共識和妥協，迴避多數制。
on top of this, we are overturning many of the rules and conventions of our parliamentary democracy, which should encourage the search for consensus and compromise, and shun majoritarianism.
去年6月，只有52%的英國選民決定要退出歐盟。
a mere 52 of british voters made the decision to exit the eu last june.
他們投票支援的到底是什麼，仍然是個謎。
what exactly they voted for remains a mystery.
但梅和脫歐派堅持聲稱，他們發出了聲音。
but they have spoken, may and the brexiteers insist.
這就結了。
so that settles it.
他們說，不要去管“人民的敵人 ” — —我們的獨立的法院中的法官 — — 要說什麼。
ignore, they say, what the enemies of the people, the judges in our independent courts, have to say.
堅決駁斥一切關於調查到底發生了什麼的觀點。
shout down any point of view inquiring about what is actually happening to us.
攻擊一切支援歐盟成員資格或公開討論這一資格的人的名聲 — — 不管是企業管理者、政客還是公民社會領袖。
attack the reputation of anyone business manager, politician, or civilsociety leader who favors eu membership or an open discussion of it.
告訴BBC，它必須熱情地接受英國脫歐，否則就會觸犯眾怒。
tell the bbc that it must accept brexit enthusiastically or face popular wrath.
最重要的是，關閉議會爭論 — — 都是以“重塑議會主權”的名義。
above all, close down parliamentary debate all in the name of restoring parliamentary sovereignty.
離婚進行得不順利。
this divorce is not going well.
過程才剛剛開始。
and the proceedings have only just started.
未來還有很長的路要走。
there is a long road ahead.
我們最後會成為什麼樣的國家，只有老天爺知道。
heaven knows what sort of country we will be at the end of it.
但是，和所有離婚一樣，我們可以篤定地認為，最苦的還是孩子。
but, as with any divorce, we can be fairly confident that it is the children who will suffer the most.
英國的挪威解決方案
britains norway solution
倫敦 — — 在英國首相特雷莎·梅出人意料地決定舉行“脫歐大選”不久後，我曾撰文指出英國的親歐勢力仍有可能從失敗中搶回勝利。
london shortly after uk prime minister theresa mays decision to call an unexpected brexit election, i wrote that proeuropeans in britain might yet snatch victory from the jaws of defeat.
但我當時所想的時間跨度是五年，而不是五個星期。
but the timescale i had in mind was five years, not five weeks.
很難預測梅還會在首相的位置上堅持多久。
how long may will survive as prime minister is impossible to predict.
不僅倫敦，而且愛丁堡和貝爾法斯特的個人仇恨和拜占庭式的鬥爭將決定她的命運。
her fate will depend on personal vendettas and byzantine political rivalries, not only in london, but also in edinburgh and belfast.
但在預測英國脫歐談判結果時，重要的問題已經不再是梅在政治上能否繼續生存。
but in trying to anticipate the outcome of the brexit negotiations, the questions that matter no longer have much to do with mays political survival.
英國的議會考量和公眾輿論究竟是贊成還是反對梅在選舉前策劃的“硬脫歐 ” — —即嚴厲打擊移民並退出歐洲關稅同盟、單一市場和法律管轄範圍？
are britains parliamentary arithmetic and public opinion moving in favor of or against the hard brexit a drastic clampdown on immigration and withdrawal from the european unions customs union, single market, and legal jurisdiction planned by may before the election?
但如果英國人反對梅的計劃，歐盟領導人能否為他們提供與挪威類似的保全顏面的妥協方案，即留在歐盟體制結構之外，但接受歐盟成員國的大部分義務和代價，以換取單一市場所帶來的商業好處？
and if britons are turning against mays agenda, will eu leaders offer them a facesaving compromise similar to that offered to norway, which remains outside the eus institutional structures, but accepts most of the obligations and costs of eu membership in exchange for the commercial benefits of the single market?
只有類似挪威這樣的對歐關係才能吸引英國的公眾和政治支援，同時不會威脅到歐盟的原則或給任何一方造成嚴重的經濟損失。
an eu relationship similar to norways is the only model that could attract public and political support in britain, without threatening eu principles or inflicting serious economic costs on either side.
這一選項的制度安排已經以歐洲經濟區（EEA）的形式存在，這從某種意義上講是歐盟成員資格的前身，目前有挪威、冰島和列支敦斯登等三個繁榮的歐洲小國都在採用這種形式。
the institutional arrangements for this option already exist, in the form of the european economic area eea, a sort of anteroom to full eu membership, currently occupied by three small but prosperous european countries norway, iceland, and liechtenstein.
上述國家在20世紀80年代末考慮成為歐盟成員，但卻出於不同的原因決定暫不加入。
these countries considered eu membership in the late 1980s, but for various reasons decided not to join.
所有國家都想在經濟和勞動力市場領域與歐洲實現一體化，而且，在脫歐公投後，人們普遍認為英國將試圖談判挪威式的歐洲經濟區方案，而不是像梅所提議的那樣與歐洲決裂。
all wanted to integrate their economies and labor markets with europe, and, after the brexit vote, britain was widely expected to try to negotiate a norwegianstyle eea arrangement, rather than the rupture proposed by may.
就在去年9月就任首相三個月後，梅實際否定歐洲經濟區選擇的做法震驚了世界，她在保守黨年會上宣佈那些自稱為“世界公民”的人其實“哪國公民也不是 ” ， 因此歐洲經濟區成員資格所要求的人口自由流動完全不可接受。
it was only last september, three months after becoming prime minister, that may surprised the world by effectively ruling out the eea option, telling the conservative partys annual conference that those who call themselves citizens of the world are really citizens of nowhere, and that the free movement of people required by eea membership was therefore unacceptable.
1月，她正式宣佈英國不會尋求成為歐洲單一市場成員，因為加入歐洲單一市場的前提是人口自由流動，這一立場在保守黨的競選宣言中得到了確認。
in january, she officially announced that britain would not seek membership of the eu single market, because this would require free movement, a position confirmed in the tories election manifesto.
但現在6月8日大選讓梅變成了跛腳鴨，動盪的議會聯盟和不斷變幻的公眾輿論將要推動接下來的脫歐談判，她對移民的厭惡究竟還重要與否？
but is mays aversion to immigrants still relevant, now that the election on june 8 has made her a lame duck and unstable parliamentary alignments and the shifting balance of public opinion will drive the brexit negotiations?
公眾輿論對移民的態度將成為未來幾個月英國歐盟政策最重要的決定因素。
public opinion on immigration will be the most important determinant of britains european policy in the months ahead.
而在民調中由強有力證據支援的出人意料的選舉結果表明公眾對人口自由流動的態度更加微妙，而不是像梅和保守黨競選宣言所認為的那樣以敵對為主。
and the unexpected election outcome, backed by strong evidence from polling, suggests that public attitudes concerning the free movement of people are more nuanced and less hostile than mays rhetoric and the conservative manifesto had assumed.
事實上，英國選民多數支援人口自由流動，前提是自由流動不被宣傳為外國官僚機構強加的反民主政治條件，而是被作為英國和歐盟民眾共同享有的一種權利。
in fact, british voters mostly support free movement, if it is presented not as an antidemocratic imposition by foreign bureaucrats, but rather as a right that british and eu citizens reciprocally enjoy.
5月，最接近預測大選結果的英國民調公司YouGov在他們對1，875名選民進行的最後一輪選前民調中加上了這樣一個問題 ： “ 在談判英國脫離歐盟的過程中，你認為我們的政府是否應該為歐盟民眾提供來英國旅遊、工作、學習或在英國退休的權利，來換取歐盟國家賦予英國民眾同樣的權利？
in may, yougov, the british polling company that came closest to predicting the election result, added to their final preelection poll of 1,875 voters the following question in negotiating britains departure from the european union, do you think our government should offer eu citizens the right to travel, work, study, or retire in britain, in exchange for eu countries giving british citizens the same rights?
” （ 全面披露，這個問題由Best for Britain設計，這是一個由我本人協助建立並主持的機構。 ）
full disclosure, this question was suggested by best for britain, an organization i helped to establish and chair.
答案顛覆了人們的傳統認知。
the answers defied conventional wisdom.
選民們面對這個經過謹慎考慮的樣本贊成自由流動的比例達到4:1。
voters in this carefully weighted sample favored free movement by four to one.
62%的人選擇“是 ” ， 17%的人選擇“否 ” ， 回答“不知道”的人為21 % 。
sixtytwo percent said yes, 17 no, and 21 answered, dont know.
不僅如此，該樣本所屬各個分組贊成人口自由流動的人都明顯佔到絕大多數，無論分組標準是年齡、地區還是政黨支援，這當中僅有一個例外：那就是支援反移民的英國獨立黨的少數選民。
moreover, there were clear majorities in favor of free movement in every subgroup of the sample, whether categorized by age, region, or politicalparty support, with one exception the small minority of voters who supported the antiimmigrant uk independence party.
要點是基於歐洲經濟區模式的新關係允許英國在容忍人口自由流動的前提下保留歐洲關稅同盟和統一市場的絕大部分好處，這不僅比硬脫歐帶來的經濟痛苦要小；而且還能夠獲得絕大部分選民的支援。
the upshot is that a new relationship based on the eea model, allowing britain to keep most of the benefits of the eu customs union and single market alongside free movement of people, would not only be economically less painful than a hard brexit it would also be supported by a large majority of voters.
單一市場準入和人口自由流動的組合在上週首次參與投票的大批年輕人中尤其有市場，他們認為在歐洲任何地方生活、工作或學習的權利是歐盟成員資格的主要好處，而不是代價。
the combination of singlemarket membership and free movement would be particularly popular with the large cohort of young people who turned out to vote last week for the first time and who consider the ability to live, work, or study anywhere in europe a major benefit of eu membership, not a cost.
從英國政治的角度看，歐洲經濟區成員資格將可能成為未來幾個月指導英國脫歐談判的最高原則。
from the standpoint of british politics, it is possible that eea membership will become the lodestar steering brexit negotiations in the months ahead.
但歐盟將會採取何種對策？
but how would the eu respond?
對其他歐盟成員國來說，以歐洲經濟區為基礎的脫歐談判應當是完全可以接受、甚至是令人歡迎的結果。
for other eu countries, a brexit negotiation based on eea membership should be a perfectly acceptable, even welcome, outcome.
歐洲經濟區成員資格不會導致英國白白擷取歐盟福利的果實，其他國家不願看到這種結果出現是完全可以理解的。
eea membership would not amount to british cherry picking of eu benefits, which other countries have understandably refused to accept.
這是因為，無論按照何種標準，歐洲經濟區成員資格都明顯遜於完整的歐盟成員資格。
this is because, by almost any standard, eea membership is clearly inferior to full eu membership.
除接受人口自由流動外，歐洲經濟區成員還必須遵守歐盟的商業規則並接受歐洲法院所作出的裁決，但卻在制定這些規則和決策時起不到任何正式作用。
in addition to accepting free movement of people, eea members must follow eu commercial rules and accept decisions by the european court of justice, without any formal role in making these rules and decisions.
出於上述原因，當歐洲經濟區在1994年最初成立時，其目的僅僅是作為計劃成為歐盟成員、但還沒有準備好最終加入的奧地利、瑞典、芬蘭和挪威等國的臨時過渡性制度。
for these reasons, when the eea was established in 1994, it was intended only as a temporary transitional arrangement for countries such as austria, sweden, finland, and norway which planned to become eu members, but were not ready to join.
對奧地利、瑞典和芬蘭而言，它們最終不出所料地成為了正式成員。
for austria, sweden, and finland, full membership came as intended.
但挪威選民卻在一次全民公投中拒絕成為歐盟成員，並且一直延續到現在。
but in norway, voters rejected eu membership in a referendum and still do.
挪威的臨時歐洲經濟區成員資格現在已經持續了23年。
norways temporary eea membership has now stretched to 23 years.
這會不會成為英國的榜樣？
could this be a precedent for britain?
英國人權革命的失敗
britains failed human rights revolution
發自倫敦 — — 英國新聯合政府的預算緊縮計劃無疑佔據了各大媒體的頭條，但大衛·卡梅隆內閣同時也與前任工黨政府在另一個關鍵領域徹底決裂 — — 那就是人權。
london the budgetcutting austerity program of britains new coalition government has been claiming all the headlines, but david camerons cabinet is breaking with its labour predecessor in another key area as well human rights.
事實上，由東尼·布萊爾的工黨政府帶給英國的人權試驗已經徹底宣告破產了。
indeed, the humanrights experiment that tony blairs labour government brought to britain has failed.
英國的人權法案如今是兩面不討好：一方面有人指責其無力制止“粗暴”的反恐監察措施，另一方面又被人批評其阻礙了反恐政策的順利實施。
faulted by some for its inability to prevent illiberal antiterrorism measures, the human rights act is criticized by just as many others for hampering counterterrorism policy.
實際上有許多人都對人權的終極理念嗤之以鼻，認為這隻會導致對罪犯和恐怖分子的“愚蠢”妥協。
indeed, many people mock the very notion of human rights, which is seen as leading to loony concessions that favor criminals and terrorists.
總的來說，媒體和公眾的反應總是介乎於理想幻滅以及冷嘲熱諷之間。
overall, the reaction of both press and public is one of disillusion andor cynicism.
英國這個國家以沒有成文憲法聞名，或者說，直到最近都沒有形成一份類似現代《權利法案》的檔案，不過我們有1215年《自由大憲章》和板球。
britain famously has no written constitution, or, until recently, anything resembling a modern bill of rights. instead, we have magna carta and cricket.
普世人權的概念其實是個舶來品 — — 它存在於《歐洲人權公約》那些籠統的原則當中，而人權法庭則遠在法國斯特拉斯堡。
the concept of universal human rights is literally foreign enshrined in the broadbrush principles of the european convention on human rights, whose court sits in strasbourg.
因此任何想以人權理由控告英國政府的人都得跑到法國才能立案。
until recently, anyone who wished to bring a humanrights case against the british government had to go to france.
不過在布萊爾1997年上臺之後，事情開始有了轉機。
times changed when tony blair came to power in 1997.
在“權利終於回家了（意指回到了發源地 ） ” 這一浮誇和理想主義口號的映襯下，英國《人權法案》終於在2000年得以頒佈實施。
with fanfare and idealism reflected in the slogan rights brought home the human rights act came into effect in 2000.
但這些充滿道德感的自由主義精英也有自己的小算盤：倘若英國政府違反了法案的話，那就得由英國自己的法庭來審判，不用飄洋過海去勞煩那些國際法官了。
but the highminded liberalism of the thenelite had a practical point as well should the government have any soiled linen, it should be laundered in british courts rather than be aired before a panel of international judges.
但這個法案在英國卻不得人心，也從未付諸法律實踐。
yet the act is unloved by the british public, which never engaged with the process.
正如布萊爾的夫人切麗·布斯（她本身就是位人權律師）哀嘆道 ： “ 大部分公眾認為人權法案與自己的生活毫不相關。 ”
as tony blairs wife, cherie booth, herself a human rights lawyer, lamented, the majority of people feel that human rights are not relevant to their lives.
這個例子告誡我們：不要畫蛇添足，或者說，事實勝於雄辯。
there is a lesson here if its not broken, dont fix it. put another way, actions speak louder than words.
與那些真正有損人道的侵犯人權行為相比，英國法院所受理的那些人權投訴簡直不值一提。
when compared with humanrights abuses that truly affect humanity, the complaints dealt with by the british courts are small beer.
哪個孩子應該上哪所學校，或者應該給政治避難者安排何種住宿這類的問題都會引發許多人的關注（而且觀點往往會分化 ） ， 但用“人權”這個粗略的概念來解決這些問題其實是貶低了這個概念。
which child goes to what school or what public housing is offered to which asylum seeker will be of concern to many people and views will differ. but using the broad brush of human rights to resolve such issues trivializes the concept.
而這同時也阻礙了真正嚴肅的討論。
it also inhibits proper debate.
最後，估計也沒有哪個公共機構願意因侵犯人權而遭到起訴。
after all, what responsible public body wants to be accused of violating human rights?
事實上，人權訴訟的威脅令到那些提供公共服務的機構變得過於謹慎和保守。
indeed, the threat of humanrights litigation has made providers of public services overly cautious and defensive.
這使得公眾媒體痛批我們正生活在一個耗資巨大，官僚習氣深重，而且低效率的“人權文化”當中 — — 這可算是一個引發深層次政治迴響的指控。
this has led the popular press to howl that we now live in a costly, bureaucratic, and inefficient human rights culture a charge with profound political resonance.
而在問鼎首相之前，卡梅隆就呼籲用某種更“英國”方式的來取代《人權法案 》 。
before he became prime minister, cameron called for the human rights act to be replaced with something more british.
但荒謬的是，在人權最需要得到承認的時候，有些人卻認為人權是一個毫無用處的東西，許多英國議員支援將歐洲人權法案編入英國法律，但他們同時也發現：如果給人權以正式承認的話，就會在對抗基地組織這類恐怖主義行為方面遭到極大不便。
paradoxically, some deem human rights to be wholly inefficacious where their recognition is most required. many mps who backed the incorporation of the european humanrights convention into british law came to view formal recognition of human rights as a grave inconvenience when faced with al qaedainspired terrorism.
簡而言之，在“權力終於回家”之後，布萊爾政府卻最終想把它塞到沙發底下藏起來。
in short, having brought rights home, the blair government ended up trying to hide them under the sofa.
而這一謎局在一場辯論上得到了最終體現 — — 關於在沒有起訴或審判的情況下關押恐怖主義嫌疑犯。
this conundrum is symbolized by the debate over detaining terrorism suspects without charge or trial.
原本布萊爾打算將拘留期設定為90天，最終議會將其定在28天 — — 但這依然是西方世界中最長的拘留期。
initially, blair attempted to force through detention without charge for up to 90 days. parliament settled on 28 days still the longest such period in the western world.
但《歐洲人權公約》第6條規定：每個受到犯罪指控的人都有權“被立刻告知”自己的罪名。
so much, then, for article 6 of the european convention, which provides that everyone charged with a criminal offense has the right to be informed promptly of the nature of the accusation against him.
而《大憲章》裡也列明“任何自由人，如未經他人之依法裁判，或經國法判決，皆不得被逮捕，監禁 … … ”
so much, also, for magna carta, which provides that no freeman shall be taken or imprisonedbut by lawful judgment of his peers, or by the law of the land.
不過布萊爾的所作所為可不是一個特例。
blairs behavior is not unique.
事實上，任何試圖實現人權的立法手段在一個議會高於一切的政治系統中都是不堪一擊的。
the fact is that any piece of legislation purporting to embody human rights is entirely vulnerable to a political system in which parliament is supreme.
《人權法案》必然要臣服於隨後頒佈的法律法規。
the human rights act must inevitably yield to subsequent legislation.
這些法律法規可都是獲得了議會簡單多數透過的。
all legislation is passed by a simple majority.
而法官是無法與這些條文抗衡的。
and judges cannot strike down legislation.
結果是什麼？
the result?
權力只回了一天家；不過嫌疑人可要在大牢裡蹲上1個月，卻不知道自己犯了什麼罪。
rights brought home one day detention for a month without charge the next.
事實上，即便人權的原則得到了推進 ， 《 人權法案》如今卻遭到了忽視。
indeed, even when the cause of human rights is being advanced, the human rights act is now overlooked.
在副首相尼克·克列格5月發表的第一次重要政策演說中，他宣告要推翻布萊爾所建成的“老大哥”國家（意指國家監控公民一切行為 ） ： 不再有身份證或者人口登記，對DNA資訊的儲存設立新限制，收緊對閉路電視監控的規管（此網路已經令英國人成為全球受監控程度最嚴重的人民）等等。
in may, in his first major policy speech, deputy prime minister nick clegg announced the sweeping away of the big brother state that blair had constructed no more id cards or national identity register, new restrictions on the storage of dna, tighter regulation of the closedcircuit television surveillance that had made the british the most monitored people on earth, and so on.
他說了那麼多，卻一句都沒提到“人權 ” — —這既反映出人權在當今英國的敏感性，同時也在默默地承認：在這種關鍵時刻 ， 《 人權法案》可是靠不住的。
all this and not one mention of human rights an absence that reflects the political sensitivity of human rights in britain today, and that tacitly acknowledges that when the stakes are high, the human rights act cannot be relied upon.
那麼卡梅隆政府究竟將如何根除“老大哥 ” ？
where, then, does that leave the cameron governments supposed extirpation of big brother?
一種方法就是比布萊爾更進一步，把某些原則特別提出來，並設立憲法法庭以維護之。
one way forward would be to go further than blair by ringfencing certain principles and creating some form of constitutional court to defend them.
但這種死板管制的成本可能會很高，而其效力，以美國飄忽不定的人權記錄來看，有時比空想更靠不住。
but the cost of such rigid rules may be high, and their effectiveness, as witnessed by the vagaries of the united states record on human rights, is less foolproof than is sometimes imagined.
因此，或許在一個成熟的民主體制內，與其虛張聲勢，不如採取實際行動去尊重人權；與其引入更多法律，既在民眾中留下壞印象，又不堪大用，不如在需要維護自由和公平競爭時相信自己的憲政體制。
so, perhaps in a mature democracy, human rights should be dignified by actions rather than words. instead of introducing more legislation that is tainted both in the popular imagination and in its utility, britain could, after all, trust its constitution to act as and when required to safeguard liberty and fair play.
不管怎麼樣，民主的觀點最終會勝利，而英國的人權記錄，雖然算不上完美，卻依然可圈可點。
for good or ill, democratic sentiment will win out, and britains humanrights record, while imperfect, remains strong.
英國的否定之路
britains path of denial
聖地亞哥 — — 如今，如果你去倫敦旅行，會發現一些奇怪的景象：英國經濟越萎靡，卡梅倫政府的各位部長和保守黨經濟學家就越頻繁地宣稱嚴厲的支出削減政策對經濟增長有利。
santiago visit london nowadays and you will notice something strange going on the worse the british economy tanks, the more fervently prime minister david camerons ministers and tory economists insist that draconian spending cuts are good for economic growth.
一些觀察家將其視為一種信念（大概是對不受束縛的自由市場的優點的信仰 ） 。
some observers see this as an act of faith presumably in the virtues of the unfettered market.
其他人，比如保羅·克魯格曼（Paul Krugman ） ， 則認為這是一種欺瞞：保守黨一心想要小政府，為此不惜犧牲經濟增長。
others, such as the economist paul krugman, see it as an act of bad faith the tories just want smaller government, regardless of the consequences for growth.
問題在於，削減支出以刺激經濟到底是不是一種無信念基礎的觀點。
the question remains whether there is a nonfaithbased argument for cutting back spending to stimulate an economy.
答案是肯定的。
the answer is yes.
事實上，這一觀點存在兩種型別。
in fact, there are two.
學術研究表明，它們在過去挺有效，比如20世紀80年代的愛爾蘭和丹麥。
academic research has shown them at work in the past for example, in ireland and denmark during the 1980s.
對保守黨來說，不幸的是這兩次刺激性支出削減都不適用英國窘迫的現狀。
unfortunately for the tories, neither case for stimulative spending cuts fits britains predicament today.
一種觀點強調財政和貨幣政策之間的聯絡。
one argument emphasizes the links between fiscal and monetary policy.
如果一國有著巨大的財政赤字，那麼其中央銀行可能不得不維持高利率以控制通脹。
in a country with large fiscal deficits, the central bank may have to keep interest rates high to control inflation.
在這種情形下，預算削減將創造降息空間。
in this scenario, budget cuts create room for interest rates to fall.
如果該國匯率是浮動的，那麼貨幣也會貶值。
if the country has a floating exchangerate regime, the currency depreciates, too.
這些變化均有利於需求和增長。
both of these changes are good for demand and growth.
如果綜合作用壓倒了一開始削減支出的緊縮效應，則經濟就能在一輪財政緊縮後大為改善。
