目前還不清楚那些既要照顧孩子又要上班的人們如何在駕駛一套“讓工作者得回報”系統的同時又承擔好兩個角色。
it is unclear how parents and workers navigating a system intended to make work pay are supposed to perform either role well.
英國的新計劃被鼓吹為一種降低成本和激勵更佳決策的方式，可以使更多的人投入工作，減少福利需求。
britains new program was championed as a way to reduce costs and incentivize better decisions, thereby moving more people into work and reducing benefit claims.
但迄今為止沒有什麼證據能支援這種樂觀設想。
but, so far, there is little evidence to support this rosy scenario.
透過減少窮人獲得的福利，政府正在確保稀缺性不斷上升以及糟糕決策倍增。
by reducing benefits received by the poor, the government is ensuring that scarcity surges and poor decisions multiply.
在頻繁改變福利體系使其更加複雜後，英國領導人也迫使窮人消耗更多的精神頻寬。
and by changing the system frequently and making it more complicated to access, britains leaders are also forcing the poor to consume more mental bandwidth.
總而言之，這些因素使得福利受助者變得日益窘迫。
taken together, these factors are leaving welfare recipients worse off.
決策者應該閱讀穆萊納森和沙菲爾的著作，並考慮如何將他們的研究應用於未來的福利改革。
policymakers should read mullainathan and shafir, and consider how their research could be applied to future welfare reforms.
目標應該是慷慨和穩定的福利，讓人們專注於找工作，同時輔導孩子的功課並照顧自己的健康。
the goal should be benefits that are generous and stable enough to let people focus on finding work, while also helping their children with homework and looking after their own health.
這類系統的建立不是不可能的。
that type of system is possible to create.
而另一種辦法是給那些最無力承受的人增加負擔。
the alternative is a system that places additional burdens on those least able to bear them.
數字脫貧之路
the digital road from poverty
哥本哈根—未來15年，全球社會注意力焦點應該匯聚到何處？
copenhagen where should the global community focus its attention over the next 15 years?
健康、營養和教育都是顯而易見的選擇；比較意外的是，實現寬頻普及也應該作為最優先事項。
health, nutrition, and education may seem like obvious choices more surprisingly, there is a strong case for making broadband access a top priority.
考慮以下簡單的事實：在未來15年將移動網際網路普及率提高兩倍將讓發展中世界增加22萬億美元財富。
consider this simple fact tripling mobile internet access over the next 15 years could make the developing world 22 trillion richer.
窮人生活和收入潛力的如此改善直接有助於其他挑戰；畢竟，更繁榮的民族身體也更健康，吃得也更好，教育程度也更高。
such improvement in the lives and earning potential of poor people could indirectly help with the other challenges after all, more prosperous people tend to be healthier, better fed, and more highly educated.
這一討論很重要，因為全世界193個國家的政府將在9月齊聚聯合國，最終確定2030年世界所要實現的發展目標。
this discussion matters, because the worlds 193 national governments will meet at the united nations in september to finalize a list of development targets for the world to meet by 2030.
我的智庫 — — 哥本哈根共識（Copenhagen Consensus）請60組經濟學家（其中包括多位諾貝爾經濟學獎獲得者）研究哪些目標的每一美元收益最大，以幫助此次會議作出最佳選擇。
my think tank, the copenhagen consensus, has asked 60 teams of economists, including several nobel laureates, to investigate which targets would do the most good for every dollar spent, to help this meeting make the best choices.
在一份新分析中，圖盧茲經濟學院（Toulouse School of Economics）的艾曼努爾·奧瑞爾（Emmanuelle Auriol）和亞歷克謝·李·岡薩雷斯·範法倫（Alexia Lee González Fanfalone）指出，寬頻也許是最好的未來投資。
in a new analysis, emmanuelle auriol and alexia lee gonzlez fanfalone of the toulouse school of economics suggest that broadband could be one of the best investments for the future.
顯然，寬頻服務的快速推進改變了工業化國家人民的生活；有充分的理由期待發展中國家至少也能獲得同樣的好處。
clearly, the rapid rollout of broadband services has transformed the lives of people in the industrialized world there is every reason to expect that developing countries could benefit at least as much.
比如，獲得市場資訊可以確保出售剩餘莊稼的農民不會被惡劣的貿易商欺騙、漁民可以把收穫運往出價最有利的港口。
access to market information, for example, can ensure that farmers selling their surplus crops are not cheated by unscrupulous traders, and that fishermen can land their catch at the port offering the best price.
一份麥肯錫報告估算，讓發展中世界移動寬頻達到工業化國家同等水平可以每年增加4,000億美元全球GDP，多創造一千萬個新崗位。
a mckinsey report estimates that bringing mobile broadband in the developing world to the levels of the industrial world could add 400 billion annually to global gdp and create more than ten million jobs.
類似地，世界銀行指出，寬頻滲透率提高10%可以讓中低收入國家GDP增長提高1.4 % 。
similarly, the world bank has shown that a 10 increase in broadband penetration increased gdp growth by 1.4 in low to mediumincome countries.
這意味著填補持續存在的發達和發展中地區數字差距可以帶來巨大的發展提振作用。
this implies that closing the persistent digital divide between the worlds developed and developing regions could give a big boost to development.
比如，發達地區的移動寬頻滲透率為83 % ， 而發展中地區只有21 % 。
for example, mobile broadband penetration stands at 83 in the former, but only 21 in the latter.
儘管歐洲和其他地區的政府一直在投資於更快更好的寬頻，但最大的好處將永遠來自向從未獲得過��帶接入的人們提供網際網路。 這些人大多生活在發展中和新興國家。
while governments in europe and elsewhere continue to invest in faster and better broadband, the biggest benefits will always come from providing internet access to people who do not already have it, most of whom live in developing and emerging countries.
事實上，發展中國家可以透過直接進入移動寬頻實現與發達國家同等的水平，從而避開鋪設昂貴的“最後一英里”網路 — — 或接入點 — — 光纖的需要。
in fact, developing countries can leapfrog the developed world by going straight to mobile broadband, thereby avoiding the need for expensive fiberoptic cables for the last mile or access point of the network.
行動電話正在發展中國家迅速普及，這使得老式固定線路基礎設施不再必不可少；資料服務可以使用相同的系統。
mobile phone use is already spreading rapidly in developing countries, making oldstyle fixed infrastructure unnecessary data services can use the same system.
在中國，四分之三的網際網路使用者已經透過行動電話上網；在衣索比亞和烏干達，這一比例達到了五分之四。
in china, threequarters of internet users get online via mobile phones already in ethiopia and uganda, four out of five do.
因此，考慮到行動電話的普及度和行動網路技術的最新進步，普及移動寬頻似乎是高價效比的解決之道。
thus, given the pervasiveness of mobile telephony and recent technological advances in mobile networks, rolling out mobile broadband seems a costeffective solution.
奧瑞爾和範法倫的研究表明，將發展中地區的移動寬頻普及度提高兩倍 — — 從21%提高到60 % — —需要花費大約1.3萬億美元巨資，因為要增加三十億個網際網路連線需要大量新增基礎設施。
the study by auriol and fanfalone shows that increasing mobile broadband about threefold in developing regions from 21 to 60 will cost a substantial 1.3 trillion, as a significant amount of extra infrastructure is needed to establish about three billion more internet connections.
但這也會增加GDP增長。
but it will also increase gdp growth.
到2020年，這方面的收益將達到每年近5,000億美元，並將繼續逐年遞增。
by 2020, the benefits would be almost 500 billion annually, and would continue to rise each year.
在未來十年中，總收益將達到約22萬億美元。
over the coming decades, the total benefit would reach about 22 trillion.
因此，花在發展中國家移動寬頻上的每一美元大約可以帶來17美元收益。
as a result, every dollar spent on mobile broadband in the developing world would yield an estimated gain of 17.
這看上去絕對是聰明的投資。
that looks like a really smart investment.
當然，寬頻是極其重要的賦能型（enabling）技術，我們很難預測它的全部經濟影響，其影響將隨地方環境的不同而不同。
of course, broadband is such an important enabling technology that it is difficult to predict its full economic impact, which will vary with local circumstances.
但是，奧瑞爾-範法倫研究的確表明，增加網際網路接入花的錢物有所值。
what the auriolfanfalone study does show, though, is that rolling out internet access is money very well spent.
就業崗位被直接（在提供網路的組織中）和間接（在供應鏈組織中）創造出來。
jobs are created directly in the organization providing the network and indirectly in the supply chain.
一旦建立，寬頻將有助於為更廣泛的經濟創造更多就業崗位。
once in place, broadband helps create more jobs in the wider economy.
公司的效率和創新力也有所提高。
companies become more efficient and innovative.
所有這些因素都能增加經濟增長速度。
all of these factors increase the pace of economic growth.
除了經濟增長和就業創造的直接效應，寬頻還能給最不發達國家帶來一些重要收益。
apart from the direct effects on economic growth and job creation, broadband can have some other very important benefits for least developed countries.
九億人生活在最不發達國家，而倫敦帝國學院的潘特利斯·科特羅姆皮斯（Pantelis Koutroumpis）指出，其中只有6.7%是網際網路使用者。
nine hundred million people live in ldcs, and, as pantelis koutroumpis of imperial college london points out, only 6.7 are internet users.
另一方面，這些人中有近60%使用行動電話。
on the other hand, almost 60 of these people use a mobile phone.
他們可以從智慧手機中獲益 — — 在手機上裝上簡單的應用，就可以用於各種健康測試（如心血管疾病、艾滋病和其他病毒以及瘧疾 ） ， 結果直接傳送到醫院並獲得即時反饋。
they could profit from smartphones with simple adaptations that can be used in a range of healthscreening tests for example, for cardiovascular disease, hiv and other pathogens, or malaria, with the results being sent straight to hospitals for an immediate response.
移動寬頻給最不發達國家帶來的潛在好處不僅於此。
the potential benefits of mobile broadband for ldcs extend even further.
網際網路接入能提供教育素材、改善教學。
internet access could provide educational material and improve schooling.
它還能為偏遠地區帶來實時的、按需提供的交通服務。
and it could enable real time, ondemand transport services for remote areas.
如今，網際網路已成為現代世界中極其重要的資源，寬頻也成為一項關鍵技術，帶來提振經濟增長、讓人們擺脫貧困、改善人民健康、營養和教育的效果。
with the internet now such an important resource in the modern world, broadband has become a vital technology, promising to boost economic growth, lift people out of poverty, and improve their health, nutrition, and education.
當各國政府最終敲定下一階段的全球發展目標時，絕對應該將寬頻接入列入其中。
when governments finalize the next set of global development targets, there is now a strong case for broadband access to be among them.
歐洲的寬頻戰爭
europes broadband battle
倫敦—在新歐盟委員會所面臨的諸多挑戰中，有一項是確定如何在不增稅也不讓歐洲通訊公司破產的情況下為全部5億歐盟居民帶來極速寬頻網際網路。
london among the many challenges facing the new european commission is determining how to provide ultrafast broadband internet access to all 500 million european union residents without raising taxes or bankrupting europes telecommunications companies.
這一使命讓許多人要求谷歌、網飛（Netflix）和Facebook等網際網路巨頭做出更大貢獻，這些公司常常被批評沒有起到應有的作用 — — 甚至被猛烈抨擊為“免費搭車者 ” ， 想掠奪歐洲資產和市場。
this imperative has led many to demand larger contributions from internet giants like google, netflix, and facebook, which are frequently criticized for failing to pull their weight and even lambasted as freeriders, intent on pillaging european assets and markets.
這樣的批評合理嗎？
is this criticism warranted?
一言以蔽之：不合理。
in a word no.
現實是大型網際網路公司 — — 大部分總部設在美國 — — 已經在投入數十億美元用於建設和維持對網際網路執行至關重要的網路和資料中心。
the reality is that major internet companies most of which are based in the united states are already contributing billions of dollars to establish and maintain the networks and data centers that are essential to the internets functioning.
事實上，這些公司在過去三年直接投資了750多億歐元的網際網路基礎設施，在此期間，每年投入都要增加10%左右。
in fact, these companies directly invested more than 75 billion 100 billion in internet infrastructure over the last three years, with spending up by about 10 annually over this period.
此外，它們還合作投資了5億多歐元用於鋪設已於2010年啟用的跨太平洋海底光纜和去年投入使用的從東南亞到日本的8,300公里光纜。
moreover, they participated in consortia that invested more than 500 million in laying a transpacific submarine fiber optic cable, which has been operational since 2010, and an 8,300kilometer 5,200mile cable from southeast asia to japan that came onstream last year.
但獲得全球網際網路基礎投資最大部分的正是歐洲 — — 過去三年高達250億歐元，接近總量的三分之一。
but it is europe that has received the lions share of global investment in internet infrastructure 25 billion, or nearly onethird of the total, in the last three years.
谷歌最近宣佈要在荷蘭建設價值6億歐元的資料中心，並且在芬蘭哈米納（Hamina）和比利時聖吉斯蘭（St. Ghislain）已開始投入重金建設資料中心。
google recently announced the construction of a new 600 million data center in the netherlands, and is already investing heavily in data centers in hamina, finland, and st. ghislain, belgium.
Facebook也在瑞典呂勒歐（Luleå）建立了自己的資料中心。
and facebook has already established its own data center in lule, sweden.
這些設施和網路 — — 以及通訊公司花數十億美元建設的寬頻網路 — — 構成了網際網路的基礎。
these facilities and networks along with the broadband networks on which telecommunications companies spend billions form the foundations of the internet.
美國網際網路巨頭投資者寫設施，為歐洲消費者和公司帶來了看得見摸得著的好處。
by investing in them, americas internet giants are providing tangible benefits for european consumers and companies.
鼓勵這類投資應該成為歐盟委員會的主要關注點。
encouraging this investment should be the european commissions main concern.
比如，這些公司的歐洲資料中心有助於所在地區的經濟，為當地居民提供工作崗位。
for example, these companies european data centers contribute to the economies of the regions where they operate, providing jobs to local residents.
與此同時，它們促進了更順利的內容交換，讓歐洲消費者能夠實現大部分網際網路連線。
at the same time, they facilitate the smooth exchange of content, enabling european consumers to make the most of their internet connections.
類似地，網際網路公司在內容傳遞網路和網際網路交換點方面的投資讓它們能夠讓自己的資訊流更加接近消費者，交給倫敦、巴黎和法蘭克福等地的歐洲通訊公司。
likewise, internet companies investments in contentdelivery networks and internet exchange points enable them to carry their own traffic close to consumers, handing it off to eu telecoms in places like london, paris, and frankfurt.
如此，它們可以幫助網際網路服務提供商削減成本，使之能夠投資於自己擁有和經營的“最後一英里”網路接入，從而改善它們提供給消費者的網際網路體驗。
in doing so, they can help internet service providers to cut costs and enable them to invest in the last mile access networks that they own and operate, thereby improving the internet experience that they offer to consumers.
從長期看，隨著歐洲日益成為數字內容和應用的沃土，這一基礎設施將能夠讓歐洲人得以在全球散播發明創造。
in the longer term, as europe becomes increasingly fertile ground for digital content and applications, this infrastructure will enable europeans to distribute their creations globally.
換句話說，谷歌和Facebook等公司今天所建立的結構將有助於為歐洲創新家、企業家和公司開啟新市場，而它們的成功將直接有助於歐洲經濟。
in other words, the structures that companies like google and facebook are building today will help to open new markets for european innovators, entrepreneurs, and companies, whose success will directly benefit europes economy.
歐洲通訊公司和來自美國和其他地區的網際網路巨頭以及公共部門決不能將能量和資源浪費在彼此的鬥爭上，而應該認識到在給所有歐盟居民創造高速平價寬頻網際網路中的共同利益。
instead of wasting energy and resources fighting one another, europes telecoms and internet giants from the us and elsewhere, together with the public sector, should recognize their shared interest in delivering fast, affordable broadband internet to all eu residents.
網際網路一直是一項合作運動，未來也必須如此，每一位參與者都起著作用。
the internet has always been a collaborative endeavor, and it must remain so, with each actor playing its role.
在整個過程中，創造性解決方案將成為主宰，而網際網路公司的貢獻將是不可估量的。
throughout the process, creative solutions will be paramount, and internet companies contributions will be invaluable.
畢竟，它們是老練的創新者，谷歌與沃達豐（Vodafone）在紐西蘭以及與西班牙電信（Telefónica）在智利合作透過大氣氣球為農村地區提供寬頻就是明證。
after all, they are seasoned innovators, as exemplified by googles collaboration with vodafone in new zealand and telefnica in chile to deliver broadband to rural areas through atmospheric balloons.
至於歐盟委員會，它決不能允許既得利益的壓力促使其走向對峙。
for its part, the european commission must not allow pressure from vested interests to drive it toward confrontation.
相反，歐盟領導人應該繼續專注於歐洲數百萬網際網路使用者的利益。
instead, eu leaders should remain focused on the interests of europes millions of internet users.
唯有采取基於事實的平衡方針和強調合作，他們才能帶來消費者的好處、投資、就業和歐洲網際網路行業的成長。
only by adopting a balanced, factbased approach and an emphasis on cooperation can they deliver consumer benefits, investment, jobs, and growth in europes internet sector.
被破壞的敘利亞兒童承諾
broken promises for syrias children
倫敦—如果你失去了希望的力量 — — 更不用說永不放棄的重要性 — — 你應該用穆罕默德·科沙（Mohammed Kosha）的故事激勵自己。
london if you ever lose faith in the power of hope, not to mention the importance of never giving up, remind yourself of the story of mohammed kosha.
這位16歲的敘利亞難民現在生活在黎巴嫩，為了取的好成績，他克服了大部分人難以想象的困難。
a 16yearold syrian refugee living in lebanon, mohammed has overcome obstacles that most of us cannot even imagine, in order to excel in his education.
世界領導人應該引起注意。
world leaders should take note.
四年前，穆罕默德和全家為了躲避敘利亞武裝力量持續不斷的炮擊而逃離了位於大馬士革市郊達爾亞（Darya）鎮的家。
four years ago, mohammed and his family fled their home in the town of darya, a suburb of damascus, to escape relentless bombardment by syrian armed forces.
在家鄉，由於上學太危險，他已經落下了一年小學功課，當全家到達他們現在居住的黎巴嫩後，他又有一年時間沒能上學。
having already lost a year of primary education in his hometown, where it was simply too dangerous to attend school, he then spent another year out of the classroom when the family arrived in lebanon, where they now reside.
黎巴嫩政府向難民開放本國公立學校後，穆罕默德的生活發生了變化。
mohammeds life changed when lebanons government opened the countrys public schools to refugees.
教室擁擠不堪，授課用的是英語，這意味著他必須得學習一門新語言。
classes were not only crowded they were also conducted in english, meaning that he would have to learn a new language.
但穆罕默德抓住了學習的機會，一頭扎進了功課中。
but mohammed seized the opportunity to learn, and threw himself into his studies.
上個月，排除萬難的他在黎巴嫩初中升學考試中取得第二名的好成績。
last month, against all odds, he scored the secondhighest marks in lebanons brevet secondaryschool exam.
他的故事還沒有完。
and he is not done yet.
穆罕默德知道，教育是構建更美好未來的關鍵。
mohammed knows that education is the key to building a better future.
用他的話說 ， “ 學習給我希望。
in his words, learning gives us hope.
”世界領導人有他一半的智慧就好了。
if only world leaders had even a fraction of his wisdom.
已經有了一些令人鼓舞的訊號。
there have been some encouraging signals.
在2月份 倫敦的會議上，國際出資者認識到教育對難民的重要性，承諾到2017年底讓所有敘利亞難民兒童上學。
at a meeting in london in february, international donors recognized the importance of education for refugees, promising to get all of syrias refugee children into school by the end of 2017.
它們甚至承諾投入14億美元用於實現這一目標。
they even pledged 1.4 billion to achieve that goal.
這是一個面向非常脆弱的兒童群體的宏大承諾。
it was an ambitious promise to a group of highly vulnerable children.
如今，大約一百萬5—17歲敘利亞難民兒童 — — 約佔總數的一半 — — 輟學。
today, about one million syrian refugee children aged 517 roughly half the total are out of school.
即使有學可上，絕大部分也進不了中學。
and most of those who are in school will drop out before starting their secondary education.
在僅僅一代小學教育的時間裡，敘利亞遭到了也許是史上最嚴重的教育倒退。
in the space of a single primaryschool generation, syria has suffered what may be the greatest education reversal in history.
敘利亞兒童入學率遠遠低於撒哈拉以南非洲的地區平均水平。
enrollment rates for the countrys children are now well below the regional average for subsaharan africa.
但如今，僅僅六個月後，所有難民接受教育的承諾眼看就要破產，擊碎數百萬敘利亞人的希望。
but now, just six months later, the promise of education for all refugees is about to be broken, dashing the hopes of millions of syrians.
今年，聯合國人道主義機構緊急教育援助需要6.62億美元資金，目��只有39%已經到位。
just 39 of the 662 million in urgent education aid sought by united nations humanitarian agencies this year has been funded.
而在今天公佈的Theirworld報告中指出，倫敦會議上所承諾的14億美元只兌現了一小部分。
and as documented in a theirworld report published today, only a fraction of the 1.4 billion pledged in london has been delivered.
在國際社會逃避責任的同時，敘利亞的鄰國繼續以極大的努力解決這場危機。
as the international community shirks its responsibilities, syrias neighbors have continued to make extraordinary efforts to address the crisis.
黎巴嫩、約旦以及（在較小程度上）土耳其向敘利亞難民開放了公立學校。
lebanon, jordan, and to a lesser extent turkey have opened up their public schools to syrian refugees.
但這些國家的教育體系在危機前便捉襟見肘，根本無法承擔它們如今被迫承擔的負擔。
but these countries education systems, which were strained even before the crisis, cannot handle the burden that they are being forced to shoulder.
目前，敘利亞難民佔了黎巴嫩公立學校學生總數的三分之一。
syrian refugees now comprise onethird of all lebanese publicschool students.
這好比是美國小學突然間必須接收所有墨西哥兒童。
this is like the american primaryschool system suddenly having to absorb all of mexicos children.
教師、教室和教科書嚴重不足，無法給難民兒童提供像樣的教育。
there are simply not enough teachers, classrooms, or textbooks to deliver decent educations to the refugee children.
2月份的會議本應產生能夠減輕敘利亞鄰國負擔的方案。
the february conference was supposed to produce solutions that would ease the burden on syrias neighbors.
東道國政府做好了自己的部分，提前計劃好如何為難民兒童提供全民教育。
hostcountry governments did their part, preparing in advance their plans for delivering universal education to refugee children.
接著，它們還與出資者合作制定覆蓋全體輟學兒童和提高教育質量的全面戰略。
they then worked with donors to develop comprehensive strategies for reaching all outofschool children and raising the quality of education.
但是，由於國際社會沒有兌現承諾，進展十分緩慢；甚至可能倒退。
yet, with the international community having failed to hold up its end of the bargain, progress has not just stalled it could be reversed.
如今，超過80,000在黎巴嫩學校上學的敘利亞難民有可能失去學習機會。
more than 80,000 syrian refugees now in school in lebanon are at risk of losing their places.
敘利亞難民所遭受的教育危機的人道後果不容忽視。
the human consequences of the education crisis among syrian refugees are impossible to miss.
在黎巴嫩貝卡谷（Bekaa Valley）種蔬菜和在土耳其（那裡由五十萬難民輟學）服裝廠工作的童工數量激增。
they are apparent in the growing army of child laborers picking vegetables in lebanons bekaa valley or working at garment factories in turkey, where a halfmillion refugees are out of school.
難民家庭仍然在冒著生命危險前往歐洲，為的就是讓他們的孩子獲得受教育的機會。
they are also reflected in the continuing flow of refugee families making the perilous journey to europe, driven by the hope that their children will have educational opportunities there.
但許多歐洲政府繼續投資鐵絲網和集中營，而不是學校和教師。
yet many european governments continue to invest in razor wire and detention centers, rather than in schools and teachers.
我們可以換一種做法 — — 但時間緊迫。
there is an alternative but the clock is ticking.
下個月，聯合國和美國將主辦新一輪難民峰會。
next month, the un and the united states will host another round of refugee summits.
在此次峰會上，政府可以拋棄車軲轆式的承諾和信誓旦旦的說辭，而應該拿出切實計劃兌現它們所承諾的14億美元。
this time, governments can leave their recycled promises and heady rhetoric at home instead, they should carry with them concrete plans to deliver the 1.4 billion they have already pledged.
國際社會還必須反思如何進行援助。
the international community must also rethink how aid is delivered.
敘利亞危機不會很快結束。
the syrian crisis will not end any time soon.
注資人不應該透過不可靠、資金不足的年度人道主義呼籲提供援助，而應該提供可預測的多年期融資，如英國所做的那樣。
instead of delivering aid through unreliable, underfunded annual humanitarian appeals, donors need to provide predictable multiyear funding, as the united kingdom has done.
更一般地說，歐盟和世界銀行應該擴大和強化它們對教育的支援。
more generally, the european union and the world bank should expand and intensify their support for education.
當然，更多的教育捐助融資只是一部分。
of course, more donor finance for education is only part of the equation.
東道國政府不管多麼捉襟見肘，總可以也應該多做一些。
there is more that hostcountry governments, however overstretched, can and should be doing.
首先，它們應該致力於打消敘利亞兒童所面臨的語言障礙。
for starters, they should be working to remove the language barriers facing syrian children.
它們還可以透過臨時招聘敘利亞難民教師來緩解教師嚴重不足的情況。
they could also address chronic teacher shortages through expedient recruitment of syrian refugee teachers.
最重要的是，東道國政府可以幫助難民更加安全和自立，這主要可以透過提高他們的法律地位和擴大他們的工作權利實現。
above all, host governments could help refugees become more secure and selfreliant, notably by upgrading their legal status and expanding the right to work.
但是，說到底，難民教育危機的可信應對措施必須包括更公平的負擔共擔機制。
ultimately, though, a credible response to the refugee education crisis must involve a fairer approach to burdensharing.
在下個月的聯合國峰會即將到來之際，各國政府應該回顧它們在倫敦會上作出的承諾。
before heading for the un summit treadmill next month, governments should review the promises they made at the london conference.
它們還應該回憶一下納爾遜·曼德拉的名言 ： “ 對兒童的承諾永遠不能破壞。 ”
and they should recall nelson mandelas dictum promises to children should never be broken.
從‘研究’到‘開發’的更好方法
a better way from r to d
華盛頓貝爾維尤 — — 在商業領袖匯聚一堂探討行業創新時，他們往往將重點放在改善基礎研究或建設技術中心及孵化器的政府資助行動上。
bellevue, washington when business leaders get together to talk about innovating their industries, they typically focus on initiatives like improving government funding for basic research, or building technology hubs and incubators.
但上述討論往往缺乏最終產品這一“創新”的關鍵元素。
but a crucial element of innovation is often absent from these discussions the final products.
這並非疏忽。
thats no oversight.
恰恰相反，缺乏以產品為核心的討論恰恰表明幾乎所有行業和大大小小的企業所面臨的問題要嚴重的多。
on the contrary, the lack of productfocused discussion is symptomatic of a far more serious problem facing businesses of all sizes in nearly every industry.
簡言之，產品開發在創新戰略中處於次要地位，因為創意和商業化之間的金融聯絡被切斷了。
simply put, product development takes a back seat in innovation strategy because the financial link between ideation and commercialization is broken.
要想實現經濟繁榮，需要推動好的理念走向市場。
for economies to prosper, good ideas need a nudge getting to market.
畢竟創新產品讓生活更健康、更高效也更快樂。
innovative products are, after all, what makes life healthier, more efficient, and more fun.
但有充分的證據表明開發 — — 也就是研發中的“發 ” — —並未能夠跟上“研究 ” — —也就是現代研究驚人的發展速度。
but theres ample evidence to suggest that development the d in rd has not kept pace with the blistering speed of r modernday research.
就連最強勁的經濟體也存在永遠無法接觸消費者的過剩的想法。
even the most robust economies have a surplus of ideas that never reach consumers.
比如在美國，僅有5%的活躍專利可以發放許可證或商業化。
in the us, for example, just 5 of all active patents are ever licensed or commercialized.
多數企業付諸應用的發明還不到其擁有專利的四分之一。
most companies use less than a quarter of the inventions they own.
學術界技術轉讓的形勢也同樣嚴峻。
technology transfers from academia arent going so well, either.
儘管自1969年以來美國大學已經被授予超過75，000項專利 — — 但絕大多數負責管理學校智慧財產權成果的技術轉讓部門所得收入甚至無法彌補其自身的運營支出。
although more than 75,000 patents have been issued to american universities since 1969, the vast majority of technology transfer offices administrative units that manage a schools intellectualproperty output are failing to generate enough revenue even to cover their operating costs.
如果想扭轉上述趨勢並最大限度地提高創新產出，我們需要更多機制來為聰明的理念提供商業化資助。
if we want to reverse these trends and maximize innovation output, we need more mechanisms for funding the commercialization of smart ideas.
目前，風險資本支援的創業企業是從研究轉向開發的標準機制。
at the moment, venture capitalbacked startups are the standard mechanism for moving from r to d.
這些企業成立的全部目的就是要推動好的理念進入開發渠道。
these companies are formed for the sole purpose of pushing good ideas through the development pipeline.
而且，考慮到某些創業企業估值很高，人們很容易認為由精明企業和風險投資資金所組成的健康生態系統是確保創新所需要的全部因素。
and, given the stellar valuations of some startups, its easy to assume that a healthy ecosystem of savvy companies and venture capital funding is all that is needed to ensure innovation.
但多數企業根本無法將好的理念推向市場，因為它們缺乏獲得創新資金的渠道。
but most companies are simply unable to take good ideas to market, because they lack access to pools of capital earmarked for innovation.
中小企業（SMEs）往往很難獲得融資來建設研發基礎設施。
small and mediumsize enterprises smes often struggle to secure financing to build rd infrastructure.
跨國企業利用留存收益作為研發資金，但因為這種方法可能對企業股票估值造成負面影響，所以就連他們往往都對推動新理念持保守態度。
multinational corporations use retained earnings to finance rd, but because this approach can adversely affect a companys stock valuation, even they tend to be conservative in pushing new ideas forward.
下面我們將這種方案與跨國公司融資基礎設施的投資方式進行比較。
compare that scenario with the way that multinationals finance infrastructure investments.
比方說，假設杜邦想要建設一家新的製造廠。
lets say, for example, that dupont wanted to build a new manufacturing facility.
它可以從銀行借款，之後用所得的利潤進行償付。
it could borrow money from a bank and repay it from resulting profits.
但如果杜邦需要資金在現有工廠生產一種新化學品，那麼它無法獲得貸款，因為銀行不知道創新產品的風險評估方法（無論是涉及化工行業還是其他 ） 。
but if dupont needed capital to produce a new chemical in an existing plant, it couldnt get a loan, because banks dont know how to assess the risks of innovative products in the chemical industry or any other.
除非你是像Alphabet、蘋果或特斯拉那樣的巨星企業，否則你無法證明一項藍天研發計劃是合理的。
unless youre a giant like alphabet, apple, or tesla, you cant justify the risk and expense of a bluesky rd program.
現在就連規模最大的企業也更樂意收購一項已經打包好的新技術，而不是進行內部研發。
these days even the biggest companies are more likely to acquire a new, prepackaged technology than to develop it inhouse.
這也是為什麼兼併和收購越來越普遍的一個理由（這還能夠解釋為什麼有些觀察家把兼併收購看成一種新的研發 ） 。
thats one reason why mergers and acquisitions are increasingly common and why some observers see mas as the new rd.
這種狀況對投資者而言同樣並不理想。
this situation isnt ideal for investors, either.
比如索尼公司的PlayStation遊戲機專案。
consider the case of sonys playstation gaming console.
PlayStation的研發在二十世紀九十年代吸引了投資者的廣泛關注。
development of the playstation attracted considerable attention from investors in the 1990s.
但支援研發計劃的唯一方法是購買母公司的股票 — — 而母公司還包括音樂、電影、相機和電視等業務。
but the only way to back the project was to buy shares in the parent companywhich encompassed music, film, camera, and television businesses as well.
這樣的錯配對企業而言像對投資者一樣低效。
this sort of misalignment is just as inefficient for companies as it is for investors.
而且對小企業這甚至算不上一項選擇；小企業出售股權難度很大。
and its not even an option for smaller companies selling equity is hard when youre an sme.
顯而易見，目前的融資模式扼殺了產品創新和投資，幾乎完全凍結了中小企業。
clearly, current funding models stifle productspecific innovation and investment, and all but freeze out smes.
與我談論這個問題的政府官員更關注保持國內中小企業的健康，而不是跨國企業的保護，他們這麼做理由非常充分：無論哪裡的中小企業都在就業和崗位創造方面都佔據絕大多數份額。
the government officials with whom i speak are more concerned with maintaining the health of their countries smes than protecting multinational corporations, for good reason smes everywhere account for an overwhelming share of employment and job creation.
但它們卻無法得到應有的融資機會。
yet they arent getting the financing opportunities they deserve.
為了扭轉這種局面，企業需要將融資工具與產品開發掛鉤。
to turn things around, businesses need financing vehicles tied to product development.
一種方法是設立債權基金，並將相關債券與可預測的新產品收入回報相掛鉤。
one idea is debtbased funds offering bonds with more predictable returns based on revenue from new products.
這類基金可以設計成在各類專案或行業之間分散風險，這可能提高它們對躲避高風險投資的投資者的吸引力。
these funds could be structured to distribute risk among a variety of projects or sectors, which might make them more attractive to investors who avoid highstakes venture financing.
這種基金也可以在投資人和創新專案之間達成更緊密的一致。
this kind of funding would also enable much closer alignment between investors and innovative projects.
擁有良好記錄、技術能力、經驗豐富的管理團隊和既有銷售渠道的企業是任何國家都不能浪費的創新資源。
companies with proven track records, technical skills, experienced management teams, and established sales channels are sources of innovation that no country can afford to squander.
現有融資機制的侷限性意味著國家正在白白浪費機會。
the limitations of the current financing regime mean that countries are letting opportunity pass them by.
儘管產品商業化現成的機會很少，但全世界的企業、研究機構、大學及政府實驗室合起來每年投入超過1萬億美元用於研發。
despite few ready avenues for product commercialization, the worlds companies, research institutes, and university and government laboratories together spend more than a trillion dollars on rd annually.
如果沒有產品融資的新方式，他們的多數發現都將被束之高閣。
without a new approach to product financing, most of what they discover will remain on the shelf.
美國領導力長盛不衰
americas enduring leadership
華盛頓—許多觀察者把烏克蘭危機作為美國全球影響力收縮和衰退的又一例證。
washington, dc many observers have cited the crisis in ukraine as yet another example of american retrenchment and declining global influence.
一些人還把它視為俄羅斯領銜動員主要新興經濟體 — — 巴西、印度和中國對抗西方的證據。
some have also interpreted it as evidence of a russianled effort to mobilize the major emerging economies brazil, india, and china against the west.
這兩種說法都不無道理，但都有些誇張，與此類似的還有美國決定和捍衛安全、繁榮的國際制度的能力正在衰退的觀點。
while there is a kernel of truth in both narratives, each is a gross exaggeration, as is the notion that americas capacity to shape a secure and prosperous international system is in decline.
美國最近幾年不是很順，在經歷了兩場漫長而艱苦的戰爭後，它開始從阿富汗緩慢地撤軍。
the us has had a rough few years. after two long, draining wars, its withdrawal from afghanistan is inching along slowly.
在敘利亞，俄羅斯和中國的從中作梗使美國無法找到外交解決途徑。
in syria, russian and chinese intransigence have frustrated its efforts to find a diplomatic solution.
中國在東海和南海自信心的日益增長正在威脅美國的地區主宰力，同時也給美國的緊密盟友日本帶來了危機風險。
and chinas growing assertiveness in the south and east china seas is threatening us regional dominance, while raising the risk of a crisis with americas close ally japan.
與此同時，美國的許多歐洲盟友陷入了經濟困境。
meanwhile, many of americas european allies are mired in economic malaise.
此外，儘管美國經濟正在從全球金融危機中復甦，但其財政狀況和名譽都遭到了重大打擊。
and, though the us economy is recovering from the global financial crisis, americas treasury and reputation has been dealt a severe blow.
儘管如此，美國仍是最有影響力的全球行動者 — — 不僅是因為它所保持的強大聯盟。
nonetheless, the us remains the most influential global actor not least because of the strong alliances that it maintains.
對中國經濟崛起的關注 — — 還有印度和巴西，儘管不如中國那樣耀眼 — — 讓人忽略了韓國、土耳其、印尼和德國等美國盟友的成功。
all of the attention given to chinas economic rise and, to a lesser extent, that of india and brazil has overshadowed the success of us allies like south korea, turkey, indonesia, and germany.
事實上，世界上最強盛經濟體絕大多數都是美國的盟友。
in fact, the vast majority of the worlds strongest economies are allied with the us.
此外，新興大國遠未結成反西方聯盟，而仍然各自為政。
moreover, far from coalescing into a united antiwestern bloc, the emerging powers remain sharply divided.
現有大國和新興大國之間存在著縱橫交錯的利益聯絡，緊密程度遠勝過“西方對抗其他國家”說；事實上，崛起大國與西方國家之間的共同利益往往不亞於它們彼此之間。
there are far more overlapping interests between the established and the emerging powers than the west versus the rest narrative suggests indeed, the rising powers often share as many interests with their western counterparts as they do with each other.
基於此，即便是非美國盟友的經濟超級大國也不想顛覆現有世界秩序，而是希望在其中獲得更大份額，比如增加在國際機構中的權威。
given this, even the economic powerhouses that are not us allies do not want to upend the existing world order, but rather to gain more space within it, such as through increased authority in international institutions.
畢竟，它們之所以崛起，正是因為它們融入了全球經濟體系中。
after all, they rose precisely by integrating themselves into the global economic system.
即使是有可能在某些領域削弱美國領導力的中國在許多外交政策問題上也別無選擇，只能與美國及其盟友合作。
even china, which arguably seeks to curtail us leadership in some domains, has no choice but to cooperate with the us and its allies on many foreignpolicy issues.
只有在其他國家追隨的情況下中國才能挑戰美國的領導力，而如今它很難找到追隨者。
china can challenge american leadership only if others follow it, and so far it has found few takers.
只有俄羅斯更積極地扮演著動搖性角色 — — 在全球金融危機、敘利亞和如今的烏克蘭都是如此。
only russia has sought to play a more destabilizing role during the global financial crisis, in syria, and now in ukraine.
平心而論，新興大國之間確實都有對抗傾向 — — 或至少有自主傾向 — — 這植根於可以被稱為“崛起心理”的東西。
to be sure, the emerging powers do share a strong inclination toward rivalry or at least toward autonomy which is rooted in what might be called the psychology of rise.
但它們知道，過於對抗性的反美立場會影響到它們在穩定的全球經濟中的利益，不利於它們的商品和恩呢高原在國際海運和空運路線安全通行。
but they know that an excessively aggressive stance toward the us would undermine their interest in a stable global economy and the safe passage of their goods and energy through international sea and air routes.
中國尤其如此，因為其國內穩定和國際影響力在很大程度上取決於其保持高速經濟增長的能力，這就需要日益大量的進口能源和其他天然資源。
this is particularly true for china, because its domestic stability and international influence depend largely on its ability to maintain rapid economic growth, which demands everlarger quantities of imported energy and other natural resources.
為了保證不受阻礙地獲得這些關鍵資源，中國需要資源來源國、投資市場目標國以及供給國與其本土之間航路的穩定性。
to ensure unimpeded access to these critical resources, china needs stability in the countries from which it can extract them, in the markets in which it can invest, and in the routes linking china to its suppliers.
但中國維持這些條件的能力非常有限 — — 在一些地區（如波斯灣 ） ， 它嚴重依賴美國的軍事實力。
but chinas capacity to maintain these conditions is extremely limited and in some cases as in the persian gulf, it is heavily dependent on us military power.
簡言之，在推動敵對和鼓勵剋制之間尋找平衡是當代國際關係最重要的動態。
in short, striking a balance between the impulse toward rivalry and incentives encouraging restraint is the most important dynamic in contemporary international affairs.
而如今，全球平衡正在導向剋制。
and, for now, the global balance is tipping toward restraint.
當然，美國將一直面臨新挑戰，烏克蘭就是明證。
of course, the us will invariably face new challenges, all of which are on vivid display in ukraine.
各國將在維持與美國的安全聯絡以及構建與中國的新經濟聯絡之間權衡。
countries will be torn between retaining their security ties to the us and building new economic linkages with china.
讓美國利益牽涉其中的複雜的全球體系將考驗美國外交。
the complex global systems in which americas interests are enmeshed will test us diplomacy.
也許最危險的挑戰是新興大國越來越傾向於自主而非結盟。
perhaps the most dangerous challenge is the prospect of emerging powers leaning increasingly toward autonomy, instead of alliance.
中國和印度或許不滿於俄羅斯在烏克蘭的行動，但新興經濟體都不會在聯合國安理會上投票反對俄羅斯，即使投票說到底沒有什麼意義。
china and india may not have been happy about russias actions in ukraine, but none of the emerging economies could bring itself to vote against russia in the united nations general assembly, even though the vote was ultimately meaningless.
（中國在安理會中最喜歡棄權。
china took the strongest position in the security council by abstaining.
）它們不與俄羅斯穿一條褲子；但也不加入西方陣營孤立俄羅斯。
they are not sticking with russia but they are not joining a western effort to isolate russia, either.
但是，最終，不斷演化的世界有利於美國最重要的優勢：與範圍廣泛、相關性極低的國家結成聯盟的獨特能力。
ultimately, however, the worlds relentless evolution plays to americas most important strength its unique ability to build broad and disparate coalitions.
美國所建立的聯盟和關係範圍 — — 包括其與一些崛起大國之間的關係 — — 是任何其他全球行動方無法比擬的，並且在可預見的未來繼續保持這一優勢。
the range of alliances and relationships that the us has created, including with several of the rising powers, far surpasses that of any other global actor and will continue to do so for the foreseeable future.
這或許是美國實力最長盛不衰的特徵。
this is perhaps the most enduring feature of american power.
不可否認，美國已不再享有冷戰結束時無人可以撼動的超級大國地位。
there is no denying that the us no longer enjoys the unrivaled hyperpower status that it did at the end of the cold war.
但是，隨著時間的流逝，國際體系仍由美國領導。
but, for the time being, the international system remains americas to lead.
泡沫的測定
bubble spotting
發自紐黑文 — — 作為一個在市場投機方面略有論述的評論者，人們總會問我：下一場大規模投機泡沫何時發生？
new haven people frequently ask me, as someone who has written on market speculation, where the next big speculative bubble is likely to be.
是在住宅市場捲土重來，還是轉移到股票市場興風作浪？
will it be in housing again? will it be in the stock market?
雖然我對此總會有一些預感，但也無法給出答案，事實上根本沒人能準確預測泡沫的來臨。
i dont know, though i have some hunches. it is impossible for anyone to predict bubbles accurately.
在我看來，泡沫是一種社會流行病，由某種人與人之間的互相傳染而催生。
in my view, bubbles are social epidemics, fostered by a sort of interpersonal contagion.
當某種觀念的“傳染率”升高到足以支撐泡沫的程度，泡沫便應運而生了，問題是這種傳染率的高低取決於人們的思維模式，而後者是極難進行判斷的。
a bubble forms when the contagion rate goes up for ideas that support a bubble. but contagion rates depend on patterns of thinking, which are difficult to judge.
大規模的投機泡沫其實極少發生。
big speculative bubbles are rare events.
（類似某隻股票的股價這樣的小型價格泡沫則是家常便飯，也不能作為問題的答案。
little bubbles, in the price of, say, individual stocks, happen all the time, and dont qualify as an answer to the question.
）與此同時，由於大規模泡沫往往持續經年，預測它們就等於要預測未來數年內會發生何事，難度堪比預測兩屆大選過後的美國總統人選。
and, because big bubbles last for many years, predicting them means predicting many years in the future, which is a bit like predicting who will be running the government two elections from now.
但有些領域似乎比其他領域更容易產生泡沫。
but some places appear a little more likely than others to give rise to bubbles.
股票市場在邏輯上首當其中，因為這是個高槓杆投資行為 — — 而且自誕生以來就不乏泡沫。
the stock market is the first logical place to look, as it is a highly leveraged investment and has a history of bubbles.
該市場光在上個世紀就出現了3次大規模資產泡沫：1920年代，1960年代和1990年代。
there have been three colossal stockmarket bubbles in the last century the 1920s, the 1960s, and the 1990s.
相比之下美國的住宅市場在過去這100年只有一次泡沫，那是在21世紀的第一個十年。
in contrast, there has been only one such bubble in the united states housing market in the last hundred years, that of the 2000s.
全球股票市場已經從2009年的谷底實現了徹底反彈。
we have had a huge rebound from the bottom of the worlds stock markets in 2009.
標準普爾500指數已較2009年3月9日的點位實質上漲了87 % 。
the sp 500 is up 87 in real terms since march 9 of that year.
但當屢戰屢敗的股票市場預測者們嘗試判斷這場反彈還能持續多久的時候，它其實不像是一場泡沫，而更像是某種蕭條恐慌的終結。
but, while the history of stockmarket prediction is littered with too much failure to try to decide whether the bounceback will continue much longer, it doesnt look like a bubble, but more like the end of a depression scare.
股票價格的上漲並未伴隨著人們口耳相傳的“新時代”財富故事，卻更像是一場“死裡逃生”的歷險記。
the rise in equity prices has not come with a contagious new era story, but rather a sigh of relief story.
同樣，世界某些地方（特別是中國，巴西和加拿大）的住宅價格也在過去一兩年出現了可觀上漲，而另外許多地方的房價也有上漲的可能。
likewise, home prices have been booming over the past year or two in several places, notably china, brazil, and canada, and prices could still be driven up in many other places.
但那些剛剛遭遇房價泡沫爆破的國家則不太會產生另一場房價泡沫,因為趨向保守的政府政策可能會減少對住房的補貼，而這些國家當前的市場氣氛似乎也無法催生泡沫。
but another housing bubble is not imminent in countries where one just burst. conservative government policies will probably reduce subsidies to housing, and the current mood in these markets does not seem conducive to a bubble.
不過當今的商品價格上漲則更可能持續下去，因為它身上更多地附著有一個“新時代”故事的光環。
a continuation of todays commodityprice boom seems more likely, for it has more of a new era story attached to it.
對全球變暖及其對食品價格影響的擔憂，以及北半球寒冷冬天及其對取暖用油價格影響的恐懼都成為了人們之間流傳的故事，甚至與當今的頭條新聞 — — 中東革命 — — 聯絡了起來，因為某些說法認為革命是被大眾對高食品價格的不滿所激發的 — — 而且還會因此引發油價的進一步上漲。
increasing worries about global warming, and its effects on food prices, or about the cold and snowy winter in the northern hemisphere and its effects on heating fuel prices, are contagious stories. they are even connected to the days top story, the revolutions in the middle east, which, according to some accounts, were triggered by popular discontent over high food prices and which could themselves trigger further increases in oil prices.
但我在未來十年最看好的潛在泡沫黑馬則是農地 — — 但這項判斷不僅僅是由美英兩國近幾個月農地價格上漲而得出的。
but my favorite darkhorse bubble candidate for the next decade or so is farmland and not just because there have been stories in recent months of booming farmland prices in the us and the united kingdom.
農地在重要性上顯然比不上其他投機資產。
of course, farmland is much less important than other speculative assets.
比如美國全國的農地在2010年總值約為1.9萬億美元，而股票市場和住宅市場則分別高達16.5萬億和16.6萬億美元。
for example, u.s. farmland had a total value of 1.9 trillion in 2010, compared with 16.5 trillion for the us stock market and 16.6 trillion for the us housing market.
同時大規模的農地泡沫也非常罕見：在20世紀的美國僅僅發生過一次，那是在1970年代人們恐慌人口過度暴增的時期。
and largescale farmland bubbles are quite rare there was only one in the us in the entire twentieth century, during the great population scare of the 1970s.
但農地，至少是某些特定地區的農地，如今正流傳著一個極富傳染性的“新時代”故事。
but, farmland, at least in certain places, seems to have the most contagious new era story right now.
美國農地的價格在過去十年曾經發生過巨大上漲，在到達2008年的頂點時已經實質上漲了74 % 。
it was recently booming, up 74 in real terms in the us in the decade ending with its price peak, in 2008.
而急劇流傳的全球變暖故事則向人們描繪了一幅食品短缺以及世界各地土地價值重估的圖景，而這將促使投資者進一步加大投資。
and the highly contagious globalwarming story paints a scenario of food shortages and shifts in land values in different parts of the world, which might boost investor interest further.
此外，如今的人們很容易會以為住宅和農地市場會經常聯動，因為在2000年之後那幾年兩者都同時上漲。
moreover, people nowadays easily imagine that the housing and farmland markets always move together, because prices in both boomed in recent memory, in the early 2000s.
但美國住宅和農地價格在1911年到2010年間的相關性其實只有區區5 % ， 而最新的農地價格資料也並沒有像住宅價格那樣下跌。
but, from 1911 to 2010 in the us, the correlation between annual real growth of prices for homes and farmland was only 5, and the latest data on farm prices have not shown anything like the decline in home prices.
截止至2010年，美國農地的實際價格較2008年最高點僅僅下跌了5 % ， 而住宅實際價格較2006年的最高點已經跌去了37 % 。
by 2010, real farm prices in the us had fallen only 5 from their 2008 peak, compared to the 37 decline in real home prices since their peak in 2006.
2000年以來的住宅價格上漲更可能是源於建築行業的供應瓶頸（無法足夠迅速地滿足市場的投資需要）並被（在某些地方將被）隨之湧出的大量供應所抵消。
the housingprice boom of the 2000s was little more than a constructionsupply bottleneck, an inability to satisfy investment demand fast enough, and was or in some places will be eliminated with massive increases in supply.
相比之下農地的供應卻沒有增加，而激發人們投資熱情廣泛流傳的故事正大行其道，正如1970年代的美國，一場類似的食品價格恐慌催生了上世紀唯一的一場農地價格泡沫。
by contrast, there has been no increase in the supply of farmland, and the stories that would support a contagion of enthusiasm for it are in place, just as they were in the 1970s in the us, when a similar foodprice scare generated the centurys only farmland bubble.
儘管如此，我們還是要將預測泡沫的困難之處牢記於心。
still, we must always bear in mind the difficulty of forecasting bubbles.
而對於那些勇敢的投資者來說，光找到一場泡沫並投身其中是不夠的，還必須決定何時要將這些泡沫中抽身離開，並將資金轉投到另一個領域。
and, for daring investors, it is not enough to find a bubble to pile into. they must also try to determine when to cash out and put their money elsewhere.
泡沫的麻煩
bubble trouble
房地產繁榮的未來以及未來數年價格大跌可能帶來的金融影響已經越來越引起世界各國政府的擔心。
the future of the housing boom, and the possible financial repercussions of a substantial price decline in coming years, is a matter of mounting concern among governments around the world.
我在參加今年在懷俄明州遙遠的荒野舉行的Jackson Hole會議瞭解了有關這方面的第一手資訊。 具有諷刺意味的是，那裡幾乎沒有房子可買。
i learned this firsthand while attending this years jackson hole symposium in the remote wilderness of wyoming, where, ironically, there are almost no homes to buy.
夜晚可以聽到郊狼和駝鹿的叫聲。
the howls of coyotes and bugling of elk rang out at night.
但是，白天大家談論的都是房地產問題。
but, by day, everyone was talking about real estate.
該會議已經發展成為各國政府貨幣政策制定者的重要國際聚會，今年的會議有來自34個國家的中央銀行的行長或副行長參加。
this conference has grown to be a major international event for government monetary policymakers, with governors or deputy governors of 34 central banks attending this year.
這些國家中大約有三分之二自2000年以來經歷了房地產的高度繁榮，其中絕大多數的繁榮看上去還會繼續下去，至少從目前來看是如此。
roughly twothirds of these countries have had dramatic housing booms since 2000, most of which appear to be continuing, at least for the time being.
但是大家對於房價的長期走勢看法卻不盡相同。
but there was no consensus on the longerrun outlook for home prices.
在所有這些國家中，美國看上去最有可能已經達到了一個迴圈的終點。
of all these countries, the united states appears to be the most likely to have reached the end of the cycle.
根據標準普爾Case-Shiller美國全國房價指數，美國的房價在1996-2006年之間去除通貨膨脹的影響實際上升了86 % ， 但是此後已經下降了6.5 % ， 並且下降的幅度還在加快。
according to the standard poorscaseshiller us national home price index, us home prices increased 86 in real, inflationcorrected, terms from 1996 to 2006, but have since fallen 6.5 and the rate of decrease has been accelerating.
看上去一段繁榮的結束已經開始了，儘管你永遠不能對此下定論。
that looks like the beginning of the end of the boom, though, of course, one can never be sure.
我提出熊市觀點，就是房價從長期來看將持續下跌，儘管許多人提出質疑，但是顯然沒有人能說服對方。
i presented a bearish longrun view, which many challenged, but no one obviously won the argument.
然而，一個局外觀察者也許會對如此多的人認定為期10年的繁榮可能會遭受一次真正的倒轉並且隨之引發房價的暴跌而感到震驚。
nevertheless, an outside observer might have been struck by the weight given to the possibility that the decadelong boom might well suffer a real reversal, followed by serious declines.
大家似乎公認存在實質性的不利風險，因為目前的信貸危機似乎與我們已經看到的美國房價的下跌相關。
there seems to be a general recognition of substantial downside risk, as the current credit crisis seems to be related to the decline in us home prices that we have already seen.
房地產的繁榮，以及大家普遍相信房價只會越來越高，導致了借貸標準的降低。
the boom, and the widespread conviction that home prices could only go higher, led to a weakening of lending standards.
抵押借貸者似乎已經認定房屋購買者不會拖欠還款，因為越來越高的價格會使得按期歸還貸款變得極有吸引力。
mortgage lenders seem to have believed that home buyers would not default, because rising prices would make keeping up with their payments very attractive.
此外，繁榮帶來了大量的金融創新產品，它們從內在來看也許是好的，但是如果考慮到跌價的風險，它們有時應用得有點過分自信了。
moreover, the boom resulted in a number of financial innovations, which may have been good ideas intrinsically, but which were sometimes applied too aggressively, given the risk of falling prices.
抵押支援證券被推銷給對於他們來說有點冒險的投資者。
mortgagebacked securities were urged onto investors for whom they were too risky.
而對於購房者來說，一切都會很好，其推理的基礎是房價會繼續以健康的步伐持續上升。
as with homebuyers, all would be well, the reasoning went, on the premise that home prices continue to rise at a healthy pace.
在Jackson Hole會議上，世界上最大的債券基金太平洋投資管理公司的Paul McCulley說，在過去的一兩個月我們已經看到了他所謂的“影子銀行系統”的運作。 影子銀行系統由伴隨這房地產的繁榮湧現出來的所有槓桿投資渠道、媒介和結構組成。
at the jackson hole conference, paul mcculley of pimco, the worlds largest bond fund, argued that in the past month or two we have been witnessing a run on what he calls the shadow banking system, which consists of all the levered investment conduits, vehicles and structures that have sprung up along with the housing boom.
它處於銀行監管者以及儲蓄保險的控制之外，透過幫助向購買者提供更多的信用來享受房價的暴漲所帶來的利益。
the shadow banking system, which is beyond the reach of bank regulators and deposit insurance, fed the boom in home prices by helping provide more credit to buyers.
當人們擔心他們在銀行的存款得不到支付而急切地取回他們的錢時就會發生銀行的擠提現象，而這正好帶來他們所擔心的破產。
bank runs occur when people, worried that their deposits will not be honored, hastily withdraw their money, thereby creating the very bankruptcy that they feared.
這種新型的擠提最早發生在美國並不是一個巧合，因為它是當今世界的房價下跌的最好例子。
it is no coincidence that this new kind of bank run originated in the us, which is the clearest example of falling home prices in the world today.
當房價停止上升，最近的房屋購買者也許會失去繼續歸還他們的抵押貸款的信心，而投資者會對抵押支援證券失去信心。
when home prices stop rising, recent homebuyers may lose the enthusiasm to continue paying their mortgages and investors lose faith in mortgagebacked securities.
美聯儲有時被指責應該對目前的抵押貸款危機負責，因為它所實行的寬鬆的貨幣政策被認為刺激了此前的價格上漲。
the us federal reserve is sometimes blamed for the current mortgage crisis, because excessively loose monetary policy allegedly fueled the price boom that preceded it.
事實上，從2002年10月至2005年4月這31個月的實際（去除通貨膨脹的影響）聯邦基金利率是負的。
indeed, the real inflationcorrected federal funds rate was negative for 31 months, from october 2002 to april 2005.
自1950年以來這樣的情況僅僅在1974年9月至1977年9月這37個月發生過，這是上個世紀美國發生最嚴重通貨膨脹的階段。
the only precedent for this since 1950 was the 37month period from september 1974 to september 1977, which launched the worst inflation the us has seen in the last century.
當時導致消費品價格上漲的情況現在引發了房屋價格的上漲。
what then helped produce a boom in consumer prices now contributed to a boom in home prices.
但是寬鬆的貨幣政策並不是所有的問題所在。
but loose monetary policy is not the whole story.
美國房地產繁榮所帶來的超低的實際基金利率已經存在很長一段時間了。
the unusually low real funds rate came after the us housing boom was already well underway.
根據標準普爾Case-Shiller美國全國房價指數，房價在2000年已經幾乎上漲了10 % ， 同期美聯儲將聯邦基金利率提到了6.5%的最高水平。
according to the standard poorscaseshiller us national home price index, home prices were already rising at almost 10 a year in 2000 a time when the fed was raising the federal funds rate, which peaked at 6.5.
於是房價的快速上升看起來很可能是利率降低前投機衝動的表現。
the rapid increase thus appears to be mostly the result of speculative momentum that occurred before the interestrate cuts.
美聯儲前主席格林斯潘最近說他現在認為投機泡沫是我們經濟的重要驅動力，但是與此同時世界各國的貨幣主管部門無法控制泡沫。
alan greenspan, the former fed chairman, recently said that he now believes that speculative bubbles are important driving forces in our economy, but that, at the same time, the worlds monetary authorities cannot control bubbles.
他在很大程度是對的：考慮到它們其他需要優先考慮的事情和擔憂，貨幣主管部門能採取的最好辦法就是倚靠房地產的繁榮，而不是阻礙它的膨脹。
he is mostly right the best thing that monetary authorities could have done, given their other priorities and concerns, is to lean against the real estate bubble, not stop it from inflating.
目前房價的下跌很明顯是與投資者投機熱情的消退相聯絡，而在很大程度上與貨幣政策並沒有聯絡。
the current decline in home prices is associated just as clearly with waning speculative enthusiasm among investors, which is likewise largely unrelated to monetary policy.
世界各國的貨幣主管部門將很難制止這種下跌以及解決參與房地產泡沫的人士的所面臨的困難，正如它們很難在房價上漲前制止它一樣。
the worlds monetary authorities will have trouble stopping this decline, and much of the attendant problems, just as they would have had trouble stopping the ascent that preceded it.
建立一個漸進性的國際體系
building a progressive international
發自雅典 — — 西方發達經濟體的政治局面目前處於自1930年代以來首次出現的動盪之中。
athens politics in the advanced economies of the west is in the throes of a political shakeup unseen since the 1930s.
侵襲大西洋兩岸的嚴重通貨緊縮正在喚醒那些在二戰後沉睡的政治力量。
the great deflation now gripping both sides of the atlantic is reviving political forces that had lain dormant since the end of world war ii.
政治生活再次充斥著激情 — — 但卻並非是以許多人所希望的方式。
passion is returning to politics, but not in the manner many of us had hoped it would.
右派勢力陷入了反體制的狂熱之中，即便這原本是左派的專利。
the right has become animated by an antiestablishment fervor that was, until recently, the preserve of the left.
在美國，共和黨總統候選人唐納德·特朗普（Donald Trump）大肆攻擊其民主黨對手希拉里·克林頓（Hillary Clinton）與華爾街關係密切、鼓吹入侵外國領土並準備接受已經拉低了數百萬工人生活水平的自由貿易協定 — — 而且似乎有理有據。
in the united states, donald trump, the republican presidential nominee, is taking hillary clinton, his democratic opponent, to task quite credibly for her close ties to wall street, eagerness to invade foreign lands, and readiness to embrace freetrade agreements that have undermined millions of workers living standards.
而在英國，脫歐使得那些撒切爾夫人的右派支持者搖身一變成為了國民醫療服務的熱情擁護者。
in the united kingdom, brexit has cast ardent thatcherites in the role of enthusiastic defenders of the national health service.
這一轉變並非史無前例。
this shift is not unprecedented.
民粹主義右派在通貨緊縮時期就接受過準左派的理論。
the populist right has traditionally adopted quasileftist rhetoric in times of deflation.
任何一個願意捏著鼻子重溫1920~30年代法西斯和納粹首領演講 — — 包括貝尼託·墨索里尼（Benito Mussolini）對社會保障體系的讚頌和約瑟夫·戈培爾（Joseph Goebbels）對金融部門的尖銳批評 — — 的人都會發現，乍一看來這些呼聲和漸進性目標似乎並無區別。
anyone who can stomach revisiting the speeches of leading fascists and nazis of the 1920s and 1930s will find appeals benito mussolinis paeans to social security or joseph goebbels stinging criticism of the financial sector that seem, at first glance, indistinguishable from progressive goals.
當前我們遇到的是中間派政治崩潰所產生的自然反應，而導致這一切的則是全球資本主義危機 — — 金融危機導致經濟大蕭條再到如今的大通縮。
what we are experiencing today is the natural repercussion of the implosion of centrist politics, owing to a crisis of global capitalism in which a financial crash led to a great recession and then to todays great deflation.
那些右派不過是簡單地故伎重演，利用受害者對合乎道義的憤怒及沮喪情緒來推動自身臭不可聞的政治議程。
the right is simply repeating its old trick of drawing upon the righteous anger and frustrated aspirations of the victims to advance its own repugnant agenda.
這一切都始於1944年佈雷頓森林體系中建立的國際貨幣體系 — — 基於“混合”經濟，對不平等狀況的遏制以及強大的金融監管的戰後政治共識 — — 的崩潰。
it all began with the death of the international monetary system established at bretton woods in 1944, which had forged a postwar political consensus based on a mixed economy, limits on inequality, and strong financial regulation.
這個“黃金時期”在1971年發生的所謂“尼克松衝擊”中走向終結，美國也同時失去了維持全球資本主義穩定的從全球各地回收的順差。
that golden era ended with the socalled nixon shock in 1971, when america lost the surpluses that, recycled internationally, kept global capitalism stable.
值得注意的是，美國在二戰後期的霸權增長是與其貿易和預算赤字增長同步的。
remarkably, americas hegemony grew in this second postwar phase, in parallel with its trade and budget deficits.
但是為了融資以維持赤字，銀行必須從羅斯福新政和佈雷頓森林體系的約束中解放出來。
but to keep financing these deficits, bankers had to be unleashed from their new deal and bretton woods restraints.
只有這樣，他們才能鼓勵和管理支撐美國的財政和經常賬戶雙赤字所需的向內資本流動。
only then would they encourage and manage the inward capital flows needed to finance americas twin fiscal and currentaccount deficits.
當年經濟金融化是目標，新自由主義是它的意識形態外衣，保羅·沃爾克（Paul Volcker）時代的美聯儲加息則是它的 觸發器，總統比爾·克林頓（Bill Clinton）在位時最為接近這種浮士德式的魔鬼交易。
financialization of the economy was the goal, neoliberalism was its ideological cloak, the paul volckerera federal reserves interestrate hikes were its trigger, and president bill clinton was the ultimate closer of the faustian bargain.
當年的時機也再合適不過了：蘇聯帝國的崩潰和中國的對外開放為全球資本主義帶來海量的勞動力供給 — — 額外多出近十億工人 — — 令利潤暴增並扼殺了所有西方國家勞動者的���資增長。
and the timing couldnt have been more congenial the soviet empires collapse and chinas opening generated a surge of labor supply for global capitalism a billion additional workers that boosted profits and stifled wage growth throughout the west.
極端金融化的結果是巨大的不平等和深層次的脆弱性。
the result of extreme financialization was enormous inequality and profound vulnerability.
但至少西方工人階級獲得了廉價貸款和房價升值來抵消工資增長停滯和財政轉移支付減少的影響。
but at least the wests working class had access to cheap loans and inflated house prices to offset the impact of stagnant wages and declining fiscal transfers.
隨後爆發的2008年金融危機令美國和歐洲產生了大規模的資金和人員供應過剩。
then came the crash of 2008, which in the us and europe produced a massive excess supply of both money and people.
縱使許多人失去了工作，家庭和希望，卻有數萬億美元存款在各個全球金融中心之間流轉，除此之外還有數萬億美元被絕望的央行抽出來緊急置換金融家造成的爛賬。
while many lost jobs, homes, and hopes, trillions of dollars in savings have been sloshing around the worlds financial centers ever since, on top of more trillions pumped out by desperate central banks eager to replace the financiers toxic money.
由於公司和機構投資者都不敢投資實體經濟，股價迅速飆升，令社會金字塔尖的前0.1％的人喜出望外，而其餘的人只能無望地看著那些憤怒的葡萄 “ . . . . . . 不斷膨脹和長大，直到採摘的那一刻。
with companies and institutional players too frightened to invest in the real economy, share prices have boomed, the top 0.1 cant believe their luck, and the rest are helplessly watching as the grapes of wrath are filling and growing heavy, growing heavy for the vintage.
結果在美國和歐洲都有一大批負債累累且失去希望的人 — — 隨時可能被特朗普的恐慌言論，法國國民陣線領導人馬琳·勒龐（Marine Le Pen）的仇外心理，或英國脫歐支持者憧憬不列顛重新掌權的偉大願景所誘惑。
and so it was that large chunks of humanity in america and europe became too indebted and too expensive to be anything other than discarded and ready to be lured by trumps fearmongering, french national front leader marine le pens xenophobia, or the brexiteers shimmering vision of a britannia ruling the waves again.
隨著他們的數量不斷增加，傳統的政黨不斷衰落，由兩個新的政治集團 取而代之。
as their number grows, traditional political parties are fading into irrelevance, supplanted by the emergence of two new political blocs.
其中一個集團代表的是自由化、全球化和金融化的舊三駕馬車。
one bloc represents the old troika of liberalization, globalization, and financialization.
它可能仍舊掌權，但其實力正迅速下降，正如戴維·卡梅倫（David Cameron ） 、 歐洲的社會民主主義者、歐盟委員會、希拉里·克林頓，甚至希臘被注資援助後的激進左翼聯盟政府所展現的那樣。
it may still be in power, but its stock is falling fast, as david cameron, europes social democrats, hillary clinton, the european commission, and even greeces postcapitulation syriza government can attest.
而特朗普、勒龐、英國右翼脫歐論者，波蘭和匈牙利兩國的反自由化政府和俄羅斯總統普京（Vladimir Putin）正在形成另一個集團。
trump, le pen, britains rightwing brexiteers, polands and hungarys illiberal governments, and russian president vladimir putin are forming the second bloc.
他們構成了一種民族主義國際體系 — — 典型的通貨緊縮時期的產物 — — 集結了那些對自由民主制度的牴觸情緒以及足以摧毀這一制度的力量。
theirs is a nationalist international a classic creature of a deflationary period united by contempt for liberal democracy and the ability to mobilize those who would crush it.
這兩個集團之間的衝突既真實又存在誤導性。
the clash between these two blocs is both real and misleading.
克林頓與特朗普之間存在一場真正的戰爭，就像歐盟迎戰英國脫歐支持者；但對戰雙方與其說是敵人，不如說是同謀，他們之間維持著一個相互強化的無限迴圈，雙方都用其反對的東西來定義自身並以此動員其支持者。
clinton vs. trump constitutes a genuine battle, for example, as does the european union vs. the brexiteers but the combatants are accomplices, not foes, in perpetuating an endless loop of mutual reinforcement, with each side defined by and mobilizing its supporters on the basis of what it opposes.
逃離這個政治陷阱的唯一方法是漸進式的國際體系，這是建立在團結遍佈世界各地希望在全球重建民主政治的大多數人的基礎上的。
the only way out of this political trap is progressive internationalism, based on solidarity among large majorities around the world who are prepared to rekindle democratic politics on a planetary scale.
這聽起來很烏托邦，但值得強調的是，所有原材料都是現成可用的。
if this sounds utopian, it is worth emphasizing that the raw materials are already available.
美國伯尼·桑德斯（Bernie Sanders）的“政治革命 ” ， 傑里米·科爾賓（Jeremy Corbyn）對英國工黨的領導，歐洲的DiEM25（歐洲民主運動組織 ） ： 這些都是國際進步運動的預兆，也可以被定義構建民主政治的智力基礎。
bernie sanderss political revolution in the us, jeremy corbyns leadership of the uks labour party, diem25 the democracy in europe movement on the continent these are the harbingers of an international progressive movement that can define the intellectual terrain upon which democratic politics must build.
但是我們正處於一個初級階段，面臨著來自全球三駕馬車的強力反擊：民主黨全國委員會對桑德斯的攻擊，一個前製藥廠說客對科爾賓領導地位的挑戰，或是試圖因為我反對歐盟的希臘計劃而起訴我的行為。
but we are at an early stage and face a remarkable backlash from the global troika witness sanders treatment by the democratic national committee, the run against corbyn by a former pharmaceutical lobbyist, and the attempt to have me indicted for daring to oppose the eus plan for greece.
大規模的通貨緊縮帶來一個極大的問題：人類能否設計和實現一個新的、技術先進的“綠色”佈雷頓森林體系 — — 一個使我們的地球生態和經濟可持續發展的系統 — — 而無需引發原有佈雷頓森林體系建立之前的那種大範圍人民疾苦和破壞效應？
the great deflation poses a great question can humanity design and implement a new, technologically advanced, green bretton woods a system that makes our planet ecologically and economically sustainable without the mass pain and destruction preceding the original bretton woods?
如果我們 — — 漸進式的國際主義者 — — 無法回答這個問題，那又有誰能回答？
if we progressive internationalists wont answer that question, who will?
要知道目前正在西方爭權奪利的兩個政治集團甚至都不希望這個問題被提出的。
neither of the two political blocs now vying for power in the west even wants it to be posed.
構建一個安全的奈米技術的未來
building a safe nanotechnology future
根據某些人的觀點我們即將迎來一場奈米技術革命，在那裡物體被以比人眼所能看到的小几千倍的尺寸製造，而我們熟悉的材料將會有令人意外的表現。
we are living according to some on the brink of a nanotechnology revolution, where matter is engineered at a scale thousands of times smaller than the eye can see, and familiar materials behave in unexpected ways.
這場革命如果成功的話，將會顛覆整個世界。
this revolution, if successful, will turn our world upside down.
奈米技術提高了我們對材料的控制以及提供了提高現有技術和開發新技術的機會。
nanotechnology gives us increasing control over the material world, providing opportunities to enhance existing technologies and develop new ones.
從建造更強、更輕的材料和製造功能極強但難以置信地小的電腦到開發新的可持續能源和設計個人化的癌症治療方案，這裡看上去有無限的機會。
the opportunities seem endless, from building stronger, lighter materials and manufacturing tremendously powerful yet incredibly small computers, to developing new sustainable energy sources and devising personalized cures for cancer.
現在市場上有超過500種不同製造商宣稱生產的奈米技術消費產品，從化妝品到汽車零件以及餐具，應有盡有。
more than 500 manufactureridentified nanotechnology consumer products are now on the market, from cosmetics to car parts to tableware. by 2014 an estimated 2.6 trillion in manufactured goods around the world or 15 of total global output will use this technology, building on the research of scientists in some 100 nations around the world.
如果現在的預測正確，那麼奈米技術將有可能對每一個行業以及我們生活中的方方面面都產生影響。
if current projections are right, nanotechnology has the potential to have an impact on nearly every industry and virtually every aspect of our lives.
然而奈米技術也在顛覆著我們對什麼東西是有害的認識。
yet nanotechnology is also shaking up our understanding of what makes something harmful.
在奈米範圍（大約比人的頭髮絲的寬度小5萬倍）上，物體的表現並不像尋常那樣：弱的物質變強了，惰性的物質變得活躍了，而良性的物質變得有害了。
at the nanometer scale about 50,000 times smaller than the width of a human hair, matter behaves in unusual ways weak materials become strong, inert materials become active, and benign materials become harmful.
以同樣的方式鐵可以被製造成像長柄平底煎鍋和劍這樣不同的產品，奈米技術產品的有用或有害完全要看它們在奈米範圍上是怎樣被製作的。
in the same way that iron can be made into products as different as skillets and swords, the usefulness or harmfulness of nanotechnology products depends on how they are crafted at the nanometer scale.
其結果是，我們不能再依賴傳統上單單根據原材料來界定危險的方式了。
as a result, we can no longer rely on conventional ways of managing risk that are based on the raw materials alone.
隨著使用奈米技術的產品越來越多，我們需要了解它們可能帶來的危險的新的科學資訊。
as the number of products using nanotechnology continues to grow, we need new scientific information on the risks that they might present.
政府、工業、學術界和其他地方的專家認為如果我們想儘可能安全地開發奈米技術那就要解決一長串的問題。
experts in government, industry, academia, and elsewhere agree that a long list of questions needs to be addressed if we are to develop nanotechnology as safely as possible.
我們面臨的挑戰是尋找到能夠使生產者和管理者作出合理的、有科學依據的決策以及建立一個能讓消費者放心的監管體系的答案。
the challenge we face is to find answers that will enable producers and regulators to make sound, sciencebased decisions, and to develop an oversight system that inspires consumer confidence.
不幸的是，迄今為止全球對於這一挑戰的回應並不那麼積極。
unfortunately, the global response to this challenge has not been overwhelming.
2005年，伍德羅威爾遜國際學者中心新興奈米技術計劃考察了由政府資助的對於奈米技術的環境、健康和安全影響的研究專案。
in 2005, the woodrow wilson international center for scholars project on emerging nanotechnologies looked closely at governmentfunded research addressing the environmental, health, and safety impact of nanotechnology.
在高度相關的研究上的投資非常低：在美國，這方面的投資大約只佔聯邦在奈米技術的研究和開發上的11億美元投資的1 % 。
investment in highly relevant research was low in the united states, it was only an estimated 1 of the 1.1 billion federal investment in nanotechnology research and development.
更令人擔心的是注資進行研究的背後明顯缺乏任何策略的現象。
more worrying was the apparent absence of any strategy behind the research being funded.
即便少得可憐的探索可能存在的危險的相關研究也缺乏明確的研究方向，無法令人相信其所開發出的資訊能夠幫助決策者確保奈米技術被長期安全地開發。
even the small handful of relevant studies exploring possible risks lacked a guiding focus, giving no indication that the information developed would help decisionmakers ensure that nanotechnology is developed safely over the long term.
美國在推動支援使用奈米技術的研究戰略上表現得非常成功，並且樹立了被全世界廣泛仿效的典型。
the us has been tremendously successful in promoting research strategies that support the use of nanotechnology, and has served as a model that is being duplicated around the world.
但是幫助開發奈米技術應用的同等戰略無法幫助回答政府和產業 今天 越來越多地問到的有關它可能帶來的影響的問題。
but the same strategies that work for developing nanotechnology applications will not help answer the growing list of questions about its possible impact that governments and industry are asking today.
與危險相關的緊迫問題需要全世界都認真行動起來。
pressing riskrelated questions require deliberate action on an international scale.
我們只有透過加強研究努力和注資水平來獲得未來安全應用奈米技術的資訊才能回答這些問題。
they will be answered only by matching research efforts and funding levels to the information needed to steer toward a safe future for nanotechnology applications.
2006年，科學雜誌《自然》刊登了在開發奈米技術研究上五 大挑戰 ：
in 2006, five research grand challenges for developing safe nanotechnology were published in the scientific journal nature
l 尋找到測量空氣和水中存在的奈米材料的數量的方式；
finding ways to measure the amount of nanomaterials in the air and water
l 瞭解如何評估衡量奈米材料的有害程度；
learning how to assess how harmful nanomaterials are
l 開發預測 — — 以及防止 — — 奈米材料有害性的方式；
developing ways to predict and prevent harm from new nanomaterials
l 能夠熟練評估奈米技術產品從出品到消亡的過程中的潛在影響；
becoming skilled at evaluating the potential impact of nanotechnology products from cradle to grave
l 制定戰略以及注入資金支援旨在應對這些挑戰的研究。
and establishing strategies and funding to support the research needed to meet these challenges.
一些國家和地區已經開始制定研究日程來應對這五大挑戰。
some nations and regions are beginning to develop research agendas that respond to these five challenges.
比如，歐盟最近宣佈了一項耗資36億歐元的奈米技術研究專案，包括與這些挑戰相關的環境、健康和安全目標。
for example, the european union has recently announced a 3.6 billion nanotechnology research program, which includes environment, health, and safety goals that align with these challenges.
同樣地，2007年3月，英國政府的科學技術高階諮詢機構警告說這個國家在奈米技術上的領先地位正在消失，因為政府沒有在瞭解和有效控制可能產生的健康和環境影響的必需有的研究進行足夠的投資。
likewise, in march 2007, the british governments top advisory body on science and technology warned that the countrys lead in nanotechnology is fading, because the government has not invested enough in research necessary for understanding and effectively managing possible health and environmental effects.
我們還有很長的路要走。
there is still a long way to go.
如果要讓可持續的奈米技術建立在合理的科學基礎上，那麼全球的研究戰略就必須得到創新的政策的支援以及得到足夠的資金支援。
if sustainable nanotechnology is to be built on sound science, global research strategies must be supported by innovative policies and accompanied by sufficient funds to do the job.
單單在美國，預計有明確目標的奈米技術危險性研究必須要有的注資水平每年在5千萬到1億美元之間，這是2005年投資額的5到10倍。
in the us alone, estimates of the necessary funding levels for goaloriented nanotechnology risk research are between 50 million and 100 million per year five to ten times the amount invested in 2005.
我們不能夠一頭霧水地衝進奈米技術的未來。
we cannot afford to drive blind into the nanotechnology future.
儘管我們已經有了一個好的開端，許多國家依然在以陳舊和目光短淺的思維模式開發這種二十一世紀的技術。
despite a good start, many countries are developing these twentyfirst century technologies within an old and blinkered mindset.
如果我們無法制定出識別和避免可能的新危險的方式和方法，那這種令人鼓舞的新技術的前景並不樂觀。
if we do not develop the ways and means to spot and navigate around possible new risks, the outlook for this exciting new technology will be uncertain.
我們必須清醒地認識到未來的奈米技術應用需要建立在對其可能影響的充分理解之上。
we must wake up to the need for future nanotechnology applications to be based on a sound understanding of the possible impact.
在對奈米技術領導地位的全球競爭中，只有那些對其危險性有很好的認識並且支援必要的研究以把這種危險性降到最低程度的國家才會成為最後的贏家。
in the global race for nanotechnology leadership, the winners will be those who understand the risks and support the research necessary to minimize them.
可持續能源之路
paths to sustainable power
紐約—對能源未來的最安全賭注是下注於低碳能源供給。
new york the surest bet on the future of energy is the need for lowcarbon energy supplies.
如今，全世界八成左右的一次能源是碳基能源：煤、石油和天然氣。
around 80 of the worlds primary energy today is carbon based coal, oil, and gas.
我們需要在本世紀中葉轉向非碳或低碳能源。
we will need to shift to no or lowcarbon energy by midcentury.
怎樣轉、何時能轉成，這是個大問題。
the big questions are how and when.
低碳一次能源有三種選擇：可再生能源，包括風能、太陽能、地熱、水電和生物能；核能；以及碳捕捉和碳儲存，即用化石燃料生產能源，但限制二氧化碳發生量，並將碳安全地儲存於地下。
lowcarbon primary energy means three options renewable energy, including wind, solar, geothermal, hydropower, and biomass nuclear energy and carbon capture and sequestration, which means using fossil fuels to create energy, but trapping the co2 emissions that result and storing the carbon safely underground.
世界需要轉向低碳能源，有三條刻不容緩的原因。
there are three compelling reasons for the world to make the shift to lowcarbon energy.
首先，二氧化碳水平的升高正在讓海洋變酸。
first, higher levels of co2 are making the worlds oceans acidic.
照目前的發展速度，我們會毀掉大量海洋生物，嚴重破壞我們賴以生存的食物鏈。
if we continue with business as usual, we will end up destroying a vast amount of marine life, severely damaging the food chains on which we rely.
其次，二氧化碳正在讓世界氣候變得越來越危險，儘管許多石油巨頭試圖讓我們相信並非如此。
second, co2 is dangerously changing the worlds climate, even if many big oil interests would have us believe otherwise.
（菸草公司也花巨資用於政治遊說和偽科學，以否認吸菸和肺癌之間的聯絡。 ）
so, too, did the tobacco companies spend vast sums on political lobbying and bogus science to deny the links between smoking and lung cancer.
第三，隨著發展中國家的增長推動了需求，而煤、石油和天然氣的常規供給越來越少，我們面臨著化石燃料價格的暴漲。
third, we face steeply rising prices for fossil fuels, as developing countries growth drives up demand and conventional supplies of coal, oil, and gas are depleted.
誠然，我們可能發現更多的化石燃料，但成本會高很多，環境風險也會高很多，如工業滲漏、廢料、洩露等。
sure, we can find more fossil fuels, but at much higher cost and at much greater environmental risk from industrial spills, waste products, leaks, and other damage.
即使最近大熱的頁岩氣革命，也是幻想多於實際 — — 一如過去的黃金熱和股市泡沫。
even the muchheralded shalegas revolution is a lot of hype similar to the gold rushes and stock bubbles of the past.
頁岩氣礦的耗竭速度遠遠快於傳統礦，且對環境影響很大。
shalegas wells deplete far more rapidly than conventional fields do. and they are environmentally dirty to boot.
美國已開發出許多新的低碳能源技術，但其他國家大規模使用這些技術的目標、遠見和決心要遠強於美國。
the united states has developed many new lowcarbon energy technologies, but other countries are currently far more intent, farsighted, and decisive than the us to put these technologies to largescale use.
從政治上說，美國仍是石油巨頭的國度。
politically, america is still the land of big oil.
美國人整天受到行業資助的媒體的狂轟濫炸，淡化氣候變化問題，而化石燃料比美國匱乏得多的國家一開始著手進行邁向低碳未來的必要轉型。
americans are bombarded by industryfunded media downplaying climate change, while countries that are much poorer in fossil fuels are already making the necessary transition to a lowcarbon future.
歐洲的兩個鄰國，德國和法國正在向我們展示通往低碳未來之路 — — 更準確地說，是新道路。
two neighbors in europe, germany and france, are showing the way forward or, more precisely, the alternative ways forward to a lowcarbon future.
它們根據各自不同的稟賦、行業歷史和政治壓力選擇著不同道路。
they are going about it in ways that reflect their different resource endowments, industrial histories, and political pressures.
德國走的是Energiewende，即轉向可持續能源，這是一個用可再生能源，特別是太陽能和風電滿足德國全部能源需求的偉大工程（事實上，從未有發達國家有此先例 ） 。
germany is undertaking the energiewende, or transition to sustainable energy a remarkable effort indeed, unprecedented for a large advanced economy to meet the countrys entire energy demand with renewable energy, especially solar and wind power.
與此同時，法國將嚴重依賴低碳核電，並在快速推廣電動汽車，比如最尖端的雷諾-日產Leaf。
meanwhile, france relies heavily on lowcarbon nuclear power, and is switching rapidly to electric vehicles, such as the pioneering renaultnissan leaf.
在這兩條路中，德國之路更加非常。
of the two approaches, germanys is the more unusual bet.
日本福島核事故後，德國決定完全關閉核電工業，轉向基於提高能源效率（更低單位國民收入能源投入量）和可再生能源。
after japans nuclear disaster at fukushima, germany decided to shut down its entire nuclear power industry and shift entirely to a strategy based on greater energy efficiency lower energy input per unit of national income and renewables.
如此巨大的能源轉型確實沒有清晰的路線圖可供依據，德國幾乎肯定需要依賴泛歐洲電網共享清潔能源，並最終需要從北美和中東進口太陽能。
there really is no clear roadmap for such a huge energy transformation, and germany almost surely will need to rely on a europeanwide electricity grid to share clean energy, and eventually on imported solar power from north africa and the middle east.
法國的押注核電是較成熟的選擇。
frances bet on nuclear power is a more proven option.
畢竟，多年前法國就已經實現大部分電力靠核電供應。
after all, most of frances electricity has come from nuclear power for many years.
此外，儘管反核情緒在歐洲頗為高漲 — — 即使在法國也在水漲船高 — — 核電仍是未來幾十年全球能源供應的一部分，這一點只要亞洲（包括中國、印度、韓國和日本）仍是核電大使用者即可保證。
and, though antinuclear sentiment is very strong in europe and, increasingly, even in france nuclear power will remain part of the global energy mix for decades to come, simply because much of asia including china, india, south korea, and japan will remain major users of it.
關鍵在於，法國和德國以及其他許多歐洲國家 — — 包括擁有豐富風能和水能的斯堪的納維亞國家 — — 都在考慮世界作為一個整體必須擺脫以化石燃料為基礎的能源體系。
the key point is that france and germany, and many other european countries including the scandinavian countries, with their considerable wind and hydropower potential are all recognizing that the world as a whole will have to move away from a fossilfuelbased energy system.
這個結論是正確的。
that is the right calculation.
哪條新道路更明智 — — 法國的核電還是德國的太陽能 — — 遠未可知。
many will no doubt argue about which alternative frances bet on nuclear power or germanys solar pathway is wiser.
但兩種戰略可能都不錯。
but both strategies are probably correct.
大部分研究表明，行現在開始到本世紀中葉，世界將經歷深刻的去碳化，這個時間長度是由環境現實決定的。 去碳化要求所有低碳選擇 — — 包括提高能源效率和可再生能源 — — 都要大幅擴大規模。
most studies show that deep decarbonization of the world economy from now to midcentury, a time horizon mandated by environmental realities, will require that all lowcarbon options including greater efficiency and renewables be scaled up massively.
一項當務之急是由我代表聯合國秘書長潘基文主管的新的可持續發展解決方案網路（Sustainable Development Solutions Network）能夠詳盡地規劃通往低碳經濟的新道路，考慮世界各國的具體條件。
one of the highest priorities of the new sustainable development solutions network, which i direct on behalf of united nations secretarygeneral ban kimoon, will be to elaborate alternative pathways to a lowcarbon economy, taking into account the specific conditions of countries around the world.
不同國家可以選擇不同戰略，但所有國家都需要到達同一個終點：基於低碳資源、汽車電動化和智慧節能建築和城市的新的能源體系。
different countries will choose different strategies, but we will all need to get to the same place a new energy system built on lowcarbon sources, electrification of vehicles, and smart, energyefficient buildings and cities.
先行者或許會在當下付出更高的代價，但它們和全世界會因此收穫長期經濟和環境好處。
early movers may pay a slightly higher price today for these strategies, but they and the world will reap longterm economic and environmental benefits.
透過採用真正可持續的技術，法國、德國和其他國家正在創造一個更能支援世界經濟安然度過本世紀的能源體系。
by embracing truly sustainable technologies, france, germany, and others are creating the energy system that will increasingly support the world economy throughout this century.
仰仗歐元
building on the euro
歐元誕生已經6年了，再也不用憑空猜測它的作用和是否能滿足誕生時人們的厚望了。
the euro is now six years old. it is past time to consider how it is performing, and whether it has lived up to the expectations that accompanied its birth.
人們對歐元寄予了很高的期望。
those expectations were not modest.
透過降低交易成本和消除匯率不確定的風險，人們熱切地盼望這種單一的歐洲貨幣能帶來完全融合的產品和金融市場，而這又最終意味著更多的貿易收益、更強的競爭力、更多的資金跨國流動、更低的借貸成本和更多的風險共擔機會，人們寄希望於上述所有因素結合在一起，能夠最終促進投資、提高生產率。
by reducing transaction costs and removing exchangerate uncertainty, the single european currency was expected to lead to fully integrated product and financial markets. this, in turn, would bring greater gains from trade, stronger competition, larger crossborder capital flows, lower borrowing costs, and more opportunities for sharing risk, all of which were expected ultimately to boost investment and productivity.
但現實卻讓人們失望了。
reality has disappointed.
與1999年歐元啟動前的5年間相比，義大利、德國、西班牙和荷蘭等國的生產率增長都有所下降，而在同一時期，丹麥、瑞典、英國等沒有參與歐元計劃的成員國生產率卻保持不變，甚至還有所增長。
compared to the five years before the euros launch in 1999, productivity growth has since slowed in italy, germany, spain, and the netherlands, while over the same period it accelerated or remained constant in denmark, sweden, and the uk, the european union members that remained out.
實際上，除法國以外，歐元似乎並沒有給其它參與國帶來福音。
indeed, with the main exception of france, the euro does not seem to have been a blessing for the countries that adopted it.
結果為什麼會令人失望？
why this disappointment?
人們預期中新貨幣的好處是否沒能變成現實？
have the expected benefits of the new currency failed to materialize?
透過研究若干指數，前不久完成的幾項經濟研究探討了這個問題。
several recent economic studies addressed this question, looking at a variety of indicators.
研究結果如下：
here is what emerges
· 單一貨幣確實促進了歐元區國際貿易的發展，增長比率約為10 % 。
the single currency has boosted international trade within the euro area, by about 10.
雖然這與人們的希望還有距離，但全面評價還為時尚早。
although a larger effect was expected, it remains too early for a complete assessment.
無論如何，這是個重要的積極因素，因為國際貿易普遍被看作高速和高效的關鍵因素。
in any case, this is an important positive outcome, because international trade is generally regarded as a key determinant of faster growth and higher efficiency.
· 人們預計歐元能提高價格透明度，從而使產品市場競爭更為激烈。
the euro was expected to increase price transparency, thereby strengthening competition in product markets.
沒有證據顯示歐元起到了這樣的作用。
no evidence exists that this happened.
在20世紀90年代初單一市場計劃的起始階段價格確曾有所靠攏，但後來很快就停止了。
prices did converge during the implementation of the single market program, in the early 1990s, but then price convergence stopped.
· 對歐元區的跨國投資的確有所增長，但要將單一貨幣和其它衍生事件（比如私有化和企業兼併）的效果區分開來顯得更加困難。
crossborder investment towards the euro area has increased, although here it is more difficult to disentangle the effect of the single currency from other concomitant events such as privatizations or corporate mergers.
· 目前歐元區的貨幣和債券市場已經實現了統一，也就是說大公司借款的資金成本有所下降。
money and bond markets are now fully integrated in the euro area, implying a reduction in the cost of capital for large corporate borrowers.
而零售銀行業仍然條塊分割，因此家庭和小生產者的借貸成本沒什麼變化。
retail banking, however, remains segmented by national borders, so that households and smaller producers have not been much affected.
· 人們希望歐元能成為國際貨幣，最終提高歐洲抵禦經濟衝擊的能力。
the euro was expected to acquire an international role, eventually improving europes resilience in the face of economic shocks.
用歐元發行的國際債券價格迅速上升，但歐元外匯市場的流動性並不比它所取代的國家貨幣強多少，而要想挑戰美元的統治地位歐元也還有很長的路要走。
there has been a surge in eurodenominated international bonds, but the liquidity of foreignexchange markets is no higher for the euro compared to the national currencies it replaced, and the euro remains a long way from challenging the supremacy of the dollar.
當然，歐元從來就不只有單純的經濟意義。
of course, the euro was never just an economic project.
歐元支持者主要的動機之一就是促進歐洲的政治融合。
one of its backers main motives was to boost europes political integration.
實際上，歐元迅速地成為歐洲統一的象徵。
indeed, the euro has quickly become a symbol of european unity.
當被問及“歐盟對你個人意味著什麼”時，2004年5月歐盟擴張之前15個原成員國50%的公民都回答“歐元”¾這種回答的普遍性居第二位（僅次於“在歐盟各地旅遊、學習和工作的能力 ” ） 。
when asked, what does the eu mean to you personally, 50 of citizens in the 15 countries that were eu members before enlargement in may 2004 say the euro the second most common response just behind the ability to travel, study, and work anywhere in the eu.
但這項標誌並未使歐盟和歐元區更受人歡迎。
yet, this symbol has not made the eu or the euro area any more popular.
歐盟擴張前15國對聯盟的支援率仍然是20世紀90年代的水平（比20世紀90年代的最高水平有所下降 ） ， 而對歐元的支援率也不比1997年的時候高。
support for eu membership within the preenlargement eu15 remains where it was in the mid1990s and below the peak reached in 1990, while support for the euro is no higher now than it was in 1997.
可以肯定的是，歐元的引入是一次真正意義的革命，我們現在還無法看到它所有的效果。
to be sure, the introduction of the euro was a true revolution, and we cannot yet see all its effects.
但有一點是十分清楚的：這次革命是在脆弱的國家經濟基礎之上發生的，它所改革的是歐洲經濟的上層建築¾金融市場和宏觀經濟制度¾而保留了20世紀七八十年代錯誤的國家政策所造成供應經濟扭曲的原有基礎。
but what is clear is that the revolution took place on shaky national economic foundations, transforming the upper floors of the european economy financial markets and macroeconomic policy institutions while leaving intact the ancien underpinnings of supplyside distortions induced by misguided national policies in the 1970s and 1980s.
造成歐元區經濟表現低迷的正是這些扭曲，而不是單一貨幣的缺陷。
these distortions, not any shortcomings of the single currency, account for the euro areas dismal economic performance.
歐元的採用國20世紀90年代末就不得不面對糟糕的勞工市場制度，過於龐大的養老金體系、對勞動者收入的高額稅收和效率低下的服務部門，這個問題到今天也還沒有解決。
the countries that adopted the euro had poor labormarket institutions, bloated pension systems, high taxes on labor income, and inefficient service sectors in the late 1990s, and they still do now.
歐元更本質的問題是它的採納並未促使各個國家解決這些潛在問題。
the more fundamental problem with the euro is that its adoption has not pushed countries to address these underlying deficiencies.
人們曾經希望產品和金融市場的徹底融合會暴露哪些低效行業，把資金流從發展遲緩的國家轉移到更加高效的使用者。
it was expected that full integration of product and financial markets would expose inefficiencies, steering investment flows away from laggards towards the more efficient countries.
可儘管20世紀90年代包括歐元區內外的整個歐洲改革力度都有所加大，但並沒有多少證據表明“區內”國比“區外”國實行了更多意義深遠的重大供應改革。
yet, while reform efforts intensified throughout europe in the late 1990s both inside and outside of the euro area, there is little evidence that ins enacted more farreaching and significant supplyside reforms than the outs.
擔任過美國財政部長的哈佛大學校長薩莫斯曾把單一歐洲貨幣稱為歐洲需要面對的真正供應改革的“干擾因素 ” 。
