and yet, in the end, greece had little choice but to restructure its debt, cutting the value of private claims by about 75 relative to their face value although even this is probably not enough to make the countrys debt burden sustainable.
這被認為是一起“信用事件 ” ， 將觸發信用違約互換：所有為該事件投了保的人都可以獲得賠付。
this was deemed a credit event, so creditdefault swaps were exercised anyone who insured against default had to pay out.
只是如此嗎？
did all hell break loose?
銀行並沒有倒閉，也沒有出現任何多米諾效應的跡象。
banks have not failed, and there is no sign of tumbling dominoes.
但這並不是因為銀行未雨綢繆留好了更多資本。
but that is not because banks prepared themselves by raising more capital.
相反，與潛在未來損失相比，歐洲銀行最近留存的資本仍顯太少 — — 切這筆資本是透過會計花招變出來的，而不是真正的用於吸收損失的股本金。
on the contrary, compared to their likely future losses, european banks have raised relatively little capital recently and much of this has been creative accounting, rather than truly lossabsorbing shareholder equity.
也許希臘債務重組引發金融崩潰的風險永遠不會很高，市場並不會對此有多大的反應。
perhaps the risk that a greek debt restructuring would cause a financial meltdown was always minimal, and quiescent markets were to be expected.
但是，既然如此，為何這一問題會引發如此關注？
but, in that case, why all the fuss?
答案現在已經很清楚了：利益集團政治和政策精英的世界觀。
the answer should be clear by now interestgroup politics and policy elites worldview.
就算金融體系的風險很小，對銀行和債權人的衝擊也會很大。
even if the risk to the financial system was minimal, the impact on banks and bondholders was substantial.
它們可能因此損失數十億美元，不少金融部門員工還將丟掉工作。
they stood to lose billions, and many financialsector employees stood to lose their jobs.
毫不奇怪，不管是公開還是暗地裡，大銀行都在遊說反對債務重組。
not surprisingly, leading bankers lobbied against debt restructuring, both behind closed doors and publicly.
比如，華盛頓有一個叫國際金融協會（Institute for International Finance）的機構，是代表大銀行利益的遊說集團。 該協會不斷強調：援助我們，否則後果自負。
for example, the institute for international finance, a preeminent washington, dcbased lobbying group for large banks, consistently argues bail us out, or else face the consequences.
但是，這一說辭的背後是政治權力，這一權力近幾年來膨脹迅速，已經到了美國和歐洲主要決策者都得唯銀行財富馬首是瞻的程度，就算這樣做會給經濟造成深遠衝擊。
but, just as important as their storyline is their political power, which has risen greatly in recent years to the point that all major policymakers in the us and europe cater to banks fortunes even when there are no wider implications for the economy.
即使是現在，大量本應由銀行家承擔的損失仍然被公共部門承擔了 — — 形式多種多樣，包括直接支援和歐洲央行高風險的非常規舉措。
even now, many of the losses that bankers should have faced are being shouldered by the public sector, including through various forms of direct support and the extraordinary and risky actions of the european central bank.
金融部門得到的補貼之巨令人咋舌，在現行政策下，補貼還將進一步增加 — — 這些補貼的首要作用是支援了最發達國家最高階1%人群的生活方式。
the extent of subsidies in this sector is stunning and, under current policies, will only increase over time thereby primarily supporting the lifestyles of the top 1 of people in very rich countries.
希臘的違約表明，咬人的狗不吠。
the greek default has turned out to be the proverbial dog that didnt bark.
歐洲 — — 還有美國 — — 能從中吸取的教訓相當淺顯：不要再聽銀行的鬼話，而應該開始關注它們的行動。
the lesson for europe and for the us is clear it is time to stop listening to what banks say, and start focusing on what they do.
我們必須重新評估被扭曲的金融部門政治經濟學，否則的話，少數人權力的過度膨脹將給其他所有人帶來更大的負擔。
we must reevaluate the distorted political economy of the financial sector, before the excessive power of the few imposes even larger costs on everyone else.
綁架歐洲央行
capturing the ecb
紐約—關於歐洲眼下的政治分歧、特殊利益和短視經濟考慮，沒有比重組希臘主權債務爭論更好的寫照了。
new york nothing illustrates better the political crosscurrents, special interests, and shortsighted economics now at play in europe than the debate over the restructuring of greeces sovereign debt.
德國堅持要實行深度重組，至少要債權人“犧牲”50 % ， 而歐洲央行堅持債務重組必須是自願的。
germany insists on a deep restructuring at least a 50 haircut for bondholders whereas the european central bank insists that any debt restructuring must be voluntary.
換做從前 — — 比如20世紀80年代的拉美債務危機 — — 急於平息事態的政府和監管者可以把債權人（主要是大型銀行）關進小黑屋，威逼利誘一番，然後就達成了協議。
in the old days think of the 1980s latin american debt crisis one could get creditors, mostly large banks, in a small room, and hammer out a deal, aided by some cajoling, or even armtwisting, by governments and regulators eager for things to go smoothly.
但是，隨著債務證券化時代的到來，債權人數量比以前有了暴增，對沖基金等監管者和政府很難對其施加影響的投資者也被包括了進來。
but, with the advent of debt securitization, creditors have become far more numerous, and include hedge funds and other investors over whom regulators and governments have little sway.
此外，金融市場的“創新”使得證券所有者可以獲得保險，這意味著他們也入了局，不再是“事不關己”了。
moreover, innovation in financial markets has made it possible for securities owners to be insured, meaning that they have a seat at the table, but no skin in the game.
他們確實有利益在其中：他們想獲得保險，這意味著重組必須是“信用事件 ” ， 也就是違約。
they do have interests they want to collect on their insurance, and that means that the restructuring must be a credit event tantamount to a default.
歐洲央行堅持“自願”重組 — — 也就是說，避免了信用事件的發生 — — 無異於站到了債權人的對立面。
the ecbs insistence on voluntary restructuring that is, avoidance of a credit event has placed the two sides at loggerheads.
其中的諷刺之處在於，監管者坐視這一怪胎體系的產生。
the irony is that the regulators have allowed the creation of this dysfunctional system.
歐洲央行的立場十分奇怪。
the ecbs stance is peculiar.
你可能寄希望於銀行透過買入保險設法消除了投資組合中的債券的違約風險。
one would have hoped that the banks might have managed the default risk on the bonds in their portfolios by buying insurance.
此外，如果它們購買了保險，那麼關心繫統穩定性的監管者將巴不得保險人在損失事件發生時予以償付。
and, if they bought insurance, a regulator concerned with systemic stability would want to be sure that the insurer pays in the event of a loss.
但歐洲央行又希望銀行承擔所持債券50%的損失而不獲得任何保險“償付 ” 。
but the ecb wants the banks to suffer a 50 loss on their bond holdings, without insurance benefits having to be paid.
歐洲央行採取這一立場可能有三個原因，但沒有一個能很好地為該機構及其監管和監督行為開脫。
there are three explanations for the ecbs position, none of which speaks well for the institution and its regulatory and supervisory conduct.
第一個原因是，銀行事實上並沒有買入保險，一些銀行的頭寸是投機性的。
the first explanation is that the banks have not, in fact, bought insurance, and some have taken speculative positions.
第二個原因是，歐洲央行明白金融體系缺乏透明度，也知道投資者明白他們無法看清非自願違約的影響，而這可能導致信用市場凍結，重現2008年9月雷曼兄弟倒閉後的亂象。
the second is that the ecb knows that the financial system lacks transparency and knows that investors know that they cannot gauge the impact of an involuntary default, which could cause credit markets to freeze, reprising the aftermath of lehman brothers collapse in september 2008.
最後，歐洲央行可能在試圖保護出售保險的幾家銀行。
finally, the ecb may be trying to protect the few banks that have written the insurance.
這三大理由都不足以成為歐洲央行反對希臘債務深度非自願重組的藉口。
none of these explanations is an adequate excuse for the ecbs opposition to deep involuntary restructuring of greeces debt.
歐洲央行應該堅持增加透明度 — — 事實上，這一點正是2008年的主要教訓。
the ecb should have insisted on more transparency indeed, that should have been one of the main lessons of 2008.
監管者本不應該允許銀行如此投機；至少應該要求銀行買入保險，然後堅持要求能夠確保保險獲得償付的重組。
regulators should not have allowed the banks to speculate as they did if anything, they should have required them to buy insurance and then insisted on restructuring in a way that ensured that the insurance paid off.
但是，沒有證據顯示深度非自願重組會比深度自願重組造成更大的混亂。
there is, moreover, little evidence that a deep involuntary restructuring would be any more traumatic than a deep voluntary restructuring.
歐洲央行或許是想透過堅持自願違約確保重組程度不至於很深，但是，這樣一來，歐洲央行便將銀行的利益置於希臘利益之前了，因為對希臘來說，深度重組是走出危機的必經之路。
by insisting on its voluntariness, the ecb may be trying to ensure that the restructuring is not deep but, in that case, it is putting the banks interests before that of greece, for which a deep restructuring is essential if it is to emerge from the crisis.
事實上，歐洲央行可能把少數出售了信用違約互換的銀行的利益置於優先於希臘、歐洲納稅人以及審慎債權人和保險購買者的利益的地位。
in fact, the ecb may be putting the interests of the few banks that have written creditdefault swaps before those of greece, europes taxpayers, and creditors who acted prudently and bought insurance.
歐洲央行立場的最後一個詭異之處與民主治理有關。
the final oddity of the ecbs stance concerns democratic governance.
決定是否讓信用事件發生的是一個國際互換和衍生品協會旗下的秘密委員會，而國際互換和衍生品委員會本身與決定結果有著千絲萬縷的聯絡。
deciding whether a credit event has occurred is left to a secret committee of the international swaps and derivatives association, an industry group that has a vested interest in the outcome.
如果新聞報道為真，則該委員會的一些成員正在利用職權推行更溫和的談判立場。
if news reports are correct, some members of the committee have been using their position to promote more accommodative negotiating positions.
但歐洲央行將決定什麼是可接受的債務重組的權利委託給一個本身也是自利市場參與者的秘密委員會，此舉實在有些說不過去。
but it seems unconscionable that the ecb would delegate to a secret committee of selfinterested market participants the right to determine what is an acceptable debt restructuring.
一種（儘管只是名義上）將公眾利益置於首位的觀點是非自願違約會導致財政問題的傳染，義大利、西班牙甚至法國等歐元起大經濟體將因此面臨借貸成本急劇升高的局面，甚至因此引發危機。
the one argument that seems at least superficially to put the public interest first is that an involuntary restructuring might lead to financial contagion, with large eurozone economies like italy, spain, and even france facing a sharp, and perhaps prohibitive, rise in borrowing costs.
但這又引出了另一個問題：為什麼非自願重組會引起比深度相仿的自願重組更嚴重的傳染？
but that begs the question why should an involuntary restructuring lead to worse contagion than a voluntary restructuring of comparable depth?
如果銀行體系有著很好的監管，持有主權債務的銀行全部購買了保險，非自願重組對金融市場的衝擊應該沒有這麼大。
if the banking system were well regulated, with banks holding sovereign debt having purchased insurance, an involuntary restructuring should perturb financial markets less.
當然，你可能會指出，如果希臘逃脫非自願違約，那麼其他國家也會試圖依樣畫葫蘆。
of course, it might be argued that if greece gets away with an involuntary restructuring, others would be tempted to try it as well.
金融市場將對此產生憂慮，造成其他歐元區風險國利率飆升，不管是大國還是小國。
financial markets, worried about this, would immediately raise interest rates on other atrisk eurozone countries, large and small.
但風險最高的國家已然被金融市場排除在外了，因此產生恐慌的可能性後果有限。
but the riskiest countries already have been shut out of financial markets, so the possibility of a panic reaction is of limited consequence.
當然，如果希臘在重組後境況確實有所改善，那麼其他國家或許真的會群起仿效。
of course, others might be tempted to imitate greece if greece were indeed better off restructuring than not doing so.
這誠然不假，但已是眾人皆知的秘密了。
that is true, but everyone already knows it.
歐洲央行的行為倒也不出人意料：放眼別處，不可被民主問責的機構往往會被特殊利益綁架。 2008年以前便是如此。
the ecbs behavior should not be surprising as we have seen elsewhere, institutions that are not democratically accountable tend to be captured by special interests.
不幸的是，對歐洲 — — 以及對全球經濟 — — 來說，此後這一問題並未得到充分的解決。
that was true before 2008 unfortunately for europe and for the global economy the problem has not been adequately addressed since then.
金融界的可持續革命
the sustainability revolution in finance
發自斯德哥爾摩 — — 金融業界正在發生一場靜悄悄的革命。
stockholm a quiet revolution is taking place in the financial industry.
根據聯合國環境計劃署所釋出的報告，可持續發展正越來越多地被涵蓋到財務決策的考慮因素之中。
according to the united nations environment programme, sustainable development is increasingly being integrated into financial decisionmaking.
迄今為止歐盟一直在這一轉變中顯得比較被動，而許多國家的金融監管機構則引領著潮流。
the european union has been rather passive so far in this transformation, but financial regulators in a number of countries are leading the charge.
法國最近推出了面向機構投資者的全球第一個強制性氣候資訊披露要求。
france recently introduced the worlds first mandatory climate disclosure requirements for institutional investors.
挪威的主權財富基金正在逐步退出煤炭行業。
norway is divesting its sovereign wealth fund from coal.
南非則將可持續發展納入其證券交易所的股票上市要求之中。
south africa has embedded sustainable development into listing requirements on its stock exchange.
同樣，巴西的銀行法規現在要求對環境風險進行評估。
likewise, brazils banking regulations now require accounting for environmental risk.
而瑞典政府正在推動一項雄心勃勃的可持續發展議程，其中列入了一系列旨在增加對投資者的資訊披露並確定哪些與氣候相關的風險必須由監管機構和金融企業進行解決的提案。
and the swedish government is pushing an ambitious sustainability agenda featuring a series of proposals aimed at improving information for investors and determining which climaterelated risks regulators and financial firms must address.
與此同時，私人部門也不遑多讓。
private industry is also moving rapidly.
全球最大的資產管理公司黑石（Blackrock）現推出非化石燃料指數（fossil-fuel-free index ） ， 而世界上最大的保險公司之一安盛（Axa）也已承諾從煤碳行業撤資。
the worlds largest asset manager, blackrock, is launching a fossilfuelfree index, and axa, one of the world's largest insurance companies, has pledged to divest from coal.
這種撤資運動是滾雪球式的：宗教社群、城市政府、社會名人、工會，大學和機構投資者都表示要撤出化石燃料資產。
meanwhile, the divestment movement is snowballing, with faithbased communities, municipalities, celebrities, trade unions, universities, and institutional investors all pledging to unload their fossilfuel assets.
總共已有管理超過$ 2.6萬億美元市值的機構承諾要從化石燃料行業撤資。
altogether, institutions worth more than 2.6 trillion have committed to divest from fossil fuels.
革命或許是寂靜的，但它引發的震盪卻日益擴大。
the revolution may be quiet, but it is getting louder.
化石燃料企業正在失去其合法性；因為它們目前的經營模式與關注氣候變化的投資組合背道而馳。
fossilfuel companies are increasingly being delegitimized their current business model is irreconcilable with a climateconscious investment portfolio.
與此同時，投資者開始認識到，關注氣候風險是合理投資戰略的一個組成部分，可以最大限度地降低風險並有助於提升金融穩健程度。
at the same time, investors are starting to understand that paying attention to climate risk is an integral part of a sound investment strategy that seeks to minimize risk and help to promote financial stability.
安盛執行長亨利·德·卡斯特（Henri de Castries）對這樣的動機表示贊同，指出脫離煤炭行業有助於從投資組合中剔除風險，並有助於建立一個更加可持續發展的社會。
axas ceo henri de castries has endorsed such motives, stating that divesting from coal helps remove risk from investment portfolios and contributes to building a more sustainable society.
英格蘭銀行行長馬克·卡尼（Mark Carney）一直在大力強調氣候變化可能帶給金融市場的風險。
bank of england governor mark carney has been particularly frank in highlighting the dangers that climate change poses to financial markets.
在今年9月於倫敦勞合社（Lloyd’s of London）發表的演講中，他警告如果繼續拖延將全球變暖限制在攝氏2ºC以內的轉型，則金融穩定性風險將增大。
in a speech at lloyds of london this september, he cautioned that a delayed transition to limit global warming to 2 celsius would increase risks to financial stability.
一系列機構也對他的警告做出了響應。
a range of institutions has echoed his warning.
與此同時，麥肯錫公司和碳信託基金估計化石燃料公司市值的30-40％可能會因為所謂“碳泡沫 ” — —對化石燃料儲量的高估 — — 而受損。
meanwhile, mckinsey and the carbon trust have estimated that 3040 of the value of fossilfuel companies could be endangered because of a socalled carbon bubble, an overvaluation of fossilfuel reserves.
據國際能源機構的統計，如���世界要避免氣候變化失控的話，2/3的燃料儲備必須留在地底不得開採，這意味著相關企業可能無法利用其全部經濟潛力。
according to the international energy agency, twothirds of these reserves must be kept in the ground if the world is to avoid runaway climate change, which implies that companies may not be able to exploit their full economic potential.
鑑於歐洲金融部門在化石燃料資產上的投資超過1萬億歐元（約合 1.1萬億美元 ） ， 歐盟所面臨的碳泡沫風險尤其巨大。
given that the european financial sector has invested more than 1 trillion 1.1 trillion in fossilfuel assets, the eu is particularly at risk of a carbon bubble.
事態嚴重，以至於歐洲央行行長馬里奧·德拉吉（Mario Draghi）要求歐洲系統性風險委員會對此進行調查。
the issue has become serious enough that european central bank president mario draghi has asked the european systemic risk board to investigate it.
此外瑞典，德國，荷蘭和英國的金融監管機構都在研究氣候變化對金融市場的影響。
financial regulators in sweden, germany, the netherlands, and the united kingdom are all studying the impact of climate change on financial markets.
G20集團還要求位於巴塞爾的金融穩定委員會召開針對碳泡沫的公私聽證會。
the g20 has also asked the baselbased financial stability board to convene a publicprivate inquiry into the carbon bubble.
去年九月，歐盟專員喬納森·希爾（Jonathan Hill）釋出了期待已久的資本市場聯盟提案。
last september, european commissioner jonathan hill published his longawaited capital markets union proposal.
但儘管他建立更為整合且多元化的資本市場的呼籲令人欽佩，卻缺乏一個可以將可持續發展融入金融體系的路線圖以及應對碳泡沫的戰略。
but while his call for more integrated and diversified capital markets in the eu is admirable, his proposal lacks both a roadmap for the integration of sustainable development into the financial system and a strategy for addressing the carbon bubble.
歐洲議會和歐洲理事會不乏機會去改進希爾的建議。
the european parliament and the european council have the opportunity to improve hills proposal.
議會已經成立了一個名為碳素集團的非正式跨黨派小組，其目的是解決碳泡沫和推進可持續金融。
the parliament has already established an informal crossparty grouping, called the carbon group, which aims to tackle the carbon bubble and advance sustainable finance.
在理事會內部，以瑞典和法國為首的幾個國家正在為更加大程度地將可持續發展指標整合入金融市場而努力。
and within the council, a range of countries, most notably sweden and france, are working for greater integration of sustainability metrics into financial markets.
此外一批機構也開始在它們的決策過程中引入可持續發展因素。
a range of institutions are starting to embrace sustainable development considerations in their financial decisionmaking.
而政策制定者們 — — 尤其是在歐盟 — — 有責任去推動這些前瞻性思維，並保護全球經濟免受氣候引發的財務危機。
policymakers especially in the eu have a responsibility to advance such forwardlooking thinking and to protect the global economy from climateinduced financial distress.
碳定價和返現計劃
a carbon priceandrebate plan
巴黎—目前，國際氣候談判沒有能夠找到可以成功降低全球溫室氣體排放的機制。
paris so far, international climate talks have failed to find a mechanism that will successfully reduce global greenhousegas emissions.
1997年京都議定書嘗試採用可交易配額系統為二氧化碳排放制定價格，但以失敗告終，因為美國和一些新興國家拒絕加入京都議定書。
the 1997 kyoto protocol attempted to use a system of tradable quotas to establish a price on carbondioxide emissions, but foundered after the united states and several emerging countries refused to join.
2009年哥本哈根氣候變化會議引入了承諾-評估程式，各國單方面決定減排多少。
the 2009 copenhagen climate change conference introduced a pledgeandreview process, in which countries unilaterally decided how much they would cut.
結果，美國和一些新興經濟體首次做出減排承諾。
as a result, the us and several emerging economies made commitments to reduce emissions for the first time.
但這一系統也有極大的缺陷。
but this system, too, is badly flawed.
它沒有解決經典 的免費搭車問題，也無法保證發展中國家的減排。
what it does not do is resolve the classical freerider problem or guarantee reductions in developing countries.
事實上，一些國家為了維持強勢談判地位，被鼓勵做得更少一些。
indeed, some countries may have been encouraged to do less than they otherwise would have in order to maintain a strong negotiating position.
11月30日—12月11日，全世界領導人將在巴黎出席聯合國氣候變化會議。 這次會議是一次形成有效協議的新機會。
as world leaders meet in paris from november 30 to december 11 for the united nations conference on climate change, they will have a new opportunity to forge an effective agreement.
為了鼓勵各國政府一致行動，致力於構建一個直觀而透明的碳定價系統至關重要。
to encourage governments to act in concert, it is essential to work toward a system of carbon pricing that is both straightforward and transparent.
我們建議採取“定價和返現”機制，制定一個高於某個閾值的排放價格，同時明確所得收入如何使用。
we propose a carbon priceandrebate mechanism, which simultaneously sets a price on emissions above a certain threshold and defines how the revenues raised should be used.
巴黎會議前的研究表明，國際公司可以迅速減少溫室氣體排放。
studies ahead of the paris conference suggest that international cooperation could allow for rapid reduction of greenhouse gases.
它們還強調了迅速採取行動遏制氣候變化所能帶來的附帶好處，包括減少地方汙染、增強能源和糧食安全以及更快的創新。
they also highlight the knockon benefits that taking quick action on climate change could have, including reduction of local pollution, greater energy and food security, and faster innovation.
要加速邁向低碳經濟，就必須有適用於所有國家的國際協定；包括一個共同的一致監測、報告和核實系統；並提供全球範圍的強經濟激勵。
to accelerate the move toward a lowcarbon economy, an international agreement must be applicable to all countries include a common and consistent system for monitoring, reporting, and verification and provide strong economic incentives at a global scale.
我們的定價和返現機制受歐洲的“獎懲”機制啟發。 在獎懲機制中，新汽車的買家會被課稅或獲得補貼，視其所購買汽車的二氧化碳排量而定。
our priceandrebate mechanism is inspired by the bonusmalus scheme in france, in which buyers of new cars are taxed or given a bonus depending on the vehicles co2 emissions.
在我們的系統中，一國如果超過了世界人均排放量，就必須向其在規定量二氧化碳（及其等價物）以上的排量部分支付每噸若干美元。
in our system, a country exceeding the worldwide average for per capita emissions would pay a specified amount on every ton of co2 or its equivalent above a set threshold.
低於人均排放量的國家將因為汙染較少而獲得補償。
countries with lowerthanaverage emissions would be compensated for polluting less.
這一系統一開始有利於人均排量最低的國家，這意味著大部分資金將流向最不發達國家。
this system would initially benefit countries with the lowest per capita emissions, meaning that most of the funds would flow towards the leastdeveloped countries.
一旦得到充分執行，定價和返現機制將鼓勵所有國家削減人均排放，從而降低支付額和返現額之間的距離。
once it is fully operational, the priceandrebate mechanism would encourage all countries to reduce their per capita emissions, thereby reducing the gap between payments and rebates.
理想的談價格將取決於協定的目標。
the ideal carbon price would depend on the objectives of the agreement.
每噸定價1—2美元可以帶來140—280億美元收入，足夠在發展中國家部署監測、評估和核實程式。
a price of 12 per ton would generate 1428 billion, enough to fund the deployment of the monitoring, review, and verification process in developing countries.
在哥本哈根協定中，發達國家承諾在2020年後每年拿出1,000億美元幫助不發達國家減輕或適應氣候變化。
the copenhagen accord included a commitment by rich countries to spend 100 billion a year after 2020 to help underdeveloped countries mitigate and adapt to climate change.
7—8美元一噸的定價便能夠產生足以兌現這一承諾的收入，資金將流向人均排量較低的國家。
a rate of 78 per ton would generate enough revenue to deliver on this promise, with the money flowing to countries with low per capita emissions.
在這1,000億美元中，略多於600億將來自西方國界和日本，只有不到200億來自碳氫化合物出口國（特別是俄羅斯和沙烏地阿拉伯）和高增長亞洲經濟體（包括中國和韓國 ） 。
of that 100 billion, a little over 60 billion would come from western countries and japan, and just under 20 billion would come from hydrocarbonexporting countries russia and saudi arabia in particular and highgrowth asian economies including china and korea.
因此，引入定價和返現系統將按照“共同但有差異的責任和各自能力” 原則重新分配各國的資金。
the introduction of a priceandrebate system would thus redistribute funds among countries in conformity with the principle of common but differentiated responsibilities and respective capabilities.
定價和返現系統將是高效而公平的。
a priceandrebate system would be both efficient and fair.
全世界所有公民都有同樣溫室氣體排放權利，所有國家都獲得同樣的邊際減排激勵。
every citizen in the world would have the same right to emit greenhouse gas, and every country would face the same incentives at the margin to reduce emissions.
克服建立這樣一套系統的主要障礙是說服出資國政府為其碳排放付錢。
the main obstacle to be overcome in establishing such a system will be to convince donor countries governments to pay for their carbon emissions.
這一成本與他們的經濟規模比起來十分微小，而任何成功的氣候變化協定都需要一樣的承諾。
this cost will be modest relative to the size of their economies, and any successful climatechange agreement will require similar commitments.
如果發達國家不同意為碳支付一個十分有限的價格，那麼巴黎談判將肯定以失敗告終。
if rich countries are unable to agree to pay even a modest price for carbon, the talks in paris will surely be judged a failure.
通往碳定價之路
the path to carbon pricing
華盛頓—區區六週後，世界領導人將齊聚巴黎協商新的全球氣候變化協定。
washington, dc in just six weeks, world leaders will meet in paris to negotiate a new global climatechange agreement.
目前，150個國家已經遞交了關於如何讓本國經濟走向恢復力更強的低碳軌跡的詳細計劃。
to date, 150 countries have submitted plans detailing how they will move their economies along a more resilient lowcarbon trajectory.
這些計劃給出了第一批為了在不讓二氧化碳排放量達到如今導致全球變暖的危險水平的情況下構建高競爭力未來而進行的投資。
these plans represent the first generation of investments to be made in order to build a competitive future without the dangerous levels of carbondioxide emissions that are now driving global warming.
通往更清潔的未來的轉型將需要政府行動起來並未私人部門提供正確的激勵。
the transition to a cleaner future will require both government action and the right incentives for the private sector.
居於核心地位的應該是強有力的碳汙染定價公共政策。
at the center should be a strong public policy that puts a price on carbon pollution.
給碳基能源、電力和工業活動定更高的價格將刺激人們使用更清潔的燃料、節約能量、促進向更綠色的投資的轉變。
placing a higher price on carbonbased fuels, electricity, and industrial activities will create incentives for the use of cleaner fuels, save energy, and promote a shift to greener investments.
碳稅和碳費、排量交易安排和其他定價機制、取消低效補貼，這些措施能夠給予企業和家庭它們所需要的確定性和可預測性，讓它們為氣候智慧（climate-smart）發展做出長期投資。
measures such as carbon taxes and fees, emissionstrading programs and other pricing mechanisms, and removal of inefficient subsidies can give businesses and households the certainty and predictability they need to make longterm investments in climatesmart development.
在國際貨幣基金組織（IMF ） ， 注意力集中在改革成員國的財政制度，從碳密集型燃料的稅收上獲得更多收入，同時減少不利於經濟表現的勞動和資本方面的稅收。
at the international monetary fund, the focus is on reforming its member countries fiscal systems in order to raise more revenue from taxes on carbonintensive fuels and less revenue from other taxes that are detrimental to economic performance, such as taxes on labor and capital.
碳定價可以是更智慧、更高效的稅收制度，並不一定要提高稅負。
pricing carbon can be about smarter, more efficient tax systems, rather than higher taxes.
碳稅必須針對源自化石燃料的排放全面收取。
carbon taxes should be applied comprehensively to emissions from fossil fuels.
其價格必須足夠高以實現宏大的環境目標，必須與國家的具體情況相結合，必須穩定以鼓勵企業和家庭投資於清潔技術。
the price must be high enough to achieve ambitious environmental goals, in alignment with national circumstances, and it must be stable, in order to encourage businesses and households to invest in clean technologies.
管理碳稅並不複雜，可以基於目前在大部分國家都在徵收的道路燃料稅。
administering carbon taxes is straightforward and can build on existing road fuel taxes, which are well established in most countries.
碳定價符合許多國家的根本利益，因為它會帶來諸多國內環境收益。
carbon pricing will be in many countries best interests, owing to the many domestic environmental benefits.
比如，燃燒更清潔的燃料有助於減少室外空氣汙染。 據世界衛生組織的資料，目前室外空氣汙染每年導致約370萬人過早死亡。
for example, burning cleaner fuels helps to reduce outdoor air pollution, which, according to the world health organization, currently causes about 3.7 million premature deaths a year.
遏制能源價格改革對各國弱勢群體的衝擊至關重要。
it is vitally important to address the impact of energyprice reforms on vulnerable groups in every society.
因此，這些改革需要輔之以財政制度和社會安全網等方面的調整，以確保窮人不受傷害。
so these reforms will need to be accompanied by adjustments to fiscal systems and safety nets, among other things, to ensure that the poor are not harmed.
世界銀行集團正在支援各個國家和企業制定環境友好型公共政策、投資碳市場、探索金融創新以便利低碳轉型。
the world bank group is supporting countries and businesses as they develop climatefriendly public policies, invest in carbon markets, and explore financial innovations to ease into lowcarbon transitions.
世界銀行集團利用其經驗和業務遍及全球的特點，透過市場合作準��計劃（Partnership for Market Readiness）等專案促進學習和知識交流。
the group is leveraging its experience and global reach for learning and knowledge exchange through programs like the partnership for market readiness.
從這方面的經驗出發，我們與經合組織一起制定了幫助指引和啟發未來談定價機制的初步原則。
from that experience, we have developed, alongside the oecd, initial principles to help guide and inspire future carbonpricing schemes.
透過實施這些原則，各個國家、地區、行政區和企業能夠更快地行動起來，解決我們所有人一起面臨的氣候挑戰。
by drawing on these principles, countries, regions, states, and businesses can move faster to tackle the climate challenge confronting us all.
這些原則以公平性、政策和目標的一致性、穩定性和可預測性、透明性、效率和價效比，以及可靠性和環境完整性為基礎。
the principles are based on fairness alignment of policies and objectives stability and predictability transparency efficiency and costeffectiveness and reliability and environmental integrity.
為了幫助實現我們的氣候目標，我們需要在巴黎氣候變化前後促進關於必要政策措施的對話。
to help achieve our climate objectives, we need to promote dialogue about the necessary policy measures before and beyond the climatechange conference in paris.
因此，我們成立了一個“碳定價委員會 ” ， 委員會將由各國首腦、城市和州省領導人以及來自頂尖公司的代表組成，敦促世界各國和企業為碳制定一個價格。
that is why we are announcing a carbon pricing panel, which will bring together heads of state, city and state leaders, and representatives of top companies to urge countries and businesses around the world to put a price on carbon.
這些領導人已開始採取行動為所在國家和地區的碳汙染定價和推動更加綠色的投資。
these leaders have taken steps to price carbon pollution and catalyze greener investment in their own countries and regions.
他們包括德國總理默克爾、智利總統巴切萊特、法國總統奧朗德、衣索比亞總理德薩萊尼、菲律賓總統阿基諾三世、墨西哥總統涅託、加利福尼亞州長傑裡·布朗（Jerry Brown）和里約熱內盧市長愛德華多·佩耶斯（Eduardo Paes ） 。
they include german chancellor angela merkel, chilean president michelle bachelet, french president franois hollande, ethiopian prime minister hailemariam desalegn, philippines president benigno aquino iii, mexican president enrique pea nieto, governor jerry brown of california, and mayor eduardo paes of rio de janeiro.
碳定價政策已開始在大約40個國家（包括世界最大排放國中國）實施，更有23個城市、州省和地區的政府正在制定碳價格。
carbon pricing policies are already being implemented by some 40 national governments, including that of china, the worlds largest emitter, and 23 cities, states, and regions that are putting a price on carbon.
其他許多政府也在改革能源價格，400多家公司報告正在採用自願的內部碳定價。
many other governments also are reforming energy prices, and more than 400 companies report using a voluntary, internal carbon price.
這些政策很有意義。
that makes sense.
頂尖公司必須有效管理氣候風險的風險敞口，這樣才能獲得更高的利潤和確保更穩定的收益。
top companies must effectively manage exposure to climate risk in order to generate higher profits and ensure more stable earnings.
所有這些行動都是值得歡迎的；但我們認為它們只是最初的步驟。
all of these actions are welcome but we view them as being only initial steps.
與碳定價委員會一起，我們呼籲各國政府抓住時機 — — 為了地球和子孫後代的命運 — — 為碳汙染制定一個反映它們所造成的環境傷害的價格。
together with the leaders of the carbon pricing panel, we call on governments to seize the moment for the sake of the planet and future generations to put a price on carbon pollution that reflects the environmental damage it causes.
我們已經做好準備支援政府行動。
we stand ready to support governments that act.
我們等待得越久，我們 — — 以及我們的子輩和孫輩 — — 保護地球的成本和困難就越大。
the longer we wait, the costlier and more difficult it will be for us and our children and grandchildren to protect the planet.
病人照護和藥物的道德貧困
caregiving and the moral impoverishment of medicine
劍橋－對病人照護，經濟學家認為是一種“負擔 ” ， 臨床心理學家認為是一個“因應過程 ” ， 醫療衛生服務研究人員認為是一種醫療成本，而醫生認為是一種臨床能力。
cambridge caregiving is understood by economists as a burden, by clinical psychologists as a coping process, by healthservices researchers in terms of healthcare costs, and by physicians as a matter of clinical competency.
然而，對許多人來說，病人照護是道德體驗的一個基本要素。
but, for many people, caregiving is a foundational component of moral experience.
它是一種承認、移情想象、見證、責任、團結和最具體的幫助行為。
it is a practice of acknowledgement, empathic imagination, witnessing, responsibility, solidarity, and the most concrete forms of assistance.
正是病人照護的這些道德方面，讓照護人，有時候甚至是接受照護的人，感受到了更多的“存在 ” — —並因而成為更完整的人。
it is this moral aspect that makes caregivers, and at times even carereceivers, feel more present and thus more fully human.
但是，除了熟練的護理之外，職業治療和理療師進行的康復活動，社會工作者的實際幫助以及家庭健康護理和照護，特別是對健康嚴重受損和處於疾病晚期的病人的健康護理和照護，與當代的醫學實踐幾乎沒有什麼關係。
but, aside from skilled nursing, rehabilitation efforts by occupational and physical therapists, and the practical assistance of social workers and home health aides, caregiving, especially for victims of health catastrophes and endstage conditions, has relatively little to do with the contemporary practice of medicine.
為了闡明上述觀點，我用我自己照護妻子的個人經歷來加以說明 — — 我妻子罹患嚴重的神經退變性疾病，這種疾病損害了她的記憶力和運動機能，使她獨立生活的能力受到了影響。
to illustrate this point, i draw on my personal experience as the caregiver for my wife, who suffers from a severe neurodegenerative disorder that has impaired her memory and motor functions, restricting her independence.
每天早晨，我將妻子叫醒，幫助她上廁所，洗澡，穿衣服，準備我們的早餐並幫她進餐。
i wake her up in the morning, assist her in toileting, bathing, and dressing, make us breakfast, and help her feed herself.
我扶著她走路，將她抱到椅子裡，並放進我們的車裡。
i assist her in walking, placing her in a chair, and getting into our car.
我幾乎一直和她在一起，以免她傷害自己，因為不管是在街上還是在我們家裡，她都是既看不見東西也不能安全地行動。
i am with her nearly all the time to protect her from injuring herself, because she can neither see nor navigate safely on the street or in our own home.
看著四十多年的伴侶 — — 一個曾經優雅、知性活潑並且非常獨立的人 — — 病情惡化，是令人困擾的。
it is disturbing to witness the deterioration of a once elegant, intellectually lively, and highly independent companion of more than four decades.
但是，由於我們的努力和長期一起的共同生活，最重要的是，由於家人和好友的支援，我們從沮喪、憤怒到悲傷的情緒反應得到了緩解和昇華。
but our emotional reactions, from frustration and anger to sadness, have been cushioned and sublimated by our work, the long rhythm of our days together, and, above all, by the support of family and close friends.
家人和朋友對我們的這種關心和責任，和我前面列出的日常行為一樣，是對我妻子的照護的一個重要組成部分，也是對我們努力的道德上的支援。
that concern and responsibility for us is as much a part of caregiving as all the mundane practices i have listed, and amounts to moral solidarity with our struggle.
我舉出這個個人例子，是因為這是我能用來說明病人照護包含什麼以及它對每個人的生活 — — 更通常地說，對人的境況 — — 如此重要的原因的最好途徑。
i give you this personal sketch because it is the best i can do to illustrate what caregiving entails, and why it is so crucial to everyones life and to the human condition more generally.
正如我們的情況所表明的那樣，病人照護包括，在希望和安慰都被放棄，神正論也結束了的時候，人們要做的事情就是和飽受疾病煎熬的人在一起，在他們身邊 — — 通常是安靜地陪在他們身邊 — — 分擔他或她的痛苦。
caregiving, as illustrated by our case, includes what happens when hope and consolation are abandoned, when theodicy ends, and when all there is to do is to be present with the sufferer, sharing his or her suffering by simply and usually silently being there.
但是，在醫學院，基礎學科和臨床實習階段的課程最關注的都是對疾病的生物學過程和高科技治療手段的理解。
in medical schools, however, the curriculum in both the basic science and clinical apprenticeship years places the greatest emphasis on understanding the biology of disease processes and hightechnology treatments.
在醫學院的學生從教室走向病房和臨床的過程中，醫學院教學對疾病體驗的關注也越來越少。
the illness experience gets less and less pedagogic attention as the student progresses from classroom to inpatient ward and clinic.
在更廣泛的醫療保健體系內，醫學院的學生們會很容易地認為，藥物在很大程度上將病人照護的實際工作和情感工作留給了護士、社會工作者、病人以及病人的支援網路。
in the broader system of healthcare, students can readily discern that medicine largely leaves the practical and emotional tasks of caregiving to nurses, social workers, and the patient and his or her network of support.
醫療服務的提供結構和資金投入，使專業人員遠離了病人照護的藝術，並在實際上削弱了醫生的治療。
the structure of service delivery and the funding of health services work to discourage professionals from the art of caregiving, and can, in fact, undermine the practitioners efforts.
其結果就是醫學實踐的道德貧困。
the result is moral impoverishment of the practice of medicine.
對醫學人類學家來說，任何地方的人都生活在當地（即社交網路、家人、機構以及社群）的人際互動之中。
for medical anthropologists, people everywhere live in the flow of interpersonal interactions in local worlds social networks, families, institutions, and communities.
也就是說，被認為是人們相互間的語言、行動以及情感流動的體驗，不僅是本地的，而且具有內在的道德性，因為我們的生活就是有關賦予價值和表現價值的。
that is to say, experience, viewed as the flow of words, movements, and emotions between us, is not only local, but also inherently moral, because living our lives is about animating and enacting values.
對面臨嚴重健康問題和嚴重慢性疾病治療過程的病人和家庭來說，遭受疾病折磨的經歷不只是一個個人體驗，還是一種會受到形成道德生活過程中的文化和歷史變化極大影響的體驗，而道德生活在不同時代和社會是不同的。
for patients and families faced with health catastrophes and serious chronic medical conditions, the experience of suffering is not just a personal one, but is strongly influenced by cultural and historical changes in the processes that contribute to moral life being distinctive in different eras and societies.
面對痛苦、畸形、機能喪失以及嚴重殘疾的威脅，個人和家庭透過用倫理、宗教和美學活動來重塑意義、情感和價值，��而在本地的道德世界裡重新定義痛苦的體驗。
faced with a threat of pain, disfigurement, loss of function, and serious disability, individuals and families reframe the experience of suffering within their local moral world by remaking meanings, emotions, and values via ethical, religious, and aesthetic activities.
在利用個人和文化資源（包括想象力、責任感、感受力、洞察力以及交流）來完成病人照護方面，醫生和外行沒有什麼不同。
doctors are no different from laypersons in drawing on personal and cultural resources involving imagination, responsibility, sensibility, insight, and communication to accomplish their caregiving.
而且，他們從事的是一個綜合了倫理、美學、宗教和實際行動的行為。
and what they engage in is an amalgam of ethical, aesthetic, religious, and practical action.
醫生的技巧 — — 這種技巧現在受到了官僚主義、政治和經濟力量的極大限制，開始了這些固有的人類資源的專業化過程，並對在醫生自身的道德生活上的一般使用產生影響。
the physicians art now so circumscribed by bureaucratic, political, and economic forces turns on both the professionalization of these inherently human resources and the impact of their routine use on the doctors own moral life.
顯然，為了為病人照護的職業生涯做準備，醫學院的學生和年青的醫生需要除了科學和技術訓練之外的東西。
to prepare for a career of caregiving, medical students and young doctors clearly require something besides scientific and technological training.
事實上，我們甚至可以認為，當前的醫學職業教育在使醫生成為技術專家的同時，也使他們失去了成為病人照護者的能力。
indeed, current professional education can even be seen as enabling the physician as a technical expert, while disabling him or her as a caregiver.
要克服這種趨勢，我們必須將把人文科學納入醫學訓練作為重新點燃和強化想象力和信念這樣的人類體驗的途徑；這些人類體驗對病人照護和抵制導致醫生技術失敗的情感反應和價值官僚化，至關重要。
to overcome this trend, we must incorporate the humanities into medical training as a means of rekindling and deepening those human experiences of imagination and commitment that are essential for caregiving, and resisting the bureaucratization of values and emotional responses that causes failure in the physicians art.
實質上，醫生必須逐漸認識到，病人照護的藝術和疾病的診斷和治療科學技術一樣重要。
in essence, the practitioner must come to feel that the art of caregiving is as much at stake as the science and technology of diagnosis and treatment.
我認為，現在我們要做的就是對當代生物醫學文化進行改革。
in my view, what is needed is reform of the very culture of contemporary biomedicine.
我們必須對醫學院的學生和醫生進行訓練：訓練他們對是什麼限制了他們的病人照護進行批判性的反思；訓練他們為病人照護的道德行為開啟空間的策略和技巧；訓練他們最具體和實際的幫助行為，以使他們永遠不會忘記病人照護的實際意義。
we must train students and practitioners in critical selfreflection on that which limits their caregiving in strategies and techniques aimed at opening a space for the moral acts of caregiving and in the most concrete and practical acts of assistance, so that they never forget what caregiving actually means.
就業中的創造性破壞
creative destruction at work
牛津—縱觀歷史，技術進步創造了無窮財富，但也導致了巨大破壞。
oxford throughout history, technological progress has created enormous wealth but also caused great disruption.
比如，美國鋼鐵業在20世紀60年代經歷了重大轉型，當時，大型綜合性鋼鐵廠逐漸被小型鋼鐵廠擠出，摧毀了賓夕法尼亞州的匹茲堡市和俄亥俄州的楊斯頓（Youngstown）市等老牌經濟重鎮。
the united states steel industry, for example, underwent a major transformation in the 1960s, when large, integrated steel mills were gradually put out of business by mini mills, destroying the existing economic base of cities like pittsburgh, pennsylvania, and youngstown, ohio.
但是，小鋼鐵廠極大地增進了生產率，在其他地區創造出新的就業方式。
the mini mills, however, vastly increased productivity, and created new types of work elsewhere.
美國鋼鐵業的故事是關於經濟學家約瑟夫·熊彼特（Joseph Schumpeter）所謂的“創造性破壞 ” （ “creative destruction ” ） 的重要例子。 長期經濟增長並不僅僅是現有工廠產出增加，也意味著就業結構的調整。
the story of us steel illustrates an important lesson about what the economist joseph schumpeter called creative destruction longrun economic growth involves more than just increasing output in existing factories it is also implies structural changes in employment.
我們可以在最近的資訊和通訊技術革命中看到類似的現象。 資訊和通訊技術革命影響了現代工作崗位的方方面面，即使是那些與計算機程式設計或軟體工程沒有直接關係的崗位。
we can observe a similar phenomenon in the current information and communications technology ict revolution, which has affected most areas of the modern workplace, even those not directly associated with computer programming or software engineering.
計算機技術創造了繁榮的新企業（甚至企業叢集 ） ， 同時也讓某些製造業工人成為冗餘，讓老牌製造業城市衰落。
computer technologies have created prosperous new businesses even business clusters while making certain manufacturing workers redundant and sending older manufacturing cities into decline.
但底特律、里爾和例子等城市之所以衰落，並不是因為製造業產出下降；相反，在過去十年中，這些城市的製造業產出在增加。
but the likes of detroit, lille, or leeds have not suffered because of falling manufacturing output on the contrary, output has been growing in these cities over the past decade.
它們的衰落的直接原因是沒能吸引不同型別的就業崗位。
instead, their decline stems directly from their failure to attract different types of jobs.
在很大程度上說，這是政策的失敗。
to a large extent, this is a failure of policy.
官員不應該試圖以振興舊產業捍衛過去，而應該專注於管理好向新工作形式的轉變。
rather than trying to preserve the past by propping up old industries, officials should focus on managing the transition to new forms of work.
這需要更好地理解新興技術以及它們如何與被取代的技術之間的區別。
this requires a better understanding of emerging technologies, and how they differ from those that they are supplanting.
工業革命早期的生產技術的一個重要特徵是它們取代了相對技能較高的工匠，這反過來增加了對技能較低的工廠工人的需求。
an important feature of the industrial revolutions early manufacturing technologies was that they replaced relatively skilled artisans, which in turn increased demand for unskilled factory workers.
類似地，亨利·福特的汽車製造流水線（1913年上線）就是專門為技能較低工人執行機械而設計的，這使得福特公司生產出大受歡迎的T型車，這也是美國中產階級能夠負擔得起的第一款轎車。
similarly, henry fords assembly line for manufacturing cars introduced in 1913 was specifically designed for unskilled workers to operate machinery, thereby allowing the company to produce its popular model t the first car that middleclass americans could afford.
事實上，過去一百年來，工業發展的歷史大多可以歸結為教育程度不斷提高的勞動力與降低他們的技能要求的新技術之間的競爭。
indeed, much of the story of industrial development over the last century can be seen in terms of competition between an increasingly educated workforce and new technology that would dispense with their skills.
我們已經可以看到機器人帶來的影響 — — 不僅侷限於汽車業 — — 機器人能夠勝任曾經需要數千中等收入流水線工人來完成的工作。
we have already seen the impact not least in the car industry of robots that can carry out the routine jobs that were once performed by thousands of middleincome assemblyline workers.
未來還將出現更大規模的勞動力替代。
even greater workplace disruption lies ahead.
儘管歷史教育我們對於預測技術進步會如何演進需要慎之又慎，但我們已經可以合理地推斷計算機可以在不就得將來做什麼，因為這些技術已在開發中。
though history counsels caution in predicting how technological progress will play out, we already have a reasonable idea of what computers will be able to do in the near future, because the technologies are already being developed.
比如，我們知道，許多高技能崗位可以在“大資料”和先進演算法的幫助下得到簡化。
we know, for example, that a wide range of skilled professions can be simplified with the help of big data and sophisticated algorithms.
關於這方面的進展，一個被廣泛引用的例子是Symantec Clearwell公司的eDiscovery平臺，該平臺用語言分析識別文件的主旨概念，據稱可以在兩天內分析570,000份文件。
one frequently cited example of this process is the symantec clearwell ediscovery platform, which uses language analysis to identify general concepts in documents, and boasts of analyzing and sorting more than 570,000 documents in just two days.
Clearwell用計算機來協助進行庭前研究和其他通常由律師幫辦處理的任務，甚至協助進行由合同或專利律師處理的任務 — — 它正在改變法律業。
clearwell is transforming the legal profession by using computers to assist in pretrial research and perform tasks normally undertaken by paralegals and even by contract or patent lawyers.
同樣地，先進的感測技術意味著許多交通和物流崗位很快就能完全自動化。
in the same way, improved sensory technology means that many transportation and logistics jobs will soon be fully automated.
谷歌的自動駕駛汽車讓巴士和計程車司機成為多餘已不再是遙遠的想象。
and it is not farfetched to imagine the likes of googles selfdriving cars making bus and taxi drivers redundant one day.
甚至到目前為止仍相當安全的低技能服務崗位也可能無法逃脫自動化的命運。
even hitherto secure, lowskilled service occupations may not escape automation.
比如，個人和家用服務機器人的需求正在以每年20%的速度增長。
demand for personal and household service robots, for example, is already growing by about 20 annually.
勞動力市場可能將再次進入技術干擾和工資不平等性加劇的新時代。
labor markets may once again be entering a new era of technological turbulence and widening wage inequality.
這凸顯出一個更大的問題：哪裡去創造新型別的工作？
and this highlights a larger question where will new types of work be created?
一些跡象指明瞭未來的方向。
there are already signs of what the future holds.
技術進步正在創造大資料架構師和分析師、雲處理專家、軟體開發人員和數字營銷專家的需求 — — 這些崗位在五年前還幾乎不存在。
technological progress is generating demand for big data architects and analysts, cloud services specialists, software developers, and digital marketing professionals occupations that barely existed just five years ago.
芬蘭提供了一個很好的例子說明城市和國家應該適應這些發展趨勢。
finland offers valuable lessons in how cities and countries should adapt to these developments.
芬蘭經濟曾經因為其最大公司諾基亞沒有順應智慧手機技術趨勢而遭遇打擊。
its economy initially suffered from the failure of its biggest company, nokia, to adapt to smartphone technologies.
但此後，芬蘭創業企業中衍生出新的智慧手機平臺公司。
yet several finnish startups have since built new enterprises on smartphone platforms.
事實上，到2011年，前諾基亞員工建立了220家類似企業，打造出狂賣1,200萬份的智慧手機遊戲“憤怒的小鳥”的Rovio公司就有大量前諾基亞員工。
indeed, by 2011, former nokia staff had created 220 such businesses, and rovio, which has sold more than 12 million copies of its smartphonebased video game, angry birds, is crowded with former nokia employees.
這一轉變並非巧合。
this transformation is no coincidence.
芬蘭對教育的集中投資創造出韌性十足的勞動力。
finlands intensive investment in education has created a resilient labor force.
芬蘭透過投資於不受特定企業或行業侷限、不受計算機化趨勢影響的可轉移技能，為如何適應技術升級提供了一份藍圖。
by investing in transferable skills that are not limited to specific businesses or industries, or susceptible to computerization, finland has provided a blueprint for how to adapt to technological upheaval.
儘管大資料驅動技術在不斷擴散，但研究表明，勞動力將繼續在社會知識和創新方面存在比較優勢。
despite the diffusion of bigdatadriven technologies, research suggests that labor will continue to have a comparative advantage in social intelligence and creativity.
因此，政府發展戰略應該集中於強化這些技能，以使勞動力與計算機技術形成互補而不是競爭的關係。
government development strategies should therefore focus on enhancing these skills, so that they complement, rather than compete with, computer technologies.
烏克蘭的歐洲危機
europes crisis in ukraine
斯德哥爾摩 — — 我們無法預測烏克蘭爆發的深刻危機將以何種方式結束。
stockholm how ukraines profound crisis will end is impossible to predict.
歐盟和美國正竭盡全力確保和平過渡到更穩定的民主政體，以及最終能夠落實迫切需要的改革。
we in the european union and the united states are doing what we can to secure a peaceful transition to a more stable democracy, and the implementation, at long last, of urgently needed reforms.
亞努科維奇總統和反對派現在達成的協議應該為此創造出新的可能性。
and the agreement now concluded between president viktor yanukovych and the opposition should create a new possibility for this.
如果協議未能兌現，烏克蘭很可能會繼續陷入混亂和衝突，而這對任何人都沒有好處。
if the agreement is not honored, ukraine could well continue its descent into chaos and conflict, which would be in no ones interest.
因此烏克蘭危機和歐洲危機實際是一碼事。
that is why ukraines crisis is a european crisis.
而且，雖然我們無法預知這場危機將如何結束，我們至少應該弄清楚危機爆發的來龍去脈。
and, though we cannot know how the crisis will end, we should be very clear about how it started.
多年來，烏克蘭積極尋求和歐盟建立密切關係。
for years, ukraine sought a closer relationship with the eu.
該國領導人熱切希望加入歐盟東部夥伴計劃，敦促簽訂歐盟聯合協議並設立深度全面自由貿易區。
its leaders warmly endorsed the promise of enhanced ties under the eus eastern partnership, and pushed for an eu association agreement, together with a deep and comprehensive free trade area.
1991年烏克蘭獨立後，全部14任當選總理和4任總統無一例外地批准了烏前政府談判訂立的協議。
when those talks, which began under the previous ukrainian government, were concluded, the agreement was endorsed by all four presidents and all 14 prime ministers to hold office since ukraine achieved independence in 1991.
烏克蘭原定在2013年11月維爾紐斯召開的東部夥伴關係首腦會議上訂立聯合協議，然而就在歐盟和烏克蘭解決遺留問題時，形勢卻突然急轉直下。
but, as the eu and ukraine were addressing remaining issues ahead of the november 2013 eastern partnership summit in vilnius, where ukraine was to sign its association agreement, something suddenly changed.
8月起，俄羅斯決策者的目標就是要迫使烏克蘭放棄它自己選擇的線路。
from august onward, russian policymakers embraced the openly declared aim of knocking ukraine off the course that it had chosen.
烏國內爆發了針對聯合協議的政治運動，同時克里姆林宮實行針對性制裁，並威脅對本已疲軟的烏克蘭經濟採取更嚴厲的措施。
a political campaign against the agreement was launched, and the kremlin mixed targeted sanctions with threats of harsher measures against the alreadyweak ukrainian economy.
俄領導人公開表態一旦烏克蘭和歐盟簽署自貿協議俄烏自貿協議將自行廢止，並將對烏克蘭輸俄的所有商品和服務徵收高額關稅。
russian leaders publicly stated that if ukraine signed a freetrade agreement with the eu, it would lose its freetrade deal with russia, and high tariffs would be imposed on all goods and services.
形勢再明顯不過，沉重的經濟壓力將升級為公開的經濟戰。
severe economic pressure, it was made clear, would become open economic warfare.
烏克蘭總統亞努科維奇選擇了讓步。
ukrainian president viktor yanukovych gave way.
在向歐盟領導人解釋無法簽署聯合協議的原因時，他明確表示自己如此決策是迫於俄國的壓力。
in explaining to eu leaders that he was not ready to sign the association agreement, he was very clear that russian pressure was responsible for his decision.
上述事態現在引發了基輔街頭的屠殺死亡事件。
this set in motion the chain of events that has now resulted in carnage and death in the streets of kyiv.
許多烏克蘭人認為歐洲象徵著美好生活的希望；但突然間他們發現遭到了不可救藥的腐敗政治精英的背叛。
for many ukrainians, europe was the symbol of hope of a better life suddenly, they felt betrayed by a political elite that they had long perceived as being incorrigibly corrupt.
因此我們必須清楚，克里姆林宮的壓力和亞努科維奇政府的動搖共同構成了當前這場危機的根源。
so, to be clear, it was the kremlins pressure, and the yanukovych administrations vacillation, that produced the current crisis.
如果亞努科維奇決定頂住俄國的壓力，烏克蘭無疑將面臨嚴重的困難。
had yanukovych decided to stand up to russian pressure, there is no doubt that ukraine would have faced difficulties.
但擁有歐盟聯合協議及國際貨幣基金組織可能提供的雄厚的資金和改革援助，俄羅斯措施的效力持續不了多長時間。
but, with an eu association agreement and the possibility of solid financial aid and reform assistance from the international monetary fund, the russian measures would not have been sustainable.
當然，歐盟將要求烏克蘭進行艱難的改革，但烏克蘭的改革也不會比其他加入歐盟陣營的前共產主義國家更加困難。
of course, the reforms asked of ukraine would have been difficult, but no more difficult than what had been asked of other excommunist countries that saw their future in and with europe.
隧道盡頭將閃爍著希望的曙光，而且隨著改革程序的深入，烏克蘭將可能作為堅定民主的歐洲國家出現在世人面前。
there would have been light at the end of the tunnel, and, as ukraine embraced the reform process, it would have been seen as a determined and democratic european country.
相反，亞努科維奇選擇了以一己政治生���為核心的短期策略 — — 這越來越被抗議者視為玩弄、欺騙和背叛。
instead, yanukovych opted for a shortterm strategy narrowly focused on his own political survival a strategy that the protesters increasingly came to view as a game of deceit and betrayal.
隨著現政權開始暴力鎮壓對手，暴力反對團體正變得越來越可信。
as the regime started to use violence to repress its opponents, violent opposition groups gained credibility.
與俄羅斯和歐盟雙方實現自由貿易顯然有利於烏克蘭經濟，而且儘管存在經常被提到的歐盟商品透過烏克蘭流入俄羅斯的虛假說法，俄烏自貿協定同樣能夠利好俄羅斯經濟。
free trade with both russia and the eu would obviously have been good for ukraines economy, thus providing a boost to the russian economy as well, notwithstanding the oftused but fundamentally bogus argument that eu goods would flow into russia via ukraine.
（有沒有人聽美國人抱怨過墨西哥和歐盟的自貿協定破壞了美國經濟？ ）
has anyone heard americans complaining that the freetrade agreement between mexico and the eu is undermining the us economy?
俄國一心想以其所謂歐亞聯盟的形式建設新的戰略堡壘，並且似乎下定決心迫使烏克蘭就範。
russia is intent on building a new strategic bastion in the form of its proposed eurasia union, and it seems determined to force ukraine to join.
雖然在公開場合抱怨歐盟對烏克蘭施壓，但現實是俄國殘酷要挾烏克蘭放棄其既定的歐盟路線。
while publicly grumbling about supposed eu pressure on ukraine, the reality is that russia brutally extorted the country into abandoning its eu course.
事實證明這才是這場危機的根源。
that is the source of this crisis the facts speak for themselves.
即使出現最好情況，烏克蘭走回頭路也難上加難。
even under the best of circumstances, the road back for ukraine will be difficult.
俄羅斯的壓力和破壞作用，以及由此所導致的危機已經在烏克蘭社會造成了新的裂縫，並進一步給該國脆弱的經濟造成損害。
russian pressure and destabilization, and the crisis to which they have led, have created new fissures in ukraines society and have caused further damage to its fragile economy.
就連俄國也總有一天會身受其害。
and that damage could, one day, spill over into russia.
像其他國家一樣與歐盟建立密切關係的穩定而積極改革的鄰國同樣應該符合克里姆林宮的利益。
the kremlin should have an interest in a stable and reforming neighbor that, like other countries, is also seeking a close relationship with the eu.
評級革命
the ratings revolution
美國劍橋 — “ 您好，先生，有什麼要幫忙的嗎？ ”在巴黎飯店，迎賓奉承地問我。
cambridge bonjour monsieur, comment pourraisje vous aider? asks the obsequious concierge at my paris hotel.
我立刻開始奇怪這座城市臭名昭著的傲慢到底發生了什麼，特別是對美國遊客。
i immediately wonder what happened to the citys infamous haughtiness especially toward american tourists.
如果說法國首都不再是歐洲最粗魯的城市，那麼我們或許得感謝TripAdvisor等線上評級工具的增長。
if the french capital is no longer europes rudest city, we can perhaps thank the growth of online rating tools, such as tripadvisor.
旅行網站大約從20世紀90年代就開始出現，Expedia、Travelocity和其他假日預定網站就興趣於那時候，旅行者輕點滑鼠就能比較航班和飯店價格。
travel web sites have been around since the 1990s, when expedia, travelocity, and other holiday booking sites were launched, allowing travelers to compare flight and hotel prices with the click of a mouse.
資訊不再掌握在旅行社手中或藏身於商務網路，旅遊業因此迎來了革命，透明度的增加刺激了價格的下降。
with information no longer controlled by travel agents or hidden in business networks, the travel industry was revolutionized, as greater transparency helped slash prices.
如今，旅遊業有受到一場新革命的洗禮 — — 這一回面貌煥然一新的服務質量。
today, the industry is in the throes of a new revolution this time transforming service quality.
線上評級平臺 — — 有的專注於飯店（TripAdvisor ） ， 有的專注於餐館（Zagat ） ， 有的專注於公寓（Airbnb ） ， 也有的專注於計程車（Uber ） — —讓旅行者能夠交換評價和體驗，供所有人參考。
online rating platforms specializing in hotels tripadvisor, restaurants zagat, apartments airbnb, and taxis uber allow travelers to exchange reviews and experiences for all to see.
如今，飯店企業不是由業內專家排名、分析和比較的，而是由飯店服務的物件 — — 客戶來做這些事。
hospitality businesses are now ranked, analyzed, and compared not by industry professionals, but by the very people for whom the service is intended the customer.
這鑄造了買賣雙方的新關係。
this has forged a new relationship between buyer and seller.
客戶永遠用腳投票；他���現在可以向任何感興趣的人解釋自己的選擇。
customers have always voted with their feet they can now explain their decision to anyone who is interested.
結果，企業受到了極大的監督，並且通常是以極其具體的角度，這創造了巨大的改善服務激勵。
as a result, businesses are much more accountable, often in very specific ways, which creates powerful incentives to improve service.
儘管一些讀者不在乎關於柏林飯店侍者態度倨傲或休斯頓飯店吹風機不能用之類的瑣碎報告，但線上評價的真正力量不在於個別故事，而在於網站有能力產生大規模評級。
although some readers might not care for gossipy reports of brusque bellboys in berlin or malfunctioning hotel hairdryers in houston, the true power of online reviews lies not just in the individual stories, but in the web sites capacity to aggregate a large volume of ratings.
影響是巨大的。
the impact cannot be overstated.
吸引頂尖評級的企業可以獲得卓越的增長，新客戶因為優異的總體評價慕名而來，並在光臨後給出更加（積極）的反饋。
businesses that attract top ratings can enjoy exponential growth, as new customers are attracted by good overall reviews and subsequently provide yet more positive feedback.
線上評級的影響力是巨大的，許多公司目前紛紛聘請數字聲譽經理以確保有利的線上名聲。
so great is the influence of online ratings that many companies now hire digital reputation managers to ensure a favorable online identity.
這套系統並非總是有益的。
the system is not always virtuous.
我們知道有一些行為不端的操盤手，他們收錢撰寫虛假評價幫你提升評級。
nefarious operators are known to pay fake review services to bolster ratings.
客戶也有可能不太地道，參與評級要挾，據TripAdvisor透露，通常的形式是“客人威脅撰寫負面評價，除非你滿足他的返現、升級或其他要求。 ”
customers, too, can be disingenuous or worse, engage in blackmail, which occurs, as tripadvisor explains, when a guest threatens to write a negative review unless a demand for a refund, upgrade, or other request is met.
幸運的是，技術正在遏制這一評級濫用現象。
fortunately, technology is countering this misuse of ratings.
演算法已可以透過識別同一評價者的持續積極（或消極）評論數檢測虛假評價。
algorithms can already detect fake reviews by identifying consistently positive or negative opinions from the same reviewer.
定位追蹤能夠確保只有真正使用了服務的客戶才能給出評價（如Airbnb ） 。
geolocation tracking can ensure that only customers who have actually used a service can express an opinion as is the case with airbnb.
事實上，惡意批評因為一個相當出乎意料的發展而受到了遏制：客戶可以就服務發表觀點，服務提供者也可以為客戶評級，Uber就是這麼做的。
indeed, obstreperous critics are being challenged as a result of another, rather surprising development while customers may express an opinion about a service, the service provider can also rate its customers, as uber has demonstrated.
事實上，熱門酒店有朝一日開始挑選客人也不是無法想象的事。
indeed, it is not inconceivable that popular hotels might one day choose their guests.
消費者和生產者的傳統關係也在被其他方式打破。
traditional relationships between consumers and producers are breaking down in other ways, too.
“共享經濟”的崛起 — — 即團體內成員共享汽車、泊位、閒置臥室等資源 — — 不但創造了互惠名譽，也模糊了買家與賣家之間的界線。
the rise of the sharing economy, in which assets such as a car, a parking space, or a spare bedroom are shared within communities, not only generates reciprocal goodwill, but also blurs the distinction between buyer and seller.
但是並不是所有服務都可以線上評級。
not every service, however, has been touched by online ratings.
評級的影響取決於典型消費者是否真的在決定前讀過線上評價。
the impact of ratings depends on whether the typical consumer actually reads online reviews before making a decision.
對預定飯店房間來說，這樣做正在日益普及，但在選擇繁忙街道上的酒吧方面，這樣做的人就要少得多（巴黎侍應生一直態度傲慢就證明了這一點 ） 。
while it is increasingly common to do so when, say, booking a hotel room, it is much less so when deciding among, say, bars on a busy street the enduring rudeness of parisian waiters attests to that.
但即使是依賴“外觀魅力”吸引客戶的服務提供商，或許也將發現好日子不多了。
yet even service establishments that rely on curb appeal to attract customers may soon find their days numbered.
“增廣現實 ” — —疊加數字資訊（如谷歌眼鏡和其他服務所開發的 ） — —可以將日常活動轉換為數字/實體的混合體驗，其中的客戶反饋將立刻無縫地與購物者聯絡起來。
the proliferation of augmented reality an overlay of digital information as developed by google glass, among others promises to transform everyday activities into a digitalphysical hybrid experience in which customer feedback is instantly and seamlessly available to shoppers.
最後一個抵禦評級者的堡壘是客戶別無選擇的服務，這些服務通常由壟斷商或政府機構提供，比如機場。
the final holdout against the raters will be services for which customers have no choice, typically monopolies or government agencies, such as airports.
新加坡樟宜機場是罕有的例外：它隨時都在懇請使用者予以評級，透過介面活潑的可觸控笑臉圖示請旅行者就從通關服務到廁所清潔程度的一切方面的效率發表意見。
singapores changi airport is a rare exception it solicits user ratings at every turn, via feedback screens with cheery, touchenabled smileyface emoticons that request travelers opinions on everything from the efficiency of immigration service to the cleanliness of toilets.
不消說，許多發達經濟體在這方面已經落後，至少在目前是如此。
needless to say, many developed economies lag behind, at least for now.
但寫東西 — — 我的意思就是“寫 ” — —必須在牆上，或至少是在螢幕上。
but the writing is, literally, on the wall or at least on the screen.
事實上，如果你正在線上閱讀本文並不同意我的觀點，你可以在本文評論欄裡解釋為什麼。
indeed, if you are reading this online and disagree with me, you can explain why in the comments section accompanying this commentary.
超級城市的生活
life in the uber city
倫敦 — — 是的！
london mais oui!
每位法國五年級小學生都知道，網際網路的發明地是巴黎。
as every french fifthgrade student knows, the internet was invented in paris.
當時它名叫迷你電傳(Minitel ) , 也就是法語Médium interactif par numérisation d’information téléphonique的縮寫，擁有近900萬臺終端，個人和組織可以實時聯網進行資訊交換。
it was called minitel, short for mdium interactif par numrisation dinformation tlphonique, a network of almost nine million terminals that allowed people and organizations to connect to each other and exchange information in real time.
迷你電傳曾在20世紀八九十年代蓬勃發展，孕育了各種��線應用的雛形，後來正是這些應用引領了全球.com狂潮。
minitel boomed during the 1980s and 1990s, as it nurtured a variety of online apps that anticipated the global dotcom frenzy.
“真正”的網際網路主宰全球后迷你電傳開始逐漸衰退，直到最終退出歷史舞臺。
it then fell into slow decline and was finally decommissioned after the real internet rose to global dominance.
迷你電傳和網際網路都基於數字資訊網路建立。
both minitel and the internet were predicated on the creation of digital information networks.
但兩者的實施模式卻截然相反。
their implementation strategies, however, differed enormously.
迷你電傳採取自上而下的模式；由法國郵政及全國電信運營商負責主要的部署工作。
minitel was a topdown system a major deployment effort launched by the french postal service and the national telecommunication operator.
Minitel網路執行效果良好，但僵化的體制和專用協議必然限制其增長和創新的潛能。
it functioned well, but its potential growth and innovation was necessarily limited by its rigid architecture and proprietary protocols.
相反，網際網路採取自下而上的模式，成功地避開了電信巨頭初期的監管。
the internet, by contrast, evolved in a bottomup way, managing to escape the telecommunication giants initial appeals for regulation.
最終演變成我們今天熟知的混亂但具有革命意義的改變世界的力量（教皇弗朗西斯不久前稱之為“來自上帝的禮物 ” 。 ）
ultimately, it became the chaotic but revolutionary worldchanger that we know today a gift from god, as pope francis recently put it.
今天，又一場技術革命已經迫在眉睫。
today, another technological revolution is looming.
無所不在的數字網路正在侵入實體空間，由此而來的是“一切的網路 ” — — “ 智慧城市”的網路命脈。
pervasive digital networks are entering physical space, giving rise to the internet of everything the networked lifeblood of the smart city.
五花八門的推廣模式正在世界各地湧現。
and, once again, a broad spectrum of implementation models is emerging in different parts of the world.
智慧城市空間的總體思路一直最受美國現代成功創業者的青睞。
in the united states, the general idea of smart urban space has been central to the current generation of successful startups.
最近的例子是智慧手機應用程式Uber，任何人都可以用它來打車出行或載客賺錢。
one of the latest examples is uber, a smartphone app that lets anyone call a cab or be a driver.
這家企業的經營狀況兩極分化 — — Uber一直是全世界（主要是歐洲）的抗議和罷工物件 — — 但不久前估值時卻達到了驚人的180億美元。
the companys operations are polarizing uber has been the subject of protests and strikes around the world mainly in europe yet it was recently valued at a stratospheric 18 billion.
除Uber外，恆溫控制裝置Nest、公寓共享站點AirBnB和蘋果剛剛釋出的“家用作業系統”等若干創新發明都證明數字資訊正在進入真實的生活。
beyond uber, the learning thermostat nest, the apartmentsharing website airbnb, and the justannounced home operating system by apple, to name just a few innovations, attest to the new frontiers of digital information when it inhabits physical space.
類似的方法很可能解放城市生活從通勤、能源使用到個人健康的方方面面 — — 並得到來自風險投資基金的積極支援。
similar approaches now promise to revolutionize most aspects of urban life from commuting to energy consumption to personal health and are receiving eager support from venture capital funds.
南美、亞洲和歐洲各級政府正迅速認識到建設“智慧”城市的潛在好處，並且積極為該領域籌集大筆投資。
in south america, asia, and europe, all levels of government are quickly identifying the potential benefits of building smart cities, and are working to unlock significant investment in that area.
里約熱內盧正在建設“智慧操作”中心；新加坡即將啟動雄心勃勃的“智慧國家”計劃；阿姆斯特丹最近投資6000萬歐元（合8100萬美元）建設新的城市創新中心阿姆斯特丹城市解決方案。
rio de janeiro is building capacity at its smart operations center singapore is about to embark in an ambitious smart nation effort and amsterdam recently channeled 60 million 81 million into a new urban innovation center called amsterdam metropolitan solutions.
歐盟的2020展望計劃已經為2014到2016年撥付了150億美元的投資 — — 尤其在這樣一個財政緊張的時刻，依然為智慧城市理念預留了大量的資源。
the european unions horizon 2020 program has earmarked 15 billion in 20142016 a significant commitment of resources to the idea of smart cities, especially at a time of severe fiscal constraints.
但上述資金如何運用才最有效？
but how can such funding be used most effectively?
事實上，大筆公共撥款是不是刺激智慧城市的正確途徑？
indeed, is allocating huge sums of public money even the right way to stimulate the emergence of smart cities?
政府當然在支援學術研究和在風險投資不感興趣的領域促進應用等方面扮演著重要的角色 — — 比方說城市垃圾或自來水服務領域，雖然單調乏味但卻至關重要。
government certainly has an important role to play in supporting academic research and promoting applications in fields that might be less appealing to venture capital unglamorous but crucial domains, such as municipal waste or water services.
公共部門也可以促進這些專案採用開放的平臺和標準，從而推動其在全球城市的應用（巴塞羅那的“城市協議”計劃在這方面邁出了重要的一步 ） 。
the public sector can also promote the use of open platforms and standards in such projects, which would speed up adoption in cities worldwide barcelonas city protocol initiative is a step in this direction.
但最重要的是，各國政府要向美國學習，投資開發出面向智慧城市的自下而上的創新生態系統。
but, most important, governments should use their funds to develop a bottomup innovation ecosystem geared toward smart cities, similar to the one that is growing in the us.
決策者必須超越傳統的孵化器思維，創造並培育出能讓創新遍地開花的監管架構。
policymakers must go beyond supporting traditional incubators by producing and nurturing the regulatory frameworks that allow innovations to thrive.
鑑於不斷困擾Uber及Airbnb的法律障礙，這種支援迫切為創新企業所需要。
considering the legal hurdles that continuously plague applications like uber or airbnb, this level of support is sorely needed.
與此同時，政府應避免扮演決定性和自上而下的角色。
at the same time, governments should steer away from the temptation to play a more deterministic and topdown role.
未來智慧城市方案是什麼樣子不應由他們決定 — — 更不能動用公共資本鞏固該領域技術跨國企業的地位。
it is not their prerogative to decide what the next smartcity solution should be or, worse, to use their citizens money to bolster the position of the technology multinationals that are now marketing themselves in this field.
這些企業所提供的專有、乏味的現成產品需要不惜一切代價加以避免 — — 以免我們一覺醒來發現自己生活的城市只有Minitel。
these companies readymade, proprietary, and typically dull offerings represent a route that should be avoided at all costs lest we wake up to find ourselves in minitel city.
汽車安全之路
the road to car safety
東京—汽車 — — 自由、地位和成功的老牌象徵 — — 正站在十字路口。
tokyo the automobile long a symbol of freedom, status, and success is at a crossroads.
一個多世紀以來，汽車讓數十億人得以旅行得更遠、更快、更高效。
for more than a century, cars have enabled billions of people to travel farther, faster, and more efficiently than ever before.
汽車幫助提高了世界經濟大國的實力，決定了現代社會和文化輪廓。
they have helped power the worlds great economies and shaped our modern social and cultural landscape.
但所有這些都是有代價的：事故、擁堵、汙染、難以擺脫的石油依賴，以及其他。
but all of this has come at a price accidents, congestion, pollution, and an uneasy dependence on oil, among other costs.
因此，我們的挑戰是增加汽車帶來的好處，降低（並最終消除）汽車帶來的傷害，從而讓未來乘車旅行變得清潔、高效、安全且人人可行。
our challenge, therefore, is to boost the benefits and reduce and eventually eliminate the harm done by our cars, so that the future of motor travel is clean, efficient, safe, and accessible to all.
因此若要讓汽車產業依然是進步的工具，我們必須與其他產業的同道以及政府在三分方面展開精誠合作：安全、環境和價格。
for our industry to remain an instrument of progress, we must therefore work closely with our peers from other industries and government in three major areas safety, the environment, and affordability.
道路安全是一個大問題。
road safety is a grave concern.
每天都有3,000多人因為與汽車有關的事故身亡。
more than 3,000 people die in autorelated accidents every day.
低收入國家擁有全世界的一半汽車，但卻佔據了致死交通事故的90%以上。
lowerincome countries account for only half of all vehicles on the road but suffer more than 90 of the fatalities.
印度的汽車數量比法國少四倍，道路相關死亡案例卻要多20倍 — — 也就是說，平均每輛車造成的事故數高80倍。
india has four times fewer cars than france, though it suffers 20 times more roadrelated deaths that is, 80 times more accidents per car.
但安全性正在改善。
but safety is improving.
在歐洲，雖然汽車數量翻番，但道路死亡降低了一半。
in europe, even as the number of vehicles has doubled, the number of road deaths has been halved.
一個原因是引入了防抱死制動、安全氣囊和電力穩定性控制等技術。
one reason for this is the introduction of technologies such as antilock brakes, airbags, and electronic stability control.
目前正在開發階段的技術甚至可以根除與汽車相關的死亡事故。
technologies now in development could even eliminate autorelated fatalities altogether.
這一方面的一個創新是自動駕駛。
one such innovation is autonomous driving.
雷諾和日產目前正在合作研發互補性技術，可用於預測、偵測和防止碰撞。
renault and nissan are currently working on complementary technologies that can predict, detect, and prevent collisions.
透過減少在交通擁堵和不熟悉地段駕駛帶來的壓力，這一技術能更好地保護司機和行人。
by reducing the stresses of driving in heavy traffic and unfamiliar locations, this technology promises greater protection for both drivers and pedestrians.
這對於行動不便的人來說價值更大，如老年或殘疾司機。
it is especially valuable to people with restricted mobility, such as elderly or disabled drivers.
但這類技術突破不能簡單地發明和使用，它們需要政府的支援 — — 如規定它們的使用範圍的一致的法律和規則。
but such breakthrough technologies are not simply invented and then implemented they need government support in the form of a coherent set of laws and regulations covering their use.
因此，要想在我們的有生之年實現道路“零致死”的目標，決策者必須在研發的早期階段就參與進來。
policymakers must therefore be involved at an early development stage if we are to reach the goal of zero fatality roads within our lifetimes.
汽車業還能為環境做出重要貢獻。
the auto industry can also make a vital contribution to the environment.
十五年前，雷諾-日產聯合公司（Renault-Nissan Alliance）便在全生命週期的基礎上評估了旗下汽車的環境影響。
fifteen years ago, the renaultnissan alliance evaluated the environmental impact of its vehicles over their life cycle.
這項研究考察了我們的原材料使用的影響、汽車尾氣對公共健康的影響（特別是在擁堵的城市地區）以及對總體溫室氣體排放的影響 — — 全世界有23%的溫室氣體來自汽車業。
the study examined the effect of our rawmaterial usage the impact of car exhaust on public health, especially in congested urban areas and the contribution to overall greenhousegas emissions 23 of which come from the auto industry worldwide.
這份評估帶來的結果是雷諾-日產投資了40多億歐元用於零排放技術。
as a result of that evaluation, the alliance invested more than 4 billion 5.5 billion in zeroemission technologies.
如今，我們是唯一一家大規模生產全系列零排放汽車和輕型商務車的汽車集團。
today, ours is the only auto group that massproduces a full line of zeroemission cars and light commercial vehicles.
雷諾和日產加起來在全球售出了10萬多部此類汽車 — — 比其他所有主要汽車生產商的總和還要多。
renault and nissan together have sold more than 100,000 such vehicles worldwide more than all of the other major carmakers combined.
更大的任務是讓這些汽車融入效率更高、更清潔的電網 — — 比如用水電代替老舊的火電廠。
the broader task is to integrate these vehicles into a more efficient and cleaner power grid for example, by replacing aging coalfired power plants with hydroelectric power.
此外，地方和國家政府應該與汽車業合作，讓零排放汽車融入國家交通基礎設施。
moreover, local and national governments should work with the automobile industry to integrate zeroemission vehicles into national transport infrastructure.
如果實現了這一點，我們相信汽車有望在可預見的未來實現對環境的零影響。
if this is achieved, we believe it will be possible for cars to have zero impact on the environment in the foreseeable future.
但是，更好的健康性和安全性不能（也不必）要以犧牲發展中國家為代價。 發展中國家的人民也希望享受到發達國家人民享受已久的繁榮果實。
greater health and safety, however, should not and need not come at the expense of developing countries, whose citizens want the fruits of prosperity that developed countries citizens have long enjoyed.
1999年，巴西、俄羅斯、印度和中國只佔全球汽車銷量的8 % ； 到2012年，這四個國家總銷量已經達到了全球總量的35 % 。
in 1999, brazil, russia, india, and china accounted for a mere 8 of vehicle sales worldwide by 2012, their combined sales had reached a staggering 35 of the global total.
並且這一比例肯定還將進一步上升。
and this proportion is sure to rise.
如此卓越的增長的一個原因是汽車生產商為注重成本的新興中產階級開發了更廉價的汽車。
one reason for this extraordinary growth is that carmakers have developed more affordable cars for a new, costconscious middle class.
在印度設計和製造的雷諾-日產的CMF-A平臺將為在所有發展中國家推廣廉價汽車掃清障礙。
the alliances cmfa platform, created and manufactured in india, will pave the way for many more affordable vehicles throughout the developing world.
這些進步站在日益明顯的通往“樸素創新”的趨勢的前沿，而發達國家市場也越來越接受這一趨勢。
these advances are at the forefront of a growing trend toward frugal innovation that is increasingly being adopted in developed markets, too.
汽車在過去一個世紀中對我們的政治、經濟、社會和文化生活所造成的影響怎麼強調都不過分。
it is hard to overestimate the impact that the automobile has had on our political, economic, social, and cultural life over the past century.
汽車業的全球銷售額比第六大經濟體的GDP還要高，併為全世界5,000多萬人提供了工作崗位。
the industrys global sales are greater than the gdp of all but the five largest economies, and it employs more than 50 million people worldwide.
汽車業的未來與世界經濟的未來息息相關。
its future is bound up with that of the world economy.
現在的挑戰是發明一種新汽車，讓它能夠在未來幾十年中依然是自由和安全的驕傲圖騰。
the challenge now is to reinvent the car so that it remains a proud totem of freedom and safety in the decades ahead.
反對氣候絕望
the case against climate despair
斯德哥爾摩—今年夏天肆虐北半球的熱浪和極端天氣事件讓氣候變化再次回到公共辯論前沿。
stockholm heat waves and extremeweather events across the northern hemisphere this summer have brought climate change back to the forefront of public debate.
早前的分析強烈表明，本月登陸美國東海岸的佛羅倫薩颶風等自然災害，因為全球氣溫的上升而加劇。
early analyses strongly suggest that natural disasters such as hurricane florence which barreled into the us east coast this month have been exacerbated by rising global temperatures.
儘管美國總統特朗普已經撕毀2015年巴黎氣候協定，但世界其他國家對於遏制溫室氣體排放的決心越來越大。
though us president donald trump has reneged on the 2015 paris climate agreement, the rest of the world is becoming increasingly convinced of the need to limit greenhousegas ghg emissions.
上個月，一群氣候科學家在《美國科學院院刊 》 （ Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences）上發表了一份報告，警告地球可能正在變成不適合人類居住的“火爐 ” 。
last month, a group of climate scientists published a report in the us proceedings of the national academy of sciences warning that the planet could be on a path to becoming a hothouse that may not be habitable for humans.
地球已錄得上一次冰河期以來的最高氣溫。
the earth has already registered the highest temperatures since the last ice age.
但報告指出，如果全球平均氣溫上升到前工業化水平以上2攝氏度以上，我們正在經歷的這些都算不上什麼。
but, as the report notes, what we are experiencing today will be nothing compared to what is in store if average global temperatures surpass 2 celsius above preindustrial levels.
到那時，作者們寫道 ， “ [全球]變暖可能會啟用引爆因素，進一步提升溫度並啟用其他引爆因素，就像多米諾骨牌那樣，讓地球系統溫度繼續升高。
at that point, the authors write, global warming could activate important tipping elements, raising the temperature further to activate other tipping elements in a dominolike cascade that could take the earth system to even higher temperatures.
”關於氣候引爆點和末日情景的科學爭論仍在繼續。
the scientific debate about climactic tipping points and nightmare scenarios is ongoing.
但沒人能夠篤定地認為 ， 《 火爐地球》報告中所列出的風險不是真的。
but no one can say for certain that the risks outlined in the hothouse earth report are not real.
但還有另一個風險：類似這樣的警告會導致絕望。
but there is another risk that warnings such as these will lead to despair.
大量報告認為，實現巴黎協定所列出的目標難於上青天。
numerous reports have already concluded that it will be exceedingly difficult to meet the targets outlined in the paris agreement.
但就此認為已經毫無希望不但十分危險；事實上也是錯誤的。
but to conclude that the situation is hopeless is not just dangerous it is also factually incorrect.
畢竟，當前政治和技術發展情況孕育著真正的希望。
after all, political and technological developments that are currently underway offer grounds for genuine hope.
在這個月的舊金山全球氣候行動峰會上，人們探討了最近幾個月到幾年中所出現的大量預警報告。
at the global climate action summit in san francisco, california, this month, there was plenty of talk about the numerous alarming reports that have come out in recent months and years.
但真正的焦點集中在《指數氣候行動路線圖上 》 ， 這項重大新研究表明，在使用非化石燃料技術等方面的進展以指數而不是線性的方式推進。
but the real focus was on the exponential climate action roadmap, a major new study showing that progress in the use of nonfossilfuel technologies is advancing not just linearly, but exponentially.
你也許沒有意識到，但太陽能和風能電力的使用每四年就能翻一番。
you may not realize it, but solar and windpower usage is doubling every four years.
如果這一趨勢持續下去，到2030年，全球至少一半發電產能可以來自這兩種可再生能源。
if that continues, at least half of global electricity production could come just from these two forms of renewable energy by 2030.
並且沒有理由認為進展不會進一步加速。
and there is no good reason to think that progress couldnt accelerate further.
在過去短短几年中，太陽能技術和能源儲存就經歷了迅速發展。
just in the past few years, there have been rapid advances in solarenergy technologies and energy storage.
全球經濟和氣候委員會估算，未來15年全球新基礎設施投資規模將達到90 萬億美元。
the global commission on the economy and climate estimates that 90 trillion will be invested in new infrastructure around the world over the course of the next 15 years.
拜目前正在興起的新技術所賜 — — 不僅包括能源方面，也包括數字技術 — — 人類將迎來進入更加可持續的碳中性棲息模式的歷史性機會。
owing to the new technologies that are now emerging not just in energy but in the digital domain as well humanity could have an historic opportunity to leapfrog into far more sustainable, carbonneutral patterns of habitation.
此外，除了技術方面的深遠進步，私人和公共部門也日益認識到所有決策都要考慮可持續性的重要性。
moreover, in addition to the farreaching advances in technology, there is also growing private and publicsector awareness of the importance of factoring sustainability into all decisions.
新的能源、工業、建築、城市規劃、交通、農業和林業方針，有望到2030年實現溫室氣體排放減半。
new approaches to energy, industry, architecture, city planning, transportation, agriculture, and forestry have the potential to halve ghg emissions by 2030.
但這只有在決策者廣泛聯手採取行動的情況下才能實現。
but that will happen only if a broad coalition of decisionmakers decides to deploy them.
幸運的是，政府和大公司開始表現出在些問題上的領導力。
fortunately, governments and major corporations have begun to show leadership on these issues.
結果，佔全球排放總量40%的49個國家的溫室氣體排放已經見頂；甚至有十個國家承諾到2050年實現碳中性。
as a result, ghg emissions have already peaked in 49 countries that account for 40 of global emissions and ten countries have even committed to being carbonneutral by 2050.
加利福尼亞州和瑞典表示將在2045年實現零淨排放。
california and sweden say that they will produce zero net emissions by 2045.
指數氣候行動路線圖表明，我們仍能夠決定我們的氣候未來。
the exponential climate action roadmap shows that we do still have a say over our climate future.
不可否認，前方充滿了危險。
the dangers that await us cannot be denied.
如果溫室氣體排放和升溫繼續按照當前趨勢發展，我們的子孫後代很有可能將必須忍受“火爐地球 ” — —假設他們能夠生存下來的話。
if ghg emissions and rising temperatures continue on their current trajectories, we could well reach the point at which future generations will have to endure hothouse earth, assuming that they can survive at all.
但最近的科學成果固然表明了氣候變化的危險，但也給出了前進方向。
but just as recent scientific work has underscored the dangers of climate change, so, too, has it shown the way forward.
在新技術的迅速擴散中，在產業、政府和公民社會內部對問題的日益清醒的認識中，存在著希望。
there is hope in the rapid diffusion of new technologies, and in the growing awareness of the problem within industry, government, and civil society.
如果我們能夠確保指數技術進步，並拿出必要的政治意願，就能處理好其後危機。
if we can ensure exponential technological progress and marshal the necessary political will, we can tackle the climate crisis.
“穩定地球”仍然在我們的可觸及範圍內。
a stable earth is still within our reach.
駁直升機撒錢
the case against helicopter money
慕尼黑—歐洲央行實施擴張性貨幣政策已經多年，但仍沒能讓通脹回到其“低於但接近2 % ” 的目標水平。
munich despite years of expansionary monetary policy, the european central bank has failed to push inflation back up to its target of below but close to 2.
最新措施 — — 對歐洲央行主要再融資操作實施零利率、月度資產購買量從600億歐元增加到800億歐元，以及進一步將存款利率下調到-0.4 % — —也無法改變局面。
the latest measures a zero interest rate on the ecbs main refinancing operations, an increase in monthly asset purchases from 60 billion 67 billion to 80 billion, and an even lower deposit rate of 0.40 are unlikely to change this.
因此，一些經濟學家正在敦促歐洲央行更進一步，採取所謂的“直升機撒錢 ” — —即透過印鈔來為私人消費融資。
that is why some economists are urging the ecb to go even further, with socalled helicopter drops that is, financing private consumption by printing money.
直升機撒錢的思想可以追溯到20世紀60年代的貨幣主義爭論。
the idea of helicopter money dates back to the monetarism debates of the 1960s.
該思想認為，央行永遠不會計窮於刺激總需求和抬高通脹，只要它願意採取極端措施。
a central bank, it was argued, never runs out of options for stimulating aggregate demand and stoking inflation, provided it is willing to resort to radical measures.
但這個曾經的理論概念現在看上去頗有切實可能性。
but what was once a theoretical notion now seems to be a concrete possibility.
在實踐中，直升機撒錢的形式將是一次性一家庭為單位支付或全民發放消費券，錢全部由央行出。
in practice, helicopter drops would arrive in the form of lumpsum payments to households or consumption vouchers for everybody, funded exclusively by central banks.
分配錢的政府或商業銀行資獲得一筆存款信用或得到一筆現金，但央行資產負債表的資產欄不會出現債權。
governments or commercial banks distributing the money would be credited with a deposit or be given cash, but no claim would be created on the lefthand side of the central banks balance sheet.
這種單式記賬（single accounting）將降低央行股本，除非它實現（賣出）其資產負債表上的價值準備金（valuation reserves ） 。
this type of single accounting would reduce the central banks equity capital, unless it realized sold valuation reserves on its balance sheet.
該方針的支持者認為央行受可以按需調整的特殊會計規則的約束。
proponents defend this approach by claiming that central banks are subject to special accounting rules that could be adjusted as needed.
如今，直升機撒錢的支持者包括一些要人，包括美聯儲前主席本·伯南克（Ben Bernanke ） 、 英國金融服務局前局長阿代爾·特納（Adair Turner）等。
the proponents of helicopter drops today include some eminent figures, including former us federal reserve chair ben bernanke and adair turner, former head of the united kingdoms financial services authority.
而儘管歐洲央行行長德拉吉強調歐洲央行採取直升機撒錢面臨技術、法律和會計方面的障礙，但並沒有將它排除在外。
and while ecb president mario draghi has highlighted the technical, legal, and accounting obstacles that stand in the way of helicopter drops by his institution, he has not ruled them out.
現在的問題是：如此極端的措施真的可行嗎？
the question now is is such an extreme step really justified?
答案是否定的。
the answer is no.
當通縮日益惡化時，如20世紀20年代末到30年代初，直升機撒錢確實是可行的政策選項，但如今並非如此 — — 不管是歐元區還是全球經濟。
while helicopter drops are a viable policy option if deflation is spiraling downward, as it was in the late 1920s and early 1930s, that is not the case today neither in the eurozone nor in the global economy.
誠然，需求增長萎靡不振，這反映出2008年爆發的全球金融危機的漫長後遺症。
true, demand growth is subdued, reflecting the lingering fallout from the global financial crisis that erupted in 2008.
銀行、企業和家庭仍然在清理資產負債表，消化他們在泡沫破裂前的信用繁榮期所累積的債務。
banks, firms, and households are still cleaning up their balance sheets and working off the heaps of debt they amassed during the credit boom that preceded the bust.
但他們已經取得了重大進展，這意味著對增長的拖累即將結束。
but they have already made significant progress, meaning that the drag on growth is set to diminish.
今天的消費者並沒有因為預期商品和服務會變得更便宜（通縮時期的預期）而抑制支出。
consumers today are not holding back on spending because they expect goods and services to become cheaper, as one would expect during a period of deflation.
相反，他們正在逐漸增加支出，以利用恢復的收入增長和因石油和大宗商品價格大跌而大大增加的購買力。
instead, they are gradually increasing their spending, taking advantage of restored income growth and large gains in purchasing power caused by collapsing oil and commodity prices.
因此，大部分發達國家再一次以接近產能的水平生產。
as a result, most advanced economies are once again producing at close to capacity.
公司利潤資料也不支援我們正陷入通縮的觀點。
data on corporate profits also contradict the view that we are mired in deflation.
物價穩定沒有讓利潤邊際承壓。
price stability has not put profit margins under pressure.
相反，在許多發達經濟體，部分拜投入品成本下降所賜，利潤相當高 — — 甚至達到了創紀錄的高位。
on the contrary, in many advanced economies, profits are high even reaching record levels owing partly to lower input costs.
在這樣的環境下，康央行之慨分錢將造成十分危險的長期系統性後果，因為它會給所有參與者帶來不當激勵。
in this environment, distributing largesse financed by the central bank would have dangerous systemic consequences in the long run, because it would create perverse incentives for everyone involved.
只要增長不如達不到希望的強度，決策者就會想到動用直升機撒錢，而不是去實施解決經濟表現萎靡的根本原因的困難的結構改革。
